rules.rule: For manyu and for the wronged stance, kshama, samatva-toward-the-offender and 'no one gives you sorrow' are not antidotes on Days 1 to 4 of week 1. tejas, satya-vak and abhaya come first.
rules.source: MBh Vana 28 (Prahlada); Valmiki Yuddha 21 (ocean); contract product rules

rules.rule: No verse with move=rebukes or flag reproach is an antidote for glani, dainya, shoka or vishada.
rules.source: rag-vs-graph comparison 6 Nov 2026: 2.2, 2.11, 4.40, 16.21 in sharp lines did the harm

rules.rule: level=self antidotes are week 3 by default; mortality-flagged ones never in week 1 for bhaya about a loved one or fresh shoka.
rules.source: progression doc 2 Nov 2026 (mortality verse on Day 4 for the chemo daughter)

rules.rule: vairagya as antidote is read as loosening the grip (Chudala, Gita 18.7-9), never as leaving duties; blocked for aspiration stance in week 1.

tap_trail.why: 14 of 22 app users tapped two or more words, often within a second, and the app keeps only the last; 6 of 12 'light' finals tapped a heavy word first (onboarding analysis 13 Nov 2026). The trail is the signal, the last word is the direction they want to face.
rules: Final word sets the door (stance vote and Day 1 register). Earlier words set what the week must still account for.

heavy then light (anxious + hopeful): stance aspiration, register light. Day 1 affirms the hope (light_fit), Day 2 is 'what will test it' built from the heavy word's states, Days 3-4 give ground against that state. Never open with names_pain.
light then heavy (hopeful + anxious): stance struggle, but toward-states include the light word's states and at least one affirming day (Day 4 or 6) is kept.
heavy + heavy: union of states, ranked by order tapped with the last word first; if 'hurt' or 'angry' is anywhere in the trail, add a wronged vote of 0.25.
light + light: seeking or aspiration by the last word; no afflictive states at all; depth may start at mind.
A word tapped and replaced in under 2 seconds counts at half weight.
One word alone never decides the stance (ai/stance.py STRUGGLE_FLOOR): situations, note, age and life stage still vote.

reading.stance: wronged (if note or situation agrees) else struggle

dwell.dwell_weight: earlier word weight = 0.4 + min(0.4, ms / 20000); kept word = 1.0; under 1.5 s and not kept = dropped
dwell.first_tiles_note: anxious and overthinking are the first two tiles and open 9 of 14 real multi-word trails inside a second; without ms, the first word of a 3+ word trail is halved.

real_trails.rule: Day 1 from light_fit verses that heal viraha or nirveda; never a verse that depicts collapse.
overthinking dropped (under 1.5 s); lonely at 13 s is the real pause.

meta.note: Reference graph for plan assembly. A candidate generator and rulebook, not a picker. Gita Vishwa was studied for structure only; no curated edge of it is copied.

state:vishada.label: viṣāda
state:vishada.modern: Collapse, despair, the will giving way
state:vishada.gloss: The sinking of the whole person when the will gives out; the Gita's first chapter is named for it (Arjuna-viṣāda-yoga).
state:vishada.self_view: The self does not sink; it is the mind that sinks (6.5).

state:shoka.label: śoka
state:shoka.gloss: The burning of loss. Arjuna says it dries up his senses (2.8); Narada says he knows the mantras and still grieves (Chandogya 7.1.3).
state:shoka.self_view: Tarati śokam ātmavit: the knower of the self crosses grief (Chandogya 7.1.3).

state:moha.label: moha
state:moha.gloss: Judgement clouded so that right and wrong, mine and not mine, blur. The Manas calls it the root of every illness of the mind; the Gita ends when it lifts (18.73).
state:moha.self_view: Naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtir labdhā: confusion ends when one remembers who one is (18.73).

state:bhaya.label: bhaya
state:bhaya.gloss: Fear of what may be lost or may come. The Upanishad traces it to a second, an other (dvitīyād vai bhayaṃ bhavati); the Gita promises that even a little of this path protects from great fear.
state:bhaya.self_view: Fear comes from a second; who knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing (Brihad 1.4.2, Taittiriya 2.9).

state:chinta.label: cintā
state:chinta.gloss: The mind running ahead over what has not happened. The Yaksha is told worries outnumber blades of grass; the Manas calls worry a snake that has bitten everyone.
state:chinta.self_view: For one who knows the self, wanting what and for whose sake would he fret (Brihad 4.4.12).

state:krodha.label: krodha
state:krodha.gloss: The fire that rises when wanting is blocked (kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate) and then clouds judgement.
state:krodha.self_view: You are the one who sees the anger rise (14.22-23).

state:kama.label: kāma
state:kama.gloss: Desire as a force that is never filled by feeding it (duṣpūra anala) and covers clear knowing like smoke over fire.
state:kama.self_view: The joy chased outside is the self's own (5.21; Taittiriya 2.7).

state:lobha.label: lobha
state:lobha.gloss: The wanting that grows with gain. One of the three gates (16.21); the Yaksha is told it is the illness without end.
state:lobha.self_view: The self is full; nothing added makes it more (Isha 1; Brihad 5.1.1).

state:ahankara.label: ahaṅkāra
state:ahankara.gloss: The sense that I alone do and own. The Gita: the guṇas act, and the self fooled by ego thinks 'I am the doer' (3.27).
state:ahankara.self_view: The guṇas act; the self is not the doer (3.27; 13.29).

state:mada.label: mada
state:mada.modern: Drunk on success, pride of wealth or standing
state:mada.gloss: Intoxication with one's own wealth, learning, birth or power. Nahusha says success blinds even the wise.
state:mada.self_view: Whatever shines is a spark of a larger light (10.41).

state:matsarya.label: mātsarya
state:matsarya.gloss: Burning at another's good. The Manas calls it an itch and a wasting disease; Vidura calls it an illness without end.
state:matsarya.self_view: The same self in all: another's good takes nothing from you (5.18; 6.29).

state:dvesha.label: dveṣa
state:dvesha.gloss: The push away from what we dislike, twin of rāga. The Gita: both wait at every sense and are the waylayers (3.34).
state:dvesha.self_view: Seeing the one self everywhere, one does not recoil (Isha 6).

state:sanga.label: saṅga
state:sanga.gloss: Holding on: to results, people, things, a picture of how it must be. First link of the Gita's ladder of fall; the Mahabharata puts it in two syllables, ma-ma.

state:samshaya.label: saṃśaya
state:samshaya.gloss: The mind that cannot settle on what is true or what to do. Arjuna asks Krishna to cut it (6.39); the Gita warns what the doubting self loses (4.40).
state:samshaya.self_view: When That is seen, all doubts are cut (Mundaka 2.2.8).

state:chanchalya.label: cāñcalya
state:chanchalya.gloss: The mind that will not stay. Arjuna's own words: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa, as hard to hold as the wind.
state:chanchalya.self_view: You are not the mind; you are the one who sees it move (Ashtavakra 15.5).

state:pramada.label: pramāda
state:pramada.gloss: Living carelessly, letting what matters slip. Sanatsujata calls it death itself; the Gita lists it as tamas' binding.

state:alasya.label: ālasya
state:alasya.gloss: Heaviness that keeps one from beginning. Bhartrihari: the great enemy living in one's own body.
state:alasya.self_view: The self is never stuck; the mood is the mind's.

state:glani.label: glāni
state:glani.gloss: The mind turned against itself over what it did or is. In the Manas this is Bharat's glāni; the Upanishad names the thought itself: 'why did I not do right, why did I do wrong?'
state:glani.caution: In the Gita the word glāni (4.7) means decline; the sense of remorse and self-reproach is the Manas and later usage. The state is the texts'; the label follows Tulsidas.
state:glani.self_view: The self is not stained by what was done (13.31-32; Taittiriya 2.9).

state:dainya.label: dainya
state:dainya.gloss: Thinking oneself low or not enough. As an affliction the texts oppose it (never look down on yourself, MBh 3.32.58); as a devotional mood before God, Tulsidas and Surdas voice it and are lifted in it.
state:dainya.caution: Two-faced: before God, dainya is a bhakti virtue. Only the self-belittling sense is treated as afflictive; devotional dainya verses carry the devotional flag.
state:dainya.self_view: Tat tvam asi: you are That (Chandogya 6.8.7).

state:viraha.label: viraha
state:viraha.gloss: The ache of being apart from someone, home or God. The Upanishad says the first being, alone, found no joy; the epics give it to Rama, Sita and the gopis.
state:viraha.self_view: The one self lives in every heart; you were never apart (18.61; Shvetashvatara 6.11).

state:nirveda.label: nirveda
state:nirveda.gloss: Having no taste left for what one was doing. In Valmiki it is losing heart (anirveda is the root of success); in the Mundaka and Gita 2.52 the same weariness is the turn toward seeking.
state:nirveda.caution: Two-faced: never tell an empty person their emptiness is wisdom on Day 1; the Mundaka reading belongs to week 2 or 3 and to the seeking stance.
state:nirveda.self_view: Joy is in the vast, not in the small (Chandogya 7.23).

state:manyu.label: manyu
state:manyu.modern: The hurt of being wronged, indignation
state:manyu.gloss: The heat that rises when one's dignity or right is denied by another. The epics let it speak in Draupadi, Sita and Rama at the ocean, and argue openly about when forbearance ends (MBh Vana 27-29).
state:manyu.caution: Manyu here is the wronged person's legitimate heat, distinct from krodha as reactivity. The Vedic Manyu Sukta (Rig Veda 10.83-84) honours it; that reference is from memory and not in the library.
state:manyu.self_view: What you are cannot be cut smaller (2.23-24); the wrong is theirs.

state:dharma_sankata.label: dharma-saṅkaṭa
state:dharma_sankata.gloss: Two rights pulling against each other. Arjuna cannot tell which is better (2.6); the Manas pictures it as a snake that can neither swallow nor spit.
state:dharma_sankata.self_view: Acting from who you are, your duty is your own nature (18.47).

state:shrama.label: śrama
state:shrama.gloss: Being worn out by ceaseless doing. Ashtavakra: everyone suffers from straining (āyāsa) and no one notices; Prahlada says he was worn out by decisions and duties.
state:shrama.self_view: Anchored within while doing the outer work, you do not burn out (Yoga Vasishtha 6a.115.43).

state:trishna.label: tṛṣṇā
state:trishna.modern: Restless wanting, expectation, hope that binds
state:trishna.gloss: Thirst that does not age: expectation of others and of the future (āśā). Bhartrihari: we aged, craving did not; Pingala slept in peace the night she stopped expecting.
state:trishna.self_view: Enjoy by letting go; the whole remains whole (Isha 1; Brihad 5.1.1).

state:shanti.label: śānti
state:shanti.gloss: The settling that follows letting go; the Gita's stated end of several ladders (2.66, 4.39, 12.12).

state:abhaya.label: abhaya
state:abhaya.gloss: First in the Gita's list of divine qualities (16.1); the Upanishad's mark of one who knows the joy of Brahman.

state:shraddha.label: śraddhā
state:shraddha.gloss: Trust that lets one begin and continue before the proof. A person is made of their śraddhā (17.3).

state:dhriti.label: dhṛti
state:dhriti.gloss: The holding power that keeps mind and action steady through what is unpleasant (18.33); a wheel of Rama's chariot of dharma.

state:kshama.label: kṣamā
state:kshama.gloss: Strength that does not strike back. The Mahabharata praises it as what holds the world, and in the same debate says it is not always right (Vana 28).
state:kshama.caution: Never the first move for a wronged person. Always read with MBh Vana 28 and Rama at the ocean.

state:karuna.label: karuṇā
state:karuna.gloss: Feeling another's pain as one's own (6.32) and acting to ease it; dayā in the thunder's teaching.

state:maitri.label: maitrī
state:maitri.gloss: Being a friend to all beings; the Gita's first mark of the one dear to God (12.13).

state:santosha.label: santoṣa
state:santosha.gloss: Being at ease with what has come. One of Vasishtha's four gatekeepers; the Yaksha is told it is the highest happiness.

state:prasada.label: prasāda
state:prasada.gloss: The clear, settled mind in which sorrows end and understanding steadies (2.64-65).

state:utsaha.label: utsāha
state:utsaha.modern: Energy, zest, the will to begin again
state:utsaha.gloss: Lakshmana to Rama: there is no strength greater than utsāha. A mark of the sattvic doer (18.26).

state:viveka.label: viveka
state:viveka.gloss: Telling the good from the pleasant, the lasting from the passing, what is mine to do from what is not.

state:vairagya.label: vairāgya
state:vairagya.gloss: Loosening the grip, the partner of practice in training the mind (6.35). Not indifference and not leaving one's duties.
state:vairagya.caution: Carries a renunciation_push risk for householders and people who are building something; Chudala and Gita 18.7-9 are the guard rails.

state:samatva.label: samatva
state:samatva.gloss: The same in success and failure, praise and blame. The Gita's own definition of yoga (2.48).
state:samatva.caution: For a wronged person, 'the same to friend and foe' reads as 'put up with it'. Gate it out of their first four days.

state:tejas.label: tejas
state:tejas.gloss: Inner fire that does not shrink before the strong. Listed with kṣamā and dhṛti (16.3) so that neither is read without the other.

state:kritajnata.label: kṛtajñatā
state:kritajnata.gloss: Knowing what was done for you. Valmiki's Rama is pleased by one kindness and cannot repay Hanuman.

state:sharanagati.label: śaraṇāgati
state:sharanagati.gloss: Handing oneself over. Arjuna's first move as a student (2.7) and Krishna's last word (18.66); Rama's vow to Vibhishana.
state:sharanagati.caution: 18.66 is a resolution verse: never before Day 5, and always with 18.63 (the library's pair.surrender_and_reflect).

state:sankalpa.label: saṅkalpa
state:sankalpa.gloss: A settled will. The Upanishad: a person is made of resolve (kratu); the Gita: the resolute understanding is one-pointed (2.41).
state:sankalpa.caution: In Gita 6.24 and the Manki Gita, saṅkalpa is also the imagining from which desire is born. As a healing state it means resolve (vyavasāya, kratu, śiva-saṅkalpa).

state:ananda.label: ānanda
state:ananda.gloss: Joy that does not depend on getting. The Taittiriya: from joy beings are born; the Chandogya: happiness is in the vast, not the small.

state:atma_jnana.label: ātma-jñāna
state:atma_jnana.gloss: Knowing oneself as what does not change. The Upanishads' answer to grief (tarati śokam ātmavit) and fear.
state:atma_jnana.caution: Week 3 material. Body-and-death verses (2.11-30) carry the mortality flag and stay out of week 1 for the frightened and the newly bereaved.

state:seva.label: sevā
state:seva.gloss: Acting for others' good: loka-saṅgraha in the Gita, para-hita in the Manas.

state:jijnasa.label: jijñāsā
state:jijnasa.gloss: The wish to know, honoured as its own kind of approach (7.16). Nachiketa holds to his question against every bribe; Shaunaka asks for the one thing that explains the rest.

chain:bg.ladder_of_fall.title: The ladder of fall
chain:bg.ladder_of_fall.summary: Dwelling on an object breeds attachment; attachment, desire; desire, anger; anger, delusion; delusion, loss of memory; loss of memory, ruin of judgement; and with judgement gone one is lost.
chain:bg.ladder_of_fall.gate: own_chain_only: eligible for Day 2 only when sanga, kama or krodha is among the person's states. It was the default Day 2 in 16 of 24 test plans and added an anger people never mentioned.

chain:bg.ladder_of_ascent.title: The ladder of ascent
chain:bg.ladder_of_ascent.summary: Moving among things with senses in hand, free of attraction and aversion, one reaches clarity; in clarity sorrows end and understanding steadies; without that steadiness there is no peace, and without peace no happiness.

chain:bg.senses_carry_mind.title: The boat and the wind
chain:bg.senses_carry_mind.summary: The mind that follows a wandering sense has its wisdom carried off, as wind carries a boat on water. Even a striving, wise person is pulled this way (2.60).

chain:bg.desire_anger_rajas.title: What drives us against our will
chain:bg.desire_anger_rajas.summary: Arjuna asks what pushes a person to do wrong against their own wish. Krishna: it is desire, it is anger, born of rajas; it covers knowing as smoke covers fire and dust a mirror.
chain:bg.desire_anger_rajas.note: 3.38-39: kāma covers jñāna; mapped to moha.

chain:bg.inner_ladder.title: Senses, mind, intellect, self
chain:bg.inner_ladder.summary: The senses are high, the mind higher, the intellect higher still, and beyond the intellect is That (the self, in Shankara's reading). Knowing what is beyond the intellect, steady the self by the self and overcome desire.
chain:bg.inner_ladder.note: This is the contract's depth ladder (situation, mind, intellect, self) and the reason weeks climb.

chain:bg.faith_to_peace.title: From trust to peace
chain:bg.faith_to_peace.summary: The one who has trust, is intent, and has the senses in hand gains knowledge; having gained it, soon reaches the highest peace.

chain:bg.doubt_to_ruin.title: The doubting self
chain:bg.doubt_to_ruin.summary: Without knowledge and without trust, the self full of doubt is lost: no happiness here or hereafter. Then the turn: cut the doubt in the heart with the sword of knowledge, take your stand in yoga, and rise.
chain:bg.doubt_to_ruin.gate: 4.40 is a warning in a rebuke tone: never Day 1, never for glani, dainya, shoka or vishada. 4.41-42 carry the remedy and are safe from Day 3.

chain:bg.ladder_of_practice.title: If you cannot do that, then this
chain:bg.ladder_of_practice.summary: Fix the mind on me; if you cannot, reach by practice; if not that, work for my sake; if not that, give up the fruit. Knowledge is better than practice, meditation than knowledge, giving up the fruit than meditation; from that giving up, peace follows at once.
chain:bg.ladder_of_practice.note: A text-stated set of doable practices graded by capacity: the natural source for act days.

chain:bg.gunas_fruits.title: What each guna yields
chain:bg.gunas_fruits.summary: From sattva comes knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, heedlessness, delusion and ignorance. Tamas binds by heedlessness, laziness and sleep (14.8); when rajas rules there is greed, restless activity and craving (14.12).
chain:bg.gunas_fruits.note: 14.17 itself is not in the library; 14.8, 14.12 and 14.13 state the same links and are.

chain:bg.three_gates.title: The three gates
chain:bg.three_gates.summary: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate that ruins the self; give up these three. Freed from them, a person does what is good for the self and reaches the highest.
chain:bg.three_gates.gate: 16.21 in a sharp line reads as a verdict. Not Day 1; not for the ashamed.

chain:bg.brahma_bhuta.title: Serene, neither grieving nor craving
chain:bg.brahma_bhuta.summary: Letting go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, without 'mine' and at peace, one is fit for Brahman. Serene in that, one neither grieves nor craves, is the same to all beings, and gains the highest devotion.

chain:bg.arjuna_collapse.title: Arjuna's collapse
chain:bg.arjuna_collapse.summary: Seeing his own people, Arjuna is overcome; his limbs fail, he drops the bow and sits down in grief; he cannot tell which course is better; confused about what is right, he asks to be taught.
chain:bg.arjuna_collapse.note: Order as narrated. The text marks the causes at 1.28 (dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanam, kṛpayā parayāviṣṭaḥ) and 2.7 (kārpaṇya-doṣa); the rest is sequence, so these links are 'text (narrative order)'. Every verse here is spoken by or about someone in the state: the library's best Day 1 pool.

chain:bg.mind_training.title: The mind is hard to hold, and can be trained
chain:bg.mind_training.summary: Arjuna: the mind is restless, strong and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees, then: by practice and letting go it is held. Little by little, with an understanding held firm, bring it back each time it wanders; to the one whose mind is calm the highest happiness comes.

chain:bg.self_as_friend.title: Lift yourself by yourself
chain:bg.self_as_friend.summary: Lift the self by the self; do not let the self sink (nātmānam avasādayet). The self is its own friend and its own enemy. For one who has mastered the self and is at peace, heat and cold, honour and dishonour are the same.

chain:bg.karma_yoga.title: Your part is the work
chain:bg.karma_yoga.summary: Your claim is on the action alone, never on its fruits; do not make the fruit your motive, and do not cling to inaction. Steady in yoga, act having let go of clinging, the same in success and failure. Those who work for the fruit are pitiable; yoga is skill in action.
chain:bg.karma_yoga.note: c:phala_sanga>chinta is Shankara's and Madhusudana's reading of 2.47-49 (phala-tṛṣṇā as the source of the worker's misery); the verse states the remedy, the commentary names the cause. That one link is provenance commentary.

chain:bg.no_effort_lost.title: What happens to one who tried and slipped
chain:bg.no_effort_lost.summary: Arjuna fears that one who has trust but falls short is lost from both worlds like a torn cloud. Krishna: no one who does good comes to a bad end; what was gained is picked up again, carries one forward, and the one who keeps at it arrives. In this path no beginning is wasted (2.40).

chain:bg.contact_pleasures.title: Pleasures with a beginning and an end
chain:bg.contact_pleasures.summary: Pleasures born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they begin and end, and the wise do not delight in them. Unhooked from outer contacts one finds the joy that is in the self; whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here is happy.

chain:bg.dvandva_moha.title: The confusion of opposites
chain:bg.dvandva_moha.summary: From the pull of wanting and the push of aversion rises the delusion of the pairs, and all beings fall into confusion.

chain:bg.what_you_dwell_on.title: You become what you hold in mind
chain:bg.what_you_dwell_on.summary: Whatever state one keeps remembering, that one becomes; a person is made of their faith, and as the faith is, so is the person.

chain:bg.asuric_spiral.title: A hundred ropes of hope
chain:bg.asuric_spiral.summary: Given to worries that end only with death, bound by a hundred ropes of hope, given over to desire and anger, they hoard: 'this I got today, that I will get next'; 'I am rich and well born, who is my equal?'
chain:bg.asuric_spiral.gate: A portrait of the demonic nature. Usable as a mirror in week 2 for success_pride and greed_more with a careful line; never Day 1, never for the ashamed.
chain:bg.asuric_spiral.note: The text lists these together; the internal order is the verses' order, not a stated causation except āśā-pāśa binding to kāma-krodha (16.12).

chain:bg.three_joys.title: Poison first, nectar after
chain:bg.three_joys.summary: The joy one grows into by practice, like poison first and nectar in the end, is born of a clear understanding of the self. Pleasure from the senses is nectar first and poison after. The pleasure of sleep, laziness and heedlessness deludes from start to finish.

chain:bg.five_causes.title: Five causes of every result
chain:bg.five_causes.summary: Every action has five causes: the ground, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and the unseen. Whoever sees the self alone as the doer does not see.
chain:bg.five_causes.note: The antidote links to glani and mada are the library's pair.daiva_and_effort rule (curated), the link to ahankara is the verse's own (18.16).

chain:katha.chariot.title: The chariot
chain:katha.chariot.summary: Know the self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the driver, the mind as the reins, the senses as the horses. Without understanding and with the mind unyoked, the senses run like bad horses and the goal is missed; with understanding and a yoked mind, they obey and the journey's end is reached.

chain:katha.ladder.title: Higher than the senses
chain:katha.ladder.summary: Beyond the senses are their objects, beyond those the mind, beyond the mind the intellect, beyond it the great self, the unmanifest, and the Person. Let the wise merge speech in mind, mind in the knowing self, that in the great, that in the peaceful self. Arise, awake, approach the best and learn.
chain:katha.ladder.note: 1.3.10-13 are not in the library; 1.3.14 is. The parallel to Gita 3.42 is noted by the commentators.

chain:katha.shreyas_preyas.title: The good and the pleasant
chain:katha.shreyas_preyas.summary: The good and the pleasant both come to a person. The wise look at them from every side and tell them apart, choosing the good; the dull choose the pleasant for the sake of getting and keeping.

chain:katha.heart_knots.title: When the knots of the heart are cut
chain:katha.heart_knots.summary: When all the desires lodged in the heart are let go, and when all the knots of the heart are cut here, the mortal becomes deathless. That is the whole teaching.

chain:katha.outward_senses.title: Senses made to face outward
chain:katha.outward_senses.summary: The senses were made to face outward, so one sees outside and not the inner self. The immature follow outer desires into the wide net of death; the wise turn the gaze inward and do not seek the lasting among passing things.

chain:chandogya.narada_ladder.title: Narada: learned and still grieving
chain:chandogya.narada_ladder.summary: Narada knows every science and says: I know the words, not the self, and I grieve; take me across. Sanatkumara leads him inward: one speaks truth when one understands, understands when one reflects, reflects when one has trust, has trust when one is steadfast, is steadfast when one acts, acts when one finds joy; and joy is in the vast, not in the small.
chain:chandogya.narada_ladder.note: The text gives the dependencies from the top down (7.17 to 7.23); they are written here in the order one would climb.

chain:chandogya.pure_food.title: From clean intake to the loosening of knots
chain:chandogya.pure_food.summary: When what one takes in is pure, one's being is pure; when one's being is pure, memory is steady; with steady memory all the knots are loosened.
chain:chandogya.pure_food.gate: No library verse; reference only until 7.26.2 is added and checked (ref_confidence from_memory).
chain:chandogya.pure_food.note: Not in the library. Shankara reads āhāra as everything taken in through the senses, which makes this usable for phone_addiction and restless_mind.

chain:chandogya.kratu.title: A person is made of resolve
chain:chandogya.kratu.summary: A person is made of resolve; as one's resolve is in this world, so one becomes. So let one form one's resolve.

chain:taittiriya.sheaths.title: Bhrigu looks five times
chain:taittiriya.sheaths.summary: Bhrigu asks his father to teach him Brahman and is told to find it by disciplined reflection. He sees it as food, then breath, then mind, then understanding, each time sent back to look again, and at last as joy: from joy beings are born, by joy they live, into joy they return.
chain:taittiriya.sheaths.note: A second text-stated depth ladder (body, energy, mind, understanding, joy) with a student who is never handed the answer. A model for weeks 1 to 3 and a seeking-stance story.

chain:taittiriya.joy_without_fear.title: The measure of joy
chain:taittiriya.joy_without_fear.summary: Each higher joy is a hundred times the one below, and each equals the joy of the one who is learned and not struck by desire. Knowing that joy one fears nothing, and is no longer tormented by 'why did I not do right, why did I do wrong'.

chain:brihad.desire_becomes.title: As your desire, so you become
chain:brihad.desire_becomes.summary: A person is made of desire: as the desire, so the will; as the will, so the deed; as the deed, so one becomes. And one who knows the self: wanting what, for whose sake, would he fret after the body?

chain:brihad.fear_of_a_second.title: Fear comes from a second
chain:brihad.fear_of_a_second.summary: Alone, he was afraid. He reflected: since there is nothing other than me, what do I fear? And the fear left; fear comes only from a second. Alone, he also found no joy, and so one who is alone does not rejoice.

chain:brihad.maitreyi.title: Hear, reflect, dwell on it
chain:brihad.maitreyi.summary: Maitreyi asks whether wealth would make her deathless; told no, she asks to be taught instead. Yajnavalkya: nothing is dear for its own sake but for the sake of the self; the self is to be seen: heard about, reflected on, dwelt upon.
chain:brihad.maitreyi.note: Hearing, reflecting, dwelling (śravaṇa, manana, nididhyāsana) is the tradition's own three-stage progression and maps onto a three-week plan as a frame, not as a claim that the texts prescribe weekly plans.

chain:mundaka.two_birds.title: Two birds on one tree
chain:mundaka.two_birds.summary: Two birds, companions, sit on one tree; one eats the fruit, the other looks on. Sunk in the same tree, the person grieves, deluded by helplessness; seeing the other, the Lord, and his greatness, the grief leaves.

chain:mundaka.weariness_to_teacher.title: Having looked at what work can win
chain:mundaka.weariness_to_teacher.summary: Having examined the worlds won by action, the seeker comes to weariness: what is not made cannot be reached by what is made. To know that, let him go to a teacher.
chain:mundaka.weariness_to_teacher.gate: Week 2 or 3, or seeking stance. Never offered to an empty person on Day 1 as praise of their emptiness.

chain:mundaka.knot_cut.title: The knot of the heart
chain:mundaka.knot_cut.summary: When that is seen, the knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are severed, and one's actions come to rest.

chain:isha.oneness.title: Where is grief for one who sees oneness
chain:isha.oneness.summary: Who sees all beings in the self and the self in all beings does not recoil from anyone. For the one who knows all beings as the self, what delusion, what grief, seeing oneness?

chain:maitrayani.mind_binds_frees.title: The mind alone binds and frees
chain:maitrayani.mind_binds_frees.summary: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and freedom: attached to objects it binds, free of objects it frees. What the mind dwells on, that one becomes.
chain:maitrayani.mind_binds_frees.note: Verse numbering of the Maitrayani differs across editions; library ids are verified, the 6.34 reference is the common one.

chain:yv.four_gatekeepers.title: The four gatekeepers
chain:yv.four_gatekeepers.summary: Calm, inquiry, contentment and good company are the four gatekeepers at the door of freedom. Befriend one with full effort and the others follow.
chain:yv.four_gatekeepers.note: Vasishtha's own point is that any one gate opens the rest, which is why one act day can serve the whole week. The Maha Upanishad repeats the list (up_maha.150).

chain:yv.inquiry_chain.title: Inquiry to the end of sorrow
chain:yv.inquiry_chain.summary: From inquiry comes knowledge of what is so; from that, rest in oneself; from rest, a calm mind; and a calm mind ends sorrow. The inquiry is: who am I, how did this trouble come?

chain:yv.effort_and_fate.title: Fate is your own past effort
chain:yv.effort_and_fate.summary: What is called fate is only one's own earlier effort. Today's effort and yesterday's meet like two rams, and the stronger wins; so make today's the stronger. 'Fate did it' is what a tired mind says. Whatever you practise, you become.
chain:yv.effort_and_fate.gate: Library pair rule: yv.2.6.1 and 2.4.17 only for someone stuck or delaying, never for the grieving or self-blaming, and always with yv.2.6.21 (do not torment yourself over what was never in your power).

chain:yv.worry_fed_by_thought.title: Worry grows when you feed it
chain:yv.worry_fed_by_thought.summary: Worry grows by being thought about, as fire grows with fuel; not fed, it dies down. The more scenarios the mind spins, the larger its world of worry.

chain:yv.craving_and_worry.title: Craving on a rope
chain:yv.craving_and_worry.summary: Craving leads a person like a bullock on a knotted rope and shrinks even the wise and brave to a blade of grass. Letting go of anxious thought is its cure.
chain:yv.craving_and_worry.note: Spoken by Rama in his lament: a person in the state, describing it from inside.

chain:mbh.vidura_sleepless.title: Who cannot sleep
chain:mbh.vidura_sleepless.summary: Sleeplessness comes to the one attacked by someone stronger, the one who has lost everything, the one in the grip of desire, and the one who has done wrong.
chain:mbh.vidura_sleepless.note: Vidura says this to a king who cannot sleep; the mapping of 'sleeplessness' to chinta is ours (curated), the four causes are the verse's.

chain:mbh.vidura_six_faults.title: Six faults that block every rise
chain:mbh.vidura_six_faults.summary: One who wants to prosper should give up six faults: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.

chain:mbh.vidura_six_miseries.title: Six who are always unhappy
chain:mbh.vidura_six_miseries.summary: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the quick to anger, the ever suspicious, and the one who lives on another's fortune: these six are always in sorrow.

chain:mbh.vidura_what_each_takes.title: What each one takes from you
chain:mbh.vidura_what_each_takes.summary: Hope takes away steadiness, envy takes right conduct, anger takes fortune, bad company takes character, desire takes modesty, and pride takes everything.

chain:mbh.vidura_brooding.title: What brooding costs
chain:mbh.vidura_brooding.summary: By burning inside one loses looks, strength and judgement, and falls ill; the enemy is pleased and nothing is changed. So do not give the mind to it.

chain:mbh.vidura_peace.title: Where peace comes from
chain:mbh.vidura_peace.summary: I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastery of the senses, apart from giving up greed.

chain:mbh.yaksha_drop_four.title: Drop these four
chain:mbh.yaksha_drop_four.summary: Giving up pride one becomes dear; giving up anger one does not grieve; giving up desire one becomes rich; giving up greed one becomes happy.

chain:mbh.yaksha_anger_greed.title: The enemy and the illness
chain:mbh.yaksha_anger_greed.summary: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat; greed is the illness without end. The mind is faster than the wind, and worries outnumber the blades of grass.

chain:mbh.ashma_two_causes.title: Two sources of the mind's pain
chain:mbh.ashma_two_causes.summary: Pain of the mind comes from two places: the mind's own confusion, or something unwanted happening. There is no third. In grief, ask: where did I come from, where am I going, who am I?

chain:mbh.narada_not_dwelling.title: Not dwelling on it is the medicine
chain:mbh.narada_not_dwelling.summary: Dwelling on what is lost adds a second sorrow to the first. This is the medicine for sorrow: not to keep thinking of it; thought about, it does not leave, it grows. Meet the mind's pain with understanding and the body's with medicine.
chain:mbh.narada_not_dwelling.gate: 'Do not dwell on it' is steady or act material. Never Day 1 for the bereaved, where it reads as 'stop grieving'.

chain:mbh.pingala.title: The night she stopped waiting
chain:mbh.pingala.summary: Hope is the greatest sorrow and giving up hope the greatest ease; having given up her expectation, Pingala slept in peace. Whatever one calls 'mine' becomes a source of pain when it is lost.
chain:mbh.pingala.note: āśā here is expectation fixed on another person's coming, which is exactly expectation_of_others. Not a counsel of hopelessness; the line must say 'expectation'.

chain:mbh.manki.title: Desire, I know your root
chain:mbh.manki.summary: Desire, I know your root: you are born of imagining. I will not imagine you, and you will be gone, root and all.
chain:mbh.manki.note: Here saṅkalpa means imagining an object as desirable (as in Gita 6.24), not the contract's healing state 'sankalpa' (resolve). Encoded as a concept to keep the two apart.

chain:mbh.shampaka.title: The more you hold
chain:mbh.shampaka.summary: The more one holds, the more one fears for it. Without letting go there is no happiness and no sleeping without fear.

chain:mbh.craving_never_ages.title: Fire fed with wood
chain:mbh.craving_never_ages.summary: Desire is never quieted by enjoying what is desired; it grows like fire fed with fuel. Hair ages, teeth age; craving alone does not age.

chain:mbh.mine_not_mine.title: Two syllables and three
chain:mbh.mine_not_mine.summary: 'Mine', two syllables, is death; 'not mine', three, is the lasting. It is not what one has but how one holds it.

chain:mbh.greed_chain.title: What greed kills, in order
chain:mbh.greed_chain.summary: Greed kills judgement; judgement gone, shame goes; shame gone, right conduct goes; that gone, fortune goes; and fortune gone, the person is destroyed.

chain:mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness.title: Heedlessness is death
chain:mbh.sanatsujata_heedlessness.summary: Heedlessness I call death; being awake I call the deathless. Those who run after desires perish with them.

chain:mbh.sanatkumara_guard.title: Guard each thing from its thief
refs: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Narada to Shuka, quoting Sanatkumara)
chain:mbh.sanatkumara_guard.summary: Guard your discipline from anger, your fortune from envy, your learning from pride and slight, and yourself from heedlessness.

chain:mbh.vyadha_regret.title: Regret, then resolve
chain:mbh.vyadha_regret.summary: By regret one is freed from the wrong done; by resolving 'I will not do it again' one is freed from repeating it. Turning to good after a wrong, one comes out like the moon from behind a cloud.
chain:mbh.vyadha_regret.note: The text's own two-step answer to guilt: it honours the regret and gives it somewhere to go.

chain:mbh.kshama_and_tejas.title: Not always force, not always forgiveness
chain:mbh.kshama_and_tejas.summary: Prahlada, quoted by Draupadi: force is not always better, nor is forgiveness always better. One who always forgives is walked over by servants, strangers and enemies; one who never does is feared and hated. Forgive the first offence and the one done in ignorance; know the time for each. Yudhishthira answers with the praise of forgiveness, and the epic lets both stand.
chain:mbh.kshama_and_tejas.gate: For the wronged stance this framework is the only door to kshama, and not before Day 5. Present both voices; never clip to Yudhishthira's half.

chain:rcm.manas_rog.title: The illnesses of the mind
chain:rcm.manas_rog.summary: Garuda asks about the illnesses of the mind. Kakbhushundi: delusion is the root of them all. Desire is wind, greed is phlegm, anger is bile that burns the chest, and when the three combine the fever is grave. 'Mine' is ringworm, envy an itch, burning at another's joy a wasting disease, ego a swelling, craving dropsy. Everyone has them; few notice. The cure: a true teacher as physician and trust in his word, restraint as the diet, devotion to Rama as the herb, taken with faith. The sign of recovery is that dispassion gains strength, good sense gains appetite, and the weakness of craving goes.
chain:rcm.manas_rog.note: Structure and the lines in the library are verified; the full list of disease pairings is from memory of the Gita Press text and should be checked before any page prints it. The passage normalises (everyone is ill) before it prescribes, which makes it one of the few diagnosis texts that is safe for the ashamed.

chain:rcm.dharma_rath.title: The chariot that wins
chain:rcm.dharma_rath.summary: Vibhishan sees Ravana in a chariot and Rama on foot, and is afraid. Rama: the chariot that wins is another one. Courage and steadiness are its wheels; truth and good conduct its flag and banner; strength, discernment, self-restraint and the good of others its horses, harnessed with forgiveness, compassion and evenness; devotion to God the driver; dispassion the shield, contentment the sword, giving the axe, understanding the spear, knowledge the bow; a still, clean mind the quiver, with calm and the restraints for arrows. Friend, whoever has this chariot has no enemy left to conquer.
chain:rcm.dharma_rath.note: A text-stated framework of what to cultivate, given to a frightened ally who is outmatched: the model for aspiration and wronged weeks (what you stand on when the other side has the chariot). Part pairings beyond the wheels and flag are from memory of the Gita Press text.

chain:rcm.three_strong.title: Three that unsettle even the wise
chain:rcm.three_strong.summary: Desire, anger and greed are three very strong ones; they shake even a sage's mind in a moment.
chain:rcm.three_strong.gate: The chaupais that follow this doha describe woman as desire's weapon. They stay out (gender_sensitive); only the doha is used.

chain:rcm.satsanga_viveka.title: No discernment without good company
chain:rcm.satsanga_viveka.summary: Without good company there is no discernment, and that company comes by grace. Doubts do not end in a passing talk; they clear with long time among the good.

chain:rcm.knowing_trust_love.title: Knowing, trust, love
chain:rcm.knowing_trust_love.summary: Without knowing there is no trust, without trust no love, and without love devotion does not hold. No one finds rest without contentment, any more than a boat moves without water.

chain:rcm.lakshman_gita.title: The night of delusion
chain:rcm.lakshman_gita.summary: Guha grieves and blames Kaikeyi as Rama sleeps on the ground. Lakshman: no one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow; all are asleep in the night of delusion, seeing dreams. Waking is turning from the pull of things; then discernment comes and delusion flees.
chain:rcm.lakshman_gita.gate: Library pair rule (pair.no_one_gives_sorrow): never to someone blaming themselves without mbh.3.32.48; never to the wronged, where 'no one gives you sorrow' erases the wrong.

chain:rcm.pride_root.title: Pride, the root
chain:rcm.pride_root.summary: Pride is the root of the round of sorrows, the giver of every pain; so the Lord removes it from those he loves, as a mother has a child's boil lanced though the child cries.

chain:rcm.every_direction_joy.title: No grudge, no hope, no fear
chain:rcm.every_direction_joy.summary: A simple nature, a mind without crookedness, contentment with what comes; no enmity, no quarrel, no hanging hope, no dread: for such a person every direction is full of joy.

chain:rcm.contentment_dries_greed.title: Autumn sun on the puddles
chain:rcm.contentment_dries_greed.summary: As the autumn sun dries the water on the paths, contentment dries up greed.

chain:bh.fear_in_everything.title: Everything comes with a fear
chain:bh.fear_in_everything.summary: In pleasure there is fear of illness, in family of decline, in wealth of the king, in honour of humiliation, in strength of the enemy, in beauty of age, in learning of the debater, in virtue of the slanderer, in the body of death. Everything on earth comes with fear; dispassion alone is fearlessness.

chain:bh.river_of_hope.title: The river called Hope
chain:bh.river_of_hope.summary: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves craving, its crocodiles attachment, its birds restless thoughts; it uproots the tree of steadiness; its whirlpools are delusion and its high banks worry. Those who cross it with a clean mind rejoice.
chain:bh.river_of_hope.note: One verse that ties expectation, clinging, restlessness, confusion and worry into one picture, and says what they cost (steadiness).

chain:bh.craving_did_not_age.title: We aged; craving did not
chain:bh.craving_did_not_age.summary: We did not enjoy pleasures; they consumed us. Time did not pass; we did. Craving did not grow old; we grew old.
chain:bh.craving_did_not_age.note: trishna>shrama is our reading of 'vayam eva bhuktāḥ' (we were the ones consumed): curated.

chain:bh.three_kinds_of_starters.title: Three kinds of people before an obstacle
chain:bh.three_kinds_of_starters.summary: The low do not begin, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin and stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
chain:bh.three_kinds_of_starters.note: For the aspiration stance this is the text's own 'what tests a resolve': it praises the one who has begun before it names the test.

chain:bh.contented_mind.title: Who is rich, who is poor
chain:bh.contented_mind.summary: Let him be called poor whose craving is large. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?

chain:bh.patience_and_anger.title: With patience, who needs armour
chain:bh.patience_and_anger.summary: If you have patience, what need of armour? If anger, what need of enemies?

chain:vr.grief_destroys.title: No enemy like grief
chain:vr.grief_destroys.summary: Grief destroys steadiness, grief destroys what one has learned, grief destroys everything; there is no enemy like grief.
chain:vr.grief_destroys.note: Kausalya says this to explain and take back her own harsh words to Dasharatha. It needs that scene: said bare to a griever it becomes a rebuke.

chain:vr.utsaha.title: No strength greater than the will to go on
chain:vr.utsaha.summary: Lakshmana to a grieving Rama: enthusiasm is strong; there is no strength greater; nothing is out of reach for one who has it. Hanuman to himself in Lanka: not losing heart is the root of fortune. Sugriva: one who gives in to despair sinks like an overloaded boat.
chain:vr.utsaha.note: Each line is said by a friend or by the sufferer to himself, inside a scene of real loss: none is a rebuke from above.

chain:vr.anger_hanuman.title: What anger made me do
chain:vr.anger_hanuman.summary: Hanuman, after burning Lanka: blessed are those who put out rising anger with good sense, as fire is put out with water. In anger a person cannot tell what should and should not be said or done. Carried away, I may have destroyed the very one I came to save.
chain:vr.anger_hanuman.note: A causal chain stated by someone who has just lived it, with the remorse included: the right Day 2 for anger_outburst.

chain:vr.ocean.title: Humble first, firm after
chain:vr.ocean.summary: Vibhishan advises asking the ocean first, though Rama has the power to force it. Rama asks humbly for three days and is ignored. He says: my patience was taken for weakness; calm, forbearance and kind words do not work on those who do not value them; and he takes up the bow. The ocean appears, and shows the way the bridge can be built.
chain:vr.ocean.note: Whole-arc rule: the story is neither 'be patient' nor 'show force'. He asks first; when asking is taken for weakness he stands firm; and the firmness ends in a workable way across, not in destruction.

chain:ashtavakra.bondage.title: What bondage is
chain:ashtavakra.bondage.summary: Bondage is when the mind wants something, grieves over something, rejects, grasps, is pleased or angry. Freedom is when it does not. Where there is 'I', there is bondage; where there is no 'I', freedom.

chain:ashtavakra.worry.title: Suffering is born of worry
chain:ashtavakra.worry.summary: Suffering is born of anxious thought and nothing else. One who is sure of this and free of it is happy and at peace everywhere.

chain:ashtavakra.doer.title: 'I am the doer' is the snakebite
chain:ashtavakra.doer.summary: You have been bitten by the great black snake of 'I am the doer'. Drink the nectar of trust that 'I am not the doer', and be happy.

chain:ashtavakra.craving.title: Where craving is, the round is
chain:ashtavakra.craving.summary: Wherever there is craving, know the round of the world is there. Done and not done: for whom has that list ever ended? Everyone suffers from straining and no one sees it.
chain:ashtavakra.craving.gate: Ashtavakra speaks to a king who has already asked for freedom. For a burned-out householder it must not become 'stop working'; pair with ashtavakra.13.3 or 18.20 (do what is in front of you, at ease).

chain:ashtavakra.as_you_think.title: As you think, so you become
chain:ashtavakra.as_you_think.summary: One who holds himself free is free; one who holds himself bound is bound. The saying is true here: as the thought, so the going.

chain:viv.attachment_misery.title: Misery comes through attachment, not through work
chain:viv.attachment_misery.summary: Attachment comes only where we expect a return. Misery comes through attachment, not through work.
chain:viv.attachment_misery.note: A modern teacher restating Gita 2.47-48 in his own words; verbatim English in the library.

chain:viv.thought_makes.title: We are what our thoughts have made us
chain:viv.thought_makes.summary: We are what our thoughts have made us. If you think yourselves weak, weak you will be. The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.

chain:viv.stages_of_work.title: Ridicule, opposition, acceptance
refs: Vivekananda, letter to the Maharaja of Khetri, 1895
chain:viv.stages_of_work.summary: Each work has to pass through these stages: ridicule, opposition, and then acceptance.
chain:viv.stages_of_work.note: For the aspiration stance: what will test a resolve, said by someone in the middle of his own work.

word:anxious.note: Fear about something ahead. In the app it is tapped by half of users and survives as the final word for almost none, so read it from the trail.

word:overthinking.note: A mind replaying; the most common final word.

word:stuck.note: Going over something without moving; could be a decision or a rut.

word:guilty.note: Going back to what they did. Triggers the no-rebuke gate.

word:hurt.note: Something someone did. A strong vote for the wronged stance when a note or situation agrees.

word:angry.note: 'Something isn't fair': the app's own line points at manyu before krodha.

word:uneasy.note: Something does not sit right and is not yet named; widest reading, lowest confidence.

word:empty.note: Something missing. Check risk before anything else.

word:hopeful.note: Things are turning and they want to keep it going. Never pathologise.

word:determined.note: Ready to stick with it: aspiration.

word:inspired.note: Wants to do something with the feeling.

word:grateful.note: Wants to hold on to it: cultivate and deepen.

word:peaceful.note: Calm and wants to go deeper: seeking, can start at depth mind.

word:curious.note: Wants to read the Gita: seeking, dialogue-led.

mech:attachment_to_results.note: The cause is phala-sanga (2.47-49), not the 2.62 ladder. Do not add anger.

mech:need_for_approval.note: No single verse states a chain for approval-seeking; the nearest text statements are praise-and-blame evenness (12.19, Vidura 33.33) and Bhartrihari Vairagya 61. Thin: mark for curation. | patch_v2 2026-11-13: viv.attachment_misery added (Vivekananda: misery comes from wanting love in return), the plainest text-stated cause for approval-seeking.

mech:expectation_of_others.note: Pingala is the text's own case of expectation fixed on another. For the wronged stance this mechanism is NOT used; use dignity_denied.

mech:anger_reactivity.note: The one mechanism for which 2.62-63 is the person's own chain. Prefer Hanuman's version on Day 2: it carries the remorse.

mech:comparison_envy.note: Manas Rog normalises envy as a common illness before it prescribes.

mech:desire_craving.note: Richest chain coverage in the library.

mech:restless_mind.note: 6.33-36 is question and answer in the text: Day 1 and Day 3 are already linked.

mech:fear_of_loss.note: Too coarse: covers fear for a loved one (illness_family) and fear of losing what one has. For a loved one, the sanga>bhaya chains read as 'you love them too much' and are gated out of week 1; use rcm.dharma_rath and yv.worry_fed_by_thought instead.

mech:grief_attachment.note: Week 1 Day 2 for grief should normalise (meeting and parting come to all), not explain a cause inside the griever. vr.grief_destroys needs its scene.

mech:self_blame.note: Vyadha's regret-then-resolve is the text-stated arc. Rebuke gate applies to every day.

mech:ego_pride.note: Use only when the person named it themselves (success_pride). credit_taken read as ego_pride was the documented misfire: that is dignity_denied.

mech:disconnection.note: Thin on stated cause chains: the texts depict loneliness and answer with company and refuge, they do not diagnose it.

mech:duty_conflict.note: Arjuna's collapse is this mechanism's own arc; 18.63 closes it.

mech:no_meaning.note: Narada (learned and still sad) and Rama's lament are the depicting voices.

mech:resolve_begin.note: Not a pain mechanism. 'Cause' slot holds what tests a resolve, in texts that praise the one who began.

mech:dignity_denied.note: The cause is in the other person, so no inner cause chain is used on Day 2. Day 2 says whose smallness it is (mbh.5.39.63, mbh.12.114.15, mbh.5.34.75 read as 'the wrong stays with the speaker', not as 'bear it').

dlg.bg.collapse.question: How can I go through with this when it means hurting my own people? What would winning even be worth?
dlg.bg.collapse.note: The answer verses are mortality-flagged apart from 2.14; in week 1 only 2.14 answers this question.

dlg.bg.tell_me_plainly.question: I can't tell what is right any more. Just tell me clearly what I should do.
dlg.bg.tell_me_plainly.note: 2.7 is the Gita's hinge: the first surrender. 2.2-3 (Krishna's first reply) is a rebuke and is not listed as an answer.

dlg.bg.steady_person.question: What does a truly steady person look like? How do they talk, sit, move through a day?
dlg.bg.steady_person.note: 2.54 itself is not in the library.

dlg.bg.mixed_advice.question: Your advice sounds contradictory. Should I think my way out or act my way out?

dlg.bg.against_my_will.question: Why do I keep doing the thing I don't want to do, as if something pushes me?
dlg.bg.against_my_will.note: Arjuna asks it without shame, which is what makes it a Day 1 for craving and phone_addiction.

dlg.bg.which_is_better.question: You praise stepping back and you praise acting. Which one is actually better for me?

dlg.bg.restless_mind.question: My mind will not stay still. Holding it feels like trying to hold the wind. How is this calm even possible?
dlg.bg.restless_mind.note: Krishna agrees first ('no doubt, it is hard'), then answers. The model for every Day 1 to Day 3 link.

dlg.bg.tried_and_slipped.question: What happens to someone who believes, tries, and falls short? Is all of it wasted?
dlg.bg.tried_and_slipped.note: Served to the real Vrindavan note (2.40, 6.37, 6.23) and was one of the better matches.

dlg.bg.overwhelmed_by_the_vast.question: This is too big for me. I'm thrilled and terrified. Can I see the familiar face again?
dlg.bg.overwhelmed_by_the_vast.note: needs_scene. 11.41-44 is Arjuna apologising to a friend he took for granted: usable for guilt toward someone loved.

dlg.bg.form_or_formless.question: Is it better to love a God with a face, or to seek what has no form?

dlg.bg.beyond_moods.question: How would I recognise someone who has gone beyond their moods? How do they behave?

dlg.bg.faith_without_rules.question: What about people who have faith but don't follow the rulebook? Where do they stand?

dlg.bg.giving_up.question: What is real renunciation? Do I have to walk away from my life?
dlg.bg.giving_up.note: Krishna's answer is the guard against renunciation_push: walking away from a duty out of confusion or because it is hard is not renunciation.

dlg.bg.resolution.question: Have you heard this with a single mind? Is your confusion gone?
dlg.bg.resolution.note: The only place the teacher asks and the student answers. Resolution verse: Day 5 or later, week 3 by default.

dlg.katha.what_can_death_do.question: My father gave me away in anger. What happens to me now?
dlg.katha.what_can_death_do.note: A child wronged by a parent's anger whose first wish is that the father sleep in peace again. Whole arc: he is not told to forgive; he chooses it from a position of having been honoured by Yama.

dlg.katha.what_lasts.question: When someone dies, some say they are, some say they are not. What is true? And I don't want the consolation prizes.
dlg.katha.what_lasts.note: The question verses are not in the library (prasang up.p.katha.three_boons holds the scene). The first answer is not the answer: Yama begins with the good and the pleasant.

dlg.katha.how_to_get_there.question: If that is what I am, why don't I live from it? What has to be in order?
dlg.katha.how_to_get_there.note: The chariot. Question is implied by the text's own turn at 1.3; marked medium.

dlg.ashtavakra.how_to_be_free.question: How do I become free? How does real understanding come, and real letting go?
dlg.ashtavakra.how_to_be_free.note: 1.1 is not in the library. A king who has everything asks; depth self from the first answer, so week 3 or a peaceful seeker.

dlg.ashtavakra.the_test.question: You say you know what can't be lost. Then why are you still chasing more?
dlg.ashtavakra.the_test.note: The teacher tests; the student's answer is his own ease. Chapter 3 is a rebuke inside its scene: needs_scene.

dlg.yv.what_is_it_for.question: I have everything and none of it means anything. What is all this for? How do I live in the world without being crushed by it?
dlg.yv.what_is_it_for.note: A young man who has seen the world and gone quiet. The elders' first response is to praise the question (yv.1.11.37: say freely what is on your heart). The first teaching is effort, not detachment.

dlg.yv.janaka_overhears.question: I've cried 'I'm ruined' again and again. Am I going to keep doing this?
dlg.yv.janaka_overhears.note: Self-dialogue; the doorkeeper's 'get up and do today's work' is the turn.

dlg.yv.chudala.question: I gave up my kingdom and came to the forest, and I am still not at peace. What did I miss?
dlg.yv.chudala.note: A wife teaches her husband what he could not hear from her as his wife. The answer guards against renunciation_push.

dlg.mbh.yaksha.question: What is faster than the wind? What outnumbers the grass? What is the greatest wonder? Who is truly happy?
dlg.mbh.yaksha.note: Yudhishthira answers with four brothers lying dead beside him, and when offered one life back chooses fairness to his other mother's son (3.314.132). The questions are not library verses; the answers are.

dlg.mbh.cannot_sleep.question: I can't sleep. I'm burning inside. Tell me something that helps.
dlg.mbh.cannot_sleep.note: Whole arc: the king who cannot sleep is losing sleep over a wrong he is allowing. Vidura's answer starts by naming who cannot sleep. He is never told it is nothing.

dlg.mbh.where_is_peace.question: Where does peace actually come from?

dlg.mbh.forgive_or_fight.question: How can you sit there calm after what they did to us? Is forgiveness always right?
dlg.mbh.forgive_or_fight.note: Both voices are the text's. For a wronged reader the question side (Prahlada's teaching, quoted by Draupadi) is the Day 3-4 footing; Yudhishthira's side is Day 5 or later.

dlg.mbh.effort_or_fate.question: We did everything right and lost everything. Was it fate? Is there any point in trying?
dlg.mbh.effort_or_fate.note: Draupadi is the one who answers here: you ploughed and sowed; if the rain did not come it is not your failure; never hold yourself in contempt.

dlg.mbh.draupadi_krishna.question: The people who should have protected me only watched. Who do I have?
dlg.mbh.draupadi_krishna.note: Krishna does not counsel patience. He promises that the wrong will be answered.

dlg.mbh.after_the_war.question: I won and I can't bear what it cost. How do I live with what I did?
dlg.mbh.after_the_war.note: Guilt after a real harm. Yudhishthira himself says a wrong can be outweighed by the good done next (12.7.34).

dlg.mbh.what_to_do_with_loss.question: Wealth gone, someone dead, a home lost: what understanding gets a person through it?

dlg.mbh.fate_or_effort.question: Which is stronger, fate or effort?

dlg.mbh.slander.question: Someone keeps running me down in public. What do I do?
dlg.mbh.slander.note: Counsels not answering back: fine as 'the fault on display is theirs' (12.114.15); 12.114.8 leans to endurance, Day 5 or later for the wronged.

dlg.mbh.krishna_family.question: My own relatives say bitter things and I'm stuck between people I love. What do I do?
dlg.mbh.krishna_family.note: Krishna himself as the one worn down by family. Narada's answer is a weapon 'not made of iron': it is strategy, not submission.

dlg.mbh.shuka.question: Everything ends. How do I not get swallowed by sorrow over it?

dlg.mbh.inner_war.question: The war outside is over. Why is there still no peace in me?

dlg.mbh.vyadha.question: I've studied and practised for years and I'm still angry and proud. What am I missing?
dlg.mbh.vyadha.note: A learned ascetic is sent to a butcher who looks after his parents. Not a story about leaving one's calling: Kaushika is sent home to the parents he walked out on.

dlg.mbh.savitri.question: He is all I have. Will you really take him?
dlg.mbh.savitri.note: Savitri does the answering: she walks beside Death and speaks of friendship and goodness until he yields. mortality theme: not for illness_family in week 1 as a promise of outcome.

dlg.mbh.vidula.question: I lost. I just want to lie low. Why won't you let me?
dlg.mbh.vidula.note: A mother's sharp speech. Excluded from despair plans by Ankur's despair doc (8 Nov): 5.133.7 and 5.133.14 are reproach. Only the later, gentler lines are listed, and only for someone already getting up.

dlg.vr.lakshman_fury.question: They have wronged you. Why are you just accepting it? Let me fight.
dlg.vr.lakshman_fury.note: Rama's calm is about his own exile, chosen to keep his father's word. Not a template for telling a wronged person to accept; stance struggle only.

dlg.vr.rama_grief.question: She is gone and I can't think. What is left for me?
dlg.vr.rama_grief.note: The roles reverse: the younger brother steadies the elder. 'Your wisdom is not gone; grief has put it to sleep.'

dlg.vr.bharata_rama.question: Father is dead and it happened because of my mother. Come back and take what is yours. How do I carry this?
dlg.vr.bharata_rama.note: Rama first says 'I see no fault in you', then teaches impermanence. vr.2.105.x are mortality-flagged.

dlg.rcm.bharat_shame.question: Everyone must think I wanted this. I can't look at anyone. Will he even see me?
dlg.rcm.bharat_shame.note: Shame carried for a wrong someone else in the family did. Every answering voice lifts it; nobody rebukes. rcm.2.256.chaupai.2 is his own relief afterwards.
refs: Manas, Ayodhya Kand (Bharat at Prayag and Chitrakoot)

dlg.rcm.guha_lakshman.question: Look where he is sleeping tonight. Whose fault is this? How do I not hate her for it?
dlg.rcm.guha_lakshman.note: Pair rule applies; never for wronged.

dlg.rcm.garuda.question: I doubted, and it shook me. Which is the worst suffering, the greatest happiness? What are the illnesses of the mind?
dlg.rcm.garuda.note: Garuda is sent from teacher to teacher and ends up learning from a crow. The first reply normalises: who has not been bitten.

dlg.rcm.parvati.question: If he is the highest, why did he weep for his wife like any man? I doubted once and it cost me everything. Clear this for me.
dlg.rcm.parvati.note: She asks with her earlier mistake behind her (Sati's doubt). Shiva praises the question before answering.

dlg.rcm.vibhishan_chariot.question: He has a chariot and armour and you are barefoot on the ground. How can we possibly win this?

dlg.rcm.ram_gita_lakshman.question: Teach me simply how to cross over.

dlg.vr.sugriva_rama.question: I have lost her and don't know where to begin.
dlg.vr.sugriva_rama.note: A new friend, himself in exile, says it 'as a friend, not to lecture you'.

dlg.brihad.maitreyi.question: If I had all the money in the world, would it give me what I'm actually after?
dlg.brihad.maitreyi.note: A woman refuses the settlement and asks for the teaching instead.

dlg.brihad.janaka_light.question: When every outer light is gone, what do we see by?

dlg.brihad.gargi.question: Everything rests on something. What does the last thing rest on?
dlg.brihad.gargi.note: A woman scholar questioning the foremost teacher before the whole court.

dlg.chandogya.shvetaketu.question: You came home proud of all you learned. Did you learn the one thing that makes sense of the rest?
dlg.chandogya.shvetaketu.note: A father deflates a son's pride without shaming him, by asking a question and then teaching with seeds and salt.

dlg.chandogya.narada.question: I have learned so much and I am still sad. I know the words, not myself. Can you get me across this?
dlg.chandogya.narada.note: The best Day 1 in the library for high achievers who feel empty.

dlg.chandogya.indra.question: I was told I am this body. But then when it fails, I fail. That can't be right, can it?
dlg.chandogya.indra.note: He comes back four times over 101 years; the teacher says 'you are right' each time. A story about not accepting an answer that does not hold.

dlg.taittiriya.bhrigu.question: Father, teach me what is real.

dlg.mundaka.shaunaka.question: What is the one thing which, once known, makes everything else known?
dlg.mundaka.shaunaka.note: A householder with a large household asks.

dlg.maitrayani.brihadratha.question: Everything dies. I am like a frog in a dark well. Is there a way out?

dlg.maha.nidagha.question: My mind runs everywhere for nothing, and every good quality I take up, craving chews through. What do I do?

dlg.shvet.first_questions.question: Where did we come from? What keeps us going? Who is running this?

dlg.kaushitaki.father_son.question: They asked me something I couldn't answer. Didn't you teach me everything?
dlg.kaushitaki.father_son.note: A father says 'I don't know either; let us both go and learn.'

thr.ashtavakra.p.frame.title: How to be free
thr.ashtavakra.p.frame.arc: The first answer to a king: what to drop, what to rest as, what the snakebite is, what you believe you become.

thr.bg.p01.4.title: Arjuna sinks down
thr.bg.p01.4.arc: A capable person's body and will give way before a fight with his own people.

thr.bg.p02.1.title: Tell me plainly
thr.bg.p02.1.arc: He cannot tell which way is better, admits confusion, asks to be taught, and says the grief is still there.

thr.bg.p02.4.title: Your part is the work
thr.bg.p02.4.arc: No effort lost; a decided mind; the work and not the fruit; evenness; skill.

thr.bg.p03.5.title: Why do I do what I do not want
thr.bg.p03.5.arc: The question, the cause, how it covers knowing, where to start, and what in you is higher.

thr.bg.p06.2.title: Be on your own side
thr.bg.p06.2.arc: Lift yourself; the self as friend or enemy; the calm of one who has done it.

thr.bg.p06.4.title: The mind like the wind
thr.bg.p06.4.arc: Arjuna names the restless mind; Krishna agrees, then gives practice and letting go, then says it is within reach.

thr.bg.p06.5.title: Tried and slipped
thr.bg.p06.5.arc: The fear that effort was wasted; the promise that nothing done well is lost; what carries forward.

thr.bg.p12.1.title: If not that, then this
thr.bg.p12.1.arc: Four practices, each for the one who cannot do the one before, ending in peace.

thr.bg.p18.6.title: Reflect, then choose
thr.bg.p18.6.arc: Hand over the work, cross obstacles, the Lord in every heart, reflect fully and decide, you are dear to me, do not grieve.

thr.mbh.p.dharma_and_effort.title: You ploughed and sowed
thr.mbh.p.dharma_and_effort.arc: Do right for its own sake; do not wait on fate; a failed harvest is not your failure; never hold yourself in contempt.

thr.mbh.p.kshama_or_tejas.title: Forgiveness or force
thr.mbh.p.kshama_or_tejas.arc: Not always one or the other; whom to forgive; what anger does; what forgiveness holds up.

thr.mbh.p.narada_shuka.title: Not dwelling is the medicine
thr.mbh.p.narada_shuka.arc: A second sorrow added to the first; the medicine; care for both mind and body; act if you can; contentment.

thr.mbh.p.senajit_brahmin.title: No one suffers forever
thr.mbh.p.senajit_brahmin.arc: Sorrow turns; meet what comes undefeated; do not let every reason to grieve in; 'mine' is where the pain enters.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.33.title: To a king who cannot sleep
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.33.arc: Who lies awake; what the wise do with loss and trouble; decide and begin; when not to decide.

thr.mbh.p.yaksha_prashna.title: The questions at the lake
thr.mbh.p.yaksha_prashna.arc: The speed of the mind and the number of worries; contentment; what to drop; the wonder; the even mind; kindness above advantage.

thr.rcm.p.bharadwaj.title: Bharadwaj lifts Bharat's shame
thr.rcm.p.bharadwaj.arc: He asks only for love; he is told he torments himself for nothing; not to eat himself up for another's act; his sorrow will lift.

thr.rcm.p.garuda_doubt.title: Garuda's doubt
thr.rcm.p.garuda_doubt.arc: Doubt needs long company; only the scorched know the shade; who has not been bitten; the eye that sees a yellow moon.

thr.rcm.p.garuda_questions.title: The illnesses of the mind
thr.rcm.p.garuda_questions.arc: No sorrow like want and no joy like good company; the root illness; envy as an itch.

thr.up.p.chhandogya.narada.title: Learned and still sad
thr.up.p.chhandogya.narada.arc: Narada admits it; the teacher leads him from doing to steadiness to joy in the vast.

thr.up.p.katha.chariot.title: The chariot
thr.up.p.katha.chariot.arc: Who is riding, what is driving, why the horses bolt, and the call to wake.

thr.up.p.maha.nidagha.title: Nidagha's lament
thr.up.p.maha.nidagha.arc: A student describes his own mind before the teacher answers.

thr.up.p.taittiriya.convocation.title: The graduation address
thr.up.p.taittiriya.convocation.arc: What to hold to when you leave: truth, duty, learning, the people who raised you, how to give, what to do when unsure.

thr.up.p.taittiriya.joy.title: The measure of joy
thr.up.p.taittiriya.joy.arc: A taste of it, how large it is, and what it frees you from: fear, then self-reproach.

thr.vr.p.lanka_burning.title: After the anger
thr.vr.p.lanka_burning.arc: Blessed who put it out; what anger makes us say; what it cost.

thr.vr.p.ram_loses_sita.title: Lakshmana steadies Rama
thr.vr.p.ram_loses_sita.arc: Do not punish the world; trouble touches everyone and passes; even sun and moon are eclipsed; your wisdom is only asleep.

thr.yv.p.four_gatekeepers.title: Four gatekeepers
thr.yv.p.four_gatekeepers.arc: Calm, inquiry, contentment, good company; any one opens the others.

thr.yv.p.paurusha.title: Today's effort
thr.yv.p.paurusha.arc: Step by step you get there; today can outweigh yesterday; do not torment yourself over what was never yours; raise the mind like a child.

thr.yv.p.ram_lament.title: What is all this for
thr.yv.p.ram_lament.arc: Rama's own description of emptiness, the leaking mind, craving on a rope, and being one's own enemy.

thr.ashtavakra.p.craving.title: Craving is the treadmill
thr.ashtavakra.p.craving.arc: More money, pleasure or achievement won't give the mind rest; easing craving will.

thr.ashtavakra.p.detachment.title: The list that never ends
thr.ashtavakra.p.detachment.arc: The to-do list and life's ups and downs never end; peace comes from loosening your grip.

thr.ashtavakra.p.peace.title: The calm of the wise
thr.ashtavakra.p.peace.arc: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

thr.ashtavakra.p.self_knowledge.title: You are not your mind
thr.ashtavakra.p.self_knowledge.arc: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

thr.ashtavakra.p.special_instruction.title: Why striving and study do not bring peace
thr.ashtavakra.p.special_instruction.arc: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.

thr.ashtavakra.p.test.title: Ashtavakra tests the king
thr.ashtavakra.p.test.arc: Real understanding shows in behaviour: less chasing, less rattled by praise and blame.

thr.ashtavakra.p.true_knower.title: Portrait of the one who knows
thr.ashtavakra.p.true_knower.arc: Contentment looks like not replaying the past or chasing the next thing.

thr.ashtavakra.p.wisdom.title: The certainties of the calm
thr.ashtavakra.p.wisdom.arc: Most suffering is made of worry; knowing what you can't control loosens it.

thr.avadhuta.p.marks_of_avadhuta.title: The marks of a free person
thr.avadhuta.p.marks_of_avadhuta.arc: A free person seeks no honour, gives it freely, and lives in the present.

thr.avadhuta.p.take_the_essence.title: Take the jewel from the mud
thr.avadhuta.p.take_the_essence.arc: Wisdom matters more than who says it or how polished it sounds.

thr.bg.p02.2.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
thr.bg.p02.2.arc: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

thr.bg.p02.5.title: The person of steady wisdom
thr.bg.p02.5.arc: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

thr.bg.p03.1.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
thr.bg.p03.1.arc: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

thr.bg.p03.3.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
thr.bg.p03.3.arc: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

thr.bg.p03.4.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
thr.bg.p03.4.arc: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

thr.bg.p04.1.title: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
thr.bg.p04.1.arc: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

thr.bg.p04.2.title: How the great yogis live
thr.bg.p04.2.arc: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

thr.bg.p04.4.title: The glory of knowledge
thr.bg.p04.4.arc: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

thr.bg.p05.2.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
thr.bg.p05.2.arc: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

thr.bg.p05.3.title: The yoga of knowledge
thr.bg.p05.3.arc: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

thr.bg.p06.3.title: Meditation in detail
thr.bg.p06.3.arc: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

thr.bg.p09.6.title: The glory of selfless devotion
thr.bg.p09.6.arc: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

thr.bg.p11.6.title: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
thr.bg.p11.6.arc: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.

thr.bg.p12.2.title: The marks of one dear to God
thr.bg.p12.2.arc: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

thr.bg.p13.2.title: Nature and spirit
thr.bg.p13.2.arc: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

thr.bg.p14.2.title: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
thr.bg.p14.2.arc: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

thr.bg.p14.3.title: Going beyond the gunas
thr.bg.p14.3.arc: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

thr.bg.p16.1.title: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
thr.bg.p16.1.arc: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

thr.bg.p16.2.title: The demonic nature and its downfall
thr.bg.p16.2.arc: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

thr.bg.p17.2.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
thr.bg.p17.2.arc: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

thr.bg.p18.1.title: What true renunciation is
thr.bg.p18.1.arc: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

thr.bg.p18.3.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
thr.bg.p18.3.arc: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

thr.bg.p18.4.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
thr.bg.p18.4.arc: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

thr.bh.p.niti.artha.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
thr.bh.p.niti.artha.arc: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

thr.bh.p.niti.dhairya.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
thr.bh.p.niti.dhairya.arc: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

thr.bh.p.niti.durjana.title: Nitishatakam: On the wicked
thr.bh.p.niti.durjana.arc: Recognise spite for what it is, keep your distance, and stop taking it personally.

thr.bh.p.niti.karma.title: Nitishatakam: On action
thr.bh.p.niti.karma.arc: Your actions are the one thing fate itself must answer to.

thr.bh.p.niti.murkha.title: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
thr.bh.p.niti.murkha.arc: Spend your effort where it can land; some minds will not move, and the first one to check is yours.

thr.bh.p.niti.paropakara.title: Nitishatakam: On helping others
thr.bh.p.niti.paropakara.arc: Success should make you bow lower; real ornaments are listening, giving and helping.

thr.bh.p.niti.sujana.title: Nitishatakam: On the good
thr.bh.p.niti.sujana.arc: Be soft in good times and firm in bad ones, and let your good deeds stay quiet.

thr.bh.p.niti.vidvat.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
thr.bh.p.niti.vidvat.arc: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.avadhuta.title: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
thr.bh.p.vairagya.avadhuta.arc: Let others' labels and small things pass; contentment makes you rich.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.bhoga.title: Vairagyashatakam: On the instability of pleasures
thr.bh.p.vairagya.bhoga.arc: Everything you hold carries fear; hold it more lightly.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.kala.title: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
thr.bh.p.vairagya.kala.arc: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.manas.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
thr.bh.p.vairagya.manas.arc: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.nitya.title: Vairagyashatakam: Weighing the lasting and the passing
thr.bh.p.vairagya.nitya.arc: Do what matters most while you still can.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.trishna.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
thr.bh.p.vairagya.trishna.arc: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.vishaya.title: Vairagyashatakam: The mockery of giving up pleasures
thr.bh.p.vairagya.vishaya.arc: Let go before you are forced to, and stop calling relief happiness.

thr.bh.p.vairagya.yati_nripati.title: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king
thr.bh.p.vairagya.yati_nripati.arc: When the mind is content, nobody is richer than you.

thr.hans_gita.p.insults.title: How the swan answers insults
thr.hans_gita.p.insults.arc: When insulted, staying calm protects you more than hitting back.

thr.hans_gita.p.swan_and_sadhyas.title: The golden swan and the Sadhyas
thr.hans_gita.p.swan_and_sadhyas.arc: Self-control, calm under insult and truth are the best way to live.

thr.mbh.p.achara.title: Bhishma on everyday conduct
thr.mbh.p.achara.arc: A good life is built from daily conduct: kind words, respect for elders, no mockery.

thr.mbh.p.ashma_gita.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
thr.mbh.p.ashma_gita.arc: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

thr.mbh.p.bali_indra.title: Bali and Indra: the fortune that moves on
thr.mbh.p.bali_indra.arc: Success is on loan. Don't gloat in a good season or despair in a bad one.

thr.mbh.p.brothers.title: Bhishma on elder and younger siblings
thr.mbh.p.brothers.arc: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

thr.mbh.p.chirakari.title: Chirakari, the one who acts slowly
