thr.mbh.p.chirakari.arc: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.

thr.mbh.p.gandhari_counsel.title: Gandhari counsels her son
thr.mbh.p.gandhari_counsel.arc: Master yourself first. Greed never made anyone rich, and indulgent parents share the blame.

thr.mbh.p.gautama_ungrateful.title: Gautama the ungrateful
thr.mbh.p.gautama_ungrateful.arc: Gratitude is the root of every friendship. Betraying a benefactor poisons everything after.

thr.mbh.p.hamsa_gita.title: Hamsa Gita: the swan's teaching on speech and anger
thr.mbh.p.hamsa_gita.arc: Words fly like arrows. The one who doesn't answer anger with anger stands highest.

thr.mbh.p.inner_war.title: Krishna on the war within
thr.mbh.p.inner_war.arc: The hardest battle is with your own mind, and no one else can fight it for you.

thr.mbh.p.k.draupadi_durvasa.title: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens
thr.mbh.p.k.draupadi_durvasa.arc: When you have nothing left to offer, calling out is enough; help can come from a single leaf.

thr.mbh.p.k.krishna_bhishma.title: Krishna and Bhishma on the bed of arrows
thr.mbh.p.k.krishna_bhishma.arc: The one you think of in your hardest hour is already thinking of you.

thr.mbh.p.krishna_narada_kin.title: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
thr.mbh.p.krishna_narada_kin.arc: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

thr.mbh.p.kshemadarshi.title: Kalakavrikshiya consoles the fallen prince
thr.mbh.p.kshemadarshi.arc: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

thr.mbh.p.manki.title: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
thr.mbh.p.manki.arc: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.

thr.mbh.p.medhavin.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
thr.mbh.p.medhavin.arc: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.

thr.mbh.p.mongoose.title: The golden mongoose and the handful of flour
thr.mbh.p.mongoose.arc: A small gift, honestly earned and given from little, outweighs the grandest show.

thr.mbh.p.nahusha.title: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers
thr.mbh.p.nahusha.arc: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.

thr.mbh.p.pigeon_fowler.title: The pigeons and the fowler
thr.mbh.p.pigeon_fowler.arc: Kindness can shame cruelty. Wherever the one you love is, that is home.

thr.mbh.p.sanatsujatiya.title: Sanatsujatiya: the sage on death and the self
thr.mbh.p.sanatsujatiya.arc: Carelessness is the real death. Stay awake to your life and be who you are.

thr.mbh.p.savitri.title: Savitri and Satyavan
thr.mbh.p.savitri.arc: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

thr.mbh.p.vidula.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
thr.mbh.p.vidula.arc: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.34.title: Vidura Niti: careful action and wounding words
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.34.arc: Think before acting; if you did it right and it failed, don't sink. Guard your tongue.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.35.title: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.35.arc: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.36.title: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.36.arc: When insulted, don't insult back. Swallow anger, and stand with your own people.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.37.title: Vidura Niti: what cuts life short
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.37.arc: Arrogance, anger and betrayal shorten a life. Rivals in a family often protect each other.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.39.title: Vidura Niti: timing, gain and loss
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.39.arc: Speak at the right time, weigh gain against cost, and repeat what is good until it becomes you.

thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.40.title: Vidura Niti: never abandon what is right
thr.mbh.p.vidura_niti.40.arc: Don't trade what's right for desire, fear or money. Only your deeds stay with you.

thr.mbh.p.vyadha_gita.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
thr.mbh.p.vyadha_gita.arc: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

thr.mbh.p.yudhishthira_grief.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
thr.mbh.p.yudhishthira_grief.arc: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.

thr.mbh.p.yudhishthira_peace_case.title: Yudhishthira's case for peace
thr.mbh.p.yudhishthira_peace_case.arc: Winning a feud still costs you peace. Hostility only ends when someone stops feeding it.

thr.ram_gita.p.meditation_and_devotion.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
thr.ram_gita.p.meditation_and_devotion.arc: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

thr.ram_gita.p.rope_and_snake.title: The rope and the snake
thr.ram_gita.p.rope_and_snake.arc: Much of our fear is a rope mistaken for a snake; look again.

thr.rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_meets_ram.title: Hanuman meets Ram
thr.rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_meets_ram.arc: You don't need the right method; being his is enough, and he weeps to have you back.

thr.rcm.p.bhakti.kakbhushundi.title: The child Ram and the crow
thr.rcm.p.bhakti.kakbhushundi.arc: You are loved for loving, not for being impressive.

thr.rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.title: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
thr.rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.arc: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

thr.rcm.p.bharat_milap.title: Ram comes home
thr.rcm.p.bharat_milap.arc: Homecoming means gratitude to those who carried you and kindness to those ashamed to face you.

thr.rcm.p.bharat_waiting.title: The last day of waiting
thr.rcm.p.bharat_waiting.arc: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.

thr.rcm.p.chitrakoot_assembly.title: The family council at Chitrakoot
thr.rcm.p.chitrakoot_assembly.arc: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

thr.rcm.p.exile_order.title: Ram hears he is to be exiled
thr.rcm.p.exile_order.arc: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.

thr.rcm.p.friendship_pact.title: Ram and Sugriva become friends
thr.rcm.p.friendship_pact.arc: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

thr.rcm.p.janaka_chitrakoot.title: Janaka's family joins the council
thr.rcm.p.janaka_chitrakoot.arc: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.

thr.rcm.p.kakbhushundi_pride.title: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
thr.rcm.p.kakbhushundi_pride.arc: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

thr.rcm.p.nishad_lakshman.title: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
thr.rcm.p.nishad_lakshman.arc: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.

thr.rcm.p.ocean.title: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after
thr.rcm.p.ocean.arc: Always ask humbly first. But don't let humility be taken for weakness.

thr.rcm.p.parashurama.title: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
thr.rcm.p.parashurama.arc: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

thr.rcm.p.parvati_tapas.title: Parvati holds to her choice
thr.rcm.p.parvati_tapas.arc: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

thr.rcm.p.ram_gita_citizens.title: Ram's address to the citizens
thr.rcm.p.ram_gita_citizens.arc: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

thr.rcm.p.ram_gita_saints.title: Ram on good people and difficult people
thr.rcm.p.ram_gita_saints.arc: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.

thr.rcm.p.ram_kausalya.title: Kausalya lets her son go
thr.rcm.p.ram_kausalya.arc: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.

thr.rcm.p.sant_asant.title: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people
thr.rcm.p.sant_asant.arc: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.

thr.rcm.p.sati_doubt.title: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
thr.rcm.p.sati_doubt.arc: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.

thr.rcm.p.seasons.title: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
thr.rcm.p.seasons.arc: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

thr.rcm.p.shiva_parvati_samvad.title: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
thr.rcm.p.shiva_parvati_samvad.arc: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.

thr.rcm.p.vasishtha_bharat.title: Bharat refuses the throne
thr.rcm.p.vasishtha_bharat.arc: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

thr.rcm.p.vibhishan_counsel.title: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
thr.rcm.p.vibhishan_counsel.arc: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

thr.shakti_gita.p.gods_praise_mother.title: The victorious gods praise the Mother's grace
thr.shakti_gita.p.gods_praise_mother.arc: Grace is not earned by praise; even the clumsy prayer is held.

thr.shambhu_gita.p.pitris_hymn.title: The ancestors' hymn to Shiva and his easy way
thr.shambhu_gita.p.pitris_hymn.arc: You can hand over the outcome and still keep working, with devotion woven through.

thr.up.p.aitareya.three_births.title: The three births of a person
thr.up.p.aitareya.three_births.arc: Care for the one who carries and raises the child; raising children continues your life.

thr.up.p.brihad.desire.title: Yajnavalkya on desire and death
thr.up.p.brihad.desire.arc: You become what you desire and do; know what matters while you are here.

thr.up.p.brihad.first_being.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
thr.up.p.brihad.first_being.arc: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

thr.up.p.brihad.gargi.title: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
thr.up.p.brihad.gargi.arc: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

thr.up.p.brihad.maitreyi.title: Maitreyi refuses the inheritance
thr.up.p.brihad.maitreyi.arc: Wealth buys comfort; ask for what lasts.

thr.up.p.chhandogya.indra_virochana.title: Indra and Virochana with Prajapati
thr.up.p.chhandogya.indra_virochana.arc: Don't settle for the first comfortable answer; keep asking until it holds.

thr.up.p.chhandogya.satyakama.title: Satyakama Jabala, the honest boy
thr.up.p.chhandogya.satyakama.arc: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

thr.up.p.chhandogya.uddalaka_lessons.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
thr.up.p.chhandogya.uddalaka_lessons.arc: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

thr.up.p.devi_who_are_you.title: The gods ask the Goddess: who are you?
thr.up.p.devi_who_are_you.arc: The Mother who is everything is also near enough to be called on in fear.

thr.up.p.isha.whole.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
thr.up.p.isha.whole.arc: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

thr.up.p.katha.deathless_self.title: Yama on what does not die
thr.up.p.katha.deathless_self.arc: What you most are cannot be lost, and a quiet, honest life is how you find it.

thr.up.p.katha.inward.title: Turning the gaze inward
thr.up.p.katha.inward.arc: Look inward; what lasts is not out there among passing things.

thr.up.p.katha.nachiketa_sent.title: Nachiketa questions his father's gift
thr.up.p.katha.nachiketa_sent.arc: A child's honest question can show up an adult's empty gesture.

thr.up.p.maha.ribhu_calm.title: Ribhu on calm and contentment
thr.up.p.maha.ribhu_calm.arc: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

thr.up.p.maha.ribhu_living.title: How a free person lives
thr.up.p.maha.ribhu_living.arc: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

thr.up.p.maitrayani.mind.title: The mind is your world
thr.up.p.maitrayani.mind.arc: Tend your mind; it decides whether you feel trapped or free.

thr.up.p.mundaka.two_birds.title: Two birds on one tree
thr.up.p.mundaka.two_birds.arc: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.

thr.up.p.mundaka.two_knowledges.title: Shaunaka's question: two kinds of knowledge
thr.up.p.mundaka.two_knowledges.arc: Skills and degrees are real knowledge, but not the deepest kind.

thr.up.p.shvet_inquiry_to_refuge.title: Shvetashvatara: from 'what governs our lives?' to refuge
thr.up.p.shvet_inquiry_to_refuge.arc: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

thr.up.p.taittiriya.bhrigu.title: Bhrigu learns from his father
thr.up.p.taittiriya.bhrigu.arc: A wise parent lets a child discover the answer instead of handing it over.

thr.viv.p.jaffna.title: 'Whatever you think, that you will be' (Jaffna, 1897)
thr.viv.p.jaffna.arc: Thoughts shape us, so teach yourself and your children strength.

thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.character.title: Karma-Yoga 1: how work makes character
thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.character.arc: Character is built in ordinary actions, and you are building it right now.

thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.duty.title: Karma-Yoga 4: what is duty?
thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.duty.arc: See others through their own eyes, and let love turn duty into something lighter.

thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.each_is_great.title: Karma-Yoga 2: each is great in his own place
thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.each_is_great.arc: Measure yourself by your own ideal, not by someone else's.

thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.freedom.title: Karma-Yoga 7: freedom
thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.freedom.arc: Be at rest, be free, and work.

thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.help_ourselves.title: Karma-Yoga 5: we help ourselves, not the world
thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.help_ourselves.arc: Helping is a privilege, not a debt someone owes you.

thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.secret_of_work.title: Karma-Yoga 3: the secret of work
thr.viv.p.karma_yoga.secret_of_work.arc: Work like a master, not a slave; give without keeping accounts.

thr.viv.p.lahore.common_bases.title: Learn from all, imitate none (Lahore, 1897)
thr.viv.p.lahore.common_bases.arc: Absorb the best of where you live, and grow into yourself.

thr.viv.p.letter.brave_boys.title: 'To my brave boys' (letter from New York, 1894)
thr.viv.p.letter.brave_boys.arc: Lead by serving, refuse gossip, and keep struggling.

thr.viv.p.practical_vedanta.faith.title: Practical Vedanta 1: faith in yourself (London, 1896)
thr.viv.p.practical_vedanta.faith.arc: Stop rehearsing your weakness; think of your strength and act.

thr.viv.p.practical_vedanta.temple_of_ma.title: Practical Vedanta 2: the temple of the human body
thr.viv.p.practical_vedanta.temple_of_ma.arc: Treat the person in front of you as sacred.

thr.viv.p.raja_yoga.monkey_mind.title: The drunken monkey: taming a restless mind
thr.viv.p.raja_yoga.monkey_mind.arc: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

thr.viv.p.universal_religion.vessels.title: Cups, jars and buckets: the ideal of a universal religion
thr.viv.p.universal_religion.vessels.arc: Let each person, and each child, grow in their own shape.

thr.viv.p.work_and_its_secret.title: Work and its secret (Los Angeles, 1900)
thr.viv.p.work_and_its_secret.arc: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

thr.vr.p.bhakti.hanuman_boon.title: Valmiki: Hanuman's boon and Ram's debt
thr.vr.p.bhakti.hanuman_boon.arc: The deepest gratitude hopes the other never needs your help.

thr.vr.p.bhakti.refuge.title: Valmiki: Ram's vow of refuge and the dove
thr.vr.p.bhakti.refuge.arc: Refuge is a vow, not a reward for the deserving: once someone says 'I'm yours', they are safe.

thr.vr.p.friendship_pact.title: Ram and Sugriva's friendship
thr.vr.p.friendship_pact.arc: Two people in trouble can carry each other.

thr.vr.p.hanuman_leap.title: Hanuman's leap
thr.vr.p.hanuman_leap.arc: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

thr.vr.p.hanuman_speaks_to_sita.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
thr.vr.p.hanuman_speaks_to_sita.arc: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.

thr.vr.p.impermanence_teaching.title: Ram on why grief must not rule us
thr.vr.p.impermanence_teaching.arc: Everything that comes together parts; let that make you gentler, not hopeless.

thr.vr.p.kaikeyi_boons.title: Kaikeyi's boons and the king's blind promise
thr.vr.p.kaikeyi_boons.arc: Envy grows when fed; never promise before you know what you are being asked.

thr.vr.p.kumbhakarna.title: Kumbhakarna's loyalty
thr.vr.p.kumbhakarna.arc: You can tell family the hard truth and still stand by them; humility does, boasting talks.

thr.vr.p.lakshman_anger_exile.title: Lakshman's fury, Ram's calm
thr.vr.p.lakshman_anger_exile.arc: Anger at injustice is natural; decide what to do with it before it decides for you.

thr.vr.p.lakshman_suspects_bharata.title: Lakshman suspects Bharata
thr.vr.p.lakshman_suspects_bharata.arc: Don't assume the worst of family on the strength of what you see from a distance.

thr.vr.p.monsoon_wait.title: Waiting out the monsoon
thr.vr.p.monsoon_wait.arc: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.

thr.vr.p.refuge.title: Ram takes in the enemy's brother
thr.vr.p.refuge.arc: Give a second chance to someone who comes to you sincerely, even across old lines.

thr.vr.p.shravana.title: The boy at the river: Dasharatha's old guilt
thr.vr.p.shravana.arc: Carelessness can wound for decades; owning it honestly is the only way to carry it.

thr.vr.p.sita_left_in_forest.title: Sita left in the forest
thr.vr.p.sita_left_in_forest.arc: Injustice from those we love is real grief; a stranger's kindness can become home.

thr.vr.p.sita_nonviolence.title: Sita questions the weapon
thr.vr.p.sita_nonviolence.arc: Disagree with someone you love openly; advice is a sign of care.

thr.vr.p.statecraft_questions.title: Ram's questions to Bharata
thr.vr.p.statecraft_questions.arc: Good leaders consult wisely, act promptly, and listen to people with no power.

thr.vr.p.sugriva_forgets.title: Sugriva forgets his promise
thr.vr.p.sugriva_forgets.arc: Comfort makes us forget our promises; a true friend reminds us in time.

thr.vr.p.tara_calms_lakshman.title: Tara calms Lakshman
thr.vr.p.tara_calms_lakshman.arc: A calm voice can turn a confrontation into an apology on both sides.

thr.vr.p.vali_last_words.title: Vali's last words
thr.vr.p.vali_last_words.arc: Rivalry seems huge until the end; then only the relationship matters.

thr.vr.p.vibhishana_counsel.title: Vibhishana tells his brother the truth
thr.vr.p.vibhishana_counsel.arc: Speak the truth to family even when it costs you; leave if you must, without hatred.

thr.vr.p.vibhishana_grieves.title: Vibhishana mourns Ravana
thr.vr.p.vibhishana_grieves.arc: Grief for someone who wronged you is real; death ends the fight.

thr.yv.p.bhushunda.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
thr.yv.p.bhushunda.arc: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

thr.yv.p.janaka.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
thr.yv.p.janaka.arc: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

thr.yv.p.prahlada.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
thr.yv.p.prahlada.arc: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

thr.yv.p.prahlada_refuge.title: Prahlada, alone after defeat, takes refuge in Narayana
thr.yv.p.prahlada_refuge.arc: Refuge is open to anyone, whatever their past; devotion kept up daily changes the mind.

thr.yv.p.punya_pavana.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
thr.yv.p.punya_pavana.arc: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

thr.yv.p.ram_questions.title: Rama asks how to live in the world without being crushed by it
thr.yv.p.ram_questions.arc: The real question isn't whether to quit life, but how to live it without being swallowed.

thr.yv.p.shiva_true_worship.title: Shiva teaches Vasishtha what worship really is
thr.yv.p.shiva_true_worship.arc: Worship can be carried into every hour as calm, kindness and gladness.

thr.yv.p.three_vows.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
thr.yv.p.three_vows.arc: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

pair:pair.daiva_and_effort.title: Fate and effort
pair:pair.daiva_and_effort.idea: Outcomes have five causes; the unseen (daiva) is only one of them. Do your part fully, and when it still goes wrong, don't carry it as your failure.
pair:pair.daiva_and_effort.rule: Never show rcm.2.165.doha.1 alone. Lead with it for grief and guilt; lead with bg.18.14 for work and failure. Never show rcm.2.165.doha.1 alone. Lead with it for grief and guilt; lead with bg.18.14 for work and failure. Show yv.2.6.1 or yv.2.4.17 only to someone who feels stuck or is making excuses (procrastination, discipline, change_life), never to someone grieving or blaming themselves, and always with yv.2.6.21 in the same plan. For outcome_anxiety and not_promoted, lead with yv.2.7.21 (results come, sooner or later).

pair:pair.no_one_gives_sorrow.title: No one else gives you sorrow, and it isn't all your fault
pair:pair.no_one_gives_sorrow.idea: Your peace isn't in others' hands, but that doesn't mean every bad outcome is your doing.
pair:pair.no_one_gives_sorrow.rule: Pair whenever rcm.2.90.chaupai.2 is shown to someone blaming themselves.

pair:pair.surrender_and_reflect.title: Surrender, after reflection
pair:pair.surrender_and_reflect.idea: Krishna asks Arjuna to think it through fully and choose before he says 'surrender to me'.
pair:pair.surrender_and_reflect.rule: Show 18.63 the day before or alongside 18.66.

pair:pair.humble_then_firm.title: Humble first, firm after
pair:pair.humble_then_firm.idea: Always start with humility. When it is repeatedly taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop the moment you're heard.
pair:pair.humble_then_firm.rule: Lead with rcm.5.48.chaupai.4 (ask politely first). Never show the firm verses on day 1 of a plan or without the three days of patience in the setting.

pair:pair.despair_to_engagement.title: From 'what's the point?' to working with a free mind
pair:pair.despair_to_engagement.idea: Rama and Bali both hit 'what is all this for?'. The Yoga Vasishtha's answer is not quitting life but living it fully with an inner anchor, like King Janaka.
pair:pair.despair_to_engagement.rule: Never show yv.1.12.15, yv.5.22.34, yv.1.10.19 or yv.1.12.22 alone. Follow each, the same day or the next, with yv.6a.115.43 or yv.1.30.17. Use yv.6a.93.29 when the user is considering quitting or running away.

pair:pair.four_gatekeepers.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
pair:pair.four_gatekeepers.idea: Four qualities guard the door to a free mind. Start with any one; each strengthens the others.
pair:pair.four_gatekeepers.rule: Use as a 4-day mini-plan: day 1 up_maha.150 (the list) or yv.2.16.19; then one gatekeeper per day (calm 2.13.64, inquiry 2.14.11, contentment 2.15.11, good company 2.16.8); close with yv.2.16.32 (one virtue grows the others).

pair:pair.effort_and_grace.title: Effort and grace
pair:pair.effort_and_grace.idea: The Yoga Vasishtha's strong case for effort does not reject devotion: sometimes we wake by our own effort, sometimes by grace reached through devotion, and daily practice ripens the mind.
pair:pair.effort_and_grace.rule: For users in doubt_faith or reconnect_faith, show yv.5.43.9 before or with any paurusha card, so effort doesn't read as anti-devotional.

bg.12.12.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.12.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
bg.12.12.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.
bg.12.12.claim: Giving up the fruit of action ranks above practice, knowledge and meditation, and peace follows that giving up at once.
bg.12.12.needs: the reader is acting and anxious about outcomes; the verse closes the ladder of options in 12.8-11

bg.12.13.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.13.line: Hate no one. Be friendly and kind, free of 'mine' and ego, steady in pain and joy, and forgiving.
bg.12.13.misuse: Forgiving is not excusing harm or staying in danger; you can forgive and still keep your distance.
bg.12.13.claim: The devotee dear to God hates no being, is friendly, compassionate, free of mine and ego, even-minded and forgiving.
bg.12.13.needs: a reader who already wants to grow in devotion; it is a portrait, not a remedy for a fresh hurt

bg.12.15.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.15.line: Unsettle no one, be unsettled by no one, free of elation, resentment, fear and agitation.
bg.12.15.misuse: Not disturbing others doesn't mean never disagreeing; it means not causing needless harm.
bg.12.15.claim: One who neither disturbs the world nor is disturbed by it, free of elation, intolerance, fear and agitation, is dear to God.

bg.12.18.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.18.line: The same to friend and foe, in respect and insult, heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
bg.12.18.misuse: Being the same in insult doesn't mean tolerating abuse; it means your worth isn't decided by it.
bg.12.18.claim: The devotee is the same to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, unattached.
bg.12.18.needs: not as a reply to a fresh insult or injury

bg.12.19.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.19.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
bg.12.19.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.
bg.12.19.claim: One to whom blame and praise are equal, silent, content with anything, homeless, steady-minded and devoted, is dear to God.

bg.16.21.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.21.line: Desire, anger and greed: three gates to self-ruin. Close all three.
bg.16.21.claim: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate of hell that ruins the self; one should give up all three.

bg.17.15.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.15.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
bg.17.15.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.
bg.17.15.claim: Speech that causes no distress, that is true, pleasant and beneficial, along with regular sacred study, is austerity of speech.

bg.17.3.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.3.line: You are made of what you deeply believe. As your faith is, so are you.
bg.17.3.claim: Each person's faith follows their inner nature; a person is made of faith, and is what their faith is.

bg.18.26.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.26.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
bg.18.26.claim: The doer free of attachment and self-talk, full of steadiness and zeal, unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.

bg.18.37.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.37.line: Some joy tastes like poison at first and like nectar in the end. That joy is worth it.
bg.18.37.claim: Sattvic happiness is like poison at first and nectar in the end, born of the clarity of one's understanding of the self.

bg.18.38.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.38.line: Some pleasure tastes like nectar at first and poison in the end. Know which kind you're choosing.
bg.18.38.claim: Rajasic happiness comes from the senses meeting their objects, like nectar at first and poison in the end.

bg.18.47.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.47.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
bg.18.47.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.
bg.18.47.claim: One's own duty done imperfectly is better than another's done well; work set by one's nature brings no fault.

bg.18.63.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.63.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
bg.18.63.claim: Krishna has taught the most secret knowledge; Arjuna should reflect on it fully and then do as he wishes.
bg.18.63.needs: the teaching before it; a closing verse, best in the last days of a plan

bg.18.66.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.66.line: Lean on me alone. I will free you from every wrong. Don't worry.
bg.18.66.misuse: This is not 'do nothing' or 'ignore your duties'. Krishna says it to a man about to act; it lifts fear, not responsibility.
bg.18.66.claim: Giving up all dharmas and taking refuge in Krishna alone, one is freed by him from all sins; do not grieve.
bg.18.66.needs: a devotional reader and the teaching before it; a resolution verse for the last days of a plan, never Day 1 to 3

bg.2.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.11.line: You grieve for what doesn't need your grief, while talking like you know better.
bg.2.11.misuse: Not 'don't cry' or 'your grief is wrong'. It opens a teaching on what in us does not die; grief still deserves time.
bg.2.11.claim: Arjuna grieves for those not to be grieved for while talking wisdom; the wise grieve for neither the dead nor the living.
bg.2.11.needs: the scene: Arjuna has just asked to be taught (2.7); only as the opening of the 2.11-30 teaching, never alone

bg.2.13.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.13.line: Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.
bg.2.13.claim: As the self passes through childhood, youth and age in this body, so it takes another body; the steady are not bewildered.
bg.2.13.needs: openness to a self that outlasts the body; not the first word to a fresh loss

bg.2.14.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.14.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
bg.2.14.misuse: Bearing passing discomfort is not putting up with harm or abuse; those are not weather to wait out.
bg.2.14.claim: Sense contacts bring heat and cold, pleasure and pain; they come and go and do not last, so bear them.
bg.2.14.needs: the pain is a passing discomfort, not an ongoing harm someone is doing

bg.2.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.20.line: The self was never born and never dies. It is not killed when the body is.
bg.2.20.misuse: Not a reason to skip mourning or to take loss lightly; it is comfort about what remains.
bg.2.20.claim: The self is never born and never dies; unborn, eternal and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.
bg.2.20.needs: openness to a self distinct from the body; not the first word to a fresh loss

bg.2.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.22.line: As we drop worn-out clothes and put on new ones, the self leaves a worn body for a new one.
bg.2.22.misuse: Not a way to brush off someone else's grief with 'they've just changed clothes'.
bg.2.22.claim: As a person discards worn-out clothes for new ones, the embodied self discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
bg.2.22.needs: belief in rebirth; fits the passing of the old, not an untimely death

bg.2.27.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.27.line: Whatever is born will die, and what dies is born again. Don't torment yourself over the unavoidable.
bg.2.27.misuse: Not a reason to stop caring for the sick or to rush someone's mourning.
bg.2.27.claim: Death is certain for the born and birth for the dead; so one should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
bg.2.27.needs: some distance from the loss; argues from the common view of birth and death

bg.2.38.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.38.line: Hold pleasure and pain, gain and loss, win and defeat as equal. Then step in and act.
bg.2.38.claim: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, one should fight; so no sin is incurred.
bg.2.38.needs: the action in question is one's rightful duty; said to a warrior before a just war

bg.2.40.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.40.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
bg.2.40.claim: On this path no beginning is lost and no harm results; even a little of this dharma protects from great fear.

bg.2.47.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.47.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
bg.2.47.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.
bg.2.47.claim: One has a right to action alone, never to its fruits; fruit must not be the motive, nor inaction the refuge.

bg.2.48.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.48.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
bg.2.48.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.
bg.2.48.claim: Established in yoga, one should act without attachment, the same in success and failure; this evenness is called yoga.

bg.2.50.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.50.line: Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.
bg.2.50.claim: One joined to wisdom sheds both merit and demerit here; so strive for yoga, which is skill in action.

bg.2.56.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.56.line: Unshaken in sorrow, not craving in joy, free of clinging, fear and anger: that is a steady mind.
bg.2.56.misuse: A steady mind still feels; it just isn't run by sorrow, fear or anger.
bg.2.56.claim: One whose mind is unshaken in sorrow, without craving in pleasure, free of attachment, fear and anger, is a steady-minded sage.
bg.2.56.needs: a wish for steadiness; not a reply to fresh grief or injury

bg.2.58.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.58.line: Like a tortoise pulling in its limbs, draw your senses back from what pulls at them.
bg.2.58.claim: When one withdraws the senses from their objects as a tortoise draws in its limbs, one's wisdom is firmly established.

bg.2.62.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.62.line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
bg.2.62.claim: Dwelling on sense objects breeds attachment to them; attachment breeds desire; desire breeds anger.
bg.2.62.needs: the trouble really is craving, fixation or anger from thwarted wanting; not a general diagnosis for grief, fear or being wronged

bg.2.63.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.63.line: Anger clouds judgement, clouded judgement loses memory, lost memory wrecks reason, and then you fall.
bg.2.63.misuse: Not 'never feel anger'. It warns about anger that takes over judgement, not about naming wrongs.
bg.2.63.claim: Anger breeds delusion, delusion loss of memory, that the ruin of understanding, and with understanding ruined one perishes.
bg.2.63.needs: the anger is one's own reactivity; never told to someone whose anger answers a real wrong

bg.2.66.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.66.line: Without inner discipline there's no clarity; without clarity, no peace; and without peace, where is happiness?
bg.2.66.claim: Without discipline there is no understanding or contemplation; without contemplation no peace; without peace, no happiness.

bg.2.7.speaker: Arjuna
bg.2.7.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
bg.2.7.claim: Overcome by faint-heartedness and confused about dharma, Arjuna asks Krishna, as a surrendered student, to say what is surely best.

bg.2.70.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.70.line: Rivers pour into the ocean and it stays full and still. Let desires enter you the same way.
bg.2.70.claim: As the full, unmoving ocean receives the waters, one whom desires enter thus attains peace, not one who craves desires.

bg.3.21.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.21.line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
bg.3.21.claim: Whatever a great person does, others do; whatever standard that person sets, the world follows.

bg.3.35.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.35.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
bg.3.35.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.
bg.3.35.claim: One's own duty done imperfectly is better than another's done well; death in one's own duty is better, another's is fearful.

bg.3.37.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.37.line: It's desire, which turns into anger when blocked. Never satisfied, it is the real enemy here.
bg.3.37.claim: Desire, which becomes anger, born of rajas, all-devouring and greatly sinful, is the enemy here.
bg.3.37.needs: answers Arjuna's question in 3.36: what drives a person to do wrong even against their will

bg.3.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.8.line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
bg.3.8.claim: One should do one's allotted work, for action is better than inaction; even bodily life is impossible without action.
bg.3.8.needs: answers the wish to withdraw from work; not for someone who is exhausted or burnt out

bg.4.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.11.line: However people come to me, I meet them there. Every path, in its own way, leads to me.
bg.4.11.claim: In whatever way people approach Krishna, in that way he receives them; people everywhere follow his path.

bg.4.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.22.line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
bg.4.22.claim: Content with what comes unasked, beyond the opposites, free of envy, even in success and failure, one acts and is not bound.

bg.4.34.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.34.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
bg.4.34.claim: That knowledge is learned by prostration, questioning and service; the wise who have seen the truth will teach it.
bg.4.34.needs: a reader who is actively seeking a teacher or deeper study; it is filler when served for anxiety, doubt or self-worth

bg.4.39.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.39.line: Trust, commitment and self-control bring understanding, and understanding soon brings peace.
bg.4.39.claim: One with faith, intent on it and with senses restrained gains knowledge, and with knowledge soon reaches supreme peace.

bg.4.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.7.line: Whenever goodness declines and wrong rises up, I come forth, Krishna promises.
bg.4.7.misuse: Not 'wait for rescue'. Many read it as a call to be the force that restores what is right.
bg.4.7.claim: Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, the Lord brings himself forth.

bg.5.10.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.10.line: Like a lotus leaf in water, do your work without letting the mess soak in.
bg.5.10.misuse: Staying unstained isn't staying silent about wrongdoing at work; you can act and still keep your peace.
bg.5.10.claim: One who acts offering actions to Brahman without attachment is untouched by sin, as a lotus leaf by water.
bg.5.10.needs: a reader open to offering work to God

bg.5.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.22.line: Pleasures born of contact have a beginning and an end and breed sorrow. The wise don't stake their joy there.
bg.5.22.claim: Pleasures born of contact are sources of sorrow, with a beginning and an end; the wise do not delight in them.

bg.5.23.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.23.line: Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.
bg.5.23.claim: One who can withstand the surge born of desire and anger, here before the body falls, is a yogi and is happy.
bg.5.23.needs: the surge is one's own impulse, not a rightful response to harm

bg.6.16.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.16.line: Balance isn't for those who eat too much or too little, or sleep too much or too little.
bg.6.16.claim: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or nothing, nor for one who oversleeps or stays awake.

bg.6.17.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.17.line: Moderate in food and rest, in work and play, in sleep and waking: that's how sorrow eases.
bg.6.17.claim: For one moderate in food, recreation, effort at work, sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.

bg.6.19.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.19.line: Like a lamp in a windless place that doesn't flicker: that's a settled mind.
bg.6.19.claim: A lamp in a windless place that does not flicker is the simile for the yogi's controlled mind in meditation.

bg.6.26.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.26.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
bg.6.26.claim: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, one should restrain it and bring it back under the self's control.

bg.6.32.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.32.line: Feel others' joy and pain as if they were your own. That is the highest practice.
bg.6.32.claim: One who sees pleasure and pain everywhere as the same by likeness to oneself is deemed the highest yogi.

bg.6.34.speaker: Arjuna
bg.6.34.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
bg.6.34.claim: The mind is restless, turbulent, strong and stubborn; restraining it seems as hard as restraining the wind.

bg.6.35.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.35.line: Yes, the mind is restless and hard to hold. But practice and letting go can train it.
bg.6.35.claim: The mind is indeed restless and hard to restrain, but it is held by practice and dispassion.

bg.6.40.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.40.line: Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.
bg.6.40.claim: For the striver in yoga there is no ruin here or hereafter; no doer of good comes to a bad end.
bg.6.40.needs: Arjuna's question in 6.37-39 about the seeker who tries with faith and falls short; it is not a promise that good people never suffer

bg.6.5.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.5.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
bg.6.5.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.
bg.6.5.claim: One should lift oneself by oneself and not let oneself sink; the self alone is one's friend and one's enemy.
bg.6.5.needs: some strength to act; a person in acute collapse needs to be met first

bg.6.6.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.6.line: Master yourself and you become your own best friend. Don't, and your own mind works against you like an enemy.
bg.6.6.claim: For one who has conquered oneself the self is a friend; for one who has not, the self acts as an enemy.

bg.6.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.7.line: Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
bg.6.7.misuse: Staying steady under insult is not accepting mistreatment; you can stay calm and still speak up.
bg.6.7.claim: For the self-conquered, peaceful one, the supreme Self stays present through heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
bg.6.7.needs: not as a reply to a fresh insult or injury

bg.9.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.22.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
bg.9.22.misuse: Not 'God will pay the bills, so don't plan'. Trust eases worry; it doesn't replace effort or prudence.
bg.9.22.claim: For those who worship Krishna with undivided thought, ever devoted, he himself carries what they lack and guards what they have.
bg.9.22.needs: a devotional reader; the promise is to those wholly given to him, not a guarantee of money

bg.9.26.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.26.line: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.
bg.9.26.claim: Whoever offers a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water with devotion, Krishna accepts that loving offering of the pure-hearted.

bg.1.28.speaker: Arjuna
bg.1.28.line: Even Arjuna, the finest archer alive, froze when the fight was against his own people.
bg.1.28.claim: Seeing his own kin arrayed and eager for battle, Arjuna is overcome by deep pity and speaks in despair.

bg.1.29.speaker: Arjuna
bg.1.29.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
bg.1.29.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.
bg.1.29.claim: Arjuna's limbs fail, his mouth dries, his body trembles, the bow slips, he cannot stand and his mind reels.

bg.1.47.speaker: Sanjaya
bg.1.47.line: Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.
bg.1.47.claim: Having spoken, Arjuna sat down in the chariot, dropping bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.

bg.10.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.10.11.line: Out of compassion, I live in their hearts and clear the darkness with the lamp of understanding.
bg.10.11.claim: Out of compassion, dwelling in their hearts, Krishna destroys the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
bg.10.11.needs: a devotional reader; 'them' are the devotees of 10.9-10

bg.10.41.speaker: Krishna
bg.10.41.line: Whatever shines with excellence, beauty or power, see it as a spark of the divine.
bg.10.41.claim: Whatever being is glorious, prosperous or powerful arises from a fraction of Krishna's splendour.

bg.11.33.speaker: Krishna
bg.11.33.line: It's already set in motion. Rise and do your part; be the instrument.
bg.11.33.misuse: 'Be the instrument' is not 'I'm not responsible for what I do'. You still choose and answer for your actions.
bg.11.33.claim: Arjuna should rise and win glory; his enemies are already slain by Krishna, and he is to be only the instrument.
bg.11.33.needs: the scene: Krishna as Time has shown the war's end; outside it the line reads as fatalism

bg.11.41.speaker: Arjuna
bg.11.41.line: I treated you casually, as just a friend, never seeing how great you were.
bg.11.41.claim: Arjuna asks forgiveness for addressing Krishna casually as a friend and slighting him in jest, not knowing his greatness.
bg.11.41.needs: the scene of the cosmic form helps; the feeling of having taken someone for granted carries on its own

bg.11.44.speaker: Arjuna
bg.11.44.line: Bear with me as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
bg.11.44.misuse: Asking for forgiveness is not demanding it; the other person still decides.
bg.11.44.claim: Prostrating, Arjuna begs the Lord to bear with him as father with son, friend with friend, lover with beloved.
bg.11.44.needs: the reader is the one who needs to apologise, not the one who was hurt

bg.11.55.speaker: Krishna
bg.11.55.line: Work for the divine, love it, drop clinging, and hold no hatred towards any being.
bg.11.55.misuse: No hatred doesn't mean no boundaries; you can wish someone no harm and still keep away.
bg.11.55.claim: One who works for Krishna, holds him supreme, is devoted, unattached and without enmity toward any being, comes to him.

bg.12.10.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.10.line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
bg.12.10.claim: If unable even to practise, one should be intent on work for Krishna; acting for his sake too brings perfection.
bg.12.10.needs: a devotional reader who feels unable to keep a practice

bg.12.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.11.line: And if even that's beyond you, then simply let go of the results of what you do.
bg.12.11.misuse: Letting go of results is not giving up on goals or planning; it's releasing the anxious grip.
bg.12.11.claim: If unable even for that, one should take refuge in Krishna, be self-restrained, and give up the fruit of all actions.

bg.12.14.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.14.line: Always content, self-disciplined, firm in resolve, heart and mind given to the divine: such a person is dear to me.
bg.12.14.claim: The devotee who is ever content, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and intellect given to Krishna, is dear to him.

bg.12.16.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.16.line: Wanting nothing extra, clean within and without, capable, unbothered, not chasing every new venture: dear to me.
bg.12.16.claim: The devotee who expects nothing, is pure, capable, impartial, untroubled and has given up all undertakings, is dear to Krishna.
bg.12.16.needs: not for someone who is starting or building something; the tradition reads it of one who has given up ventures

bg.12.17.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.17.line: Not swinging between thrill and hate, grief and craving, letting go of 'good' and 'bad' outcomes: dear to me.
bg.12.17.misuse: Not feeling grief is not the goal; the verse is about not being swept away by it.
bg.12.17.claim: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, has renounced good and bad, and is devoted, is dear to Krishna.
bg.12.17.needs: a settled reader; to someone grieving or hurt, 'does not grieve, does not hate' reads as a rebuke

bg.12.9.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.9.line: If you can't keep your mind fixed yet, then reach for it through regular practice.
bg.12.9.claim: If one cannot fix the mind steadily on Krishna, one should seek to reach him through the yoga of practice.

bg.13.28.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.28.line: Whoever sees the same undying presence in all beings, even as they perish, truly sees.
bg.13.28.claim: One who sees the supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishing, truly sees.
bg.13.28.needs: openness to a self or Lord that does not die with the body

bg.13.29.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.29.line: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, you stop wounding yourself through yourself.
bg.13.29.claim: Seeing the Lord equally present everywhere, one does not harm the self by the self and so reaches the highest goal.

bg.13.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.8.line: No need for status, no pretence, no harm, patience, straightness, respect for teachers, purity, steadiness, self-control.
bg.13.8.misuse: Patience and humility aren't silence in the face of mistreatment.
bg.13.8.claim: Humility, no pretence, non-violence, forbearance, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control are counted as knowledge.
bg.13.8.needs: a seeker asking what a life aimed at knowledge looks like; a bare list otherwise

bg.13.9.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.9.line: Not chasing pleasures, not puffed up, and clear-eyed about birth, death, old age and illness.
bg.13.9.claim: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing the pain and defect in birth, death, age and sickness are knowledge.
bg.13.9.needs: a seeker's contemplation; cruel if shown to someone nursing a sick or ageing parent

bg.14.12.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.12.line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
bg.14.12.claim: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving arise when rajas predominates.

bg.14.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.22.line: Don't hate your moods when they come, or long for them when they go.
bg.14.22.claim: The one beyond the gunas does not hate illumination, activity or delusion when present, nor long for them when gone.
bg.14.22.needs: answers Arjuna's question in 14.21 about the marks of one beyond the three gunas

bg.14.24.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.24.line: Even in pain and pleasure, at ease in yourself; earth, stone and gold the same; praise and blame alike.
bg.14.24.claim: Alike in pain and pleasure, abiding in the self, regarding clod, stone and gold alike, steady, alike in blame and praise.

bg.14.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.25.line: The same in respect and disrespect, to friend and foe, letting go of the need to start everything: free.
bg.14.25.misuse: Not 'tolerate disrespect'. It means your steadiness doesn't depend on how others treat you.
bg.14.25.claim: Alike in honour and dishonour, alike to friend and foe, having given up all undertakings, one is called beyond the gunas.
bg.14.25.needs: a seeker's ideal; not for someone disrespected or someone starting out

bg.16.1.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.1.line: Fearlessness, a clean heart, steady learning, generosity, self-control, study and straightforwardness.
bg.16.1.claim: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadiness in knowledge and yoga, giving, self-control, sacrifice, study, austerity and uprightness mark the divine nature.

bg.16.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.11.line: Clinging to worries that only end at death, they believe owning and enjoying is all there is.
bg.16.11.claim: The demonic cling to measureless worry ending only at death, hold sense enjoyment as highest, convinced that this is all.
bg.16.11.needs: only as a diagnosis of a materialist outlook; the speaker is describing the demonic nature, so it must never be shown to an anxious person as a mirror

bg.16.12.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.12.line: Tied by a hundred ropes of hope, pushed by desire and anger, they pile up wealth by any means.
bg.16.12.claim: Bound by a hundred cords of hope, given to desire and anger, the demonic amass wealth unjustly for sense enjoyment.
bg.16.12.needs: describes the demonic nature; never for someone under honest money stress

bg.16.13.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.13.line: 'I got this today, I'll get that next. This is mine, and more will be mine.' The mind of more.
bg.16.13.claim: The demonic person thinks: this I gained today, this wish I will fulfil; this wealth is mine and more will be.
bg.16.13.needs: serve as a mirror for the wanting mind, without the 'demonic' label attached to the reader

bg.16.2.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.2.line: No harm, truthfulness, no anger, no gossip, compassion for all, no greed, gentleness, modesty, no fidgeting.
bg.16.2.claim: Non-violence, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peace, no slander, compassion to beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty and steadiness mark the divine nature.

bg.16.3.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.3.line: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, no malice, no arrogance: the marks of a good nature.
bg.16.3.misuse: Forgiveness here is a strength, not an obligation to stay in harm's way.
bg.16.3.claim: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of malice and of excessive pride belong to one born to the divine nature.

bg.16.4.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.4.line: Show-off, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance: the marks of a nature heading the wrong way.
bg.16.4.misuse: A mirror for yourself, not a label to throw at others.
bg.16.4.claim: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born to the demonic nature.
bg.16.4.needs: a reader examining pride or harshness; as a mirror it is a verdict

bg.17.16.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.16.line: A calm mind, gentleness, quiet, self-restraint and a clean heart: that is discipline of mind.
bg.17.16.claim: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling are called austerity of mind.

bg.17.18.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.18.line: Effort made for respect, status or show is shaky and doesn't last.
bg.17.18.claim: Austerity done with show to gain respect, honour and reverence is rajasic, unstable and impermanent.

bg.17.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.20.line: Give because giving is right, to someone who can't repay you, at the right time and place.
bg.17.20.claim: A gift given as duty, to a worthy person who cannot repay, at the right place and time, is sattvic.

bg.17.21.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.21.line: Giving to get something back, or giving grudgingly, isn't really giving.
bg.17.21.claim: A gift given for a return, or with an eye to reward, or reluctantly, is rajasic.

bg.18.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.11.line: No one with a body can give up action completely. Letting go of the payoff is the real renouncing.
bg.18.11.claim: An embodied being cannot give up action entirely; one who gives up the fruit of action is called a renouncer.

bg.18.14.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.14.line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
bg.18.14.misuse: Not 'it wasn't my fault'. You own your part; you just aren't the only cause.
bg.18.14.claim: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the distinct efforts, and providence as fifth are the five causes of action.

bg.18.28.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.28.line: Careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and always putting things off: the dull kind of doer.
bg.18.28.misuse: A mirror for your own habits, not a label for anyone with depression or burnout.
bg.18.28.claim: The doer who is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating is called tamasic.
bg.18.28.needs: a reader who can take a hard mirror; it places despondency beside deceit and malice

bg.18.30.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.30.line: Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.
bg.18.30.claim: The intellect that knows action and withdrawal, duty and non-duty, fear and fearlessness, bondage and freedom, is sattvic.

bg.18.45.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.45.line: Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
bg.18.45.misuse: Not 'stay in the job your community or birth assigned'. 'Your own work' means the work that fits your nature.
bg.18.45.claim: Each person devoted to his own work attains perfection; Krishna will explain how.

bg.18.46.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.46.line: Doing your own work well can be your worship of the source of all life.
bg.18.46.misuse: Work as worship doesn't mean overwork or tolerating exploitation.
bg.18.46.claim: By worshipping through one's own work the One from whom all beings arise and who pervades all, a person attains perfection.

bg.18.48.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.48.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
bg.18.48.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.
bg.18.48.claim: One should not abandon work born of one's nature though faulty; all undertakings are clouded by fault as fire by smoke.

bg.18.53.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.53.line: Let go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness. Without 'mine', you become peaceful.
bg.18.53.claim: Giving up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, free of mine and peaceful, one becomes fit to be Brahman.
bg.18.53.needs: a seeker far along; the passage 18.51-53 describes the renunciate's final discipline

bg.18.54.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.54.line: Serene within, they neither grieve nor crave, and treat all beings alike.
bg.18.54.misuse: Not 'don't grieve'. It describes a serenity that grows, not a rule against sorrow.
bg.18.54.claim: One who has become Brahman, serene, neither grieves nor craves; alike to all beings, he gains supreme devotion to Krishna.
bg.18.54.needs: a seeker's horizon; to a griever 'does not grieve' reads as a verdict

bg.18.58.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.58.line: Heart turned to the divine, you'll cross every obstacle. Refuse out of ego, and you'll be lost.
bg.18.58.claim: With mind fixed on Krishna one crosses all difficulties by his grace; refusing to listen out of ego, one perishes.
bg.18.58.needs: a devotional reader; the second half is a teacher's warning to Arjuna and is harsh without the scene

bg.18.62.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.62.line: Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
bg.18.62.misuse: Surrender is trust, not giving up your judgement or your effort.
bg.18.62.claim: Taking refuge in the Lord alone with one's whole being, one attains by his grace supreme peace and the eternal abode.
bg.18.62.needs: a devotional reader; 'him' is the Lord seated in the heart of all beings (18.61)

bg.18.73.speaker: Arjuna
bg.18.73.line: My confusion is gone, my clarity is back. I stand firm, free of doubt, and I'll act.
bg.18.73.misuse: Not blind obedience: Krishna told him to reflect and choose (18.63), and Arjuna acts from his own clarity.
bg.18.73.claim: By Krishna's grace Arjuna's delusion is destroyed and memory regained; firm and free of doubt, he will do Krishna's word.
bg.18.73.needs: the whole arc from 2.7; a closing verse for the last day of a plan, never early

bg.18.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.8.line: Dropping a duty just because it's hard or you fear the strain isn't freedom. It gains you nothing.
bg.18.8.misuse: Not 'never quit'. Leaving for good reasons is wise; this warns against fleeing out of fear alone.
bg.18.8.claim: Giving up work as painful, from fear of bodily strain, is rajasic renunciation and wins no fruit of renunciation.
bg.18.8.needs: a reader weighing whether to quit out of discomfort; not for someone exhausted or being harmed by their work

bg.2.12.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.12.line: There was never a time when you, I, or anyone here did not exist, and never will be.
bg.2.12.claim: Never was there a time when Krishna, Arjuna or these kings did not exist, nor will any ever cease to be.
bg.2.12.needs: openness to a self that outlasts the body; not the first word to a fresh loss

bg.2.15.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.15.line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
bg.2.15.misuse: Steadiness is not numbness or hiding what you feel.
bg.2.15.claim: The steady person whom these contacts do not afflict, alike in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
bg.2.15.needs: follows 2.14 on bearing what comes and goes

bg.2.23.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.23.line: No weapon cuts it, no fire burns it, no water wets it, no wind dries it.
bg.2.23.claim: Weapons do not cut the self, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, wind does not dry it.
bg.2.23.needs: openness to a self distinct from the body

bg.2.28.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.28.line: We come from the unseen and return to it; only the middle is visible. Why break over that?
bg.2.28.misuse: Grief is natural; the verse widens the frame, it doesn't forbid tears.
bg.2.28.claim: Beings are unmanifest in the beginning, manifest in the middle and unmanifest again at the end; what is there to lament?
bg.2.28.needs: distance from the loss; the closing question dismisses lament and stings a fresh griever

bg.2.3.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.3.line: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.
bg.2.3.misuse: Not 'feelings are weakness' or 'man up'. It is a friend reminding you of your strength, said once, then explained for 700 verses.
bg.2.3.claim: Arjuna must not yield to unmanliness, which does not befit him; he should cast off petty faint-heartedness and rise.
bg.2.3.needs: the scene: a charioteer and friend speaking to a great warrior moments before battle; alone it calls a struggling reader's distress petty

bg.2.41.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.41.line: A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.
bg.2.41.claim: The resolute understanding is single; the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

bg.2.49.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.49.line: Working only for the payoff makes you poor inside. Take shelter in clear understanding.
bg.2.49.misuse: Not 'ambition is wrong'. It's about not letting rewards be the only reason you work.
bg.2.49.claim: Action for reward is far inferior to the yoga of understanding; seek refuge in understanding; pitiable are those moved by fruit.

bg.2.53.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.53.line: Pulled by conflicting advice, the mind wobbles. When it settles and stays still, you've arrived.
bg.2.53.claim: When the intellect, confused by what it has heard, stands unmoving and steady in samadhi, one attains yoga.

bg.2.55.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.55.line: When you stop chasing every desire and find contentment within yourself, your wisdom becomes steady.
bg.2.55.claim: One who gives up all desires of the mind and is content in the self alone is called steady in wisdom.

bg.2.57.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.57.line: Good news doesn't inflate them, bad news doesn't embitter them. That's steady wisdom.
bg.2.57.claim: One without attachment anywhere, who neither rejoices at good nor hates bad when it comes, has firmly established wisdom.
bg.2.57.needs: not a reply to fresh grief or injury

bg.2.6.speaker: Arjuna
bg.2.6.line: I can't tell which is better, or even what winning would look like.
bg.2.6.claim: Arjuna does not know which is better, to conquer or be conquered; those whose death would make life unwanted stand before him.

bg.2.60.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.60.line: Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.
bg.2.60.claim: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving.

bg.2.64.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.64.line: Move through the world with your senses in hand, free of grabbing and pushing away, and you find calm.
bg.2.64.claim: The self-controlled one who moves among objects with senses free of attraction and aversion attains serenity.

bg.2.67.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.67.line: When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.
bg.2.67.claim: The mind that follows the roving senses carries away one's wisdom as wind carries a boat on water.

bg.2.71.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.71.line: Drop the cravings, the sense of 'mine' and the 'I' that keeps score. That's where peace is.
bg.2.71.misuse: Dropping 'mine' is about possessiveness, not about loving your people less.
bg.2.71.claim: One who gives up all desires and lives free of longing, without mine or ego, attains peace.

bg.3.19.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.19.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
bg.3.19.claim: One should always do the work that must be done without attachment; acting unattached, a person attains the supreme.

bg.3.2.speaker: Arjuna
bg.3.2.line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
bg.3.2.claim: Krishna's seemingly mixed words confuse Arjuna's understanding; he asks for the one sure thing leading to the highest good.

bg.3.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.20.line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
bg.3.20.claim: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone; one should act also with a view to the welfare of the world.

bg.3.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.22.line: I have nothing left to gain anywhere, Krishna says, and still I keep working.
bg.3.22.claim: Krishna has no duty in the three worlds and nothing unattained to attain, yet he continues in action.

bg.3.26.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.26.line: Don't unsettle people who are still learning by doing. Do the work well alongside them and show them.
bg.3.26.claim: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant attached to action, but engage them by acting steadily themselves.

bg.3.27.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.27.line: Countless forces do the work; the ego, fooled, says 'I did it all'.
bg.3.27.claim: All actions are done by the gunas of nature; one deluded by ego thinks 'I am the doer'.

bg.3.30.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.30.line: Hand your work to something higher, drop the 'mine' and the hoping, and act with the fever gone.
bg.3.30.misuse: Surrender here means letting go of anxious grasping, not handing over your judgement or responsibility.
bg.3.30.claim: Surrendering all actions to Krishna with mind on the self, free of hope and mine, one should fight with fever gone.
bg.3.30.needs: a reader open to offering work to God

bg.3.33.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.33.line: Even wise people move as their nature moves them. Brute suppression achieves little.
bg.3.33.misuse: Not 'I can't change, it's my nature'. The next verse says not to come under the sway of likes and dislikes.
bg.3.33.claim: Even the wise act according to their own nature; beings follow nature, so what can repression accomplish?
bg.3.33.needs: read with 3.34, which says where effort does work; alone it can sound like 'nothing can change'

bg.3.34.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.34.line: Liking and disliking lie in wait behind every sense. Don't let either take the wheel.
bg.3.34.claim: Attraction and aversion are lodged in each sense toward its objects; one should not come under their sway, for they are enemies.

bg.3.36.speaker: Arjuna
bg.3.36.line: Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?
bg.3.36.claim: Arjuna asks what impels a person to commit sin even unwillingly, as if driven by force.

bg.3.38.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.38.line: Like smoke over fire, dust on a mirror, desire covers your clear sight.
bg.3.38.claim: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust and an embryo by the womb, so knowledge is covered by desire.

bg.3.4.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.4.line: You don't get free by not starting, and you don't get perfect by just walking away.
bg.3.4.claim: Not by abstaining from action does one reach actionlessness, nor by mere renunciation does one attain perfection.

bg.3.43.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.43.line: Knowing what is higher in you, steady yourself with yourself and defeat the desire that's hard to beat.
bg.3.43.claim: Knowing the self as higher than intellect and steadying the self by the self, one should slay the enemy that is desire.
bg.3.43.needs: the ladder of 3.42: senses, mind, intellect, and that which is beyond

bg.3.5.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.5.line: No one can stay without acting, even for a moment. Your nature keeps moving you.
bg.3.5.claim: No one can remain even a moment without acting; everyone is made to act helplessly by the gunas born of nature.

bg.3.6.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.6.line: Holding back your hands while your mind keeps feasting on the craving is self-deception.
bg.3.6.claim: One who restrains the organs of action but dwells mentally on sense objects is deluded and called a hypocrite.

bg.4.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.20.line: Content and leaning on no one's approval, fully busy, and yet inwardly at rest.
bg.4.20.claim: Having given up attachment to fruit, ever content and dependent on nothing, he does nothing though fully engaged in action.

bg.4.24.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.24.line: The offering, the giver, the fire, the act: see the sacred in all of it, and you reach the sacred.
bg.4.24.claim: The offering, the oblation, the fire and the offerer are Brahman; one absorbed in Brahman as action reaches Brahman.

bg.4.36.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.36.line: Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
bg.4.36.misuse: Not 'understanding cancels the harm done to others'; it frees you to change and make amends.
bg.4.36.claim: Even the most sinful of all sinners crosses all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
bg.4.36.needs: the reader's burden is guilt for something they did; it says nothing about being loved or unloved

bg.4.40.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.40.line: A mind that doubts everything finds no happiness here or anywhere.
bg.4.40.misuse: Questioning is welcome in the Gita; Arjuna asks constantly. This is about corrosive doubt that blocks every step.
bg.4.40.claim: The ignorant, faithless, doubting person perishes; for the doubter there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
bg.4.40.needs: doubt here is refusal to trust teacher and teaching at all, not honest questioning or an anxious mind

bg.4.42.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.42.line: Cut the doubt in your heart with clear understanding, then stand up and act.
bg.4.42.claim: Cutting the heart's ignorance-born doubt with the sword of knowledge, one should take to yoga and stand up.
bg.4.42.needs: the reader has done the thinking and is stuck at the edge of acting

bg.4.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.8.line: To protect the good, end the harm, and set right what's broken, I appear age after age.
bg.4.8.misuse: Not a licence to punish people you judge wicked; the work of setting right belongs to the divine and to justice.
bg.4.8.claim: For protecting the good, destroying evildoers and establishing dharma, the Lord takes birth age after age.

bg.5.12.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.12.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
bg.5.12.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.
bg.5.12.claim: The yogi giving up the fruit of action attains abiding peace; the non-yogi, attached to fruit through desire, is bound.

bg.5.18.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.18.line: The wise see the same self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast.
bg.5.18.claim: The wise see the same in a learned, humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.

bg.5.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.20.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
bg.5.20.claim: The knower of Brahman, steady and undeluded, abiding in Brahman, neither rejoices at the pleasant nor is agitated by the unpleasant.
bg.5.20.needs: not a reply to fresh grief or injury

bg.5.21.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.21.line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
bg.5.21.claim: One unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness in the self; joined to Brahman, he enjoys undying happiness.

bg.5.29.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.29.line: The divine is the well-wisher of every being, you included. Knowing this, you find peace.
bg.5.29.claim: Knowing Krishna as enjoyer of sacrifices, great Lord of all worlds and friend of all beings, one attains peace.

bg.5.3.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.3.line: The one who neither resents nor craves is the real renouncer, wherever they live.
bg.5.3.claim: One who neither hates nor desires is a constant renouncer; free of the pairs, he is easily released from bondage.

bg.6.1.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.1.line: The real renouncer does the work that's needed without leaning on its rewards, not the one who quits.
bg.6.1.claim: One who does due work without depending on its fruit is the renouncer and yogi, not the fireless or inactive.

bg.6.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.22.line: Find the gain beyond all gains, and even heavy sorrow can't shake you.
bg.6.22.claim: Having gained that, one counts no other gain greater; established in it, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.
bg.6.22.needs: the passage 6.20-21 names what is gained; alone the line promises immunity to sorrow and can read as a reproach to someone grieving

bg.6.23.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.23.line: Yoga is unhooking from sorrow. Practise it with resolve and a heart that doesn't lose hope.
bg.6.23.claim: Yoga is disconnection from union with sorrow; it should be practised with determination and an undespairing mind.

bg.6.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.25.line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
bg.6.25.claim: Little by little one should withdraw, with intellect held by steadiness; fixing the mind in the self, think of nothing.

bg.6.30.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.30.line: See me in everything and everything in me, and I never lose you, nor you me.
bg.6.30.claim: One who sees Krishna everywhere and everything in him is never lost to Krishna, nor Krishna to him.

bg.6.36.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.36.line: Without self-control it's hard. With sincere effort and the right means, it's within reach.
bg.6.36.claim: Yoga is hard to attain for the uncontrolled, but attainable through right means by the self-controlled who strive.

bg.6.37.speaker: Arjuna
bg.6.37.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
bg.6.37.claim: Arjuna asks what end awaits one with faith who strives too little, strays from yoga and misses its perfection.

bg.6.38.speaker: Arjuna
bg.6.38.line: Fallen from both sides, does he scatter like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand?
bg.6.38.claim: Arjuna asks whether one fallen from both paths perishes like a torn cloud, unsupported and bewildered.

bg.6.9.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.9.line: Friend, enemy, stranger, relative, saint or wrongdoer: the one who sees all with an even mind stands highest.
bg.6.9.misuse: Even-minded is not naive; you can treat someone fairly and still keep a boundary.
bg.6.9.claim: One who is even-minded toward well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutrals, the hateful, kin, the good and sinners excels.
bg.6.9.needs: a seeker's ideal; told to someone being mistreated it asks them to feel the same toward the one harming them

bg.7.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.11.line: In the strong, I am strength without greed or grasping. In all, I am desire that stays within what's right.
bg.7.11.claim: Krishna is the strength of the strong free of desire and passion, and in beings the desire not opposed to dharma.

bg.7.16.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.16.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
bg.7.16.claim: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Krishna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth and the wise.

bg.8.6.speaker: Krishna
bg.8.6.line: Whatever you keep thinking about shapes who you become, right to the end.
bg.8.6.claim: Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body at the end, that one attains, being always absorbed in it.
bg.8.6.needs: a reader thinking about how to live toward death; never someone with a dying relative

bg.8.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.8.7.line: So remember the divine at all times, and keep doing your work.
bg.8.7.misuse: 'Fight' here means do your rightful work; it is not a call to pick battles.
bg.8.7.claim: Therefore one should remember Krishna at all times and fight; with mind and intellect offered to him, one surely reaches him.

bg.9.27.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.27.line: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
bg.9.27.claim: Whatever one does, eats, offers, gives or practises as austerity should be done as an offering to Krishna.

bg.9.29.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.29.line: I am the same towards all; no one is hated, no one favoured. Those who love me live in me.
bg.9.29.claim: Krishna is the same to all, none hated or dear; yet his devotees are in him and he in them.

bg.9.30.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.30.line: Even if you've done great wrong, the moment you turn wholeheartedly, count yourself among the good.
bg.9.30.misuse: Not 'devotion erases harm done to others'; turning around still includes making amends.
bg.9.30.claim: Even one of very bad conduct who worships Krishna with undivided devotion is to be deemed good, having resolved rightly.
bg.9.30.needs: a reader open to God who carries guilt for their own conduct

bg.9.31.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.31.line: Such a person soon turns good and finds lasting peace. Mark it: no one devoted to me is ever lost.
bg.9.31.claim: Such a one quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace; Krishna's devotee never perishes.

bg.10.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.10.20.line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
bg.10.20.claim: Krishna is the self seated in the hearts of all beings, and their beginning, middle and end.

bg.10.9.speaker: Krishna
bg.10.9.line: Their minds on me, they talk of me with each other, and find joy and contentment in it.
bg.10.9.claim: With minds and lives given to Krishna, enlightening one another and always speaking of him, his devotees are content and delight.

bg.11.24.speaker: Arjuna
bg.11.24.line: Seeing something too big to take in, my heart trembles and I can't find steadiness or calm.
bg.11.24.claim: Seeing the blazing, sky-touching, open-mouthed form, Arjuna trembles within and finds neither steadiness nor peace.
bg.11.24.needs: the scene of the cosmic form; the fear is awe before God's terrible aspect

bg.11.45.speaker: Arjuna
bg.11.45.line: I'm thrilled and terrified at once. Show me the familiar face again.
bg.11.45.claim: Thrilled at seeing the unseen yet shaken with fear, Arjuna asks the Lord to show his familiar form and be gracious.
bg.11.45.needs: the scene of the cosmic form

bg.11.49.speaker: Krishna
bg.11.49.line: Don't be afraid or confused by what you've seen. Let the fear go and look again with a calm heart.
bg.11.49.claim: Krishna tells Arjuna not to be afraid or bewildered at the terrible form, and to see his familiar form again, fear gone.
bg.11.49.needs: the scene: God withdrawing a terrifying vision; alone it just tells a frightened person not to be afraid

bg.12.4.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.4.line: Senses in hand, even-minded everywhere, glad in the good of all beings: they reach me too.
