bg.12.4.claim: Those who restrain the senses, are even-minded everywhere and delight in the welfare of all beings also reach Krishna.
bg.12.4.needs: completes 12.3 on those who worship the formless

bg.13.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.25.line: Some find the truth by meditation, some by thinking it through, some by selfless work.
bg.13.25.claim: Some see the self in themselves by meditation, others by the yoga of knowledge, and others by the yoga of action.

bg.13.26.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.26.line: Others, not knowing these paths, learn by listening to others, and they too cross over.
bg.13.26.claim: Others who do not know these ways worship as they have heard from others; they too cross beyond death, devoted to hearing.

bg.13.33.speaker: Krishna
bg.13.33.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
bg.13.33.claim: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, the self present in every body is not tainted.
bg.13.33.needs: week three; a reader already introduced to the self as distinct from body and mind

bg.14.13.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.13.line: When dullness rules: darkness, sluggishness, carelessness and confusion.
bg.14.13.claim: Darkness, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion arise when tamas predominates.

bg.14.23.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.23.line: Sit like a witness, unshaken, knowing it's just moods moving through, and stay steady.
bg.14.23.claim: Seated like one unconcerned, unshaken by the gunas, knowing that only the gunas act, he stays firm and does not waver.

bg.14.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.14.8.line: Dullness, born of ignorance, ties you down through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.
bg.14.8.claim: Tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all embodied beings and binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep.

bg.15.15.speaker: Krishna
bg.15.15.line: I am seated in every heart. Memory, knowledge and their fading come from me.
bg.15.15.claim: Krishna is seated in every heart; from him come memory, knowledge and their loss; all the Vedas make him known.

bg.15.5.speaker: Krishna
bg.15.5.line: Free of pride and delusion, past the pull of attachment, the steady reach what doesn't fade.
bg.15.5.claim: Free of pride and delusion, attachment conquered, ever in the self, desires gone, freed from the pairs, the undeluded reach the imperishable.

bg.15.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.15.7.line: Every living being is an eternal part of me, says Krishna.
bg.15.7.claim: An eternal portion of Krishna becomes the living soul in the world and draws the mind and five senses abiding in nature.

bg.16.15.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.15.line: 'I'm rich, well-born; who else is like me?' So speaks the deluded mind.
bg.16.15.claim: The demonic, deluded by ignorance, say: I am rich and well-born, who equals me; I will sacrifice, give and rejoice.
bg.16.15.needs: a reader examining their own pride; the speaker is describing the demonic nature

bg.16.17.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.17.line: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on money and status, they give for show.
bg.16.17.claim: Self-conceited, stubborn, drunk with wealth and honour, the demonic perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against rule.
bg.16.17.needs: describes the demonic nature; a mirror only for one examining pride

bg.16.22.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.22.line: Freed from these three dark gates, you do what's truly good for you and reach the highest.
bg.16.22.claim: One released from these three gates of darkness does what is good for the self and reaches the highest goal.
bg.16.22.needs: follows 16.21, which names the three gates

bg.16.5.speaker: Krishna
bg.16.5.line: Good qualities free you; harsh ones bind. Don't worry; you were born with the good.
bg.16.5.claim: The divine nature leads to liberation and the demonic to bondage; Arjuna need not grieve, being born to the divine.

bg.17.19.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.19.line: Discipline done through stubborn self-torment, or to harm another, is the dark kind.
bg.17.19.claim: Austerity done from foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to ruin another, is called tamasic.

bg.17.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.17.8.line: Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm: that's the food of a clear mind.
bg.17.8.claim: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheer, savoury, smooth, firm and pleasant, are dear to the sattvic.

bg.18.10.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.10.line: The wise don't hate unpleasant work or cling to pleasant work. Doubts gone, they just do it.
bg.18.10.claim: The wise renouncer, pervaded by sattva and free of doubt, neither hates disagreeable work nor clings to agreeable work.

bg.18.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.20.line: Clear understanding sees one undivided life in all beings, though they appear separate.
bg.18.20.claim: The knowledge by which one sees one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided, is sattvic.

bg.18.23.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.23.line: Good action is steady, done without clinging, not driven by like or dislike, or by what you'll get.
bg.18.23.claim: Obligatory action done without attachment, without love or hate, by one not seeking its fruit, is sattvic.

bg.18.24.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.24.line: Work done with huge strain, for ego or pleasure, is the restless kind.
bg.18.24.claim: Action done by one craving desires, or with ego, or with great strain, is called rajasic.

bg.18.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.25.line: Action begun in confusion, without weighing consequences, cost, harm or your own capacity, is dark action.
bg.18.25.claim: Action begun from delusion, heedless of consequence, loss, injury and one's own capacity, is called tamasic.

bg.18.27.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.27.line: Hungry for results, greedy, willing to harm, unclean, tossed by joy and grief: the restless kind of doer.
bg.18.27.claim: The doer who is passionate, eager for fruit, greedy, harmful, impure and swayed by joy and sorrow is called rajasic.
bg.18.27.needs: a hard mirror; pairs 'tossed by joy and grief' with greed and harm

bg.18.31.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.31.line: A mind clouded by restlessness can't quite tell right from wrong, or what to do from what to avoid.
bg.18.31.claim: The intellect that knows dharma and adharma, duty and non-duty incorrectly is rajasic.

bg.18.32.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.32.line: A mind wrapped in darkness takes wrong for right and sees everything upside down.
bg.18.32.claim: The intellect that, wrapped in darkness, takes adharma for dharma and sees all things inverted is tamasic.

bg.18.33.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.33.line: True resolve holds mind, breath and senses steady through unwavering practice.
bg.18.33.claim: The unswerving firmness by which one holds the activities of mind, breath and senses through yoga is sattvic.

bg.18.34.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.34.line: Clinging to duty, pleasure and wealth for what they'll bring you is restless resolve.
bg.18.34.claim: The firmness by which one holds to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, craving their fruit, is rajasic.

bg.18.35.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.35.line: Stubbornly holding on to sleep, fear, grief, despair and pride is the dark kind of resolve.
bg.18.35.misuse: Not a judgement on depression or grief; it names the habit of clinging to them as if they were safety.
bg.18.35.claim: The firmness by which a dull-minded person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and pride is tamasic.
bg.18.35.needs: never as a mirror for grief or fear: it calls holding on to them dull-minded

bg.18.36.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.36.line: There is a joy you grow into through practice, one that brings sorrow to an end.
bg.18.36.claim: Happiness is of three kinds; in the sattvic kind one comes to delight through practice and reaches the end of sorrow.

bg.18.39.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.39.line: Pleasure from sleep, laziness and carelessness dulls you from start to finish.
bg.18.39.claim: Happiness that deludes the self both at first and afterward, arising from sleep, laziness and heedlessness, is tamasic.

bg.18.49.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.49.line: Unattached everywhere, self-mastered, free of craving: that's the highest freedom.
bg.18.49.misuse: Unattached is not uncaring; it doesn't ask you to step back from family or friends.
bg.18.49.claim: One with intellect unattached everywhere, self-mastered and free of longing attains by renunciation the supreme perfection of actionlessness.

bg.18.57.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.57.line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
bg.18.57.claim: Mentally resigning all actions to Krishna, holding him supreme and relying on buddhi yoga, one should keep the mind always on him.

bg.18.6.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.6.line: Even good work should be done without clinging to it or its rewards. That's my settled view.
bg.18.6.claim: Even sacrifice, giving and austerity should be done giving up attachment and fruit; this is Krishna's settled and highest view.
bg.18.6.needs: 'these actions' are sacrifice, giving and austerity (18.5)

bg.18.65.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.65.line: Mind on me, heart devoted to me, you will come to me. I promise: you are dear to me.
bg.18.65.claim: Fixing the mind on Krishna, devoted, sacrificing and bowing to him, one comes to him; he promises this, for Arjuna is dear.
bg.18.65.needs: a devotional reader; part of the closing word 18.64-66, best late in a plan

bg.18.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.7.line: Walking away from a real responsibility out of confusion is the darkest kind of letting go.
bg.18.7.misuse: Not 'you can never leave'. Leaving thoughtfully is different from abandoning out of confusion.
bg.18.7.claim: Renouncing obligatory action is not proper; abandoning it out of delusion is declared tamasic.
bg.18.7.needs: a reader tempted to drop a duty in confusion; not for someone leaving harm or worn out by care

bg.18.78.speaker: Sanjaya
bg.18.78.line: Where wisdom and skilled effort stand together, there is fortune, victory, wellbeing and steady justice.
bg.18.78.claim: Where Krishna, lord of yoga, and Arjuna the archer are, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and firm justice.

bg.18.9.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.9.line: Do what must be done because it must be done, letting go of clinging and the payoff.
bg.18.9.misuse: Not 'never question your duties'. Choose them wisely, then do them without clinging.
bg.18.9.claim: Obligatory work done simply because it ought to be done, giving up attachment and fruit, is sattvic renunciation.

bg.2.16.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.16.line: What is unreal never truly lasts; what is real never stops being.
bg.2.16.claim: The unreal has no being and the real never ceases to be; seers of truth have seen the conclusion about both.

bg.2.2.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.2.line: Where did this weakness come from, at the very moment it matters most?
bg.2.2.misuse: Not shaming fear; it's the opening of a long, patient answer.
bg.2.2.claim: Krishna asks whence this faintness came on Arjuna in a crisis: unworthy of the noble, barring heaven, and bringing disgrace.
bg.2.2.needs: the scene: Krishna's first words to a great warrior who has just put down his bow; the teaching begins only after 2.7

bg.2.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.25.line: It is unseen, beyond thought, unchanging. Knowing this, ease your grief.
bg.2.25.claim: The self is called unmanifest, unthinkable and unchangeable; knowing it so, one should not grieve.
bg.2.25.needs: some distance from the loss; ends with 'you should not grieve'

bg.2.26.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.26.line: Even if you believe life simply begins and ends, there's still no need to be crushed by grief.
bg.2.26.misuse: Grief is human; this asks you not to be destroyed by it, not to stop feeling it.
bg.2.26.claim: Even if one thinks the self constantly born and constantly dying, still one should not grieve so.
bg.2.26.needs: some distance from the loss; read with 2.27

bg.2.30.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.30.line: The self within every body can never be destroyed. So don't grieve for any creature as lost.
bg.2.30.misuse: Not a reason to hurry anyone through mourning a person or a pet.
bg.2.30.claim: The self dwelling in every body is eternal and cannot be slain; so one should not grieve for any being.
bg.2.30.needs: some distance from the loss; closes the teaching of 2.11-30

bg.2.44.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.44.line: Chasing comfort and power, the mind can never settle into a single purpose.
bg.2.44.claim: For those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away, a resolute understanding does not form in concentration.

bg.2.45.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.45.line: Rise above the pull of opposites. Stay centred, not obsessed with getting and keeping.
bg.2.45.misuse: Not 'don't save or plan'; it's about not being consumed by getting and holding.
bg.2.45.claim: The Vedas concern the three gunas; one should be beyond them, free of opposites, ever in sattva, unacquisitive and self-possessed.
bg.2.45.needs: a seeker; not for someone under real money stress

bg.2.52.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.52.line: When your mind clears the fog, you'll tire of all you've heard and all you're yet to hear.
bg.2.52.claim: When the intellect crosses the mire of delusion, one grows dispassionate toward all heard and yet to be heard.

bg.2.59.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.59.line: Staying away from a craving dims it, but the taste lingers until something higher replaces it.
bg.2.59.claim: Objects fall away from one who abstains, but the taste remains; even the taste ceases on seeing the Supreme.

bg.2.61.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.61.line: Gather the senses in, sit steady with your mind on what's highest. Mastery of the senses steadies wisdom.
bg.2.61.claim: Restraining all the senses, one should sit disciplined, intent on Krishna; wisdom is firm in one whose senses are controlled.

bg.2.65.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.65.line: When the mind clears, sorrows start to dissolve, and understanding settles quickly.
bg.2.65.claim: In serenity all sorrows end; the understanding of the serene-minded soon becomes steady.
bg.2.65.needs: follows 2.64, which says how serenity is reached

bg.2.69.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.69.line: What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.
bg.2.69.claim: What is night to all beings, the self-controlled sage is awake in; where beings are awake is night to the seeing sage.

bg.2.72.speaker: Krishna
bg.2.72.line: Rooted in this steadiness, you aren't lost, even at the very end.
bg.2.72.claim: This is the state of Brahman; attaining it one is not deluded, and abiding in it even at death one reaches Brahman-nirvana.
bg.2.72.needs: a seeker reflecting on their own end; not for someone with an ill relative

bg.2.8.speaker: Arjuna
bg.2.8.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
bg.2.8.claim: Arjuna sees nothing that could remove the grief drying up his senses, not even an unrivalled kingdom or lordship over the gods.

bg.3.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.11.line: Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.
bg.3.11.claim: By sacrifice humans should nourish the gods and the gods nourish them; nourishing one another, both attain the highest good.

bg.3.13.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.13.line: Those who share first are freed; those who cook only for themselves feed on wrong.
bg.3.13.claim: The good who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sins; the wicked who cook for themselves alone eat sin.

bg.3.17.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.17.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
bg.3.17.claim: For one who delights in the self, is satisfied in the self and content in the self alone, there is no duty.

bg.3.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.25.line: Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.
bg.3.25.claim: As the unwise act attached to work, so the wise should act unattached, wishing the welfare of the world.

bg.3.39.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.39.line: Desire is a fire that never gets enough. It quietly covers even the wise person's clarity.
bg.3.39.claim: Knowledge is covered by desire, the constant enemy of the wise, an insatiable fire.

bg.3.41.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.41.line: So start with the senses. Get them in hand, then let go of the desire that wrecks clear thinking.
bg.3.41.claim: One should first control the senses and then cast off desire, the sinful destroyer of knowledge and realisation.
bg.3.41.needs: follows 3.40, which names senses, mind and intellect as desire's seat

bg.3.42.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.42.line: Senses are strong, the mind stronger, clear judgement stronger still, and your true self strongest of all.
bg.3.42.claim: The senses are high; higher is the mind; higher than mind the intellect; and beyond the intellect is the self.

bg.3.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.3.7.line: Better: guide your senses with your mind and get to work, without being hooked.
bg.3.7.claim: One who controls the senses by the mind and, unattached, engages the organs of action in karma yoga excels.

bg.4.10.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.10.line: Many have dropped craving, fear and anger, been refined by wisdom, and found their way home.
bg.4.10.claim: Freed from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in Krishna and taking refuge in him, many purified by knowledge have attained his being.

bg.4.17.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.17.line: What to do, what to avoid, when to hold back: the way of action is deep.
bg.4.17.claim: One must understand action, forbidden action and inaction; the way of action is hard to fathom.

bg.4.18.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.18.line: See the stillness inside activity and the activity inside stillness, and you're truly wise.
bg.4.18.claim: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people, a yogi who has done all action.

bg.4.21.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.21.line: Expecting nothing, mind steady, letting go of possessiveness, you can work without being stained.
bg.4.21.claim: Without expectation, mind and self controlled, all possessions given up, doing only bodily action, one incurs no fault.
bg.4.21.needs: the tradition reads this of the renunciate

bg.4.37.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.37.line: As a blazing fire turns wood to ash, real understanding burns away the hold of past actions.
bg.4.37.misuse: Not a way to skip accountability; amends still matter.
bg.4.37.claim: As blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
bg.4.37.needs: the burden is guilt for one's own acts

bg.4.38.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.38.line: Nothing here cleanses like understanding, and with steady practice you find it within, in time.
bg.4.38.claim: Nothing here purifies like knowledge; one perfected in yoga finds it within oneself in time.

bg.4.41.speaker: Krishna
bg.4.41.line: Doubts cut away by understanding, steady within, your actions stop binding you.
bg.4.41.claim: Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts knowledge has cut, and who is self-possessed.

bg.5.11.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.11.line: Wise people work with body, mind and heart, not for gain, but to become clearer within.
bg.5.11.claim: Yogis act with body, mind, intellect and senses alone, giving up attachment, for the purification of the self.

bg.5.19.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.19.line: Those whose minds rest in evenness have already won, right here in this life.
bg.5.19.claim: Those whose minds rest in evenness have conquered birth here itself; Brahman is flawless and same, so they rest in Brahman.

bg.5.2.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.2.line: Stepping back and acting selflessly both lead to good, but of the two, acting is better.
bg.5.2.misuse: Not 'never rest or retire'; it prefers engaged, selfless work over withdrawal.
bg.5.2.claim: Renunciation and karma yoga both lead to the highest good, but karma yoga is better than renunciation of action.

bg.5.24.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.24.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
bg.5.24.claim: The yogi whose happiness, delight and light are within becomes Brahman and attains Brahman-nirvana.

bg.5.25.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.25.line: Doubts cut away, mind mastered, they give themselves to the good of all beings and find peace.
bg.5.25.claim: Seers whose sins are destroyed, doubts cut, selves controlled, who delight in the good of all beings, attain Brahman-nirvana.

bg.5.28.speaker: Krishna
bg.5.28.line: Senses, mind and judgement in hand, free of desire, fear and anger: that person is already free.
bg.5.28.claim: The sage with senses, mind and intellect controlled, intent on liberation, free of desire, fear and anger, is ever free.
bg.5.28.needs: completes 5.27 on the practice of meditation

bg.6.20.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.20.line: When the mind finally goes still, you see yourself as you are, and you're content.
bg.6.20.claim: When the mind restrained by yoga comes to rest, one sees the self by the self and is content in it.

bg.6.27.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.27.line: A calm mind, its turmoil settled, finds the highest happiness.
bg.6.27.claim: Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is tranquil, whose rajas is stilled, who is sinless and has become Brahman.

bg.6.29.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.29.line: See yourself in every being and every being in yourself, and you see the same everywhere.
bg.6.29.claim: The yogi sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self, seeing the same everywhere.

bg.6.33.speaker: Arjuna
bg.6.33.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
bg.6.33.claim: Arjuna says he cannot see this yoga of evenness lasting, because of the mind's restlessness.

bg.6.43.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.43.line: What you learned before isn't lost. You pick it up again and push on harder.
bg.6.43.claim: Reborn, the fallen yogi regains the understanding of his former body and strives again, harder, for perfection.
bg.6.43.needs: the verse speaks of carrying practice across births; the app line applies it within one life

bg.6.44.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.44.line: Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.
bg.6.44.claim: By former practice the fallen yogi is carried on even helplessly; even the mere inquirer into yoga goes beyond Vedic rite.
bg.6.44.needs: the context is rebirth of one who fell from yoga

bg.6.45.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.45.line: The one who keeps at it, steadily, over a long time, gets there.
bg.6.45.claim: The yogi striving diligently, cleansed of sin and perfected through many births, then reaches the highest goal.

bg.6.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.6.8.line: To the settled mind, a lump of earth, a stone and a bar of gold are worth the same.
bg.6.8.misuse: Not a reason to neglect money or family finances; it is about not being ruled by them.
bg.6.8.claim: The yogi satisfied by knowledge and realisation, unshaken, senses conquered, to whom clod, stone and gold are alike, is called steadfast.
bg.6.8.needs: a seeker's ideal; not for someone short of money

bg.7.21.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.21.line: Whatever form someone chooses to worship with faith, I make that faith steady.
bg.7.21.claim: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, Krishna makes that very faith unwavering.
bg.7.21.needs: a reader open to God; 7.20-23 add that such worshippers gain limited fruits

bg.7.27.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.27.line: From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.
bg.7.27.claim: All beings fall into delusion at birth through the delusion of opposites arising from desire and aversion.

bg.8.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.8.8.line: With a mind trained by practice and not wandering elsewhere, you reach what you meditate on.
bg.8.8.claim: With a mind disciplined by practice and not straying elsewhere, constantly meditating, one goes to the supreme divine Person.

bg.9.34.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.34.line: Fix your mind on me, love me, honour me, bow to me. Joined this way, you come to me.
bg.9.34.claim: Fixing mind on Krishna, devoted, sacrificing and bowing to him, united and holding him as the goal, one comes to him.

up_aitareya.31.speaker: Seer
up_aitareya.31.line: She who nourishes the child must herself be nourished.
up_aitareya.31.claim: The woman who nourishes the unborn child must herself be nourished and protected.
up_aitareya.31.needs: The verse speaks from the father's side: his own self has entered her as the embryo. Use only as a duty of care toward the mother, never as a statement about women.

up_brihadaranyak.188.speaker: Maitreyi and Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.188.line: 'If the whole earth's wealth were mine, would it make me deathless?' 'No. Wealth buys comfort, not that.'
up_brihadaranyak.188.claim: Wealth can give a comfortable life but cannot give immortality.
up_brihadaranyak.188.needs: The scene: Yajnavalkya is leaving home and dividing his property. Not for someone in real money trouble, to whom it sounds dismissive.

up_brihadaranyak.189.speaker: Maitreyi
up_brihadaranyak.189.line: What would I do with something that cannot save me? Teach me what you know instead.
up_brihadaranyak.189.claim: What cannot make me immortal is of no use to me; teach me what you know.
up_brihadaranyak.189.needs: Reads best after 2.4.2 where the offer of property is made.

up_brihadaranyak.418.speaker: Yajnavalkya and Janaka
up_brihadaranyak.418.line: 'You are rich and learned. When you die, where will you go?' The king said, 'I don't know.'
up_brihadaranyak.418.claim: Wealth, honour and learning do not tell a person where he goes when he leaves this world.
up_brihadaranyak.418.needs: Must be followed by the answer (the self as one's own light, 4.3), or it only frightens.

up_brihadaranyak.429.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.429.line: When sun, moon and fire are gone and even voices fall silent, the self is your light.
up_brihadaranyak.429.claim: When every outer light and even speech has gone, the self is the light by which a person sits, moves and works.

up_brihadaranyak.477.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.477.line: As your desire, so your will; as your will, so your deeds; as your deeds, so you become.
up_brihadaranyak.477.claim: A person is made of desire: desire shapes resolve, resolve shapes action, and action shapes what one becomes.
up_brihadaranyak.477.needs: In context this explains rebirth and bondage; the next verse praises the one free of desire. The motivational reading is partial.

up_brihadaranyak.488.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.488.line: While we are still here, let us know it. Not knowing it is the great loss.
up_brihadaranyak.488.claim: The self is to be known in this very life; not knowing it is the great loss.

up_brihadaranyak.495.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.495.line: Know the one thing, and let wisdom grow from it. Don't brood over many words; that only tires you.
up_brihadaranyak.495.claim: Having known the self alone, cultivate insight and do not dwell on many words, which only weary speech.
up_brihadaranyak.495.needs: Addressed to a seeker of the self; applying it to ordinary overthinking is an extension.

up_brihadaranyak.534.speaker: Prajapati
up_brihadaranyak.534.line: The thunder says Da Da Da: be self-controlled, be giving, be compassionate.
up_brihadaranyak.534.claim: The one syllable Da teaches three duties: self-control, giving and compassion.

up_brihadaranyak.56.speaker: Seer
up_brihadaranyak.56.line: Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to the deathless.
up_brihadaranyak.56.claim: A prayer to be led from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.

up_brihadaranyak.86.speaker: Seer
up_brihadaranyak.86.line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
up_brihadaranyak.86.claim: Nothing is higher than dharma; through it the weak can stand up to the strong, and dharma is truth.

up_chhandogya.247.speaker: Shandilya
up_chhandogya.247.line: A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well.
up_chhandogya.247.claim: All this is Brahman; a person is made of resolve and becomes what he resolves, so one should form a resolve.
up_chhandogya.247.needs: The resolve meant is a settled conviction in meditation on Brahman as one's own self (3.14.2-4), not any life goal.

up_chhandogya.304.speaker: Jabala
up_chhandogya.304.line: His mother said, 'I don't know your father's line. I am Jabala, you are Satyakama. Say exactly that.'
up_chhandogya.304.claim: A mother tells her son plainly that she does not know his lineage and that he should say exactly that.
up_chhandogya.304.needs: Tell the whole Satyakama story. Do not speculate about the mother's past.

up_chhandogya.308.speaker: Haridrumata Gautama
up_chhandogya.308.line: Only someone truly noble could speak this plainly. You have not swerved from truth; I will teach you.
up_chhandogya.308.claim: The teacher accepts the boy because he did not swerve from the truth about himself.

up_chhandogya.309.speaker: Satyakama
up_chhandogya.309.line: Given four hundred weak cows, he said, 'I won't come back until they are a thousand.' He stayed years.
up_chhandogya.309.claim: Given four hundred weak cows, Satyakama vowed not to return until they were a thousand and stayed away for years.

up_chhandogya.455.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.455.line: Shvetaketu came home proud of his learning. His father asked: did you learn what makes everything else make sense?
up_chhandogya.455.claim: A father asks his conceited, learned son whether he asked for the teaching by which the unknown becomes known.

up_chhandogya.492.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.492.line: Like a bird on a string, the mind flies everywhere, finds no rest, and returns to the breath.
up_chhandogya.492.claim: The mind flies in every direction, finds no resting place elsewhere, and settles on that to which it is tied.

up_chhandogya.498.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.498.line: That subtle essence is the self of all that is. That is truth. You are that, Shvetaketu.
up_chhandogya.498.claim: The subtle essence that is the self of all this is the truth and the self, and you are that.

up_chhandogya.508.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.508.line: The body dies when life leaves it. Life itself does not die.
up_chhandogya.508.claim: The body dies when the living self leaves it; the living self does not die.
up_chhandogya.508.needs: The reader must accept a self distinct from the body. Not for the first raw days of a loss.

up_chhandogya.509.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.509.line: Break a banyan seed and you find nothing. From that unseen nothing, a great tree stands. Have faith.
up_chhandogya.509.claim: The great banyan stands from a subtle essence in the seed that the eye cannot see; so have faith.

up_chhandogya.512.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.512.line: Salt dissolved in water can't be seen, yet every sip tastes of it. What you can't see is still here.
up_chhandogya.512.claim: Like salt dissolved in water, the real is present everywhere here though it cannot be seen.

up_chhandogya.515.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.515.line: Lost and blindfolded, you need someone to point the way; then ask village by village until you're home.
up_chhandogya.515.claim: As a blindfolded man gets home once someone frees his eyes and points the way, one with a teacher comes to know.

up_chhandogya.526.speaker: Narada
up_chhandogya.526.line: I have learned so much, yet I am sad. I know words, not myself. Help me cross this sorrow.
up_chhandogya.526.claim: One who knows many texts but not the self remains in sorrow; the knower of the self crosses sorrow.

up_chhandogya.581.speaker: Sanatkumara
up_chhandogya.581.line: Steadiness comes from doing. No one becomes steady without acting; act, and steadiness follows.
up_chhandogya.581.claim: Steadfastness comes only through doing; no one becomes steadfast without acting.

up_chhandogya.583.speaker: Sanatkumara
up_chhandogya.583.line: Happiness is in the vast. There is no happiness in the small.
up_chhandogya.583.claim: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small.

up_chhandogya.612.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
up_chhandogya.612.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
up_chhandogya.612.claim: Like people walking over buried gold, all beings enter the world of Brahman daily in sleep and do not find it.

up_isha.1.speaker: Seer
up_isha.1.line: Everything is held by the divine. Enjoy by letting go; do not covet. Whose wealth is it, really?
up_isha.1.misuse: Not a call to neglect your finances; it is about how you hold what you have.
up_isha.1.claim: All that moves in this world is pervaded by the Lord; live by renouncing and do not covet anyone's wealth.
up_isha.1.needs: Not for someone in real money stress; it is about how one holds what one has.

up_isha.2.speaker: Seer
up_isha.2.line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
up_isha.2.claim: One should wish to live a hundred years doing one's work; for such a person action does not cling.

up_isha.6.speaker: Seer
up_isha.6.line: See yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself, and you stop recoiling from people.
up_isha.6.claim: One who sees all beings in the self and the self in all beings does not recoil from anyone.
up_isha.6.needs: Never as advice to someone being mistreated to stop objecting.

up_kath.1.2.2.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.2.2.line: The good and the pleasant both knock. The wise choose the good; the foolish grab the pleasant.
up_kath.1.2.2.claim: The good and the pleasant both come to a person; the wise choose the good, the dull choose the pleasant.
up_kath.1.2.2.needs: 'The dull' and 'the foolish' can sting someone already ashamed of a choice.

up_kath.1.3.14.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.3.14.line: Arise, awake! Find the wise and learn. The path is sharp as a razor's edge, hard to cross.
up_kath.1.3.14.claim: Arise, awake, go to the great teachers and learn; the path is sharp and hard to cross like a razor's edge.
up_kath.1.3.14.needs: Too loud for an exhausted or collapsed reader.

up_kath.1.3.3.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.3.3.line: You are the rider, your body the chariot, your intellect the driver, your mind the reins.
up_kath.1.3.3.claim: The self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the charioteer, the mind the reins and the senses the horses.

up_kath.2.1.1.speaker: Yama
up_kath.2.1.1.line: Our senses face outward, so we look out. A rare wise person turns the gaze inward.
up_kath.2.1.1.claim: The senses face outward, so people look out; a rare wise one turns the gaze inward and sees the self.

up_katharudra.17.speaker: Teacher
up_katharudra.17.line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.
up_katharudra.17.claim: Do not torment the body over pleasure and pain; do not gloat when praised or curse others when blamed.
up_katharudra.17.needs: A rule from a renunciant's code; offer it as conduct under criticism, never to someone who has been wronged.

up_kaushitaki.126.speaker: Indra
up_kaushitaki.126.line: Without attention, nothing reaches us. We say, 'Sorry, my mind was elsewhere; I didn't catch that.'
up_kaushitaki.126.claim: Without attention behind them, speech and the senses convey nothing; one says, my mind was elsewhere.

up_kaushitaki.3.speaker: Shvetaketu and Uddalaka Aruni
up_kaushitaki.3.line: 'I don't know either,' the father told his son. 'Let's both go and learn, as students.'
up_kaushitaki.3.claim: A father admits to his son that he too does not know and proposes that they both go and learn.

up_maha.107.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.107.line: Trouble comes from ego, anxiety comes from ego, craving comes from ego. There is no greater enemy.
up_maha.107.claim: Misfortune, mental distress and craving all come from ego; there is no greater enemy than ego.
up_maha.107.needs: Nidagha is speaking of his own ego. Turned on a reader in pain it becomes blame.

up_maha.109.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.109.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
up_maha.109.claim: The mind runs here and there, restless and to no purpose, wandering far like a dog in a village.

up_maha.111.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.111.line: Drinking the ocean, uprooting a mountain, swallowing fire: mastering the mind is harder than all of these.
up_maha.111.claim: Mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean, uprooting Mount Meru or swallowing fire.
up_maha.111.needs: Follow with a verse that gives a way in (4.2-3), or it reads as hopeless.

up_maha.144.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.144.line: Hard times arrive in a moment; good times arrive in a moment. Everything passes.
up_maha.144.claim: Misfortune, good fortune, birth and death each come in a moment; all of it is perishable.

up_maha.150.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.150.line: Freedom has four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. Win one, and the others follow.
up_maha.150.claim: Calm, inquiry, contentment and good company guard the door of freedom; win one fully and the other three follow.

up_maha.178.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.178.line: Sorrow, craving and unbearable anxiety all vanish in a calm mind, like darkness before the sun.
up_maha.178.claim: All sorrows, craving and unbearable anxieties vanish in calm minds, as darkness vanishes before the sun.
up_maha.178.needs: Gives no method. To an anxious reader alone it can sound like 'just be calm'; pair with a practice.

up_maha.180.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.180.line: No elixir and no fortune brings the happiness that inner calm brings.
up_maha.180.claim: No elixir and no wealth gives the happiness that inner calm gives.

up_maha.248.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.248.line: A mind without restlessness is nowhere to be found. Restlessness is its nature, as heat is fire's.
up_maha.248.claim: Restlessness is the nature of the mind, as heat is the nature of fire; no mind is without it.

up_maha.255.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.255.line: Use the mind to cut the mind's own noose. Lift yourself out; no one else can do it for you.
up_maha.255.claim: Your own mind is the boat across craving; cut the mind's noose with the mind, for no one else can lift you.
up_maha.255.needs: 'No one else can carry you' is wrong for a lonely or collapsed reader and sits against a devotional plan.

up_maha.370.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.370.line: With full effort, steady work, good guidance and no panic, who would not succeed?
up_maha.370.claim: One who takes up full effort and acts by sound guidance without anxiety is sure to succeed.
up_maha.370.needs: Not after a failure, when 'who would not succeed' reads as blame.

up_maha.452.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.452.line: Let what is lost go. Take up what comes.
up_maha.452.claim: In worldly dealings, let go of what is lost and take up what comes.
up_maha.452.needs: About gains and losses in dealings, not about people one has lost or wrongs one has suffered.

up_maha.467.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.467.line: Rice sheds its husk and copper its tarnish through work. Your flaws can go too, so keep at it.
up_maha.467.claim: As husk leaves rice and tarnish leaves copper through work, a person's inborn impurity surely goes through effort; so be industrious.

up_maha.532.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.532.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
up_maha.532.claim: One who does the work that comes, sees friend and foe alike and speaks gently does not sink in worldly life.
up_maha.532.needs: A portrait of a free person, not a demand to be pleasant to someone who is mistreating you.

up_maha.536.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.536.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
up_maha.536.claim: Be outwardly active and inwardly unagitated, a doer outside and a non-doer within, moving through the world with a clear mind.

up_maha.539.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.539.line: 'Ours' and 'theirs' is how small minds count. For the large-hearted, the whole earth is family.
up_maha.539.claim: Counting people as one's own or not is small-minded; for the generous-hearted the whole earth is family.
up_maha.539.needs: Not as a reply to someone whose family is treating them badly.

up_maitrayani.78.speaker: Shakayanya
up_maitrayani.78.line: Your mind is your world; clean it with care. What your mind dwells on, you become.
up_maitrayani.78.claim: The mind itself is samsara, so purify it with effort; what one's mind dwells on, that one becomes.

up_maitrayani.80.speaker: Shakayanya
up_maitrayani.80.line: If the mind clung to the highest as tightly as it clings to things, who would not be free?
up_maitrayani.80.claim: If the mind were as attached to Brahman as it is to sense objects, anyone would be freed from bondage.

up_maitrayani.86.speaker: Shakayanya
up_maitrayani.86.line: The mind alone binds or frees us: hooked on things, it binds; free of them, it liberates.
up_maitrayani.86.claim: The mind alone causes bondage and liberation: attached to objects it binds, free of objects it liberates.

up_maitreya.24.speaker: Mahadeva (Shiva)
up_maitreya.24.line: Your body is a temple, and the life within it is divine. Toss out ignorance like yesterday's flowers.
up_maitreya.24.claim: The body is a temple and the living being in it is Shiva alone; discard ignorance and worship as 'I am He'.

up_mundaka.1.1.4.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.1.1.4.line: There are two kinds of knowledge: the lower, all our learning and skills; the higher, knowing what never perishes.
up_mundaka.1.1.4.claim: There are two kinds of knowledge: the lower, the Vedas and their sciences, and the higher, by which the imperishable is reached.

up_mundaka.1.2.12.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.1.2.12.line: Having seen what work can win, know this: what is not made cannot be gained by making. Find a teacher.
up_mundaka.1.2.12.claim: Seeing that the unmade cannot be won by action, a seeker should turn dispassionate and go to a teacher established in Brahman.
up_mundaka.1.2.12.needs: In Shankara this qualifies a person for renunciation. Offer it as a turn toward inquiry, not as a reason to quit work or family.

up_mundaka.3.1.1.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.1.1.line: Two birds, close friends, sit on one tree. One eats the sweet fruit; the other just watches.
up_mundaka.3.1.1.claim: Two companion birds cling to one tree; one eats the sweet fruit, the other looks on without eating.
up_mundaka.3.1.1.needs: Reads fully with 3.1.2: sunk and grieving, the one sees the other and is freed from sorrow.

up_mundaka.3.1.6.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.1.6.line: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. Truth lays the road that the wise walk.
up_mundaka.3.1.6.misuse: Truth wins in the long run; it is not a promise of quick victory.
up_mundaka.3.1.6.claim: Truth alone prevails, not falsehood; by truth is laid the path the sages walk to the highest abode of truth.
up_mundaka.3.1.6.needs: Truth prevails in the long run; no promise of a quick result.

up_niralamb.13.speaker: Teacher
up_niralamb.13.line: Caste is not in skin, blood, flesh or bone. The self has no caste; caste is a social convention.
up_niralamb.13.claim: Caste belongs to no part of the body and not to the self; it is a convention made for worldly dealings.

up_prashn.72.speaker: Sukesha
up_prashn.72.line: I told him plainly, 'I do not know.' Whoever speaks falsehood dries up to the very root.
up_prashn.72.claim: Sukesha told the prince plainly that he did not know, for one who speaks untruth dries up to the root.

up_taittiriya.108.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.108.line: Give a good young man health, learning and the whole earth's wealth: one human joy. The desireless already hold more.
up_taittiriya.108.claim: The joy of a learned person untouched by desire equals each order of joy above the fullest human happiness.

up_taittiriya.125.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.125.line: Free in that joy, one no longer agonises: 'Why didn't I do right? Why did I do wrong?'
up_taittiriya.125.misuse: Not a licence to stop caring about harm done; it frees you from self-torment so you can make amends.
up_taittiriya.125.claim: The knower of the bliss of Brahman is no longer tormented by thoughts of good left undone or wrong done.
up_taittiriya.125.needs: Said of one who knows the self. It ends self-torment; it does not cancel the need to make amends.

up_taittiriya.146.speaker: Narrator
up_taittiriya.146.line: At last Bhrigu saw: from joy all beings are born, by joy they live, into joy they return.
up_taittiriya.146.claim: Joy is Brahman: from joy beings are born, by joy they live, and into joy they return.
up_taittiriya.146.needs: The last clause speaks of beings departing into joy; keep the line's wording and do not use it as comfort about someone's dying.

up_taittiriya.49.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.49.line: Speak the truth. Do what is right. Never stop learning.
up_taittiriya.49.claim: Speak the truth, practise dharma, and do not neglect your study.

up_taittiriya.52.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.52.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
up_taittiriya.52.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.
up_taittiriya.52.claim: Do not neglect duties to gods and ancestors; regard mother, father, teacher and guest as divine.
up_taittiriya.52.needs: Honouring parents never means accepting mistreatment.

up_taittiriya.54.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.54.line: Give with faith, not without it. Give generously, give modestly, give with respect, give with understanding.
up_taittiriya.54.claim: Give with faith, in plenty, with modesty, with awe and with understanding; do not give without faith.

up_taittiriya.56.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.56.line: When unsure what to do, ask how thoughtful, gentle, fair-minded people would act, and do that.
up_taittiriya.56.claim: When in doubt about an action or conduct, act as thoughtful, gentle, dharma-loving people there would act.

up_adhyatma.22.speaker: Seer
up_adhyatma.22.line: Push moss aside and it closes back at once. So confusion returns to the wise who look away.
up_adhyatma.22.claim: As moss pushed aside closes back at once, maya covers again even a wise person who turns away.

up_adhyatma.54.speaker: Seer
up_adhyatma.54.line: Praised by the good or harassed by the cruel, the free person stays the same.
up_adhyatma.54.misuse: Staying even does not mean staying in a harmful situation.
up_adhyatma.54.claim: One who stays even whether honoured by the good or tormented by the wicked is called liberated while living.
up_adhyatma.54.needs: A mark of a liberated person, not an instruction to stay where one is being harmed.

up_adhyatma.60.speaker: Seer
up_adhyatma.60.line: An arrow already shot does not stop because you changed your mind. Past actions run their course.
up_adhyatma.60.misuse: Facing consequences is not punishment for being bad; it is how actions work.
up_adhyatma.60.claim: Action begun before knowledge is not destroyed by knowledge and yields its fruit, like an arrow already released.
up_adhyatma.60.needs: The prarabdha teaching for a knower. Never as an explanation of someone's illness, loss or mistreatment.

up_aitareya.33.speaker: Seer
up_aitareya.33.line: Caring for your child, you care for yourself. Through them you are born a second time.
up_aitareya.33.claim: A father who cares for his child from birth is caring for his own self and for the continuity of the worlds.

up_aitareya.34.speaker: Seer
up_aitareya.34.line: The child takes up the good work; the parent, duties done and years full, departs and is born again.
up_aitareya.34.claim: The child takes the parent's place for good works; the parent, duties done and old, departs and is born again.
up_aitareya.34.needs: Assumes rebirth. For someone looking back on a parent's full life, not for a parent still ill.

up_brihadaranyak.191.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.191.line: A husband is not dear for the husband's sake, but for the self within. So too wife and children.
up_brihadaranyak.191.misuse: This is not 'love is selfish'; it says we love the one self shining in the other.
up_brihadaranyak.191.claim: A husband, wife or child is dear not for their own sake but for the sake of the self.
up_brihadaranyak.191.needs: Shankara reads this as teaching dispassion toward family so that the self is sought. Easily heard as 'love is selfish'; not for a marriage in conflict or a fresh loss.

up_brihadaranyak.283.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.283.line: Wanting children, wanting money, wanting status: it is one desire. Learn, then live with a child's simplicity.
up_brihadaranyak.283.claim: Desire for sons, wealth and worlds is one desire; the knower, done with learning, should live by the strength of knowing.
up_brihadaranyak.283.needs: The passage is the classic text for renunciation: knowers give up these desires and live on alms.

up_brihadaranyak.323.speaker: Gargi Vachaknavi
up_brihadaranyak.323.line: As a warrior strings her bow with two sharp arrows, Gargi rose before the assembly with two questions.
up_brihadaranyak.323.claim: Gargi rises before Yajnavalkya like a warrior with two arrows in hand, bringing two questions.

up_brihadaranyak.332.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.332.line: Years of effort without knowing what lasts all come to an end. To leave life without knowing it is poverty.
up_brihadaranyak.332.claim: Rites and austerity without knowing the imperishable come to an end; one who dies without knowing it is pitiable.
up_brihadaranyak.332.needs: A hard verdict on a life; only for a seeker who asked the question.

up_brihadaranyak.334.speaker: Gargi Vachaknavi
up_brihadaranyak.334.line: Gargi told the assembly: none of you will beat him; be glad to bow and leave.
up_brihadaranyak.334.claim: Gargi tells the assembly that none of them will defeat Yajnavalkya and they should be glad to leave with a bow.

up_brihadaranyak.387.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.387.line: A felled tree sprouts again from its root. When death fells a person, from what root do they grow?
up_brihadaranyak.387.claim: A felled tree grows again from its root; from what root does a mortal grow again when cut down by death?
up_brihadaranyak.387.needs: A challenge left unanswered by the assembly; the Upanishad itself answers with Brahman as knowledge and bliss. Alone it leaves a griever with nothing.

up_brihadaranyak.473.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.473.line: Like a caterpillar at a grass tip, the self lets go of one body only after grasping the next.
up_brihadaranyak.473.claim: As a caterpillar grasps the next blade before leaving the first, the self at death takes hold of another body.

up_brihadaranyak.474.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.474.line: As a goldsmith reshapes old gold into a newer, lovelier form, so the self takes a new and finer form.
up_brihadaranyak.474.claim: As a goldsmith makes a newer, finer form from gold, the self at death makes for itself a newer form.
up_brihadaranyak.474.needs: Assumes rebirth; the next verse ties the new form to one's deeds, so 'finer' is not promised to all.

up_brihadaranyak.486.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.486.line: Once you know who you really are, what is left to want, and for whose sake would you fret?
up_brihadaranyak.486.claim: One who knows the self as 'I am this' has nothing left to desire and no one for whose sake to suffer.

up_brihadaranyak.501.speaker: Yajnavalkya
up_brihadaranyak.501.line: Calm, self-controlled, quiet within, patient and collected: that is how you come to see clearly.
up_brihadaranyak.501.misuse: Patience here is inner steadiness, not tolerating mistreatment.
up_brihadaranyak.501.claim: The knower's eternal greatness neither grows nor shrinks by action; calm and collected, he sees everything as the self.
up_brihadaranyak.501.needs: 'Not stained by wrong action' describes the knower; it is no licence. Patience here is inner steadiness.

up_brihadaranyak.533.speaker: Seer
up_brihadaranyak.533.line: That is whole, this is whole. Take the whole from the whole, and the whole remains.
up_brihadaranyak.533.claim: That is whole and this is whole; when the whole is taken from the whole, the whole remains.

up_brihadaranyak.62.speaker: Seer
up_brihadaranyak.62.line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?
up_brihadaranyak.62.claim: The first being feared when alone; seeing nothing other than himself, his fear left, for fear comes only from a second.
up_brihadaranyak.62.needs: For free-floating fear and dread. Not an answer to a concrete danger such as a diagnosis.

up_brihadaranyak.63.speaker: Seer (quoting Yajnavalkya)
up_brihadaranyak.63.line: Alone, he found no joy and longed for another. So, said Yajnavalkya, each of us is like a half.
up_brihadaranyak.63.claim: The first being found no delight alone and longed for a second; so each person is like one half.
up_brihadaranyak.63.needs: Shankara reads the longing as desire still at work even in Prajapati, not as an ideal. Keep to the line; the following words on wife and progeny need their context.

up_brihadaranyak.92.speaker: Seer
up_brihadaranyak.92.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
up_brihadaranyak.92.claim: By sheltering and feeding people, animals, birds and even ants, a householder becomes a world for them.

up_chhandogya.10.speaker: Seer
up_chhandogya.10.line: Whatever you do with knowledge, faith and real understanding becomes far more powerful.
up_chhandogya.10.claim: What is done with knowledge, faith and meditation becomes more powerful than the same act done without them.

up_chhandogya.268.speaker: Ghora Angirasa
up_chhandogya.268.line: Self-discipline, giving, honesty, non-harm and truthful speech: these are the real offerings of a life.
up_chhandogya.268.claim: Austerity, giving, straightforwardness, non-harming and truthful speech are the gifts of the sacrifice that is a person's life.

up_chhandogya.306.speaker: Satyakama
up_chhandogya.306.line: Asked his lineage, the boy did not invent one. He repeated his mother's words: 'I am Satyakama Jabala.'
up_chhandogya.306.claim: Asked his lineage, Satyakama repeats his mother's words exactly and gives his name as Satyakama Jabala.

up_chhandogya.326.speaker: Satyakama
up_chhandogya.326.line: Though nature had taught him, he still asked his teacher: knowledge learned from a teacher goes deepest.
up_chhandogya.326.claim: Though taught by others than men, Satyakama asks his teacher, since knowledge learned from a teacher best reaches its goal.

up_chhandogya.368.speaker: Prajapati
up_chhandogya.368.line: The senses argued over who was greatest. The answer: the one whose absence hurts the whole body most.
up_chhandogya.368.claim: The best among the senses is the one whose departure leaves the body worst off.

up_chhandogya.391.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.391.line: The father admitted, 'I don't know one of these answers. If I knew, wouldn't I have taught you?'
up_chhandogya.391.claim: A father admits to his humiliated son that he does not know the answers either, or he would have taught them.

up_chhandogya.393.speaker: Gautama (Uddalaka)
up_chhandogya.393.line: Offered wealth, the father said, 'Keep your riches. Just teach me what you asked my son.'
up_chhandogya.393.claim: Offered wealth by the king, the father declines it and asks only for the teaching.

up_chhandogya.419.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.419.line: Knowing he could not answer everything, the sage sent his visitors to a better teacher.
up_chhandogya.419.claim: Knowing he could not answer everything, Uddalaka chose to direct the scholars to another teacher.

up_chhandogya.423.speaker: The visiting scholars
up_chhandogya.423.line: State plainly the purpose you came for.
up_chhandogya.423.claim: A person should state the very purpose for which he has come.

up_chhandogya.489.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.489.line: A tiny ember, fed with straw, blazes again. Fed well, a depleted mind remembers everything.
up_chhandogya.489.claim: As one ember fed with straw blazes again, a mind reduced by fasting revives when fed, for mind is made of food.

up_chhandogya.503.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.503.line: Rivers flowing east and west all become the sea, and no longer say 'I am this one.'
up_chhandogya.503.claim: Rivers that merge in the sea become the sea and no longer know themselves as this or that river.
up_chhandogya.503.needs: The point continues in 6.10.2: creatures coming from Being do not know it. Not a call to give up one's culture or identity.

up_chhandogya.518.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.518.line: Family gathers at the bedside asking, 'Do you know me?' He knows them, until speech returns into mind.
up_chhandogya.518.claim: A dying man knows his relatives until speech merges in mind, mind in breath, breath in heat and heat in the highest.
up_chhandogya.518.needs: Only for someone looking back on a death already past. Never while a relative is ill.

up_chhandogya.521.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
up_chhandogya.521.line: Covered in truth, the accused held the red-hot axe and was not burned. The liar was.
up_chhandogya.521.misuse: An ancient ordeal used as a picture of how truth protects; not a literal test.
up_chhandogya.521.claim: One who covers himself with truth is not burned by the heated axe; one who covers himself with falsehood is burned.
up_chhandogya.521.needs: An ancient ordeal used as an image for knowing or not knowing Being. Read plainly it implies that whoever suffers was guilty.

up_chhandogya.582.speaker: Sanatkumara
up_chhandogya.582.line: We act only when we find joy in it. Understand the joy, and action follows.
up_chhandogya.582.claim: One acts only on finding happiness in it; no one acts without finding happiness.

up_chhandogya.585.speaker: Sanatkumara
up_chhandogya.585.line: People call cattle, gold, land and houses greatness. I don't. Each of those depends on something else.
up_chhandogya.585.claim: What people call greatness, cattle, gold, land and houses, is not greatness, since each rests on something else.
up_chhandogya.585.needs: The Sanskrit list includes servants and wives among possessions; keep to the line.

up_chhandogya.639.speaker: Virochana
up_chhandogya.639.line: Virochana taught his people: only the body matters; pamper it and you win everything.
up_chhandogya.639.misuse: This is the mistaken teaching in the story; caring for your health is fine.
up_chhandogya.639.claim: Virochana taught the asuras that the body alone is the self to be served, and that this wins both worlds.
up_chhandogya.639.needs: This is the mistaken doctrine in the story. Never standalone.

up_chhandogya.641.speaker: Indra
up_chhandogya.641.line: Indra stopped halfway home: if I am the body, I go blind when it does. There's no good in this.
up_chhandogya.641.claim: If the self is the body, it is blind, lame and destroyed when the body is; Indra sees no good in that.
up_chhandogya.641.needs: The list of blindness and injury is hard on someone ill or disabled.

up_chhandogya.644.speaker: Prajapati
up_chhandogya.644.line: 'You are right,' his teacher said. 'I will explain more. Stay another thirty-two years.' Indra stayed.
up_chhandogya.644.claim: Prajapati confirms Indra's doubt and asks him to stay another thirty-two years to be taught further.

up_chhandogya.655.speaker: Prajapati
up_chhandogya.655.line: As long as you take yourself to be the body, pleasure and pain will keep their grip.
up_chhandogya.655.claim: The mortal body is the dwelling of the deathless, bodiless self, whom pleasure and pain do not touch.

up_chhandogya.663.speaker: Narrator
up_chhandogya.663.line: Keep learning, keep a clean home, raise good children, gather your senses inward, and harm no living being.
up_chhandogya.663.claim: One who studies, lives as a householder, keeps learning, raises virtuous children, steadies the senses and harms no being reaches Brahman's world.

up_isha.15.speaker: Seer
up_isha.15.line: Truth's face is hidden behind a golden lid. Lift it, so I can see what is real.
up_isha.15.claim: The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel; the seer asks the Sun to uncover it.

up_isha.18.speaker: Seer
up_isha.18.line: Lead us by the good path. Keep crooked dealing far from us.
up_isha.18.claim: A prayer to Agni to lead us by the good path and keep crooked wrongdoing away.

up_isha.7.speaker: Seer
up_isha.7.line: When you see the same life in everyone, where is there room for confusion or grief?
up_isha.7.claim: For one who sees all beings as the one self, there is no delusion and no sorrow.
up_isha.7.needs: Describes the knower. Never say it to a griever as 'there is no reason to grieve'.

up_kath.1.1.11.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.1.11.line: Your father will know you again, sleep well at night, his anger gone, when he sees you home.
up_kath.1.1.11.claim: Yama grants that Nachiketa's father will recognise him, lose his anger and sleep in peace.
up_kath.1.1.11.needs: Nachiketa's own choice inside his story. Not a rule that the hurt child must make peace first.

up_kath.1.1.4.speaker: Nachiketa
up_kath.1.1.4.line: A boy asks his father three times, 'To whom will you give me?' The angry answer: 'To Death.'
up_kath.1.1.4.claim: Pressed three times by his son, the father says in anger, 'I give you to Death.'
up_kath.1.1.4.needs: Only inside the Nachiketa story, where the father regrets it at once.

up_kath.1.1.5.speaker: Nachiketa
up_kath.1.1.5.line: Among many I have gone first, among many in the middle. What can Death really do with me today?
up_kath.1.1.5.claim: Nachiketa reflects that he has never been last among sons or pupils and wonders what purpose of Yama he will serve.

up_kath.1.1.6.speaker: Nachiketa
up_kath.1.1.6.line: Look at those before us and those to come: like grain, we ripen, fall and spring up again.
up_kath.1.1.6.claim: Mortals ripen and fall like grain and like grain are born again, as those before and after us show.
up_kath.1.1.6.needs: In the story Nachiketa says this so that his father keeps his word. Assumes rebirth.

up_kath.1.2.22.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.2.22.line: Knowing what stays steady inside all that changes, the wise do not grieve.
up_kath.1.2.22.claim: Knowing the self as bodiless within bodies, steady among the unsteady, great and all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve.

up_kath.1.2.23.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.2.23.line: Not by lectures, intellect or much study is the self reached; it opens to the one it chooses.
up_kath.1.2.23.claim: The self is not reached by teaching, intellect or much learning; it reveals itself to the one it chooses.

up_kath.1.2.24.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.2.24.line: No amount of cleverness helps if you have not stopped wrong habits and calmed your mind.
up_kath.1.2.24.claim: One who has not ceased from wrong conduct and whose mind is not calm and collected cannot reach the self by intelligence.
up_kath.1.2.24.needs: Reads as blame to someone already ashamed of a habit.

up_kath.1.3.5.speaker: Yama
up_kath.1.3.5.line: Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.
up_kath.1.3.5.claim: Without understanding and a steady mind the senses bolt like wild horses; with them the senses obey like good horses.

up_kath.2.1.2.speaker: Yama
up_kath.2.1.2.line: The immature chase outward pleasures into death's wide net. The wise don't seek permanence in passing things.
up_kath.2.1.2.claim: The immature follow outward desires into death's wide net; the wise do not seek the lasting among things that pass.

up_kath.2.2.11.speaker: Yama
up_kath.2.2.11.line: The sun shows every flaw yet stays untouched. Your deepest self stays untouched by the world's sorrow.
up_kath.2.2.11.claim: As the sun is not stained by faults the eyes see, the one inner self is not stained by the world's sorrow.

up_kath.2.2.15.speaker: Yama
up_kath.2.2.15.line: There the sun does not shine, nor moon or stars. By its light alone, everything else shines.
up_kath.2.2.15.claim: Sun, moon, stars, lightning and fire do not light that; everything shines after it and by its light.

up_kath.2.3.15.speaker: Yama
up_kath.2.3.15.line: When the knots of the heart are cut, even here, a mortal becomes deathless. That is the whole teaching.
up_kath.2.3.15.claim: When all the knots of the heart are cut here in this life, the mortal becomes immortal; that is the whole teaching.

up_kaushitaki.131.speaker: Indra
up_kaushitaki.131.line: Don't chase your pleasures and pains. Know the one who feels them.
up_kaushitaki.131.claim: One should not seek to know speech, action or pleasure and pain, but the knower of them.

up_kaushitaki.93.speaker: A dying father and his son
up_kaushitaki.93.line: The dying father says, 'I place my joys and sorrows in you.' The son replies, 'I take them.'
up_kaushitaki.93.claim: A dying father places his faculties, joys and sorrows in his son, and the son receives each.
up_kaushitaki.93.needs: For someone looking back on a parent's death. Never while the parent is ill.

up_maha.104.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.104.line: Trees live, animals and birds live. Truly alive is the one whose mind lives by reflection.
up_maha.104.claim: Trees, animals and birds also live; the one who truly lives is the one whose mind lives by reflection.
up_maha.104.needs: Can sound like a verdict that an unreflective life is worthless.

up_maha.106.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.106.line: Books weigh on the undiscerning, knowledge on the obsessed, the mind on the restless, the body on the self-unaware.
up_maha.106.claim: Scripture burdens the undiscerning, knowledge the passionate, the mind the restless, and the body one who does not know the self.

up_maha.113.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.113.line: Every good quality I take up, craving gnaws through, like a mouse chewing a string.
up_maha.113.claim: Whatever good quality I take up, craving cuts through it, as a mouse gnaws through a string.

up_maha.114.speaker: Nidagha
up_maha.114.line: Craving is a restless monkey: never in one place, never satisfied, reaching even where it cannot go.
up_maha.114.claim: Craving is a restless monkey: it reaches where it cannot go, strives even when satisfied, and never stays in one place.

up_maha.165.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.165.line: Good people do not wilt in hard times, like a golden lotus that stays open at night.
up_maha.165.claim: The good do not wilt in adversity, want nothing beyond what is at hand and delight in the path of the good.
up_maha.165.needs: Praise of the steady can read as a reproach to someone who has wilted. Use as an aspiration.

up_maha.179.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.179.line: Everyone, gentle or fierce, comes to trust a calm person, the way we trust a mother.
up_maha.179.claim: All beings, harsh and gentle alike, come to trust a calm person as they would a mother.

up_maha.185.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.185.line: Contentment: not pining for what hasn't come, enjoying what has, staying even either way.
up_maha.185.claim: The content person does not long for what has not come, enjoys what has come and stays even in gain and loss.
up_maha.185.needs: Not an answer to being passed over unfairly.

up_maha.221.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.221.line: Two words bind or free you: 'mine' and 'not mine.' With 'mine,' we are bound.
up_maha.221.misuse: Not a call to stop caring for family; it is about clinging.
up_maha.221.claim: 'I am Brahman' frees; the word 'mine' binds a creature and 'not mine' releases it.
up_maha.221.needs: About clinging, not about ceasing to care for one's family.

up_maha.260.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.260.line: Not clinging is freedom. Clinging is sorrow.
up_maha.260.misuse: Not clinging is not the same as not caring.
up_maha.260.claim: Non-clinging alone is freedom; clinging is sorrow.
up_maha.260.needs: Not clinging is not the same as not caring. Not for bereavement or for someone wronged.

up_maha.369.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.369.line: Brave, learned, well born or great, anyone can be chained by craving, like a lion on a chain.
up_maha.369.claim: However brave, learned, well born or great, a person is bound by craving as a lion by a chain.

up_maha.40.speaker: Narrator
up_maha.40.line: Ignored for days, then pampered with luxury, Shuka stayed the same, steady as a mountain in a breeze.
up_maha.40.claim: Neither neglect nor luxury moved Shuka's mind; he stayed even, clear, silent and glad, like the full moon.

up_maha.453.speaker: Ribhu
up_maha.453.line: Not pining for pleasures still to come, and enjoying the ones already here: that is wisdom.
up_maha.453.claim: The mark of the wise is not longing for pleasures yet to come and enjoying those that have come.

up_maitrayani.13.speaker: King Brihadratha
up_maitrayani.13.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.
up_maitrayani.13.claim: A king asks what use enjoyments are and begs to be lifted out like a frog from a dark well.

up_maitrayani.8.speaker: King Brihadratha
up_maitrayani.8.line: Everything perishes, like gnats and mosquitoes, like grass that springs up and withers.
up_maitrayani.8.claim: Everything here is seen to perish, like gnats, mosquitoes, grass and trees that arise and are destroyed.
up_maitrayani.8.needs: Only as the opening of Brihadratha's story, followed by the sage's answer.

up_maitreya.25.speaker: Mahadeva (Shiva)
up_maitreya.25.line: True knowledge is seeing no difference. Meditation is a mind at rest. Real bathing is washing the mind.
up_maitreya.25.claim: Seeing non-difference is knowledge, an objectless mind is meditation, shedding the mind's dirt is bathing, and sense-restraint is purity.

up_mundaka.1.1.3.speaker: Shaunaka
up_mundaka.1.1.3.line: Shaunaka asked: what is the one thing which, once known, makes everything else make sense?
up_mundaka.1.1.3.claim: Shaunaka asks what it is that, once known, makes all this known.

up_mundaka.1.2.8.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.1.2.8.line: Wise in their own eyes, the deluded go round in circles, like the blind led by the blind.
up_mundaka.1.2.8.claim: Those who live in ignorance yet think themselves wise go round and round, like the blind led by the blind.
up_mundaka.1.2.8.needs: Aimed at those satisfied with ritual and status. As a line to a struggling reader it is an insult.

up_mundaka.2.2.4.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.2.2.4.line: Focus like an archer: steady, undistracted, until you and your target become one.
up_mundaka.2.2.4.claim: Om is the bow, the self the arrow and Brahman the target; hit it undistracted and become one with it.

up_mundaka.2.2.8.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.2.2.8.line: When you see the highest, the heart's knot loosens, every doubt is cut, old deeds lose their grip.
up_mundaka.2.2.8.claim: When the highest is seen, the knot of the heart is cut, all doubts end and one's deeds wear away.

up_mundaka.3.1.2.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.1.2.line: The bird that eats grieves, lost in its helplessness. When it sees the calm one beside it, grief falls away.
up_mundaka.3.1.2.claim: On the same tree the person sits sunk, grieving in helplessness; seeing the other, the Lord, he becomes free of sorrow.

up_mundaka.3.1.4.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.1.4.line: Knowing this, the wise stop arguing. Their joy is within, and they stay fully active.
up_mundaka.3.1.4.claim: The knower of the one life in all beings does not out-talk others; delighting in the self, he stays active.

up_mundaka.3.2.2.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.2.2.line: Chase desires and they keep giving birth to more. Be whole within, and they dissolve here and now.
up_mundaka.3.2.2.claim: One who dwells on desires is born wherever they lead; for one fulfilled in the self all desires dissolve here.

up_mundaka.3.2.4.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.2.4.line: This is not won by the weak or the careless. Whoever strives wisely gets there.
up_mundaka.3.2.4.claim: The self is not won by the weak, the careless or by aimless austerity, but by the wise who strive.
up_mundaka.3.2.4.needs: 'Not for the weak' wounds someone who feels weak.

up_mundaka.3.2.8.speaker: Angiras
up_mundaka.3.2.8.line: As rivers lose their names in the sea, so the wise, freed of name and form, merge in the highest.
up_mundaka.3.2.8.claim: As rivers enter the sea and give up name and form, the knower, freed from name and form, reaches the supreme Person.
up_mundaka.3.2.8.needs: Speaks of the knower's liberation, not of an ordinary death. Do not offer it as a statement about someone who has died or is ill.

up_niralamb.21.speaker: Teacher
up_niralamb.21.line: Heaven is good company. Hell is keeping company with what is hollow and the people lost in it.
up_niralamb.21.claim: Heaven is the company of the good; hell is keeping company with the unreal and with people absorbed in it.

up_prashn.19.speaker: Pippalada
up_prashn.19.line: The pure world belongs to those with no crookedness, no lying and no trickery in them.
up_prashn.19.claim: The stainless world of Brahman belongs to those in whom there is no crookedness, falsehood or deceit.

up_prashn.23.speaker: Pippalada
up_prashn.23.line: When the life-breath rose to leave, all the senses had to follow, like bees after their queen.
up_prashn.23.claim: When the life-breath rose to leave, all the senses had to rise with it, like bees following their queen.

up_prashn.3.speaker: Pippalada
up_prashn.3.line: Stay a year in discipline and faith, then ask. If I know, I will tell you everything.
up_prashn.3.claim: The sage asks the seekers to live one more year in discipline and faith and then ask their questions.

up_shwetashwetar.1.1.speaker: Seekers of Brahman
up_shwetashwetar.1.1.line: Where did we come from? What keeps us alive? Where do we go? Who governs our joys and sorrows?
up_shwetashwetar.1.1.claim: Seekers ask whence we are born, by what we live, where we rest and who governs our joy and sorrow.

up_shwetashwetar.1.15.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.1.15.line: Like oil in sesame or butter in curd, what you seek is already within. Sincere effort brings it out.
up_shwetashwetar.1.15.claim: As oil is in sesame and butter in curd, the self is found within by one who seeks with truth and discipline.

up_taittiriya.103.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.103.line: It is the very flavour of life. Whoever tastes it is filled with joy.
up_taittiriya.103.claim: That self-made reality is the very essence; on gaining that essence a person becomes joyful.

up_taittiriya.124.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.124.line: Where words and thoughts turn back unable to reach: whoever knows that joy fears nothing.
up_taittiriya.124.claim: One who knows the bliss of Brahman, from which words and mind turn back, fears nothing at all.

up_taittiriya.127.speaker: Varuna
up_taittiriya.127.line: Bhrigu asked his father to teach him. 'Seek that from which all is born and to which all returns.'
up_taittiriya.127.claim: Varuna tells Bhrigu to seek that from which beings are born, by which they live and into which they return.

up_taittiriya.132.speaker: Varuna
up_taittiriya.132.line: His father did not hand him answers: 'Seek it through disciplined reflection. That effort is the way.'
up_taittiriya.132.claim: Brahman is to be sought through tapas, concentrated reflection, which is itself Brahman.

up_taittiriya.149.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.149.line: Never speak ill of food. Treat that as a vow.
up_taittiriya.149.claim: One should not speak ill of food; that is a vow.

up_taittiriya.158.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.158.line: Turn no one away from your door. Make that a vow, and keep enough to share.
up_taittiriya.158.claim: One should turn no one away from one's dwelling; that is a vow, so one should gather plenty of food.
up_taittiriya.158.needs: Hospitality, not a duty to house someone who mistreats you.

up_taittiriya.43.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.43.line: Do what is right, speak truth, keep discipline, and never stop learning and teaching.
up_taittiriya.43.claim: Right conduct, truth, austerity and self-control are each to be practised together with study and teaching.

up_taittiriya.50.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.50.line: Do not drift from truth or duty. Do not neglect your wellbeing, your prosperity, or your learning.
up_taittiriya.50.claim: Do not be careless about truth, dharma, your welfare, your prosperity, or study and teaching.
up_taittiriya.50.needs: The verse also says not to cut the family line; the line rightly leaves that out for general use.

up_taittiriya.53.speaker: Teacher
up_taittiriya.53.line: Do only what is blameless. Follow what is good in us, your teachers, and not the rest.
up_taittiriya.53.claim: Only blameless actions are to be done; of the teachers' conduct, only the good is to be followed.

ashtavakra.1.11.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.11.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
ashtavakra.1.11.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.
ashtavakra.1.11.claim: Whoever holds 'I am free' is free and whoever holds 'I am bound' stays bound; one's understanding decides one's end.
ashtavakra.1.11.needs: the reader must take 'free' and 'bound' as statements about the self, not about outer circumstances

ashtavakra.1.17.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.17.line: Be free of expectations, steady, self-reliant and cool at heart: deep, and impossible to rattle.
ashtavakra.1.17.claim: Be free of expectation, unchanging, self-reliant, cool at heart, deep and unshaken, resting in pure awareness alone.
ashtavakra.1.17.needs: accepts awareness as what one is

ashtavakra.1.2.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.2.line: Treat craving like poison. Drink forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.
ashtavakra.1.2.misuse: Forgiveness here is a quality you grow, not a duty to excuse ongoing harm.
ashtavakra.1.2.claim: If you want freedom, shun sense objects like poison and take forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.
ashtavakra.1.2.needs: the reader wants freedom; the verse is the first instruction to one who has asked

ashtavakra.1.4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.4.line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
ashtavakra.1.4.claim: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, you will be happy, at peace and free this very moment.
ashtavakra.1.4.needs: accepts that one is awareness, distinct from the body

ashtavakra.1.8.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.8.line: 'Everything depends on me' is a snakebite. The antidote is trusting you are not the only doer.
ashtavakra.1.8.misuse: Not being the only doer does not mean you are not responsible for what you do.
ashtavakra.1.8.claim: 'I am the doer' is the bite of ego's black snake; drink the nectar of trust that you are not the doer, and be happy.
ashtavakra.1.8.needs: accepts the Advaita claim that the self does not act

ashtavakra.10.3.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.10.3.line: Wherever craving lives, the treadmill runs. Let go of the craving, and be happy.
ashtavakra.10.3.claim: Wherever craving is, the round of becoming is there; take up mature dispassion, be free of craving and be happy.

ashtavakra.10.7.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.10.7.line: Money, pleasure, even good deeds: none of them ever gave this mind rest.
ashtavakra.10.7.misuse: Not against good deeds; it says they cannot be the source of inner rest.
ashtavakra.10.7.claim: Enough of wealth, desire and even good deeds; in the wilderness of the world the mind never found rest in them.

ashtavakra.11.5.speaker: Ashtavakra
