ashtavakra.11.5.line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
ashtavakra.11.5.misuse: Real problems still need attention; this is about the extra pain rumination adds.
ashtavakra.11.5.claim: One certain that suffering here comes from worry alone, and nothing else, is free of it, happy and at peace.
ashtavakra.11.5.needs: the reader's trouble is mostly rumination, not a present danger or loss

ashtavakra.15.11.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.11.line: Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.
ashtavakra.15.11.claim: You are the boundless ocean; let the waves of the world rise or fall, you neither grow nor shrink.
ashtavakra.15.11.needs: accepts the self as awareness in which the world appears

ashtavakra.15.19.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.19.line: Don't churn your mind with plans and second thoughts. Be still and rest in yourself.
ashtavakra.15.19.misuse: Not a reason to avoid decisions; decide, then stop churning.
ashtavakra.15.19.claim: Do not stir the mind with yes and no; grow still and rest happily in your own self, whose form is joy.

ashtavakra.15.2.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.2.line: Freedom is losing your taste for what hooks you; bondage is savouring it. That's all you need to know.
ashtavakra.15.2.misuse: 'Do as you wish' assumes the craving is gone; it is not a licence.
ashtavakra.15.2.claim: Liberation is losing the taste for sense objects and bondage is relishing them; that is all there is to know.

ashtavakra.15.4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.4.line: You are not your body or your achievements. You are the awareness watching it all. Live lightly.
ashtavakra.15.4.claim: You are not the body, nor is it yours; not the doer or enjoyer but awareness, the ever-present witness. Live happily.

ashtavakra.15.5.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.5.line: Liking and disliking belong to the mind. You are not your mind.
ashtavakra.15.5.claim: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and you are never the mind; you are awareness, changeless. Live happily.

ashtavakra.15.9.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.9.line: The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
ashtavakra.15.9.misuse: Grief is natural; this offers perspective, not a rule against mourning.
ashtavakra.15.9.claim: The body made of the gunas comes, stays and goes; the self neither comes nor goes, so why grieve for it?
ashtavakra.15.9.needs: the reader must already hold the self as deathless; a fresh griever hears 'stop grieving'

ashtavakra.16.3.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.16.3.line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
ashtavakra.16.3.misuse: Not against effort; against the anxious straining that rides on it.
ashtavakra.16.3.claim: Everyone is miserable from straining, yet no one sees it; by this one teaching the fortunate find peace.

ashtavakra.16.9.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.16.9.line: Running away won't free you from pain. Free of clinging, you can be at peace right where you are.
ashtavakra.16.9.misuse: Not advice to stay somewhere harmful; it says escape alone won't fix inner restlessness.
ashtavakra.16.9.claim: The attached one wants to leave the world to escape pain; the unattached has no pain and is untroubled even in it.
ashtavakra.16.9.needs: the reader is not in a harmful situation; for someone being harmed leaving is right

ashtavakra.17.4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.17.4.line: Rare is the person who doesn't replay old pleasures or pine for new ones.
ashtavakra.17.4.claim: Rare is one who does not dwell on pleasures enjoyed or long for those not yet had.

ashtavakra.18.100.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.100.line: A calm mind doesn't need the crowd or the forest. It is the same wherever it is.
ashtavakra.18.100.claim: The calm mind runs neither to crowds nor to the forest; whatever and wherever, it stays the same.

ashtavakra.18.2.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.2.line: You can earn everything and enjoy everything, and still not be happy until you let go.
ashtavakra.18.2.claim: One may gain all wealth and abundant pleasure, yet without giving up everything no one is happy.

ashtavakra.18.3.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.3.line: When 'I still have to do this' burns you up inside, only a rain of calm brings relief.
ashtavakra.18.3.claim: For a heart scorched by the blazing sun of things one must do, where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?

ashtavakra.18.39.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.39.line: Chasing calm keeps it away. Seeing clearly, the wise are calm without trying.
ashtavakra.18.39.claim: The deluded never find peace because they are trying to get it; the wise, sure of the truth, are always calm.

ashtavakra.18.58.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.58.line: A restless mind is agitated even doing nothing; a skilled one stays calm doing everything.
ashtavakra.18.58.claim: The confused are agitated even doing nothing; the skilful stay calm even while doing all that must be done.

ashtavakra.18.59.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.59.line: Sit, sleep, come, go, talk and eat at ease. Calm can live inside ordinary days.
ashtavakra.18.59.claim: The calm-minded sit, sleep, come, go, speak and eat at ease, even in the business of daily life.

ashtavakra.18.81.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.81.line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
ashtavakra.18.81.claim: The steady one neither prays for gain nor grieves loss; his cool mind is filled as if with nectar.

ashtavakra.18.99.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.99.line: Praise doesn't inflate you, blame doesn't enrage you, death doesn't frighten you. That is freedom.
ashtavakra.18.99.claim: Praised, he is not pleased; blamed, not angry; he neither dreads death nor delights in living.

ashtavakra.3.10.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.3.10.line: Watch yourself as you'd watch anyone else, and praise or blame stops shaking you.
ashtavakra.3.10.claim: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's cannot be shaken by praise or blame.

ashtavakra.3.3.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.3.3.line: You are the ocean these waves rise in. Why run around like a beggar for more?
ashtavakra.3.3.claim: Knowing 'I am That in which the world rises like waves', why do you run about like a beggar?
ashtavakra.3.3.needs: the reader claims self-knowledge; Ashtavakra is testing Janaka

ashtavakra.8.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.8.1.line: Bondage is a mind that wants, grieves, grabs and rages. Freedom is a mind that stops.
ashtavakra.8.1.misuse: Not a call to stop feeling; it is about not being dragged by every feeling.
ashtavakra.8.1.claim: Bondage is the mind wanting, grieving, grabbing, dropping, delighting or raging; freedom is the mind doing none of these.

ashtavakra.9.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.9.1.line: Done and not done: has that list ever ended for anyone? Knowing this, ease your grip.
ashtavakra.9.1.misuse: Not permission to drop responsibilities; it is about the to-do list ruling your peace.
ashtavakra.9.1.claim: The pairs of done and not-done have never come to rest for anyone; knowing this, through weariness, turn to renunciation.

ashtavakra.9.4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.9.4.line: No age of life comes without ups and downs. Accept what comes and keep going.
ashtavakra.9.4.misuse: Accepting life's swings is not accepting mistreatment.
ashtavakra.9.4.claim: No time or age of life is free of opposites; let them be, live with what comes, and you reach fulfilment.

avadhuta.1.68.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.1.68.line: Friend mind, why all this chatter? It's all speculation. You are vast as the sky.
avadhuta.1.68.claim: Friend mind, why so much chatter; it is all speculation. The essence is this: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.

avadhuta.2.1.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.2.1.line: Take wisdom from anyone. Nobody throws away a jewel just because it fell in the mud.
avadhuta.2.1.misuse: Valuing the lesson doesn't mean excusing the messenger's harmful behaviour.
avadhuta.2.1.claim: Do not weigh whether a teacher is young, worldly, unlearned, a servant or a householder; no one throws away a jewel fallen in dirt.

avadhuta.2.2.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.2.2.line: An unpainted boat still carries you across. Look for substance, not polish.
avadhuta.2.2.claim: Look not for poetic merit but take the essence; an unpainted boat still carries across those who wish to cross.
avadhuta.2.2.needs: the verse is about reading this text; applying it to one's own worth is an extension

avadhuta.8.3.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.8.3.line: Seek no honour for yourself, give it freely to others; stay alert, deep, friendly and kind.
avadhuta.8.3.claim: The free sage is alert, deep, steadfast, master of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; humble, honouring others, friendly, kind, wise.

avadhuta.8.7.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.8.7.line: Let go of old cravings, speak only what heals, and live in the present.
avadhuta.8.7.claim: The syllable va marks one who has left old cravings, whose speech is wholesome, and who lives in the present.

hans_gita.21.ref: Hamsa Gita 21 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.21 in our data)
hans_gita.21.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.21.line: Like the moon slipping out of clouds, the steady one waits for the right time and succeeds.
hans_gita.21.misuse: Waiting for the right time is active patience, not giving up.
hans_gita.21.claim: Freed from wrongs like the moon from clouds, spotless, awaiting his time, the steady one succeeds through fortitude.

hans_gita.26.ref: Hamsa Gita 26 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.26 in our data)
hans_gita.26.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.26.line: Insulted, you can still sleep in peace. The one who insults carries the damage.
hans_gita.26.misuse: Not a call to welcome mistreatment; it is about not letting it poison you.
hans_gita.26.claim: The wise should take insult as contentedly as nectar; the insulted sleeps in peace while the one who insults is ruined.
hans_gita.26.needs: the reader is past the first hurt and wants to stop carrying it; never as the first word to someone being mistreated

hans_gita.40.ref: Hamsa Gita 40 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.40 in our data)
hans_gita.40.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.40.line: Envy dims our light; greed is how friends are lost.
hans_gita.40.claim: The world is covered by ignorance, envy keeps it from shining, greed makes people abandon friends, attachment keeps them from heaven.

ashtavakra.1.16.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.16.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
ashtavakra.1.16.claim: The universe is pervaded by you and strung on you; by nature you are pure awareness, so do not fall into smallness of mind.
ashtavakra.1.16.needs: accepts the self as pervading consciousness

ashtavakra.1.5.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.1.5.line: You are not your caste, your stage of life, or what others can see. You are the witness. Be happy.
ashtavakra.1.5.claim: You belong to no caste or stage of life and are not an object of the senses; unattached, formless witness of all, be happy.

ashtavakra.10.8.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.10.8.line: You have toiled so long with body, mind and speech. Now, at last, stop.
ashtavakra.10.8.claim: Through how many lives have you done painful, wearying work with body, mind and speech; now at least, let it cease.
ashtavakra.10.8.needs: the reader understands cessation as ceasing the doer-sense, not quitting duties

ashtavakra.11.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.11.1.line: Things arise, change and end by their own nature. Seeing that, you can be at peace.
ashtavakra.11.1.claim: One certain that arising, change and ceasing happen by nature stays unchanged, free of pain, and easily finds peace.

ashtavakra.11.3.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.11.3.line: Good times and hard times arrive on their own schedule. Knowing that, you can stop longing and grieving.
ashtavakra.11.3.misuse: Not a reason to stop trying; it loosens anxiety over what you can't control.
ashtavakra.11.3.claim: One certain that misfortune and fortune come in their time by destiny is content, senses at rest, neither longing nor grieving.

ashtavakra.13.1.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra.13.1.line: Even monks rarely find the ease of wanting nothing. I stopped grabbing and stopped renouncing, and live happily.
ashtavakra.13.1.claim: The ease of owning nothing is rare even in a loincloth; so I have dropped both renouncing and acquiring and live at ease.

ashtavakra.13.3.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra.13.3.line: Do what comes to you to do, then let it go and live at ease.
ashtavakra.13.3.claim: Seeing truly that nothing is ever really done by me, I do whatever comes to be done and live at ease.

ashtavakra.15.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.1.line: A clear mind gets it from one plain teaching; a muddled one searches all its life.
ashtavakra.15.1.claim: A clear-minded person is fulfilled by a simple teaching; another stays confused after a lifetime of inquiry.

ashtavakra.15.10.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.10.line: Whether the body lasts a hundred years or ends today, what you are neither gains nor loses.
ashtavakra.15.10.claim: Let the body last till the end of the age or go today; what gain or loss is that to you, pure awareness?
ashtavakra.15.10.needs: only for a seeker contemplating his own mortality; harmful to someone afraid for a sick parent or child

ashtavakra.15.8.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.15.8.line: Have faith, my child, have faith. You are more than everything that happens to you.
ashtavakra.15.8.claim: Have faith, my son, have faith and do not be confused: you are knowledge itself, the Lord, the Self beyond nature.

ashtavakra.16.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.16.1.line: Read and recite all the scriptures you like; peace comes when you set them all down.
ashtavakra.16.1.misuse: Not anti-learning; it warns against mistaking information for peace.
ashtavakra.16.1.claim: You may recite or hear many scriptures again and again, yet you will not be at ease until you forget them all.
ashtavakra.16.1.needs: the reader is a seeker who reads a lot; it says nothing against learning for a student

ashtavakra.16.10.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.16.10.line: Pride in being spiritual is still pride. It only adds to your suffering.
ashtavakra.16.10.claim: One who is proud even of being liberated and possessive of the body is neither wise nor a yogi, only a sufferer.

ashtavakra.16.2.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.16.2.line: Enjoy, work or meditate all you like: your heart still longs for the place where wanting stops.
ashtavakra.16.2.claim: Enjoy, work or meditate as you will; your mind will still long most for the state where every want has dropped.

ashtavakra.17.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.17.1.line: Content, clear-minded and happy in your own company: that is the fruit of all practice.
ashtavakra.17.1.claim: One who is content, senses clear, and always happy alone has gained the fruit of knowledge and of yoga.

ashtavakra.17.7.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.17.7.line: Not wishing life away, not resenting it, the blessed one lives happily on whatever comes.
ashtavakra.17.7.claim: He neither longs for the world to end nor resents its going on; so the blessed one lives happily on whatever livelihood comes.

ashtavakra.18.11.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.11.line: Throne or begging bowl, gain or loss, crowd or solitude: a steady person stays the same.
ashtavakra.18.11.claim: For the steady yogi there is no difference between kingship and begging, gain and loss, the crowd and the forest.

ashtavakra.18.20.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.20.line: Don't cling to doing or to not doing. Do what's in front of you and stay at ease.
ashtavakra.18.20.claim: The steady one clings neither to doing nor to not doing; doing whatever comes to be done, he stays at ease.

ashtavakra.18.55.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.55.line: Even when family laughs at you or scolds you, you can stay unshaken inside.
ashtavakra.18.55.misuse: Staying calm inside is not putting up with abuse; you can still set boundaries.
ashtavakra.18.55.claim: Laughed at and scolded by servants, children, spouses, grandchildren and kin, the yogi is not disturbed in the least.
ashtavakra.18.55.needs: never as advice to someone being mistreated at home

ashtavakra.18.61.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.61.line: A restless mind turns even rest into busyness. A still mind finds rest even in work.
ashtavakra.18.61.claim: Even the deluded one's withdrawal turns into activity, while even the wise one's activity bears the fruit of stillness.

ashtavakra.18.91.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.91.line: Beggar or king: whoever is free of craving shines.
ashtavakra.18.91.claim: Beggar or king, whoever is free of desire shines, the one for whom things no longer look good or bad.

ashtavakra.18.98.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.18.98.line: Free of craving, you stop replaying what you did and didn't do.
ashtavakra.18.98.misuse: Not a way to dodge accountability; make amends, then stop replaying.
ashtavakra.18.98.claim: The free one is at ease in any state, done with duty, even everywhere, and without craving does not recall what he did or left undone.
ashtavakra.18.98.needs: the reader has already faced and repaired what they did; it does not excuse wrongdoing

ashtavakra.2.14.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra.2.14.line: Wonder of wonders: I own nothing, and yet everything is mine.
ashtavakra.2.14.claim: Wonderful am I, I bow to myself: I own nothing at all, or else all that speech and mind can reach is mine.
ashtavakra.2.14.needs: the wonder is at the self, not the ego; may read as self-praise without that

ashtavakra.3.1.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.3.1.line: If you know what in you can't be lost, why still chase more money?
ashtavakra.3.1.misuse: Not a case against earning a living; it questions compulsive accumulation.
ashtavakra.3.1.claim: Knowing the self as one and indestructible, how can you, wise and steady, still delight in piling up wealth?
ashtavakra.3.1.needs: the listener claims self-knowledge; Ashtavakra is testing Janaka

ashtavakra.3.11.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.3.11.line: When the world's show stops dazzling you, even death close by loses its terror.
ashtavakra.3.11.claim: Seeing this world as mere illusion and losing all fascination with it, how could a steady mind fear even death close at hand?
ashtavakra.3.11.needs: only for a seeker who already holds the world to be maya

ashtavakra.3.12.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.3.12.line: Even when every hope collapses, a mind that wants nothing stays whole.
ashtavakra.3.12.claim: None can compare with the great soul whose mind wants nothing even when hope is gone, content in knowing the self.
ashtavakra.3.12.needs: a portrait of attainment, not a verdict on someone whose plans just failed

ashtavakra.3.14.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.3.14.line: Wanting nothing, you can take what comes your way without being thrilled or hurt.
ashtavakra.3.14.claim: For one with inner stains dropped, beyond opposites and wishes, pleasure that comes by chance brings neither pain nor elation.

ashtavakra.5.4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.5.4.line: Be the same in pain and pleasure, hope and despair. That evenness is freedom.
ashtavakra.5.4.claim: Same in pain and pleasure, full, even in hope and despair, even in life and death: in this way, dissolve now.
ashtavakra.5.4.needs: a seeker practising the dissolution of the separate self

ashtavakra.8.4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.8.4.line: Where 'I' and 'mine' take over, you are bound. Hold things lightly; grab nothing, push nothing away.
ashtavakra.8.4.claim: When there is no 'I' there is freedom, and when there is 'I' there is bondage; knowing this, lightly grasp nothing and reject nothing.

ashtavakra.9.5.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra.9.5.line: Even the great sages disagree. Seeing that, who would keep fighting over opinions?
ashtavakra.9.5.claim: Seeing how the great sages, saints and yogis all hold different views, who would not grow weary of it and become calm?
ashtavakra.9.5.needs: the reader is tired of conflicting teachings; it does not say all views are false

avadhuta.1.18.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.1.18.line: Mind, why are you running around like a lost ghost? Drop the clinging and be happy.
avadhuta.1.18.claim: Mind, why do you run about confused like a ghost? See the self as undivided, drop attachment, and be happy.

avadhuta.2.24.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.2.24.line: Drop the likes and grudges, work for everyone's good, stay steady: that is the highest path.
avadhuta.2.24.claim: Free of attachment and aversion, devoted to the good of all beings, firm in understanding and steady, one reaches the highest state.

avadhuta.2.7.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.2.7.line: Thoughts rise and burst like bubbles in water. You don't have to chase them.
avadhuta.2.7.claim: Thoughts rise and dissolve like bubbles in water; what is there for me to do about them?

avadhuta.3.34.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.3.34.line: Why weep, friend? What you truly are does not age, die or change.
avadhuta.3.34.misuse: Tears are allowed; this offers comfort, not a ban on grief.
avadhuta.3.34.claim: Why weep, friend? You have no old age, death or birth-sorrow, and no change; I am the nectar of knowledge, sky-like.
avadhuta.3.34.needs: only for a seeker for whom the deathless self is already the frame; to a griever it reads as 'stop crying'

avadhuta.7.9.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.7.9.line: Not chasing pleasure, not refusing it, he walks slowly, slowly, in natural joy.
avadhuta.7.9.claim: Free of union and separation, of enjoying and refusing, the free one walks slowly, slowly, in his natural joy.

avadhuta.8.2.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.8.2.line: Gentle, self-restrained, content with little, moderate in food, calm and steady: that is quiet strength.
avadhuta.8.2.claim: The sage is unshaken by desires, restrained, gentle, pure, owning and seeking nothing, moderate, calm, steady, and has taken refuge in Me.

avadhuta.8.4.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.8.4.line: Kind, harming no one, patient with everyone, truthful to the core, and helpful to all.
avadhuta.8.4.misuse: Patience with others includes protecting yourself from harm.
avadhuta.8.4.claim: The sage is compassionate, harms no one, bears with all beings, is true to the core, blameless, even and helpful to all.

avadhuta.8.6.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.8.6.line: Free of the noose of expectation, he lives in joy from start to finish.
avadhuta.8.6.claim: The syllable a marks one freed from the noose of expectation, pure from beginning to end, always abiding in joy.

hans_gita.10.ref: Hamsa Gita 10 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.10 in our data)
hans_gita.10.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.10.line: When someone shoots harsh words at you, stay calm. The calm one walks away the richer.
hans_gita.10.misuse: Calm is not silence about abuse; you can stay calm and still set limits.
hans_gita.10.claim: If another wounds him hard with arrows of harsh words he should stay calm; one cheerful under provocation takes the provoker's merit.
hans_gita.10.needs: the reader wants to master their own reaction; not a counsel to tolerate ongoing abuse

hans_gita.11.ref: Hamsa Gita 11 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.11 in our data)
hans_gita.11.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.11.line: Hold back the anger that flares at an insult; stay clean-hearted and cheerful.
hans_gita.11.misuse: Holding back anger is not swallowing mistreatment; it is choosing how to respond.
hans_gita.11.claim: One who restrains the blazing anger an insult stirs, staying clean-hearted, cheerful and free of envy, takes the merit of others.

hans_gita.17.ref: Hamsa Gita 17 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.17 in our data)
hans_gita.17.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.17.line: Hurt by someone, you need not hit back or wish them harm. That steadiness is rare.
hans_gita.17.misuse: Not wishing harm is not the same as staying where you are hurt.
hans_gita.17.claim: One who, spoken to harshly, answers neither harshly nor sweetly, and struck, does not strike back or wish harm: the gods long for him.
hans_gita.17.needs: never as counsel to someone being hit or harmed; a portrait of the forbearing sage

hans_gita.25.ref: Hamsa Gita 25 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.25 in our data)
hans_gita.25.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.25.line: Don't answer insults with insults. It inflames them and harms you.
hans_gita.25.claim: The wise should not answer the ignorant with abuse and insult, for that inflames the other and harms oneself.

hans_gita.31.ref: Hamsa Gita 31 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.31 in our data)
hans_gita.31.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.31.line: Truth is the ladder up and the boat across.
hans_gita.31.claim: Going among humans and gods I tell them all: truth is the ladder to heaven, as a boat is the way across the sea.

hans_gita.42.ref: Hamsa Gita 42 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.42 in our data)
hans_gita.42.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.42.line: The wise can be happy, quiet in a crowd, strong though weak, and stay out of quarrels.
hans_gita.42.claim: Among the learned only the wise one is truly happy, stays quiet among many, is strong though weak, and joins no quarrel.

hans_gita.7.ref: Hamsa Gita 7 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.7 in our data)
hans_gita.7.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
hans_gita.7.line: Untie the knots in your heart, and bring your likes and dislikes under your own control.
hans_gita.7.claim: Seekers of immortality, this is the work: austerity, restraint, truth, guarding the self, untying the heart's knots, mastering likes and dislikes.

ram_gita.24.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.24.line: With faith, a good teacher and a clear mind, you can become as unshakable as a mountain.
ram_gita.24.claim: Through faith, the teacher's grace and the words 'You are That', a pure mind knows the self and individual as one and stands firm as Meru.

ram_gita.34.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.34.line: Take the sweetness and set down the shell, like drinking coconut water and letting the coconut go.
ram_gita.34.claim: Having negated everything with 'not this' and tasted awareness in the heart, give up the whole world, as one drinks the water and drops the coconut.
ram_gita.34.needs: a renunciate seeker; it is about the world after neti neti, not about a life stage

ram_gita.35.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.35.line: What you truly are is never born, never dies, never shrinks and never grows.
ram_gita.35.claim: The self is never born and never dies, neither wanes nor grows; ancient, incomparable, blissful, self-luminous, all-pervading, one without a second.

ram_gita.37.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.37.line: Confusion sees one thing as another, a rope as a snake. Look again.
ram_gita.37.claim: Superimposition is taking one thing for another through error, like a snake seen in a rope; so the world is seen in the Lord.
ram_gita.37.needs: the reader is a seeker studying Vedanta; for an anxious reader with a real threat it says the threat is imagined

ram_gita.39.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.39.line: Wanting belongs to the mind. In deep sleep it stops, and we are simply at ease.
ram_gita.39.claim: Desire, attachment and pleasure belong to the mind and cause bondage; in deep sleep they are absent and the self is felt as happiness.

ram_gita.46.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.46.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
ram_gita.46.claim: Sitting in a quiet place, senses withdrawn, self-mastered and pure within, contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the self.

ram_gita.52.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.52.line: Content in an inner joy, he becomes like an ocean of still water.
ram_gita.52.claim: Ever absorbed in the supreme self, content in his own joy and forgetting all else, the free one rests like an ocean of still water.

ram_gita.58.speaker: Rama
ram_gita.58.line: Until you see the divine everywhere, keep praying with faith; it will live in your heart day and night.
ram_gita.58.claim: Until one sees everything as Me, one should be intent on worshipping Me; to one of faith and strong devotion I am visible in the heart always.

surya_gita.3.36.speaker: Surya
surya_gita.3.36.line: When you've tasted enough pleasure and pain to tire of both, wisdom begins.
surya_gita.3.36.claim: When one has tasted pleasure and pain until weary of them, discernment leads him to freedom from craving.

vishnu_gita.1.98.speaker: Vishnu
vishnu_gita.1.98.line: Honour fears disgrace, virtue fears the wicked, power fears critics, learning fears debate. Every gain brings a fear.
vishnu_gita.1.98.claim: Honour fears disgrace, virtue fears the wicked, power fears critics, and learning fears rival debaters.

avadhuta.3.46.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta.3.46.line: Let go, and then let go of your pride in letting go.
avadhuta.3.46.claim: Let go of the world and let go of renouncing it too; renouncing and not renouncing are poison, your nature is pure natural nectar.

shambhu_gita.4.83.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita.4.83.line: Better than punishing people is helping them so they never deserve punishment.
shambhu_gita.4.83.claim: Better than punishment is the effort, made with the wise, by which people never come to deserve punishment at all.

surya_gita.7.54.speaker: Surya
surya_gita.7.54.line: Much of our pain comes from the plans and fears the mind keeps making.
surya_gita.7.54.claim: Great suffering comes to the one with a busy mind; how can it touch one beyond the mind? The mind makes the painful resolves.

mbh.12.104.16.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
mbh.12.104.16.line: What was ends, and what wasn't begins. Grief has no power to change it.
mbh.12.104.16.misuse: Feeling grief is human; the point is not to feed it endlessly.
mbh.12.104.16.claim: What existed passes and what did not exist arises; grief cannot change this, so grieving serves nothing.
mbh.12.104.16.needs: That the loss is final and cannot be argued back

mbh.12.104.28.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
mbh.12.104.28.line: Want what is within reach. Enjoy what is here now. Don't grieve over what hasn't happened.
mbh.12.104.28.claim: Desire only what can be had, enjoy what is present, and do not grieve over what has not come.

mbh.12.104.57.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
mbh.12.104.57.line: A churned-up lake settles and clears on its own. So does a mind, given time.
mbh.12.104.57.claim: As a churned lake clears by itself, a person of formed understanding regains clarity from within.

mbh.12.113.9.speaker: The river Ganga (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.113.9.line: The cane bends when the flood comes, and stands up again once it has passed.
mbh.12.113.9.misuse: Bending under pressure is not giving up your values.
mbh.12.113.9.claim: The cane bends before the flood and stands again when it passes; yielding in time preserves you.
mbh.12.113.9.needs: That the force faced is truly stronger and temporary

mbh.12.144.12.speaker: The male pigeon (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.144.12.line: Wherever the one you love is, even under a tree, is home. Without them, a palace is a wilderness.
mbh.12.144.12.claim: Where the beloved is, even the foot of a tree is home; without her a palace is a wilderness.

mbh.12.145.5.speaker: The pigeon (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.145.5.line: Be kind even to one who wronged you. A tree shades even the one who comes to cut it.
mbh.12.145.5.misuse: Kindness is not letting someone keep harming you.
mbh.12.145.5.claim: Hospitality is owed even to an enemy who arrives at your home, as a tree shades its cutter.
mbh.12.145.5.needs: The story: a guest in need has come to one's door

mbh.12.17.3.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.17.3.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.12.17.3.line: Even someone who owns the whole world has only one stomach.
mbh.12.17.3.claim: Even the sole ruler of the whole earth has only one stomach, so more possession adds little.

mbh.12.172.20.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.172.20.line: Keep a grateful heart. Everything good grows out of friendship.
mbh.12.172.20.claim: Keep a grateful mind and a friendly spirit, for everything comes through a friend.

mbh.12.173.21.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.21.line: You went from happiness to sorrow; you will find happiness again. No one suffers forever.
mbh.12.173.21.claim: You have fallen from happiness into sorrow and will reach happiness again; neither lasts forever.

mbh.12.173.40.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.40.line: Idleness feels good and ends in misery. Effort feels hard and ends in happiness.
mbh.12.173.40.misuse: Effort is not overwork; rest is not idleness.
mbh.12.173.40.claim: Idleness is pleasant and ends in sorrow; capable effort is hard and brings happiness and prosperity.

mbh.12.173.41.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.41.line: Pleasant or painful, meet whatever comes with a heart that refuses to be defeated.
mbh.12.173.41.claim: Whether what comes is pleasant or painful, receive it with a heart that is not defeated.

mbh.12.173.42.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.42.line: Every day brings a thousand reasons to grieve and a hundred to fear. The wise don't let them all in.
mbh.12.173.42.misuse: Anxiety is not a character flaw; this is about learning not to take every trigger in.
mbh.12.173.42.claim: Countless occasions for grief and fear enter the unwise every day, but not the wise.

mbh.12.173.47.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.47.line: All the pleasures of earth and heaven are not worth a sixteenth of the peace when craving ends.
mbh.12.173.47.claim: Neither worldly pleasure nor heavenly joy equals a sixteenth of the happiness of craving ended.
mbh.12.173.47.needs: Some taste of the tiredness of wanting

mbh.12.173.64.speaker: Pingala (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.64.line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
mbh.12.173.64.misuse: This is about clinging to an outcome, not about giving up hope in life.
mbh.12.173.64.claim: One who has dropped expectation sleeps in peace; Pingala found that freedom from expectation is the highest ease.
mbh.12.173.64.needs: Asha here is clinging to one awaited person or outcome, not hope in life

mbh.12.174.15.speaker: Medhavin
mbh.12.174.15.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
mbh.12.174.15.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.
mbh.12.174.15.claim: Do today what is due tomorrow, because death does not wait for your work to be finished.

mbh.12.174.20.speaker: Medhavin
mbh.12.174.20.line: 'This is done, this is next, this is half-done.' Life slips by while we keep busy like this.
mbh.12.174.20.claim: While a person stays absorbed in the done and the undone, death takes hold of him.

mbh.12.174.35.speaker: Medhavin
mbh.12.174.35.line: No eye like knowledge, no discipline like truth, no pain like clinging, no happiness like letting go.
mbh.12.174.35.claim: Knowledge is the best eye, truth the best austerity, attachment the worst sorrow, letting go the best happiness.

mbh.12.176.25.speaker: Manki
mbh.12.176.25.line: Desire, I know your root: my own imagining. I'll stop feeding you, and you'll be gone.
mbh.12.176.25.claim: Desire is born of one's own imagining, and ends at the root when the imagining stops.

mbh.12.176.43.speaker: Manki
mbh.12.176.43.line: I will forgive those who insult me, and answer harsh words with kind ones.
mbh.12.176.43.misuse: Forgiving is not staying in harm's way; protect yourself and still refuse to hit back.
mbh.12.176.43.claim: I will forgive those who abuse me, not injure those who injure me, and answer hatred with kind words.
mbh.12.176.43.needs: A reader who is choosing non-retaliation freely, not one being pressed to accept mistreatment

mbh.12.178.12.speaker: Indra, disguised as a jackal
mbh.12.178.12.line: I long for hands the way you long for money. There's no gain greater than having hands.
mbh.12.178.12.claim: Having hands is the greatest gain; a creature without them longs for hands as you long for wealth.

mbh.12.231.62.speaker: Bali
mbh.12.231.62.line: The success you think is yours sat with thousands before you. It moved to you, and it will move on.
mbh.12.231.62.claim: Royal fortune stays with no one; it sat with thousands before and has only moved to you.

mbh.12.25.31.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.25.31.speaker: Senajit (quoted by Vyasa)
mbh.12.25.31.line: Gain and loss, joy and sorrow come to everyone in turn. Don't be crushed, and don't get carried away.
mbh.12.25.31.claim: Joy and sorrow, gain and loss, life and death reach everyone in turn, so be neither bewildered nor elated.

mbh.12.27.49.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.27.49.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
mbh.12.27.49.line: Days don't come back, nor months, nor years. Be here for the ones in front of you.
mbh.12.27.49.claim: Days, months and years do not return, and beings once parted do not meet again.

mbh.12.272.30.speaker: Chirakari
mbh.12.272.30.line: We only truly feel old, and the world only feels empty, the day we lose our mother.
mbh.12.272.30.claim: A person becomes old, sorrowful and alone in an empty world when parted from his mother.

mbh.12.272.31.speaker: Chirakari
mbh.12.272.31.line: There is no shelter like a mother, no refuge like her, and no one as dear.
mbh.12.272.31.claim: There is no shade, refuge, protection or loved one equal to a mother.

mbh.12.272.69.speaker: Gautama (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.272.69.line: Make friends slowly and let them go slowly. Friendships built slowly last.
mbh.12.272.69.claim: Form a friendship slowly and end one slowly, because a slowly made friendship endures.

mbh.12.272.70.speaker: Gautama (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.272.70.line: When a loved one seems to have wronged you and it isn't clear yet, slow down before you react.
mbh.12.272.70.misuse: Slowing down is not ignoring a wrong once it is clear.
mbh.12.272.70.claim: In passion, pride, hostility and when a close one's fault is unclear, the one who acts slowly is praised.

mbh.12.305.15.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.15.line: The one who doesn't get angry is above the angry. The patient is above the impatient.
mbh.12.305.15.claim: The one without anger is superior to the angry, the forbearing to the unforbearing, the knowing to the ignorant.

mbh.12.305.32.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.32.line: You become like the people you spend time with, the way cloth takes the colour of the dye.
mbh.12.305.32.claim: A person becomes like those he keeps company with and like what he wishes to be, as cloth takes its dye.

mbh.12.305.38.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.38.line: Silence is good. Truth is better. True and right is better still. True, right and kind is best.
mbh.12.305.38.claim: Silence is better than idle speech; if one speaks, let it be true, then righteous, then also kind.

mbh.12.305.8.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.8.line: Never speak words that make another person flinch.
mbh.12.305.8.claim: Do not strike at another's tender spots or speak cruelly; never say the scorching word that makes someone recoil.

mbh.12.305.9.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.9.line: Words fly like arrows and hurt someone day and night. The wise don't let them fly.
mbh.12.305.9.claim: Word-arrows strike another's vital spots and leave him grieving day and night, so the wise never loose them.

mbh.12.337.13.speaker: Sanatkumara (quoted by Narada)
mbh.12.337.13.line: Telling the truth is good. Better still is saying what truly helps.
mbh.12.337.13.misuse: Not a licence to lie; choose true words that help.
mbh.12.337.13.claim: Truthful speech is good, but speech that serves the lasting good of beings is higher and is the real truth.

mbh.12.338.12.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.12.line: Not dwelling on it is the medicine. Brooding doesn't make pain leave; it makes it grow.
mbh.12.338.12.misuse: Applies to what truly cannot be changed; where action is possible, act (see 12.338.15).
mbh.12.338.12.claim: Sorrow that cannot be remedied is best treated by not dwelling on it, since brooding makes it grow.
mbh.12.338.12.needs: That nothing more can be done about the cause

mbh.12.338.13.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.13.line: Treat the body's pain with medicine and the mind's pain with understanding. Both deserve care.
mbh.12.338.13.misuse: Understanding helps, but mental health care is medicine too; this is not advice to skip treatment.
mbh.12.338.13.claim: Mental pain should be destroyed by wisdom and bodily pain by medicine; one should not behave like the childish.

mbh.12.338.9.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.9.line: Dwelling on what is lost adds a second sorrow to the first.
mbh.12.338.9.misuse: Mourning is natural; this is about endless replaying.
mbh.12.338.9.claim: Grieving over what is dead or lost adds a second sorrow to the first.

mbh.12.55.16.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.55.16.line: When something you started fails, don't torment yourself. Gather yourself and apply yourself again.
mbh.12.55.16.claim: When an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself; apply yourself again, which is the highest policy.

mbh.12.7.34.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.7.34.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.12.7.34.line: A wrong you did can be outweighed by the good you do next: own it, regret it, give back.
mbh.12.7.34.misuse: Doing good after a wrong doesn't replace owning it to the person you hurt.
mbh.12.7.34.claim: A wrong once done is destroyed by good action, by confession, remorse, giving and austerity.

mbh.12.80.17.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.80.17.line: A real friend isn't stung by your success and is genuinely sad at your setbacks.
mbh.12.80.17.claim: The best friend is one not pained by your rise and more saddened than you at your decline.

mbh.12.81.11.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.81.11.line: Caught between two people you love, you can't cheer for one without losing the other.
mbh.12.81.11.claim: Like the mother of two rival gamblers, I cannot wish victory for one or defeat for the other.

mbh.12.81.21.speaker: Narada (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.81.21.line: With family, the weapon that works isn't iron: generosity, patience, honesty, gentleness and respect.
mbh.12.81.21.misuse: Patience with family is not tolerating abuse; gentleness can go with firm boundaries.
mbh.12.81.21.claim: Feeding others as one can, forbearance, straightness, gentleness and due honour are the weapon not made of iron.

mbh.12.84.5.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.84.5.line: The one who always frowns and says nothing is disliked. Speak first, with a smile, and people warm to you.
mbh.12.84.5.claim: One who never speaks and always frowns is disliked; one who greets first with a smile wins goodwill.

mbh.12.84.7.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.84.7.line: A gift given without kind words pleases no one. It's like food with no seasoning.
mbh.12.84.7.claim: A gift given without kind words does not please, like food without seasoning.

mbh.13.10.25.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.10.25.line: Hair ages, teeth age, eyes and ears age. Only wanting never seems to age.
mbh.13.10.25.claim: As a person ages, hair, teeth, eyes and ears wear out, but craving alone does not age.

mbh.13.11.26.speaker: The parrot (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.13.11.26.line: I lived off this tree when it flourished. How can I leave it now that it's struggling?
mbh.13.11.26.misuse: Loyalty is not staying where you're harmed.
mbh.13.11.26.claim: One who lived off a tree in its good days should not abandon it when it has fallen on hard times.

mbh.13.161.35.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.161.35.line: Arrows can be pulled out of the body. A cruel word stays lodged in the heart.
mbh.13.161.35.claim: Arrows can be drawn out of the body, but a harsh word lodges in the heart and cannot be removed.

mbh.13.162.15.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.162.15.line: There is no teacher like a mother.
mbh.13.162.15.claim: A mother outweighs ten fathers and the whole earth in worth; there is no teacher equal to her.

mbh.13.175.8.speaker: Brihaspati
mbh.13.175.8.line: Don't do to others what would hurt you. That, in short, is the whole of right conduct.
mbh.13.175.8.claim: Do not do to another what would be painful to yourself; this is dharma in brief.

mbh.13.9.9.speaker: Brahma (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.13.9.9.line: Fate is the seed, effort is the field. Without the field, the seed bears nothing.
mbh.13.9.9.claim: Destiny bears nothing without human effort, as seed bears nothing without a field.

mbh.14.12.15.speaker: Krishna
mbh.14.12.15.line: Some battles no one can fight for you. This one is with your own mind.
mbh.14.12.15.claim: The battle now before you needs no arrows or allies; it must be fought alone with your own mind.

mbh.14.13.3.speaker: Krishna
mbh.14.13.3.line: Two syllables, 'mine', are death. Three syllables, 'not mine', are freedom.
mbh.14.13.3.claim: The two syllables 'mama', mine, are death; the three syllables 'na mama', not mine, are the eternal Brahman.
mbh.14.13.3.needs: That one can hold duties and people without the claim of ownership

mbh.14.92.75.speaker: Dharma (told by the mongoose)
mbh.14.92.75.line: A hundred from a thousand, or a glass of water from nothing: given honestly, it counts the same.
mbh.14.92.75.claim: Whoever gives according to his means, whether a hundred from a thousand or only water, earns equal merit.

mbh.3.135.12.speaker: Ashtavakra
mbh.3.135.12.line: Grey hair doesn't make anyone wise. Whoever understands, however young, is the real elder.
mbh.3.135.12.claim: Grey hair does not make an elder; the one who truly knows, even a child, is the elder.

mbh.3.183.30.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.30.speaker: Nahusha
mbh.3.183.30.line: Success can blind even the wise and brave. In comfort, nobody notices it happening.
mbh.3.183.30.claim: Prosperity deludes even the wise and brave; one living in comfort does not notice it.

mbh.3.210.44.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.210.44.line: Don't drop your principles out of desire, rage or hatred, and don't overreact to good news or bad.
mbh.3.210.44.claim: Never abandon dharma out of desire, rage or hatred; do not exult in the pleasant or burn at the unpleasant.

mbh.3.210.46.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.210.46.line: Don't become bad because someone was bad to you. Stay good.
mbh.3.210.46.misuse: Staying good does not mean staying silent or unprotected.
mbh.3.210.46.claim: Fix the mind on what is good and do not become wicked toward the wicked; remain good always.
mbh.3.210.46.needs: The hurt has first been acknowledged; this does not ask for silence or for staying unprotected

mbh.3.210.53.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.210.53.line: Regret frees you from a mistake; resolving 'never again' frees you from repeating it.
mbh.3.210.53.claim: Remorse frees one from a wrong done, and resolving never to repeat it frees one from the next.

mbh.3.210.59.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.210.59.line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
mbh.3.210.59.claim: A person who turns to good after doing wrong is freed from it, like the moon from a cloud.

mbh.3.216.50.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.216.50.line: You've been given this one life. Don't spend it making enemies.
mbh.3.216.50.claim: Harm no being, live in friendliness, and having obtained this life make an enemy of no one.

mbh.3.28.27.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.28.27.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
mbh.3.28.27.line: If someone who once helped you now wrongs you, let the old kindness weigh against the new hurt.
mbh.3.28.27.misuse: Past kindness does not license present abuse.
mbh.3.28.27.claim: A past benefactor who later offends, even gravely, should be forgiven on account of that earlier help.
mbh.3.28.27.needs: The whole list: Prahlada also names when forgiveness must not be given

mbh.3.28.6.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.28.6.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
mbh.3.28.6.line: Force isn't always right, and forgiveness isn't always right. Wisdom is knowing which the moment needs.
mbh.3.28.6.misuse: Forgiveness never means accepting ongoing harm; this verse itself says it has limits.
mbh.3.28.6.claim: Neither force nor forgiveness is always the better course; each has its time.

mbh.3.29.12.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.12.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.12.line: Don't answer anger with anger. The one who stays calm protects both people, and heals both.
mbh.3.29.12.misuse: Staying calm is not the same as staying in a situation where you are unsafe.
mbh.3.29.12.claim: One who does not return anger to the angry saves both himself and the other, and heals both.

mbh.3.29.28.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.28.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.28.line: Without people patient as the earth, no quarrel would ever end. Every fight has its root in anger.
mbh.3.29.28.misuse: Patience keeps relationships alive; it does not mean one person absorbs all the harm.
mbh.3.29.28.claim: Without people as forbearing as the earth there would be no reconciliation, because conflict is rooted in anger.

mbh.3.29.8.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.8.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.8.line: Anger can't tell what should and shouldn't be said. To an angry mind, nothing is off-limits.
mbh.3.29.8.claim: An angry person cannot tell what should or should not be said; nothing is beyond his doing or saying.

mbh.3.297.7.speaker: Savitri
mbh.3.297.7.line: I started this with determination, and determination will carry me to the end.
mbh.3.297.7.claim: A vow begun with resolve is carried through by that same resolve, so there is no cause for distress.

mbh.3.298.31.speaker: Savitri
mbh.3.298.31.line: Even one meeting with a good person is a gift. Time with good people is never wasted.
mbh.3.298.31.claim: Even one meeting with the good is precious and never fruitless, so one should live in their company.

mbh.3.298.36.speaker: Savitri
mbh.3.298.36.line: Wish no one harm in what you do, think or say. Help, and give. That's the way of good people.
mbh.3.298.36.claim: Ill will toward none in deed, thought or word, with kindness and giving, is the eternal dharma of the good.

mbh.3.31.2.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.31.2.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.31.2.line: I don't do the right thing for the reward. I do it because it's right.
mbh.3.31.2.claim: I do what is right because it ought to be done, not out of desire for its reward.
mbh.3.31.2.needs: That the reader is asking why to keep doing right, not asking for their injury to be recognised

mbh.3.314.114.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.114.line: Speak kindly and you'll be loved; think before acting and you'll win more; make friends and live happily.
mbh.3.314.114.claim: Kind speech makes one loved, considered action brings success, many friends bring happiness, devotion to dharma brings the goal.

mbh.3.314.116.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.116.line: Every day people die, yet the rest of us live as if we never will. That is the wonder.
mbh.3.314.116.claim: Beings go to death every day, yet those remaining wish to stay forever; that is the greatest wonder.

mbh.3.314.119.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.119.line: When arguments go in circles and experts disagree, follow the path good people have walked.
mbh.3.314.119.misuse: Not blind conformity; it means learning from people whose lives show integrity.
mbh.3.314.119.claim: Reasoning is unsettled and authorities differ, so the path is the one the great have walked.

mbh.3.314.61.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.61.line: The mind is faster than the wind, and worries outnumber the blades of grass.
mbh.3.314.61.claim: The mind is faster than the wind and worries are more numerous than grass; mother and father outweigh earth and sky.

mbh.3.314.75.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.75.line: The best gain is health. The highest happiness is contentment.
mbh.3.314.75.claim: Competence is the best fortune, learning the best wealth, health the best gain, contentment the best happiness.

mbh.3.314.79.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.79.line: Drop pride, be loved. Drop anger, no regrets. Drop craving, be rich. Drop greed, be happy.
mbh.3.314.79.claim: Giving up pride makes one loved, anger frees from grief, desire makes one rich, greed makes one happy.

mbh.3.314.93.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.93.line: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat; greed is the illness that never ends.
mbh.3.314.93.claim: Anger is the hardest enemy to conquer and greed the endless disease; the good wish all beings well.

mbh.3.32.14.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.32.14.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.32.14.line: Wait on fate and do nothing, and you'll dissolve like an unbaked clay pot in water.
mbh.3.32.14.claim: One who waits on fate without acting, sleeping at ease, sinks like an unbaked pot in water.

mbh.3.32.48.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.32.48.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.32.48.line: You ploughed and sowed. If the rain didn't come, that isn't your failure. Don't condemn yourself.
mbh.3.32.48.claim: A farmer who has done all that could be done is not at fault if rain fails, and should not blame himself.

mbh.3.32.50.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.32.50.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.32.50.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
mbh.3.32.50.claim: Unrewarded effort is no reason for despair, since every action can end in either success or failure.

mbh.3.32.58.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.32.58.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.32.58.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
mbh.3.32.58.claim: A person should never despise himself, for one who holds himself in contempt does not reach real prosperity.

mbh.5.129.11.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.11.speaker: Gandhari
mbh.5.129.11.line: A parent who sees a child's wrong and still goes along with it shares the blame.
mbh.5.129.11.claim: A parent who knows a child's wrongdoing and still follows the child's will is the one most to blame.

mbh.5.129.29.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.29.speaker: Gandhari
mbh.5.129.29.line: Win the contest with yourself first. Then winning over others becomes possible.
mbh.5.129.29.claim: One must first conquer oneself as one would an enemy; then conquering advisers and rivals does not fail.

mbh.5.129.54.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.54.speaker: Gandhari
mbh.5.129.54.line: Greed has never made anyone truly rich. Enough of it, my child. Be at peace.
mbh.5.129.54.claim: Greed never brings real wealth, so enough of greed; be at peace.

mbh.5.133.14.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.133.14.line: Blaze like a torch, even for a moment. Don't just smoulder to stay alive.
mbh.5.133.14.misuse: About wholehearted effort, not reckless risk or burnout.
mbh.5.133.14.claim: It is better to blaze briefly like a torch than to smoulder long without flame merely to stay alive.
mbh.5.133.14.needs: The scene: a kshatriya mother rousing a defeated son to reclaim what was taken

mbh.5.133.17.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.133.17.line: Win or lose, don't keep grieving. Start the next thing right away.
mbh.5.133.17.claim: Whether he gains or fails, the wise person does not keep grieving but begins the next task at once.

mbh.5.133.7.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.133.7.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
mbh.5.133.7.claim: Do not despise yourself or settle for little; set your mind on the good and do not be afraid.

mbh.5.135.25.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.135.25.line: Don't look down on yourself because of past failures. Fortunes come and go, and can come again.
mbh.5.135.25.claim: Do not despise yourself for past failures, since fortunes arise and vanish; yet do not act from mere resentment.

mbh.5.135.26.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.135.26.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
mbh.5.135.26.claim: Every result is uncertain, yet those who act may succeed while those who never act never do.

mbh.5.33.108.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.108.line: Don't decide when you are angry, exhausted, hungry, rushed, greedy or afraid; right and wrong blur then.
mbh.5.33.108.claim: The drunk, heedless, exhausted, angry, hungry, hurried, greedy, frightened and lustful cannot see dharma, so avoid these states.

mbh.5.33.119.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.119.line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.
mbh.5.33.119.claim: Noble conduct does not rekindle a settled quarrel, mount on pride, or do wrong pleading hardship.

mbh.5.33.29.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.29.line: Understand quickly, listen long, act from judgement not impulse, and stay out of others' business unless asked.
mbh.5.33.29.claim: The wise grasp quickly, listen long, act from understanding and not desire, and do not intrude unasked.

mbh.5.33.30.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.30.line: Don't chase what can't be had, don't keep mourning what is gone, and don't lose your head in trouble.
mbh.5.33.30.claim: The wise do not long for the unattainable, grieve for what is lost, or lose clarity in calamity.

mbh.5.33.31.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.31.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
mbh.5.33.31.claim: The wise person begins only after deciding, does not stop midway, wastes no time and stays self-controlled.

mbh.5.33.33.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.33.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.
mbh.5.33.33.claim: The wise person is neither elated by honour nor pained by insult, and stays unshaken like a Ganga pool.

mbh.5.33.42.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.42.line: Stretching tasks out, doubting everything, going slow when speed matters: that is what foolishness looks like.
mbh.5.33.42.claim: One who drags out tasks, doubts everything and is slow where speed is needed is a fool.

mbh.5.33.45.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.45.line: Blaming others for your own fault, or raging where you have no power, is the height of folly.
mbh.5.33.45.claim: Blaming another for one's own fault, and raging when powerless, mark the greatest fool.

mbh.5.33.55.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.55.line: People may mistake your forgiveness for weakness. It isn't. Forgiveness is the greatest strength.
mbh.5.33.55.misuse: Forgiving is not the same as staying in harm's way or excusing abuse.
mbh.5.33.55.claim: The forgiving have one fault, being thought weak, but forgiveness is the supreme strength and an ornament of the strong.
mbh.5.33.55.needs: A reader who has already chosen to forgive and doubts it; never as an instruction to someone wronged

mbh.5.33.85.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.85.line: Six habits block every rise: oversleeping, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
mbh.5.33.85.claim: One who seeks prosperity must give up sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.

mbh.5.33.96.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.96.line: Health, no debt, home, good people, work of your own, a life without fear: that is real happiness.
mbh.5.33.96.claim: Health, freedom from debt, living at home, good company, one's own livelihood and fearless living are the six joys.

mbh.5.33.97.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.97.line: Envy, scorn, discontent, short temper, constant suspicion, living off others' luck: six sure roads to misery.
mbh.5.33.97.claim: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the irritable, the ever suspicious and the dependent are always unhappy.

mbh.5.34.7.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.34.7.line: If you did it the right way and it still failed, don't let your mind sink.
mbh.5.34.7.claim: When a task done by right method and means still fails, the wise person should not let his mind sink.

mbh.5.34.75.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.34.75.line: When someone abuses you, the wrong stays with the speaker; the one who bears it walks free.
mbh.5.34.75.misuse: Bearing an insult calmly does not mean accepting ongoing abuse.
mbh.5.34.75.claim: When the foolish abuse the wise, the abuser takes on the wrong and the one who bears it is freed.

mbh.5.34.79.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.34.79.line: A forest cut down grows back. A wound made with harsh words does not heal.
mbh.5.34.79.claim: A forest cut by arrows or axe grows back, but a wound made by harsh words does not heal.

mbh.5.35.51.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.35.51.line: The gods don't stand guard with a stick; whom they protect, they give clear judgement.
mbh.5.35.51.claim: The gods do not guard with a staff like herdsmen; they give sound judgement to those they wish to protect.

mbh.5.35.60.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.35.60.line: Gold shows in fire, character in conduct, courage in danger, and true friends in hard times.
mbh.5.35.60.claim: Gold is tested by fire, character by conduct, courage by danger, and friends and enemies by hard times.

mbh.5.35.79.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.35.79.line: Do today what lets you sleep tonight, and in youth what lets you rest in old age.
mbh.5.35.79.claim: Do by day what lets you sleep at night, and in youth what lets you live at ease in age.

mbh.5.36.37.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.36.37.line: If you fear someone's anger or must tiptoe around them, they are not really your friend.
mbh.5.36.37.claim: One whose anger you fear or whom you must approach warily is no friend; a friend is trusted like a father.

mbh.5.36.44.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.36.44.line: Brooding drains your looks, strength and judgement, makes you ill, and changes nothing. Don't give your mind to it.
mbh.5.36.44.claim: Brooding destroys beauty, strength and understanding and brings illness, and grief gains nothing, so do not dwell in it.

mbh.5.36.50.speaker: Dhritarashtra asks; Vidura answers
mbh.5.36.50.line: Peace comes from learning, discipline, mastering your senses, and letting go of always wanting more.
mbh.5.36.50.claim: There is no peace apart from learning, austerity, restraint of the senses and giving up greed.

mbh.5.36.68.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.36.68.line: Anger is a bitter drink the wise swallow and the foolish can't. Swallow it and find peace.
mbh.5.36.68.misuse: Swallowing anger means not acting it out, not denying a real hurt.
mbh.5.36.68.claim: Anger is a bitter, burning drink that the good swallow and the bad cannot; drink it and be calm.

mbh.5.39.56.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.39.56.line: What you repeat in deed, thought and word is what shapes you. So repeat what is good.
mbh.5.39.56.claim: Whatever one constantly practises in deed, thought and word carries one along, so practise the good.

mbh.5.39.6.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.39.6.line: Don't prize a gain that leads to loss; value a loss that leads to growth.
mbh.5.39.6.claim: A gain that leads to loss is not to be prized, and a loss that leads to gain is.

mbh.5.39.63.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.39.63.line: Small minds mistake your honesty and modesty for weakness, and try to push you around.
mbh.5.39.63.misuse: Not a reason to stop being straightforward; a reason to hold firm boundaries.
mbh.5.39.63.claim: The crooked-minded take a straightforward, modest person for weak and so mistreat him.

mbh.5.40.12.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.40.12.line: Never give up what is right, not for desire, not from fear, not for money.
mbh.5.40.12.claim: Dharma must never be abandoned out of desire, fear or greed, not even to save one's life.

mbh.5.42.35.speaker: Sanatsujata
mbh.5.42.35.line: Pretending to be someone you're not is theft, and what you steal is yourself.
mbh.5.42.35.claim: One who takes the self to be other than what it is has robbed himself and committed every wrong.

mbh.5.71.67.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.67.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.67.line: Winning breeds resentment and losing breeds pain. Drop the scorecard, and you'll sleep in peace.
mbh.5.71.67.claim: Victory breeds enmity and the defeated lie in pain; one who has set aside victory and defeat sleeps in peace.

mbh.5.71.71.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.71.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.71.line: Hostility never ends hostility. It only grows, like a fire fed with ghee.
mbh.5.71.71.misuse: Ending a feud does not require pretending the wrong never happened.
mbh.5.71.71.claim: Enmity is never ended by enmity; it only grows, like fire fed with ghee.

mbh.12.103.34.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.103.34.line: People walk over the soft and fear the harsh. Be firm when it's needed, gentle when it's needed.
mbh.12.103.34.misuse: Firmness here means clarity, not cruelty.
mbh.12.103.34.claim: People despise the soft and recoil from the harsh, so be neither only harsh nor only mild but both in season.

mbh.12.104.33.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
mbh.12.104.33.line: Make peace with other people's success, even when you lack it. The wise can enjoy good fortune that isn't theirs.
mbh.12.104.33.claim: Bear the prosperity of others even when you lack it, for fortune drains away from one who resents.

mbh.12.108.3.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.108.3.line: Of all duties, honouring your mother, father and teachers stands among the highest.
mbh.12.108.3.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean obeying them into harm; verses 108.4-5 (obey even against dharma) are deliberately left out.
mbh.12.108.3.claim: Honouring mother, father and teachers is the most esteemed duty and brings great renown.

mbh.12.114.15.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.114.15.line: Whoever runs others down in public only puts their own faults on display.
mbh.12.114.15.claim: One who slanders others before a crowd only displays his own faults, like a snake raising its hood.

mbh.12.114.8.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.114.8.line: Whether a careless person praises or blames you, what can it do? It's a crow cawing in the forest.
mbh.12.114.8.misuse: Fair criticism is worth hearing; this is about mindless abuse.
mbh.12.114.8.claim: The praise or blame of a senseless person achieves nothing, like a crow cawing in the forest.

mbh.12.138.46.speaker: Palita the mouse (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.138.46.line: A wise opponent is better than a foolish friend.
mbh.12.138.46.claim: A wise enemy is better than a foolish friend.

mbh.12.140.66.speaker: Bharadvaja (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.140.66.line: Gentleness wins over both the gentle and the harsh. It is sharper than harshness.
mbh.12.140.66.claim: Gentleness overcomes both the gentle and the harsh, so nothing is beyond it and it is the sharper weapon.

mbh.12.144.13.speaker: The male pigeon (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.144.13.line: A partner shares your values, your work and your joys. Far from home, they're the one you trust.
mbh.12.144.13.claim: A wife is her husband's companion in dharma, livelihood and love, and the one he trusts when far from home.

mbh.12.17.4.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.17.4.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.12.17.4.line: Desire can't be filled in a day, a month, or a whole lifetime. Stop trying to fill it.
mbh.12.17.4.claim: Desire cannot be filled in a day, in months, or even in a lifetime of trying.

mbh.12.172.18.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.172.18.line: Ingratitude costs you trust, and without trust there's no peace or standing anywhere.
mbh.12.172.18.claim: The ungrateful have no good name, standing or happiness, cannot be trusted, and have no expiation.

mbh.12.172.21.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.172.21.line: A good friend is worth more than money. Money comes and goes; a friend helps you face anything.
mbh.12.172.21.claim: Gaining a friend is better than gaining wealth, since wealth comes through friends and with a friend one can strive.

mbh.12.173.53.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
mbh.12.173.53.line: Whatever you start calling 'mine' becomes a source of pain the day you lose it.
mbh.12.173.53.claim: Whatever is taken as 'mine' becomes a cause of anguish when it is lost.

mbh.12.174.16.speaker: Medhavin
mbh.12.174.16.line: No one knows which day is their last. Live well now, while you still can.
mbh.12.174.16.claim: No one knows whose death comes today, so one should live by dharma while still young.

mbh.12.174.9.speaker: Medhavin
mbh.12.174.9.line: Days and nights keep falling away. Wake up to how short this is.
mbh.12.174.9.claim: The world is struck by death and ringed by old age while days and nights fall away; why do you not wake?

mbh.12.175.11.speaker: Shampaka (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.175.11.line: The more you hold, the more you fear losing. Wealth can come with constant anxiety.
mbh.12.175.11.misuse: Not a case against earning a living or providing for family; it is about the anxiety that comes with clinging.
mbh.12.175.11.claim: The wealthy are always anxious, as if in the jaws of death, which is the great difference from having nothing.

mbh.12.175.22.speaker: Shampaka (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.175.22.line: Without letting go, there's no happiness and no fearless sleep.
mbh.12.175.22.claim: Without giving up there is no happiness, no highest goal and no fearless sleep; give up everything and be happy.

mbh.12.176.56.speaker: King Janaka (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.176.56.line: My wealth feels endless because nothing is 'mine'. If my whole city burned, nothing of mine would burn.
mbh.12.176.56.misuse: Not 'don't care for anything'; care without clutching.
mbh.12.176.56.claim: Because nothing is mine my wealth is endless, and if Mithila burns nothing of mine burns.
mbh.12.176.56.needs: Janaka is a ruling king; this is non-possessiveness, not indifference

mbh.12.176.63.speaker: Bodhya
mbh.12.176.63.line: The bird holding the scrap of meat gets attacked. Drop it, and you're left in peace.
mbh.12.176.63.claim: An osprey carrying meat is attacked by others and finds peace by dropping it.

mbh.12.177.24.speaker: The Ajagara sage
mbh.12.177.24.line: I don't refuse good things that come to me, and I don't chase what's hard to get.
mbh.12.177.24.claim: I neither refuse a rightful enjoyment that comes unsought nor pursue one that is hard to obtain.

mbh.12.178.26.speaker: Indra, disguised as a jackal
mbh.12.178.26.line: Getting what you want doesn't satisfy. Craving grows like a fire fed with more wood.
mbh.12.178.26.claim: Gaining what one wants gives no satisfaction; craving blazes higher, like fire fed with fuel.

mbh.12.230.31.speaker: Bali
mbh.12.230.31.line: Gloating over someone who has fallen says more about you than about them.
mbh.12.230.31.claim: It does not befit one who has everything to boast over one who has lost everything.

mbh.12.231.41.speaker: Bali
mbh.12.231.41.line: Not every season is for pushing. Some are for calm. Time ripens everything.
mbh.12.231.41.misuse: A season for calm is not a reason to accept injustice.
mbh.12.231.41.claim: This is a time for calm, not for valour; Time establishes and ripens everything.

mbh.12.26.29.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.26.29.speaker: Vyasa
mbh.12.26.29.line: Meeting and parting come to everyone. Like bubbles on water, they rise and they vanish.
mbh.12.26.29.claim: For all born beings meeting and parting are certain, arising and vanishing like bubbles on water.

mbh.12.268.9.speaker: Tuladhara
mbh.12.268.9.line: The one who is a friend to everyone, in action, thought and word, truly knows what is right.
mbh.12.268.9.claim: One who is always a friend to all and devoted to their good in deed, mind and speech knows dharma.

mbh.12.27.12.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.27.12.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
mbh.12.27.12.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
mbh.12.27.12.claim: Mental suffering has only two sources: confusion of the mind or the arrival of something unwanted.

mbh.12.27.40.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.27.40.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
mbh.12.27.40.line: In grief, ask: where did I come from, where am I going, who am I? Let that steady you.
mbh.12.27.40.misuse: These questions are for steadying grief, not for dismissing it; mourning is natural.
mbh.12.27.40.claim: Steady the mind by asking where one was, where one goes, who one is, and why one grieves.
mbh.12.27.40.needs: Some distance from the first shock of loss

mbh.12.27.52.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.27.52.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
mbh.12.27.52.line: No one gets to stay with anyone forever, not even with their own body.
mbh.12.27.52.claim: No one obtains unending togetherness with anyone, not even with one's own body.

mbh.12.272.23.speaker: Chirakari
mbh.12.272.23.line: Children grow and leave like fruit from a tree. A father's love, even when it hurts him, never lets go.
mbh.12.272.23.claim: Fruit drops from the tree, but a father does not let go of his child even while suffering through love.

mbh.12.272.28.speaker: Chirakari
mbh.12.272.28.line: Whoever still has their mother to turn to is a little child, even at a hundred.
mbh.12.272.28.claim: One who still has a mother to lean on lives like a small child even at a hundred.

mbh.12.272.29.speaker: Chirakari
mbh.12.272.29.line: Strong or weak, thriving or struggling, a mother protects her child. No one nurtures like that.
mbh.12.272.29.claim: A mother protects her child whether he is capable or not, and no one else nurtures as she does.

mbh.12.272.51.speaker: Gautama
mbh.12.272.51.line: Jealousy can drown even a disciplined person. Mine threw me into a sea of wrongs.
mbh.12.272.51.claim: Jealousy brings ruin even to ascetics; it threw me into a sea of wrongdoing.

mbh.12.272.73.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.272.73.line: Think it over and decide slowly, and you'll spend far less time in regret.
mbh.12.272.73.claim: One who deliberates and decides slowly in every matter does not suffer long regret.

mbh.12.28.14.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.28.14.speaker: Narada (retold by Krishna)
mbh.12.28.14.line: You, I and everyone will die, all of us still mixed with joy and sorrow. You're not alone in this.
mbh.12.28.14.misuse: It is not telling a grieving parent to stop crying; the story ends with the son restored.
mbh.12.28.14.claim: You, I and all beings will die without escaping joy and sorrow, so what is there to lament?

mbh.12.305.14.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.14.line: Whoever can ride out the urge to speak, the surge of anger and the itch to grab is truly wise.
mbh.12.305.14.claim: One who withstands the surges of speech, anger, ambition, hunger and lust when they rise is the true sage.

mbh.12.305.23.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.23.line: Critics never talk about your good qualities as eagerly as they talk about your flaws.
mbh.12.305.23.claim: Fault-finders are far more eager to speak of a person's flaws than of his good qualities.

mbh.12.305.27.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
mbh.12.305.27.line: Whatever you do in anger, the good of it is lost. Anger wastes all your effort.
mbh.12.305.27.claim: Whatever an angry person gives, sacrifices or practises is carried off by Yama; his labour is wasted.

mbh.12.337.11.speaker: Sanatkumara (quoted by Narada)
mbh.12.337.11.line: Guard your effort from anger, your success from envy, your learning from pride, and yourself from carelessness.
mbh.12.337.11.claim: Guard austerity from anger, fortune from envy, learning from pride and insult, and oneself from heedlessness.

mbh.12.338.15.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.15.line: Don't just grieve over a problem everyone faces. If you see a way to fix it, act.
mbh.12.338.15.claim: One should not grieve alone over a trouble shared by all, but act to remedy it if a way is seen.

mbh.12.338.19.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.19.line: Each new level of wealth just reveals the next one. The wise stop and find contentment.
mbh.12.338.19.claim: People who reach one level of wealth after another stay unsatisfied and are ruined; the wise reach contentment.

mbh.12.338.21.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.21.line: There's no end to wanting. Contentment is the highest happiness, and the real wealth.
mbh.12.338.21.claim: Thirst has no end and contentment is the highest happiness, so the wise regard contentment as wealth.

mbh.12.338.22.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.338.22.line: Life doesn't pause, not even for the blink of an eye. Don't spend it brooding.
mbh.12.338.22.claim: Life does not stand still even for a blink, so why dwell on perishable bodies as if they were lasting?

mbh.12.7.13.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
mbh.12.7.13.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.12.7.13.line: Parents give years of patience, prayer and sacrifice, hoping only for their children's good.
mbh.12.7.13.claim: Fathers strive and mothers fast, vow and carry a child ten months, wishing every good for their children.

mbh.12.80.36.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.80.36.line: When the world wrongs you, family is the refuge. Nobody feels your hurt like they do.
mbh.12.80.36.claim: When one is wronged by others, kinsmen are the refuge, for kin never tolerate the humiliation of kin.
mbh.12.80.36.needs: That the wrong came from outside the family

mbh.12.81.22.speaker: Narada (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.81.22.line: When relatives are about to say something bitter, calm things down with your own gentle words.
mbh.12.81.22.claim: When kinsmen are ready to speak bitter or petty words, calm their hearts and minds with your own speech.

mbh.12.81.6.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
mbh.12.81.6.line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
mbh.12.81.6.claim: The harsh words of my own kin churn my heart like a fire stick and burn me every day.

mbh.13.161.111.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.161.111.line: Don't speak ill of others, and don't go out of your way to provoke anyone's anger.
mbh.13.161.111.claim: One who seeks well-being should never slander, speak unpleasantly or provoke anyone's anger.

mbh.13.161.119.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.161.119.line: An aging relative, a friend in need, a sister with no support: make room for them as you can.
mbh.13.161.119.claim: An aged relative, a friend, an unsupported sister, a teacher and the worthy poor should be sheltered as one is able.

mbh.13.161.14.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.161.14.line: Slow to anger, honest, harmless, free of envy and straight with people: that is how to live long.
mbh.13.161.14.claim: One free of anger, truthful, harmless, without envy and straight lives a hundred years.

mbh.13.161.36.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.161.36.line: Never mock anyone for their body, their age, their looks, their money or their schooling.
mbh.13.161.36.claim: One should never taunt people for bodily difference, lack of learning, age, looks, poverty or standing.

mbh.13.161.45.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.161.45.line: Start the day by greeting your mother and father. Small daily respect adds up to a good life.
