mbh.13.161.45.claim: One should rise before the sun and first greet mother, father and teacher; this brings long life.

mbh.13.162.12.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.162.12.line: When parents divide what they have, unequal shares plant resentment for a generation. Be fair.
mbh.13.162.12.claim: A father should never give his sons unequal shares.

mbh.13.162.4.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.162.4.line: Sometimes the wise choice is to not see every mistake. When you must correct someone, do it gently.
mbh.13.162.4.misuse: Overlooking small slips is different from ignoring real harm or danger.
mbh.13.162.4.claim: The elder should at times act blind or slow though wise, and point out a younger one's lapse indirectly.

mbh.13.162.5.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.162.5.line: People who envy a family's good fortune try to divide it. Don't let them come between you.
mbh.13.162.5.claim: Enemies who burn at a family's prosperity seek to divide brothers; those who stay united are not broken.

mbh.13.162.6.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.162.6.line: The eldest can make a family flourish or break it, and arrogance is usually what breaks it.
mbh.13.162.6.claim: The eldest can raise or ruin a family, and it is usually his lack of humility that ruins it.

mbh.14.13.13.speaker: Desire (the Kama Gita, quoted by Krishna)
mbh.14.13.13.line: Fight a craving with force alone, and it comes back inside the very thing you fought it with.
mbh.14.13.13.claim: Desire says that whoever tries to destroy it with some weapon finds it reborn in that very weapon.

mbh.14.13.6.speaker: Krishna
mbh.14.13.6.line: It isn't what you have but how tightly you hold it. A mansion can be light, a hut heavy.
mbh.14.13.6.claim: One who owns the earth without 'mine' is unharmed by it; a forest dweller who clings to possessions is in death's jaws.

mbh.14.32.12.speaker: King Ambarisha (quoted in the Anugita)
mbh.14.32.12.line: Master your own greed and rule yourself. That is the only kingdom worth having.
mbh.14.32.12.claim: Seeing greed for what it is, restrain it with steadiness and seek rule over oneself, the only real kingdom.

mbh.14.53.15.speaker: Krishna
mbh.14.53.15.line: I tried hard to make peace. When people refuse to be reconciled, you can't force it.
mbh.14.53.15.claim: I made every effort for peace with the Kauravas, but they could not be brought to it.

mbh.14.92.69.speaker: Dharma (told by the mongoose)
mbh.14.92.69.line: Real need wears down judgement. Be gentle with yourself and others when money is tight.
mbh.14.92.69.claim: Hunger drives out wisdom, the sense of dharma and steadiness.

mbh.14.92.77.speaker: Dharma (told by the mongoose)
mbh.14.92.77.line: A small gift, honestly earned and sincerely given, is worth more than a lavish one.
mbh.14.92.77.claim: Dharma is pleased less by lavish gifts than by small ones justly earned and given in faith.

mbh.3.133.13.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Shibi and the dove
mbh.3.133.13.speaker: The hawk (Indra in disguise)
mbh.3.133.13.line: When two duties pull against each other, weigh them, and choose the one that does more good.
mbh.3.133.13.claim: In deciding dharma, weigh the heavier against the lighter and choose where the greater good lies.

mbh.3.135.10.speaker: Ashtavakra
mbh.3.135.10.line: Growth isn't size. A small tree bearing fruit has grown more than a tall, empty one.
mbh.3.135.10.claim: Growth is not measured by bodily size; the small tree that bears fruit is the grown one.

mbh.3.152.27.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Bhima and Hanuman
mbh.3.152.27.speaker: Hanuman
mbh.3.152.27.line: No one, however brilliant, knows what is right without learning and listening to those who've lived it.
mbh.3.152.27.claim: Dharma cannot be known without study and attending on elders, even by one as wise as Brihaspati.

mbh.3.183.33.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.33.speaker: Nahusha
mbh.3.183.33.line: When I was riding high, drunk on pride, I stopped thinking about anyone but myself.
mbh.3.183.33.claim: Riding the heavens and drunk with pride, I gave no thought to anyone else.

mbh.3.183.43.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.43.speaker: Nahusha
mbh.3.183.43.line: Truth, self-control and kindness make a person good, not their birth or family.
mbh.3.183.43.claim: Truth, self-restraint, austerity, non-harm and constant learning make a person good, not birth or family.

mbh.3.183.5.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh.3.183.5.speaker: Nahusha asks; Yudhishthira answers
mbh.3.183.5.line: Sometimes honesty matters more than generosity, sometimes the reverse. It depends on what's at stake.
mbh.3.183.5.claim: Sometimes truth outweighs giving and sometimes giving outweighs truth; the weight depends on the case.

mbh.3.210.51.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.210.51.line: Self-praise never made anyone shine; real ability shows even without polish.
mbh.3.210.51.claim: A fool does not shine by praising himself, while a truly learned person shines even unadorned.

mbh.3.211.34.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.211.34.line: Good people walk three steps: never betray anyone, give generously, and always tell the truth.
mbh.3.211.34.claim: The conduct of the good has three steps: betray no one, give, and always speak truth.

mbh.3.211.8.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.211.8.line: The heart of wisdom is truth; the heart of truth is self-control; the heart of self-control is letting go.
mbh.3.211.8.claim: The secret of the Veda is truth, of truth self-restraint, and of self-restraint letting go.

mbh.3.213.43.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh.3.213.43.line: Let go of envy and stay grateful, and good things keep finding their way to you.
mbh.3.213.43.claim: One free of envy and grateful keeps to the good and gains happiness, dharma, prosperity and heaven.

mbh.3.234.14.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Satyabhama
mbh.3.234.14.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.234.14.line: No one can be at peace while being managed or manipulated. Without peace, love has nowhere to grow.
mbh.3.234.14.claim: An anxious person has no peace and no happiness, and a husband is never truly won by charms.

mbh.3.28.28.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.28.28.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
mbh.3.28.28.line: Forgive people who hurt you out of foolishness. Good judgement isn't easy for anyone.
mbh.3.28.28.misuse: Forgiving a mistake is not the same as accepting a pattern of harm.
mbh.3.28.28.claim: Those who offend through lack of understanding should be forgiven, since wisdom is not easily found in everyone.
mbh.3.28.28.needs: The whole list, including when not to forgive

mbh.3.29.20.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.20.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.20.line: Real strength is catching your anger as it rises and steadying it with good sense.
mbh.3.29.20.claim: One who restrains arisen anger by wisdom is the one the wise call truly powerful.

mbh.3.29.40.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
mbh.3.29.40.speaker: Kashyapa (quoted by Yudhishthira)
mbh.3.29.40.line: Forgiveness is truth, discipline and purity. It is what holds the world together.
mbh.3.29.40.misuse: Forgiveness is a strength you choose; no one is owed it as a way to keep hurting you.
mbh.3.29.40.claim: Forgiveness is Brahman, truth, austerity and purity, and it upholds the world.

mbh.3.298.24.speaker: Savitri
mbh.3.298.24.line: The wise say that walking seven steps together makes two people friends.
mbh.3.298.24.claim: The wise say friendship is made by walking seven steps together.

mbh.3.298.44.speaker: Savitri
mbh.3.298.44.line: Trust grows out of goodwill. People trust those who wish everyone well.
mbh.3.298.44.claim: Trust is born of goodwill toward all beings, which is why people trust the good above all.

mbh.3.298.50.speaker: Savitri
mbh.3.298.50.line: Good people help others without keeping score or waiting for something back.
mbh.3.298.50.misuse: Helping without keeping score is different from letting others use you; boundaries still matter.
mbh.3.298.50.claim: The good work for others' benefit without looking for any return.

mbh.3.314.112.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.112.line: Reading and talking about wisdom isn't wisdom. The one who acts on it is wise.
mbh.3.314.112.misuse: Not anti-learning; it is against learning that never becomes action.
mbh.3.314.112.claim: Those who only read, teach and ponder scripture are fools; the one who acts on it is learned.

mbh.3.314.121.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.121.line: Truly whole is the one who meets pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future with an even mind.
mbh.3.314.121.claim: A true person is one to whom pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future are alike.

mbh.3.314.132.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.132.line: I hold kindness higher than even the greatest advantage.
mbh.3.314.132.claim: Non-cruelty is the highest dharma, higher than the greatest gain, so let Nakula live.

mbh.3.314.65.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.65.line: Abroad, your learning is your friend; at home, your spouse; when ill, a doctor; at the end, what you gave.
mbh.3.314.65.claim: Learning is the friend abroad, a wife at home, the physician in illness, and charity at death.

mbh.3.314.71.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.71.line: Competence is the way to goodness, giving to a good name, truth to heaven, good character to happiness.
mbh.3.314.71.claim: Competence is the one path to dharma, giving to fame, truth to heaven, and good character to happiness.

mbh.3.314.89.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.89.line: Real restraint is taming the mind; real patience is bearing life's ups and downs.
mbh.3.314.89.claim: Austerity is keeping to one's own duty, restraint is taming the mind, forbearance is bearing opposites, shame is turning from wrong.

mbh.3.314.91.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.91.line: Calm is simply a quiet mind. Compassion is wishing every being well.
mbh.3.314.91.claim: Knowledge is grasping things as they are, calm is a quiet mind, compassion is wishing happiness for all.

mbh.3.314.97.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.97.line: The best bath is washing the mind clean; the truest gift is protecting others.
mbh.3.314.97.claim: Steadiness is firmness in one's duty, fortitude is sense-mastery, the true bath is cleansing the mind, true giving is protecting beings.

mbh.3.57.15.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
mbh.3.57.15.speaker: Narrator (Brihadashva)
mbh.3.57.15.line: The more Nala lost, the harder he found it to stop playing.
mbh.3.57.15.claim: The more Nala lost at dice, the more his passion for the game grew.

mbh.3.58.30.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
mbh.3.58.30.speaker: Damayanti
mbh.3.58.30.line: In every sorrow, no medicine works like a partner who stays by your side.
mbh.3.58.30.claim: For a suffering man there is no medicine equal to a wife, in every sorrow.

mbh.5.129.27.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.27.speaker: Gandhari
mbh.5.129.27.line: Untamed urges are like wild horses. Let them run, and they'll wreck the one holding the reins.
mbh.5.129.27.claim: Uncontrolled senses can destroy a person, as unbroken horses destroy a poor charioteer.

mbh.5.129.44.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.129.44.speaker: Gandhari
mbh.5.129.44.line: Half is more than enough. Share, and listen to the people who want good things for you.
mbh.5.129.44.claim: Half the earth is enough to live on; heed your well-wishers and you will gain a good name.

mbh.5.133.21.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.133.21.line: Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and self-respect, and know the power in you.
mbh.5.133.21.claim: Take up the yoke and pull like a thoroughbred; summon your courage and self-respect and know your own strength.

mbh.5.136.1.speaker: Vidula
mbh.5.136.1.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
mbh.5.136.1.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.
mbh.5.136.1.claim: A king should never show fear in a crisis, and even if shaken should not behave as one shaken.

mbh.5.27.26.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Sanjaya's counsel
mbh.5.27.26.speaker: Sanjaya
mbh.5.27.26.line: Win the whole world and you still won't escape old age, death, joy and sorrow.
mbh.5.27.26.claim: Even one who wins the whole earth does not escape old age, death, joy and sorrow.

mbh.5.33.106.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.106.line: Eight things make a person shine: wisdom, upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, few words, generosity, gratitude.
mbh.5.33.106.claim: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, good breeding, restraint, learning, valour, few words, giving and gratitude.

mbh.5.33.120.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.120.line: Don't gloat over your joy, don't enjoy another's pain, and never regret what you gave.
mbh.5.33.120.claim: The noble do not exult in their own joy, delight in another's sorrow, or regret a gift.

mbh.5.33.14.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.33.14.line: Sleepless nights come to the overpowered, the stripped, the craving and the guilty.
mbh.5.33.14.claim: Sleeplessness comes to one attacked by the stronger, the weak, the resourceless, the robbed, the lustful and the thief.

mbh.5.34.19.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.34.19.line: Before acting, ask two questions: what happens if I do this, and what happens if I don't?
mbh.5.34.19.claim: Before acting, consider what will follow from doing it and from not doing it, then act or refrain.

mbh.5.34.43.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.34.43.line: Envying others' wealth, looks, luck or praise is a sickness that never ends.
mbh.5.34.43.claim: Envy of others' wealth, beauty, strength, family, happiness or honour is a disease without end.

mbh.5.35.61.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.35.61.line: Craving steals your patience, anger your fortune, bad company your character, and pride takes everything.
mbh.5.35.61.claim: Craving takes patience, envy takes goodness, anger takes fortune, bad company takes character, and pride takes everything.

mbh.5.36.5.speaker: Vidura, quoting the sage Atreya
mbh.5.36.5.line: Insulted, don't insult back. The one who holds back keeps their worth; the insulter loses his.
mbh.5.36.5.misuse: Not a wish for harm to come to the other person; the point is your own restraint.
mbh.5.36.5.claim: When abused do not abuse in return; the forbearer's held anger burns the abuser and wins his merit.

mbh.5.36.62.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.36.62.line: A lone tree falls to the storm; trees that stand together hold each other up.
mbh.5.36.62.claim: A lone tree, however strong, is felled by wind, while trees standing together withstand it by supporting each other.

mbh.5.37.10.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.37.10.line: Arrogance, overtalking, stinginess, anger, selfishness, betraying friends: these, not death, cut a life short.
mbh.5.37.10.claim: Excessive pride, overtalking, not giving, anger, selfishness and betraying friends are the swords that cut life short.

mbh.5.37.46.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.37.46.line: No forest without tigers, no tigers without the forest. Families that fight forget they protect each other.
mbh.5.37.46.claim: The forest and its tigers protect each other, and neither survives without the other.

mbh.5.37.51.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.37.51.line: Rein in the rush of anger and of excitement alike, and keep your head in trouble.
mbh.5.37.51.claim: One who checks the rising surge of anger and of elation, and keeps clear in calamity, is fit for fortune.

mbh.5.38.16.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.38.16.line: Don't announce your plans; let people see your results.
mbh.5.38.16.claim: Do not speak of what you intend to do; show only what is done.

mbh.5.39.2.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.39.2.line: Even the wisest voice gets dismissed when it speaks at the wrong moment.
mbh.5.39.2.claim: Even Brihaspati, speaking at the wrong time, meets contempt and disregard.

mbh.5.39.51.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.39.51.line: Everyone wants a friend who is grateful, honest, generous, loyal and steady. Be that friend.
mbh.5.39.51.claim: People wish for a friend who is grateful, righteous, truthful, large-hearted, loyal, self-controlled and steady.

mbh.5.40.18.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.40.18.line: In the end only what we did goes with us. Gather goodness slowly, a little each day.
mbh.5.40.18.claim: Only one's own deeds follow a person from the pyre, so one should gather dharma carefully, little by little.

mbh.5.40.2.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.40.2.line: Walk away from a big gain that isn't clean, and you'll sleep like a snake that shed its skin.
mbh.5.40.2.claim: One who gives up even a great gain joined to wrong sleeps at ease, like a snake freed of its old skin.

mbh.5.40.22.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.40.22.line: Make steadiness your boat. Cross the river of the senses, where desire and anger wait like crocodiles.
mbh.5.40.22.claim: Make steadiness the boat and cross the river whose water is the senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger.

mbh.5.40.23.speaker: Vidura
mbh.5.40.23.line: When unsure what to do, respectfully ask someone older and wiser. You won't go astray.
mbh.5.40.23.claim: One who respectfully consults a kinsman mature in wisdom, virtue, learning and years is never confused about what to do.

mbh.5.42.13.speaker: Sanatsujata
mbh.5.42.13.line: Chase every desire and you go down with them; let them go and you shake off the dust.
mbh.5.42.13.claim: One who follows desires perishes with them; one who casts them off shakes off every stain.

mbh.5.42.4.speaker: Sanatsujata
mbh.5.42.4.line: Drifting through life carelessly is a kind of death; staying awake to it is immortality.
mbh.5.42.4.claim: Heedlessness is death and heedfulness is immortality.

mbh.5.43.61.speaker: Sanatsujata
mbh.5.43.61.line: Silence and retreat don't make you wise. Knowing your own nature does.
mbh.5.43.61.claim: Silence or forest dwelling does not make a sage; one who knows his own nature is the best of sages.

mbh.5.71.26.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.26.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.26.line: Greed kills judgement, then shame, then integrity, and finally the person. It always starts small.
mbh.5.71.26.claim: Greed destroys judgement, lost judgement destroys shame, lost shame destroys dharma, then prosperity, then the person.

mbh.5.71.28.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.28.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.28.line: When money runs out, some friends drift away, like birds leaving a tree with no fruit.
mbh.5.71.28.claim: Kinsmen and friends turn away from one without wealth, as birds leave a tree without flowers or fruit.

mbh.5.71.37.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.37.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.37.line: Losing comfort you were used to hurts more than never having had it. Be gentle with yourself.
mbh.5.71.37.claim: One born poor does not suffer as much as one who had fortune, grew used to comfort, and lost it.

mbh.5.71.38.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.38.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.38.line: When things fall apart through our own fault, we blame everyone except ourselves.
mbh.5.71.38.claim: One who falls into great trouble through his own fault blames even the gods, but never himself.

mbh.5.71.92.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.71.92.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.5.71.92.line: No amount of money or power would make me happy if it came from betraying a friend.
mbh.5.71.92.claim: No wealth, godhood or lordship could please us if gained by betraying you.

mbh.5.95.46.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.95.46.speaker: Krishna (speaking for the Pandavas)
mbh.5.95.46.line: When children go astray, a parent's job is to set them back on the path, not look away.
mbh.5.95.46.claim: We have treated you as a father, so treat us as your children; a father must set right those who stray.

mbh.5.95.48.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
mbh.5.95.48.speaker: Krishna
mbh.5.95.48.line: When wrong crushes right while others watch in silence, the silent are wounded too.
mbh.5.95.48.claim: Where dharma is struck down by adharma before an assembly that only watches, the onlookers themselves are destroyed.

mbh.12.176.67.speaker: Bodhya
mbh.12.176.67.line: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
mbh.12.176.67.claim: An arrow-maker absorbed in his arrow did not notice even the king passing beside him.

mbh.3.314.120.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh.3.314.120.line: The only real news: time is slowly cooking us all, day by day, season by season.
mbh.3.314.120.claim: With earth as pot, sun as fire and days and nights as fuel, Time is cooking all beings.

vr.1.2.36.speaker: Narrator
vr.1.2.36.line: His grief, said over and over, turned into a poem. Sorrow can become something you make.
vr.1.2.36.claim: Grief, voiced in measured lines and repeated, became poetry.

vr.1.63.9.speaker: Vishvamitra
vr.1.63.9.line: Ten years passed like a single day. Distraction rarely feels like lost time while it is happening.
vr.1.63.9.claim: Ten years slipped by like one day while I was lost in desire and did not see the obstacle.

vr.1.64.15.speaker: Narrator (Shatananda)
vr.1.64.15.line: Temper cost him years of work. He resolved: I won't give way to anger again, or speak from it.
vr.1.64.15.misuse: A vow of restraint, not a vow to swallow every hurt in silence.
vr.1.64.15.claim: Anger destroyed what years of effort earned and left him without peace; he vowed never to act or speak from anger again.

vr.2.1.11.speaker: Narrator
vr.2.1.11.line: One kindness was enough to please him. A hundred wrongs he did not keep count of.
vr.2.1.11.misuse: Not keeping score is not the same as ignoring a pattern of harm.
vr.2.1.11.claim: A self-possessed person is satisfied by one kindness and does not store up even a hundred wrongs.

vr.2.100.16.speaker: Ram
vr.2.100.16.line: Don't decide entirely alone, nor with too many voices. Keep plans close until they are ready.
vr.2.100.16.claim: A leader should take counsel neither alone nor with too many, and keep a decided plan from leaking.

vr.2.101.14.speaker: Ram
vr.2.101.14.line: I see no fault in you. And don't hold your mother's mistake against her out of youthful anger.
vr.2.101.14.misuse: Not blaming a parent in anger is different from pretending harm did not happen.
vr.2.101.14.claim: I see no fault at all in you, and you should not condemn your mother out of immaturity.

vr.2.103.10.speaker: Ram
vr.2.103.10.line: When I did well, my father had words for me. Who will say them now?
vr.2.103.10.claim: The kind words my father spoke when I did well, I will never hear again.

vr.2.105.13.speaker: Ram
vr.2.105.13.line: Whatever is gathered runs out, whatever rises falls, and whatever comes together will part.
vr.2.105.13.misuse: A reason to hold outcomes loosely, not a reason to stop building or caring.
vr.2.105.13.claim: All that is gathered is spent, all that rises falls, every meeting ends in parting and every life in death.
vr.2.105.13.needs: The reader has already been allowed to grieve; in the first days of a loss it lands cold.

vr.2.105.23.speaker: Ram
vr.2.105.23.line: Like two logs that meet on the ocean, people come together for a while and then drift apart.
vr.2.105.23.misuse: Not a case for coldness toward family; a case for treasuring the time together.
vr.2.105.23.claim: As driftwood meets and parts at sea, family and wealth come together and part; their separation is certain.
vr.2.105.23.needs: The reader has already been allowed to grieve.

vr.2.109.4.speaker: Ram
vr.2.109.4.line: Your conduct, not your family or your claims, shows whether you are noble, brave or honest.
vr.2.109.4.claim: Conduct alone shows whether a person is noble or base, brave or boastful, pure or impure.
vr.2.109.4.needs: The reader is not carrying guilt over a past act; then it reads as a verdict.

vr.2.11.3.speaker: Kaikeyi
vr.2.11.3.line: 'Promise first, then I'll tell you what I want.' Never agree before you know the ask.
vr.2.11.3.claim: Kaikeyi demands a binding promise before she will reveal what she wants.

vr.2.112.19.speaker: Ram
vr.2.112.19.line: She did it for you, out of wanting or greed. Don't carry it; treat her as your mother still.
vr.2.112.19.misuse: Not a call to keep an abusive parent close; Ram asks Bharata to drop resentment, not his judgement.
vr.2.112.19.claim: Your mother acted for you, from desire or greed; do not hold it in mind, and treat her as a mother.

vr.2.19.32.speaker: Narrator
vr.2.19.32.line: He had just lost the kingdom, and his mind showed no change at all.
vr.2.19.32.misuse: Calm in loss is not pretending it does not hurt; Ram grieves elsewhere in the story.
vr.2.19.32.claim: As Rama gave up the earth and left for the forest, no change showed in his mind, like one beyond the world.

vr.2.19.6.speaker: Ram
vr.2.19.6.line: What hurt most was not the news, but that he didn't tell me himself.
vr.2.19.6.claim: One thing alone burns my heart: that the king did not tell me himself.

vr.2.22.2.speaker: Ram
vr.2.22.2.line: Rein in anger and grief, lean on your steadiness, and set the insult aside.
vr.2.22.2.misuse: Not a call to ignore injustice; it is about choosing your response.
vr.2.22.2.claim: Hold back anger and grief, rely on steadiness, set the insult aside, and get on with what must be done.

vr.2.30.9.speaker: Sita
vr.2.30.9.line: Hardship, wilderness or heaven: I choose to face it with you.
vr.2.30.9.claim: Do not leave for the forest without me; hardship, wilderness or heaven, let it be with you.

vr.2.40.8.speaker: Sumitra
vr.2.40.8.line: Treat the forest as home, and the people with you as family. Go well, my son.
vr.2.40.8.claim: See Rama as your father, Sita as your mother, the forest as Ayodhya, and go gladly, my son.

vr.2.58.18.speaker: Ram
vr.2.58.18.line: Your father has grown old. Don't push him aside; let him still feel he leads.
vr.2.58.18.claim: Do not sideline your aged father; live as prince by carrying out his word.

vr.2.62.14.speaker: Kausalya
vr.2.62.14.line: Grief wears away your steadiness and your judgement. There is no enemy like it.
vr.2.62.14.misuse: Not a ban on grieving; a warning not to let sorrow make your decisions.
vr.2.62.14.claim: Grief destroys steadiness, learning and everything else; there is no enemy like grief.

vr.2.63.7.speaker: Dasharatha
vr.2.63.7.line: Before you start, weigh what is at stake, where it leads and what could go wrong.
vr.2.63.7.claim: One who begins an act without weighing its gravity, its result and its harm is called a fool.

vr.2.72.25.speaker: Bharata
vr.2.72.25.line: He died while I was away. Blessed are those who were there to say goodbye.
vr.2.72.25.claim: My father died while I was away; fortunate are those who could perform his last rites themselves.

vr.2.72.27.speaker: Bharata
vr.2.72.27.line: Where is that gentle hand that used to brush the dust off me?
vr.2.72.27.claim: Where is my father's gentle hand that used to wipe the dust from me again and again?

vr.2.97.4.speaker: Ram
vr.2.97.4.line: Anything gained by ruining family or friends is poisoned food. Don't take it.
vr.2.97.4.claim: Wealth that comes through the ruin of kin or friends is to be refused like poisoned food.

vr.2.97.7.speaker: Ram
vr.2.97.7.line: I could win it. But I wouldn't want even heaven's throne if it came through wrongdoing.
vr.2.97.7.claim: The earth is not hard for me to win, yet I would not want even Indra's throne through adharma.

vr.3.10.17.speaker: Ram
vr.3.10.17.line: No one bothers to advise a person they don't care about.
vr.3.10.17.misuse: Not every criticism is care; but honest counsel from people close to you usually is.
vr.3.10.17.claim: You spoke from love and friendship; no one counsels a person they do not care for.

vr.3.43.6.speaker: Lakshman
vr.3.43.6.line: No deer like this exists anywhere. If something looks too perfect to be real, it probably isn't.
vr.3.43.6.claim: No jewelled deer like this exists on earth; its form is certainly a trick of illusion.

vr.3.50.15.speaker: Jatayu
vr.3.50.15.line: Carry only the load that won't crush you; take on only what you can digest.
vr.3.50.15.claim: Take up only the burden that will not break you, and eat only what you can digest without harm.

vr.3.65.4.speaker: Lakshman
vr.3.65.4.line: Don't punish the whole world for one person's wrong.
vr.3.65.4.claim: You should not destroy the worlds for the offence of one being.

vr.3.66.5.speaker: Lakshman
vr.3.66.5.line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
vr.3.66.5.claim: Take heart: trouble touches every living being, like fire, and passes in a moment.

vr.3.9.26.speaker: Sita
vr.3.9.26.line: Happiness is not reached through comfort. It comes through discipline and effort.
vr.3.9.26.claim: Dharma is won by the skilful through effortful self-discipline; happiness does not come from ease.

vr.4.1.101.speaker: Lakshman
vr.4.1.101.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
vr.4.1.101.claim: Resolute energy is the greatest strength; nothing is out of reach for one who has it.

vr.4.15.22.speaker: Tara
vr.4.15.22.line: Near or far, your brother is still your family. No one else on earth can take his place.
vr.4.15.22.claim: Your younger brother deserves your affection; near or far he is your kin, and no kinsman equals him.

vr.4.15.7.speaker: Tara
vr.4.15.7.line: Let this anger go, the way you drop last night's garland in the morning.
vr.4.15.7.claim: Drop this flood of anger the way you cast off last night's garland on rising.

vr.4.22.23.speaker: Vali
vr.4.22.23.line: Don't be too familiar, and don't be cold. Both are mistakes; find the middle.
vr.4.22.23.claim: Be neither too familiar nor too distant; both are grave faults, so keep to the middle.

vr.4.22.4.speaker: Vali
vr.4.22.4.line: We couldn't have both, the love between brothers and the kingdom. It went the wrong way.
vr.4.22.4.claim: We were not given brotherly love and happiness together; it turned out otherwise.

vr.4.27.29.speaker: Lakshman
vr.4.27.29.line: The rains are here. Wait for autumn. Some seasons are for waiting, not fighting.
vr.4.27.29.claim: The rains have come; wait for autumn, and then you will defeat Ravana.

vr.4.3.19.speaker: Ram
vr.4.3.19.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
vr.4.3.19.claim: His speech was not wordy, unclear, hurried or strained, and came in an even, middle tone.

vr.4.32.15.speaker: Hanuman
vr.4.32.15.line: When someone in deep pain speaks harshly to you, bear it with patience.
vr.4.32.15.misuse: Patience with a hurting person's outburst, not tolerance of ongoing abuse.
vr.4.32.15.claim: You should bear the harsh words of Rama, who is in pain and has lost his wife.

vr.4.32.7.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.32.7.line: Making a friend is easy; keeping one is hard. Affection can break over very little.
vr.4.32.7.claim: A friend is easily made but hard to keep; minds are changeable and affection breaks over little.

vr.4.33.39.speaker: Tara
vr.4.33.39.line: This is no time for anger. Bear the slip of someone who is on your side.
vr.4.33.39.misuse: About lapses by people who mean well, not about repeated mistreatment.
vr.4.33.39.claim: This is no time for anger, least of all at your own; bear the lapse of one who wishes you well.

vr.4.35.9.speaker: Tara
vr.4.35.9.line: Strong people don't let anger take over before they have thought things through.
vr.4.35.9.claim: People of real character do not fall under anger's control suddenly, without first reflecting.

vr.4.49.6.speaker: Angada
vr.4.49.6.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
vr.4.49.6.claim: Those who keep acting surely see the fruit of their action, so weariness is no reason to stop now.

vr.4.66.7.speaker: Jambavan
vr.4.66.7.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
vr.4.66.7.claim: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage surpass all beings; why do you not ready yourself?

vr.4.7.9.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.7.9.line: In loss, money trouble or fear, the steady person thinks it through and does not go under.
vr.4.7.9.claim: In calamity, loss of wealth or mortal fear, the steady person who reflects with their own mind does not sink.

vr.5.1.146.speaker: Beings of the sky
vr.5.1.146.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
vr.5.1.146.claim: One who has steadiness, foresight, judgement and skill does not sink in any task.

vr.5.1.94.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.1.94.line: Thank you, but the work is waiting and I promised not to stop halfway.
vr.5.1.94.misuse: Focus is not refusing all rest; Hanuman rests once he lands.
vr.5.1.94.claim: My task's hour is pressing and the day is passing; I have given my word not to stop midway.

vr.5.12.10.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.12.10.line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.
vr.5.12.10.claim: Not losing heart is the root of fortune and the highest happiness; I will search again where I have not searched.

vr.5.30.18.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.30.18.line: To comfort someone, use their language, not the one that impresses.
vr.5.30.18.claim: I must speak plain human words that carry meaning; otherwise she cannot be comforted.

vr.5.34.5.speaker: Sita
vr.5.34.5.line: As long as you are still alive, joy can find you again, even after a hundred years.
vr.5.34.5.claim: The old saying is true: joy comes to a person who stays alive, even after a hundred years.

vr.5.55.3.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.55.3.line: Blessed are those who use good sense to put out rising anger, the way water puts out fire.
vr.5.55.3.claim: Fortunate are the great souls who check rising anger with reason, as water puts out fire.

vr.6.1.12.speaker: Ram
vr.6.1.12.line: It pains me that I can't repay this kindness in kind. So I'll give what I have: a hug.
vr.6.1.12.claim: It weighs on me that, poor as I am here, I cannot repay the one who brought me this good news.

vr.6.101.18.speaker: Ram
vr.6.101.18.line: In every forest and every low moment, you were the one who lifted me up.
vr.6.101.18.claim: When I was grief-stricken, heedless and despairing in the forests, you were the one who consoled me.

vr.6.111.11.speaker: Mandodari
vr.6.111.11.line: You once mastered your desires and won the world. In the end, your desires mastered you.
vr.6.111.11.claim: You conquered the worlds by first conquering your senses, and those same senses have now conquered you.

vr.6.113.29.speaker: Sita
vr.6.113.29.line: Show compassion even to those who wronged you. No one is without fault.
vr.6.113.29.misuse: Compassion does not mean letting anyone keep hurting you.
vr.6.113.29.claim: The noble do not return evil for evil and show compassion even to the guilty, for no one is without fault.

vr.6.121.16.speaker: Ram
vr.6.121.16.line: Thank you, truly. But my heart is in a hurry to see my brother again.
vr.6.121.16.claim: I do not refuse you, but my mind hurries to see my brother Bharata, whose plea I once turned down.

vr.6.125.12.speaker: Ram
vr.6.125.12.line: If my brother wants to keep what he's been holding, let him have it. I won't fight family for it.
vr.6.125.12.claim: If Bharata, after holding it so long, wants the kingdom himself, let him rule the whole earth.

vr.6.127.38.speaker: Bharata
vr.6.127.38.line: Everything you left in my care, I hand back. Seeing you home makes the long wait worth it.
vr.6.127.38.claim: I return the kingdom you left in my trust; today my life is fulfilled, seeing you back as king.

vr.6.16.20.speaker: Vibhishana
vr.6.16.20.line: Flatterers are easy to find. Rare is the one who tells the hard truth, rarer the one who hears it.
vr.6.16.20.claim: Pleasant speakers are always easy to find; one who speaks or hears an unwelcome but wholesome truth is rare.

vr.6.16.24.speaker: Vibhishana
vr.6.16.24.line: I said it for your good. I wish you well. I'm leaving. Be happy without me.
vr.6.16.24.misuse: Walking away from family is a last resort after honest counsel fails, not a first response to disagreement.
vr.6.16.24.claim: Forgive what I said for your good; guard yourself and this city; I am leaving, be happy without me.

vr.6.18.31.speaker: Ram
vr.6.18.31.line: Whoever comes once and says 'I'm with you', I will protect. That is my promise.
vr.6.18.31.claim: To anyone who comes even once saying 'I am yours', I give freedom from fear of all beings; this is my vow.

vr.6.63.5.speaker: Kumbhakarna
vr.6.63.5.line: Whoever does first what should come last, and last what should come first, lacks judgement.
vr.6.63.5.claim: One in power who does later tasks first and first tasks last does not know good policy from bad.

vr.6.65.4.speaker: Kumbhakarna
vr.6.65.4.line: The brave don't praise themselves. They quietly do the hard thing.
vr.6.65.4.claim: The truly brave cannot bear to praise themselves; without display they do what is hard.

vr.1.2.16.speaker: Valmiki
vr.1.2.16.line: Even a sage stops after an outburst and asks: what did I just say?
vr.1.2.16.claim: Overcome by grief for the bird, what is this that I have said?

vr.1.21.21.speaker: Vasishtha
vr.1.21.21.line: Sometimes the person asking you to let your child go is asking for your child's sake.
vr.1.21.21.misuse: Letting a child grow is not handing them to anyone who asks; Dasharatha trusts a proven teacher.
vr.1.21.21.claim: Vishvamitra could subdue them himself; he asks for your son for your son's own good.

vr.1.33.8.speaker: Kushanabha
vr.1.33.8.line: Forbearance is generosity, truth and honour. The world rests on people who can forbear.
vr.1.33.8.misuse: Forbearance means not retaliating, not accepting harm; the daughters had refused the god's advances.
vr.1.33.8.claim: Forbearance is giving, truth, sacrifice, fame and dharma; the world rests on forbearance.

vr.1.44.10.speaker: Brahma
vr.1.44.10.line: Three generations tried and failed. You finished it. Effort carried forward is not wasted.
vr.1.44.10.claim: You have fulfilled the vow your forefathers could not, and have won the highest honour in the world.

vr.1.53.9.speaker: Vasishtha
vr.1.53.9.line: Not for any price. Some things are not for sale, however powerful the buyer.
vr.1.53.9.claim: Not for a hundred thousand cows or heaps of silver will I give up Shabala; she stays with me.

vr.1.65.3.speaker: Narrator (Shatananda)
vr.1.65.3.line: Many things shook him. Anger could not get in.
vr.1.65.3.claim: After a thousand years he stood like wood; many obstacles shook him, yet anger found no way in.

vr.1.77.20.speaker: Narrator
vr.1.77.20.line: Love that began by arrangement kept growing because of who each one was.
vr.1.77.20.claim: Sita was dear as the wife his father chose, and his love grew further through her qualities; she held him doubly dear.

vr.2.1.10.speaker: Narrator
vr.2.1.10.line: He spoke gently first, and when someone spoke harshly, he did not answer in kind.
vr.2.1.10.misuse: Not returning harshness is a choice of strength, not an obligation to accept abuse.
vr.2.1.10.claim: Always calm within, he spoke gently first and did not answer harsh words in kind.

vr.2.100.17.speaker: Ram
vr.2.100.17.line: When a small effort promises a big result, start now. Don't drag it out.
vr.2.100.17.claim: Once a task of small cost and great yield is decided, begin it quickly and do not delay.

vr.2.100.20.speaker: Ram
vr.2.100.20.line: One wise adviser is worth more than a thousand fools, especially in a crisis.
vr.2.100.20.claim: One wise person is to be preferred to a thousand fools, for in a crisis the wise bring great good.

vr.2.105.21.speaker: Ram
vr.2.105.21.line: We cheer each sunrise and each evening, and miss that our days are running out.
vr.2.105.21.claim: People rejoice at each sunrise and sunset and do not notice their own life wearing away.

vr.2.109.8.speaker: Ram
vr.2.109.8.line: People follow the example of those who lead them.
vr.2.109.8.claim: As rulers conduct themselves, so do the people; if I live by desire, the whole world will follow.

vr.2.115.17.speaker: Bharata
vr.2.115.17.line: This was entrusted to me out of love. I'll look after it until he returns.
vr.2.115.17.claim: My brother placed this trust in me out of affection; I will guard it until he returns.

vr.2.22.24.speaker: Ram
vr.2.22.24.line: Don't torment yourself over a setback. The road you didn't choose may turn out better.
vr.2.22.24.claim: Do not anguish over this reversal of fortune; between kingdom and forest, the forest is the greater gain.

vr.2.23.9.speaker: Lakshman
vr.2.23.9.line: Those who answer bad luck with effort don't lose heart when things go wrong.
vr.2.23.9.misuse: Lakshman is speaking in anger, and Ram chose restraint; take the line about effort, not the urge to fight.
vr.2.23.9.claim: One able to push back fate with effort does not sink when fate damages his aims.

vr.2.24.20.speaker: Ram
vr.2.24.20.line: When I'm gone, look after him. Don't let his grief wear him down.
vr.2.24.20.claim: Take watchful care that the old king is not worn down or destroyed by grief for his son.

vr.2.29.2.speaker: Sita
vr.2.29.2.line: Every hardship you list sounds like a blessing to me, because I'd face it with you.
vr.2.29.2.claim: The hardships of forest life you list are blessings to me, because your love goes before me.

vr.2.34.28.speaker: Dasharatha
vr.2.34.28.line: Stay tonight. Let your mother and me see you. You can leave in the morning.
vr.2.34.28.claim: Stay this one night where your mother and I can see you; leave tomorrow morning.

vr.2.44.17.speaker: Sumitra
vr.2.44.17.line: You will see him again. Let go of this grief.
vr.2.44.17.misuse: Comfort for a long separation, not a promise that every loss will be undone.
vr.2.44.17.claim: You will see him return from the forest; give up grief and confusion, I tell you truly.

vr.2.46.22.speaker: Ram
vr.2.46.22.line: Lead people out of their troubles; never drag them into yours.
vr.2.46.22.claim: A prince should free the people from suffering caused on his account and never bind them to his own sorrow.

vr.2.58.14.speaker: Ram
vr.2.58.14.line: Drop your pride with the rest of the family, even the one who hurt us.
vr.2.58.14.misuse: Respect is not submission; Ram asks his mother not to feed a feud, not to accept mistreatment.
vr.2.58.14.claim: Give up pride and self-regard among my mothers, and see that Kaikeyi is honoured as the king honours her.

vr.2.62.13.speaker: Kausalya
vr.2.62.13.line: I know you are honest. I said those words out of my own pain.
vr.2.62.13.claim: I know dharma and I know you are truthful; what I said, I said in anguish for my son.

vr.2.63.11.speaker: Dasharatha
vr.2.63.11.line: This sorrow is of my own making, like a child who swallowed poison without knowing.
vr.2.63.11.misuse: Owning a mistake is not deserving endless punishment for it.
vr.2.63.11.claim: This sorrow has come to me by my own doing, like poison a child eats in ignorance.

vr.2.64.19.speaker: The ascetic's father
vr.2.64.19.line: Because you told us yourself, you were spared. Confession changes what comes next.
vr.2.64.19.misuse: Confessing is right because it is honest, not because it buys a lighter sentence.
vr.2.64.19.claim: Had you not confessed this evil deed yourself, your head would have burst into a hundred thousand pieces.

vr.2.64.9.speaker: The ascetic's blind father
vr.2.64.9.line: You are our eyes, our support. Our lives hang on you. Why don't you answer?
vr.2.64.9.claim: You are our refuge and our eyes; our lives rest on you; why do you not speak?

vr.2.7.27.speaker: Kaikeyi
vr.2.7.27.line: 'I see no difference between his son and mine. I'm glad for him.' The heart before envy is fed.
vr.2.7.27.claim: I see no difference between Rama and Bharata, so I am glad the king will crown Rama.

vr.2.75.15.speaker: Bharata
vr.2.75.15.line: Why blame me, who knew nothing? You know what I feel for him.
vr.2.75.15.claim: Why do you blame me, who knew nothing and am without fault? You know how deep my love for Rama is.

vr.2.77.21.speaker: Vasishtha
vr.2.77.21.line: Hunger, grief, old age and death come to every living being. None of us is singled out.
vr.2.77.21.misuse: Grief is natural; this is said to help a mourner stand up, not to forbid tears.
vr.2.77.21.claim: Three pairs come to all beings alike and cannot be avoided, so you should not collapse like this.
vr.2.77.21.needs: A mourner who has already wept and now needs help to stand.

vr.2.82.11.speaker: Bharata
vr.2.82.11.line: How could I take what belongs to my brother? Some gains I won't accept.
vr.2.82.11.claim: How could a son of Dasharatha usurp a kingdom? The kingdom and I both belong to Rama.

vr.2.84.9.speaker: Guha
vr.2.84.9.line: Prepare for the worst if you must, but find out their intent before you judge.
vr.2.84.9.claim: If Bharata is well disposed toward Rama, this army will cross the Ganga safely today.

vr.2.97.12.speaker: Ram
vr.2.97.12.line: When has this person ever wronged you? Why suspect them now?
vr.2.97.12.claim: When has Bharata ever wronged you, that you now fear and suspect him?

vr.3.41.20.speaker: Maricha
vr.3.41.20.line: People heading for a fall are the ones who won't take good advice from friends.
vr.3.41.20.claim: Those whose time has run out do not accept the good advice their friends give.

vr.3.50.18.speaker: Jatayu
vr.3.50.18.line: I am old, and you are young and armed. I'll still stand up to you.
vr.3.50.18.claim: I am old and you are young and armed, yet you will not carry Vaidehi off unharmed.

vr.3.72.7.speaker: Kabandha
vr.3.72.7.line: Find a friend who knows your kind of trouble. You won't get through this alone.
vr.3.72.7.claim: You must make Sugriva your friend; I see no success for you without doing so.

vr.3.74.12.speaker: Shabari
vr.3.74.12.line: I was told you would come, so I kept gathering for you. Waiting was a kind of preparing.
vr.3.74.12.claim: As the great ones told me, I have gathered forest food of many kinds from Pampa's banks for you.

vr.3.9.19.speaker: Sita
vr.3.9.19.line: Keep a weapon always at hand and it slowly changes you, as fire changes wood.
vr.3.9.19.claim: Keeping weapons close changes the mind, as nearness to fire changes what it touches.

vr.4.10.6.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.10.6.line: It wasn't what I wanted. Please forgive me. Sometimes a rift begins with a misunderstanding.
vr.4.10.6.claim: Seeing me distressed, the citizens and ministers crowned me; it was not my wish, so please forgive me.

vr.4.2.16.speaker: Hanuman
vr.4.2.16.line: Your mind keeps jumping, so you can't settle on a clear thought.
vr.4.2.16.claim: Your monkey nature shows: with so flighty a mind you cannot settle yourself in clear judgement.

vr.4.22.3.speaker: Vali
vr.4.22.3.line: Don't hold my wrongs against me. I was not thinking clearly.
vr.4.22.3.claim: Do not hold my offence against me; I was dragged along by a fated confusion of mind.

vr.4.24.9.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.24.9.line: Weigh the prize against the grief of what it cost. No win is worth a brother.
vr.4.24.9.claim: How could any brother, even one led by desire, be glad of a brother's death once he weighs kingdom against this grief?

vr.4.27.24.speaker: Lakshman
vr.4.27.24.line: Those who keep grieving lose every purpose they had. Don't let sorrow take all of you.
vr.4.27.24.misuse: Not a rule that grief must be cut short; a friend's nudge back towards living.
vr.4.27.24.claim: Enough of this anguish; you should not grieve, for every aim of one who keeps grieving falls away.

vr.4.28.62.speaker: Ram
vr.4.28.62.line: Give people time. Once rested, a good friend remembers what they owe.
vr.4.28.62.misuse: Patience with a friend has limits; when it runs out, Ram sends Lakshman (4.30).
vr.4.28.62.claim: Sugriva, once rested, will himself know the time has come and remember the help he received.

vr.4.29.7.speaker: Hanuman
vr.4.29.7.line: Help that comes after the moment has passed counts for little, however big it is.
vr.4.29.7.claim: One who acts on a friend's need after its time has passed does not serve the friend, however great the deed.

vr.4.36.20.speaker: Lakshman
vr.4.36.20.line: Forgive me, friend, for the harsh words I said while carrying someone else's grief.
vr.4.36.20.claim: Forgive me, friend, for the harsh words I spoke after hearing the grieving Rama.

vr.4.62.13.speaker: Sage Nishakara
vr.4.62.13.line: You are needed exactly where you are, as you are. Your use isn't over.
vr.4.62.13.claim: I could restore your wings today, but by staying here you will do a work for the good of the world.

vr.4.66.28.speaker: Jambavan
vr.4.66.28.line: My strength has faded with age. This is your time, and you have what it takes.
vr.4.66.28.claim: I am old now and my strength has waned; this is your hour, and you have every quality it needs.

vr.4.7.10.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.7.10.line: Keep giving in to despair and you sink, like an overloaded boat.
vr.4.7.10.claim: The foolish person who always yields to helplessness sinks powerless in grief, like an overloaded boat.

vr.4.7.14.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.7.14.line: I tell you this as a friend, for your good, not to lecture you.
vr.4.7.14.claim: I speak for your good as a friend, not to instruct you; honouring our friendship, do not grieve.

vr.4.8.8.speaker: Sugriva
vr.4.8.8.line: Rich or poor, happy or sad, flawed or not, a friend is your greatest refuge.
vr.4.8.8.claim: Rich or poor, happy or unhappy, faultless or flawed, a friend is the highest refuge.

vr.5.1.91.speaker: Mainaka mountain
vr.5.1.91.line: The time to return a kindness has come. Let me thank you.
vr.5.1.91.claim: Now that this task is before you, let the ocean and me do you a kindness; please accept it gladly.

vr.5.13.43.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.13.43.line: Giving up costs too much. Whoever keeps going finds good things again.
vr.5.13.43.misuse: Hanuman is rejecting despair; anyone in crisis should reach out to someone right away.
vr.5.13.43.claim: Self-destruction has many faults and the living find good, so I will hold on to life; reunion awaits the living.

vr.5.21.14.speaker: Sita
vr.5.21.14.line: You can't buy me with money or power. Some loyalties are not for sale.
vr.5.21.14.claim: I cannot be tempted with power or wealth; I am inseparable from Raghava as light is from the sun.

vr.5.26.39.speaker: Sita
vr.5.26.39.line: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is true only of the ungrateful. Real love survives distance.
vr.5.26.39.claim: Out of sight, affection fades only among the ungrateful; Rama will not let it fade.

vr.5.30.34.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.30.34.line: Don't turn a sure thing into a gamble. Do the certain part first.
vr.5.30.34.claim: Battles are uncertain and I dislike a gamble; what wise person would do a sure task in a doubtful way?

vr.5.30.40.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.30.40.line: Start gently, with what they love, so they can trust what you say next.
vr.5.30.40.claim: I will speak good, truthful words of Rama in a gentle voice and arrange it all so that Sita can trust me.

vr.5.41.6.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.41.6.line: No single approach gets even a small job done. Know several ways to your goal.
vr.5.41.6.claim: No single means accomplishes even a small task; one who knows many ways to the goal can achieve it.

vr.5.55.10.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.55.10.line: Carried away by anger, I won a small fight and wrecked the very thing I came to do.
vr.5.55.10.claim: Overcome by anger I destroyed the root of a nearly finished task; surely Janaki has perished in the fire I lit.

vr.5.55.5.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.55.5.line: In anger we lose the sense of what should never be said.
vr.5.55.5.claim: An angry person cannot tell what may be said from what may not; for the angry nothing is undoable or unsayable.

vr.6.10.17.speaker: Vibhishana
vr.6.10.17.line: Everyone else held back. I must still say what I have seen and heard.
vr.6.10.17.claim: The other ministers have held back; I must tell you what I have seen and heard; weigh it and act.

vr.6.109.15.speaker: Ram
vr.6.109.15.line: No one has ever won every battle. Sometimes you win, and sometimes you fall.
vr.6.109.15.claim: No one has ever known only victory in battle; a warrior either falls to others or fells them.

vr.6.109.23.speaker: Ram
vr.6.109.23.line: Enmity ends with death. The fight is over; give him his due. He is mine as much as yours.
vr.6.109.23.misuse: About letting a conflict end once it is over, not excusing harm while it continues.
vr.6.109.23.claim: Enmity ends with death and our purpose is done; perform his rites, for he is now mine as he is yours.

vr.6.116.10.speaker: Sita
vr.6.116.10.line: After all these years together, if you still don't know me, that loss is forever.
vr.6.116.10.misuse: This is Sita's protest against unjust suspicion; the app does not endorse the test that follows.
vr.6.116.10.claim: If after growing up and living together you still have not known me, then I am lost forever.

vr.6.17.50.speaker: Hanuman
vr.6.17.50.line: Speak not to win, compete or show off, but because the matter needs saying.
vr.6.17.50.claim: I speak not to argue, compete, show superiority or serve my wishes, but truthfully, out of regard for you.

vr.6.18.3.speaker: Ram
vr.6.18.3.line: I won't turn away someone who comes in friendship, even if they have faults.
vr.6.18.3.misuse: Openness to people, not ignoring clear warning signs.
vr.6.18.3.claim: I would never abandon one who has come in friendship, even if he has faults; the good find no blame in this.

vr.6.22.42.speaker: Nala
vr.6.22.42.line: I can build this. Let's start today.
vr.6.22.42.claim: I am able to build a bridge over the ocean, so let the work begin this very day.

vr.6.34.11.speaker: Sita
vr.6.34.11.line: Whatever has been decided, just tell me. Not knowing is the hardest part.
vr.6.34.11.claim: Tell me whatever is being said or decided there; that would be the greatest kindness to me.

vr.6.59.131.speaker: Ram
vr.6.59.131.line: Go and rest. I know you're exhausted. Come back when you're ready.
vr.6.59.131.claim: Go, I know you are worn from battle; rest and return armed, and then you will see my strength.

vr.6.63.4.speaker: Kumbhakarna
vr.6.63.4.line: Proud of your strength, you never stopped to ask where it would lead.
vr.6.63.4.claim: From the start this was never thought through; proud of your strength alone, you did not weigh the consequences.

vr.7.48.14.speaker: Sita
vr.7.48.14.line: It isn't the hardship I mind most. It's what people are saying that wasn't true.
vr.7.48.14.misuse: Sita is the one wronged here; the verse names unjust gossip, not her fault.
vr.7.48.14.claim: I do not grieve for my own body as much as for the slander the people have spread.

vr.7.48.6.speaker: Sita
vr.7.48.6.line: Cut off from everyone I love, who will I tell my sorrow to?
vr.7.48.6.misuse: Read as the grief of someone wronged; the app does not endorse the abandonment.
vr.7.48.6.claim: How shall I live in a hermitage, cut off from everyone, and to whom shall I tell my sorrow?

vr.7.49.10.speaker: Valmiki
vr.7.49.10.line: Trust me and rest. Think of this as your own home.
vr.7.49.10.claim: Accept this welcome with trust and without distress, as if you had come to your own home; do not despair.

vr.7.53.4.speaker: Ram
vr.7.53.4.line: Four days of putting off what people needed from me, and it cuts me to the core.
vr.7.53.4.claim: For four days I have not attended to the people's work, and it cuts me to the quick.

vr.7.83.15.speaker: Ram
vr.7.83.15.line: Take good advice even from the young, and do nothing that makes people suffer.
vr.7.83.15.claim: The wise should do nothing that harms the people, and good counsel is to be accepted even from the young.

vr.2.100.51.speaker: Ram
vr.2.100.51.line: The tears of the falsely accused bring ruin on the leader who ignored them.
vr.2.100.51.claim: The tears of the falsely accused destroy the children and herds of a ruler who governs for his own pleasure.

vr.2.8.8.speaker: Manthara
vr.2.8.8.line: 'Lucky her.' Envy often begins as someone counting another person's blessings for you.
vr.2.8.8.misuse: This is the voice of envy, quoted as a warning, not as advice.
vr.2.8.8.claim: Fortunate indeed is Kausalya, whose son will be crowned heir tomorrow.

vr.7.97.4.speaker: Ram
vr.7.97.4.line: I knew she was innocent, and I gave in to what people said. Please forgive me.
vr.7.97.4.misuse: An admission of a wrong done under social pressure, not a justification of it.
vr.7.97.4.claim: Public slander is powerful; knowing her blameless, I abandoned Sita out of fear of the people.

rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.speaker: Vishnu
rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.line: A good doctor won't give the patient what he begs for if it will harm him.
rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.misuse: Not every refusal is for your good; this is a way to reframe, not a reason to accept harm.
rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.claim: God withholds what we crave when it would harm us, as a doctor refuses a sick man harmful food.
rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.needs: trust that a caring Lord stands behind what is granted and refused

rcm.1.247.chaupai.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.247.chaupai.1.line: What use is rain after the crops have dried? Act while the moment is still here.
rcm.1.247.chaupai.1.claim: Help that comes after the moment has passed is useless, so act while it still matters.

rcm.1.260.doha.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.260.doha.1.line: Sharp replies feed an angry fire like ghee. Answer with words like water.
rcm.1.260.doha.1.claim: Sharp replies feed another's anger like ghee on fire; cool words quiet it.

rcm.1.261.doha.1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm.1.261.doha.1.line: Anger is the root of wrongdoing; in its grip we do what we shouldn't.
rcm.1.261.doha.1.claim: Anger is the root of wrongdoing; in its grip people act wrongly and turn against everyone.

rcm.1.262.chaupai.1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm.1.262.chaupai.1.line: A broken bow won't mend because you are angry. Sit down.
rcm.1.262.chaupai.1.claim: Anger cannot mend what is already broken.

rcm.1.3.chaupai.4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.3.chaupai.4.line: Without good company, there is no clear judgement.
rcm.1.3.chaupai.4.claim: Discernment does not arise without good company, and such company comes easily only by Ram's grace.

rcm.1.318.chaupai.3.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.318.chaupai.3.line: Known for his calm, he held his daughter close as she left, and all his wisdom gave way.
rcm.1.318.chaupai.3.claim: Even the most detached sage breaks down when his daughter leaves home.

rcm.1.54.sortha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.54.sortha.1.line: Love turns water into milk. One drop of deceit, and it curdles.
rcm.1.54.sortha.1.claim: Love makes two one as water sells for milk, but deceit separates them and the sweetness goes.

rcm.1.58.chaupai.3.speaker: Shiva
rcm.1.58.chaupai.3.line: You may visit family without an invitation. But where there is hostility toward you, going brings no good.
rcm.1.58.chaupai.3.misuse: Not a rule to cut off family; a caution about walking into known hostility.
rcm.1.58.chaupai.3.claim: One may visit kin uninvited, but going where someone holds hostility toward you brings no good.

rcm.1.6.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.6.doha.1.line: The world is a mix of good and bad. Like the swan, take the milk and leave the water.
rcm.1.6.doha.1.claim: Creation mixes virtue and fault; the wise take the virtue and leave the fault.

rcm.1.76.chaupai.3.speaker: Parvati
rcm.1.76.chaupai.3.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
rcm.1.76.chaupai.3.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.
rcm.1.76.chaupai.3.claim: True resolve does not break even if the body does, as gold keeps its nature in fire.

rcm.1.8.chaupai.7.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.8.chaupai.7.line: Most of us swell only at our own rise. Rare is the one who surges at another's.
rcm.1.8.chaupai.7.claim: Most people rejoice only in their own gain; rare is the good person who rejoices at another's rise.

rcm.2.11.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.11.chaupai.3.line: We grew up together, every milestone shared. Why should one brother alone be crowned?
rcm.2.11.chaupai.3.claim: Ram, told he alone will be crowned, feels it unjust to brothers who shared everything with him.

rcm.2.146.chaupai.3.speaker: Sumantra
rcm.2.146.chaupai.3.line: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come like day and night. The steady hold both alike.
rcm.2.146.chaupai.3.claim: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come by time and karma like day and night; the steady hold both alike.
rcm.2.146.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader is past the first shock and can hear a wider view

rcm.2.159.chaupai.3.speaker: Kausalya
rcm.2.159.chaupai.3.line: Hold on, child. The times turned against us. Don't carry this loss as your shame.
rcm.2.159.chaupai.3.misuse: Easing shame is not denying responsibility where it is real.
rcm.2.159.chaupai.3.claim: What time and karma brought could not be turned; do not carry this loss as your own shame.

rcm.2.163.doha.1.speaker: Vasishtha
rcm.2.163.doha.1.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
rcm.2.163.doha.1.claim: In grief, hold courage in the heart and do what this moment requires.

rcm.2.170.chaupai.7.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.170.chaupai.7.line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
rcm.2.170.chaupai.7.claim: Advice can be sound and fully understood, and the heart can still find no rest in it.

rcm.2.176.chaupai.2.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.176.chaupai.2.line: I am at fault. Still I will go to him face to face, trusting his heart to forgive.
rcm.2.176.chaupai.2.claim: Though I am the cause of this harm, if I go to him for refuge he will forgive.
rcm.2.176.chaupai.2.needs: knowing that Bharat is in fact innocent and takes the blame out of love

rcm.2.185.chaupai.4.speaker: Guha
rcm.2.185.chaupai.4.line: Fools act in haste and repent. Know someone's nature before you fight them.
rcm.2.185.chaupai.4.claim: Acting in haste brings regret; learn a person's nature and intent before you fight them.

rcm.2.198.doha.1.speaker: Bharadwaj
rcm.2.198.doha.1.line: Don't eat yourself up with shame for what someone else in your family did.
rcm.2.198.doha.1.claim: Do not carry shame for your mother's deed; she too is not to blame, for her mind was clouded.

rcm.2.222.chaupai.2.speaker: A voice from the sky
rcm.2.222.chaupai.2.line: Think before you act. Acting in haste and regretting later is not wisdom.
rcm.2.222.chaupai.2.claim: Think a deed through before doing it; those who act in haste and repent are not wise.

rcm.2.23.chaupai.2.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.23.chaupai.2.line: Some advice is soft to hear and harsh in its end: poison dissolved in honey.
rcm.2.23.chaupai.2.claim: Some counsel sounds sweet and ends in ruin, like poison mixed in honey.

rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.line: He went first to the one who had wronged him, and comforted her.
rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.misuse: Forgiving is not pretending the harm didn't happen.
rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.claim: Ram goes first to the mother who exiled him and comforts her, laying the blame on time and fate.
rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.needs: that the reader has chosen to forgive and is looking for how

rcm.2.247.chaupai.1.speaker: Vasishtha
rcm.2.247.chaupai.1.line: People in distress never speak with judgement; the gambler sees only his own throw.
rcm.2.247.chaupai.1.misuse: Not a reason to dismiss people who are hurting; a reason to wait before deciding.
rcm.2.247.chaupai.1.claim: A person in distress cannot speak with weighed judgement; like a gambler he sees only his own stake.

rcm.2.249.chaupai.4.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.249.chaupai.4.line: Since childhood he never broke my heart. Even when I lost at games, he let me win.
rcm.2.249.chaupai.4.claim: Ram never once broke his younger brother's heart, and even let him win the games he lost.

rcm.2.252.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.252.chaupai.3.line: You torment yourself with shame for nothing. In my eyes you stand above them all.
rcm.2.252.chaupai.3.claim: Your shame is baseless; a soul's course lies in God's hands, and you stand above all the virtuous.
rcm.2.252.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader's guilt is larger than anything they actually did

rcm.2.256.chaupai.2.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.256.chaupai.2.line: I was frightened by fears I had imagined. My worry had no root at all.
rcm.2.256.chaupai.2.claim: The dread was self-made and had no root; when one loses direction the sun is not to blame.
rcm.2.256.chaupai.2.needs: that the feared thing is a guess about someone's heart, not a real threat

rcm.2.271.chaupai.3.speaker: Kausalya
rcm.2.271.chaupai.3.line: Gold is proved on the touchstone. People are proved by time.
rcm.2.271.chaupai.3.claim: As gold is known on the touchstone, a person is known by how they act when time tests them.

rcm.2.292.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.292.chaupai.4.line: In bad times, good siblings are the hands that rise to block the blow.
rcm.2.292.chaupai.4.claim: In hard times it is good brothers who take the blow, as hands rise to shield against a thunderbolt.

rcm.2.301.doha.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.301.doha.1.line: A leader is like the mouth: it takes in, but only to nourish the whole body.
rcm.2.301.doha.1.claim: A leader should be like the mouth: it alone eats, yet with discernment it nourishes every limb.

rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.line: My beloved brother gets the throne. Fate is favouring me in every way today.
rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.misuse: Grace in loss is not pretending it doesn't hurt.
rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.claim: Ram receives his exile as good fortune, glad that his beloved brother gains the throne.
rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.needs: that the reader is not in fresh hurt over a loss

rcm.2.42.doha.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.42.doha.1.line: A twisted mind reads straight words as crooked, as a leech wriggles through still water.
rcm.2.42.doha.1.claim: A crooked mind takes even plain, sincere words as crooked.

rcm.2.50.doha.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.50.doha.1.line: The crown had been a tether. Losing it, he felt like an elephant set free.
rcm.2.50.doha.1.misuse: Losing a role can free you; that does not make every loss a gift.
rcm.2.50.doha.1.claim: To Ram the kingship was a tether; hearing of exile he felt freed and his joy grew.
rcm.2.50.doha.1.needs: that the reader is ready to see what the loss opened

rcm.2.55.doha.1.speaker: Kausalya
rcm.2.55.doha.1.line: I won't hold you back with false affection. Go, son. Just don't forget your mother.
rcm.2.55.doha.1.claim: A mother's true love does not hold her son back from his duty; she asks only to be remembered.

rcm.2.67.chaupai.4.speaker: Kausalya
rcm.2.67.chaupai.4.line: When will that day come, when your mother, still living, sees your face again?
rcm.2.67.chaupai.4.claim: A mother parting from her child wonders whether she will live to see that face again.

rcm.2.73.chaupai.2.speaker: Sumitra
rcm.2.73.chaupai.2.line: Home is wherever your people are, as day is wherever the sun shines.
rcm.2.73.chaupai.2.claim: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives, as day is wherever the sun shines.

rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.speaker: Lakshman
rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.line: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow. You live out the fruit of your own actions.
rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.misuse: Not "you deserve your suffering"; it is about not handing your peace to others.
rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.claim: No one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow; each lives out the fruit of their own deeds.
rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.needs: acceptance of karma; the reader must be asking why, not asking to be heard

rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.line: Think it through: don't give way to anger, and don't blame anyone needlessly.
rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.misuse: Not blaming is not the same as excusing harm.
rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.claim: Knowing this, do not be angry or blame anyone; all are asleep in delusion's night, seeing dreams.
rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.needs: willingness to take the Vedantic view of the world as dream-like

rcm.2.99.chaupai.3.speaker: Kevat
rcm.2.99.chaupai.3.line: I've worked for wages all my life. Today I was paid in full.
rcm.2.99.chaupai.3.claim: Having served Ram, the boatman counts himself paid in full and wants nothing more.

rcm.3.32.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.32.chaupai.2.line: Be content with what comes, and don't go looking for faults in others, not even in your dreams.
rcm.3.32.chaupai.2.claim: Devotion includes seeing all the world as filled with Ram, being content with what comes, and seeing no one's faults.

rcm.3.42.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.42.chaupai.1.line: Good people squirm at their own praise and light up when others are praised.
rcm.3.42.chaupai.1.claim: Good people shrink from their own praise, delight in praise of others, and stay even, simple and loving to all.

rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.line: The body of five elements lies before you; the self lives on. For whom do you weep?
rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.misuse: This is comfort for later, not a reason to stop someone from grieving.
rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.claim: The body of five elements lies here and the soul is eternal, so there is no one to weep for.
rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.needs: grief already voiced and heard; this is week 3 material, never a first word

rcm.4.15.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.15.chaupai.2.line: Mountains take the pounding rain the way steady people take harsh words.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.2.misuse: Bearing words calmly is not the same as accepting mistreatment.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.2.claim: The learned grow humble with knowledge, and the good bear the wicked's harsh words as mountains bear rain.

rcm.4.15.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.15.chaupai.4.line: Ponds fill drop by drop. Good qualities gather in a person the same way.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.4.claim: Good qualities gather in a good person little by little, as water collects to fill a pond.

rcm.4.21.chaupai.4.speaker: Sugriva
rcm.4.21.chaupai.4.line: No drink intoxicates like comfort. It can cloud even a wise mind in a moment.
rcm.4.21.chaupai.4.claim: Nothing intoxicates like sense pleasures; they delude even a sage's mind in a moment.

rcm.4.30.chaupai.1.speaker: Sampati
rcm.4.30.chaupai.1.line: Look at me and take heart. My burned wings have grown back.
rcm.4.30.chaupai.1.claim: Seeing Sampati's body restored by Ram's grace, take heart: the task can be done.

rcm.4.31.chaupai.3.speaker: Jambavant
rcm.4.31.chaupai.3.line: What task in the world is too hard for you? You were made for this.
rcm.4.31.chaupai.3.claim: No task in the world is too hard for you; you were born for Ram's work.

rcm.4.8.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.8.chaupai.1.line: A real friend treats his own troubles as dust and his friend's troubles as a mountain.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.1.claim: A true friend counts his own mountain of sorrow as dust and a friend's speck of sorrow as a mountain.

rcm.5.12.chaupai.1.speaker: Sita
rcm.5.12.chaupai.1.line: I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you became my ship.
rcm.5.12.chaupai.1.claim: To one drowning in separation, a messenger from the beloved is a ship.

rcm.5.13.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.13.chaupai.3.line: Speaking of pain lightens it. But whom can I tell? No one knows this ache.
rcm.5.13.chaupai.3.claim: Speaking of sorrow lightens it, but this sorrow has no one who would understand it.

rcm.5.2.chaupai.5.speaker: Narrator
rcm.5.2.chaupai.5.line: As the obstacle grew, he grew twice as big. Then he made himself tiny and slipped through.
rcm.5.2.chaupai.5.claim: Hanuman matches the obstacle by growing, then passes it by becoming very small.

rcm.5.3.doha.1.speaker: Lankini
rcm.5.3.doha.1.line: All of heaven on one side of the scale can't outweigh one moment in good company.
rcm.5.3.doha.1.claim: All the joys of heaven and liberation together do not equal one moment of good company.

rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.line: All of it was your strength, not my greatness.
rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.misuse: Humility about success, not denying your own effort.
rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.claim: Hanuman credits his whole feat to Ram's power and none of it to himself.
rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.needs: this is for someone carrying success, never for someone who doubts their worth

rcm.5.35.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.5.35.doha.1.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.
rcm.5.35.doha.1.claim: When minister, physician and teacher say only what pleases, from fear or hope of gain, kingdom, body and dharma soon perish.

rcm.5.36.chaupai.4.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.36.chaupai.4.line: You may be gifted and clever, but even a little greed and people stop calling you good.
rcm.5.36.chaupai.4.claim: No power survives enmity toward living beings, and even a little greed ruins a gifted person's name.

rcm.5.38.chaupai.3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.38.chaupai.3.line: Good sense and bad sense live in every heart. Which you feed decides what follows.
rcm.5.38.chaupai.3.claim: Good and bad judgement live in every heart; good judgement brings prosperity and bad judgement brings ruin.

rcm.5.39.doha.1.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.39.doha.1.line: I've said what I had to say. I am leaving now; don't blame me.
rcm.5.39.doha.1.claim: Having warned his brother in vain and been struck, Vibhishan leaves for Ram's refuge and asks not to be blamed.

rcm.5.48.chaupai.4.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.48.chaupai.4.line: Even when you have the power to force it, ask politely first.
rcm.5.48.chaupai.4.claim: Even one with the power to force a matter should first make a humble request.

rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.line: Calm advice to an angry person, or detachment to a greedy one, is seed sown in barren soil.
rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.misuse: Firmness after real patience, not permission to bully. The doha 'bhay binu hoi na priti' is deliberately not used.
rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.claim: Pleading with the stubborn and good counsel to the unreceptive are wasted, like seed sown in barren ground.
rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.needs: the three days of humble asking that come before; firmness follows patience, it does not replace it

rcm.5.6.chaupai.1.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.6.chaupai.1.line: I live here like the tongue among the teeth.
rcm.5.6.chaupai.1.claim: A good person among the hostile lives like the tongue among teeth, unsure if grace will ever reach him.

rcm.6.110.doha.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.6.110.doha.1.line: All you offer is mine too. But thinking of my brother back home, each moment feels like an age.
rcm.6.110.doha.1.claim: Remembering a brother who waits at home, every moment away feels like an age.

rcm.6.19.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.6.19.chaupai.4.line: Speak with your opponent so the work gets done and it does them good too.
rcm.6.19.chaupai.4.claim: Speak with an opponent so that your purpose is served and his good as well.

rcm.6.34.doha.2.speaker: Narrator
rcm.6.34.doha.2.line: A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.
rcm.6.34.doha.2.claim: A good person's mind does not abandon what is right though countless obstacles come.

rcm.6.60.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.6.60.chaupai.2.line: You could never bear to see me sad. For me you left home and bore every hardship.
rcm.6.60.chaupai.2.claim: Ram, holding his fallen brother, recalls how Lakshman left everything and bore every hardship for him.

rcm.6.76.chaupai.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.6.76.chaupai.1.line: Many are skilled at advising others. Few live by the advice themselves.
rcm.6.76.chaupai.1.claim: Many are skilled at advising others; few practise what they advise.

rcm.6.79.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.6.79.chaupai.3.line: Courage and patience are the wheels; truth and character, the flag. That is the chariot that wins.
rcm.6.79.chaupai.3.claim: The chariot that wins is made of valour, patience, truth, conduct, self-control, forgiveness, compassion and evenness.

rcm.7.10.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.10.chaupai.4.line: These friends carried me across the battle. For me they staked their lives.
rcm.7.10.chaupai.4.claim: Ram credits his victory to his companions and calls them dearer to him than his own brother.

rcm.7.104.doha.3.speaker: Kakbhushundi's teacher
rcm.7.104.doha.3.line: He is confused and lost. Don't be angry with him.
rcm.7.104.doha.3.claim: A soul in maya's grip wanders astray without knowing it, so it deserves mercy and not anger.
rcm.7.104.doha.3.needs: that the reader is the stronger or elder party and has chosen to forgive

rcm.7.106.chaupai.1.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.106.chaupai.1.line: One thorn never left me: how gentle the teacher I insulted had been.
rcm.7.106.chaupai.1.claim: Through many births one pain never left him: the memory of the gentle teacher he had insulted.

rcm.7.107.chaupai.8.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.107.chaupai.8.line: Rub even sandalwood too hard, and it bursts into flame.
rcm.7.107.chaupai.8.claim: Repeated slights anger even the wise, as hard rubbing brings fire out of cool sandalwood.

rcm.7.117.chaupai.11.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.117.chaupai.11.line: Non-harm is the highest duty. No wrong weighs as much as slandering others.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.11.claim: Non-harm is the highest duty, and no sin is as heavy as slandering others.

rcm.7.117.chaupai.15.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.117.chaupai.15.line: Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.15.claim: Delusion is the root of all the mind's diseases; desire, greed and anger are its wind, phlegm and bile.

rcm.7.12.chaupai.1.speaker: Shiva
rcm.7.12.chaupai.1.line: Seeing her shame, he went to her house first and put her at ease.
rcm.7.12.chaupai.1.claim: Seeing that Kaikeyi is ashamed, Ram goes first to her house and puts her at ease.
rcm.7.12.chaupai.1.needs: that the reader has chosen to forgive and is looking for how

rcm.7.3.chaupai.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.7.3.chaupai.1.line: One day left, and still no word. Has he forgotten me?
rcm.7.3.chaupai.1.claim: With one day left and no word, Bharat fears he has been forgotten for his own unworthiness.

rcm.7.3.doha.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.7.3.doha.1.line: Just as he was going under, help arrived like a boat.
rcm.7.3.doha.1.claim: As Bharat was sinking in separation, Hanuman arrived like a boat.

rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.line: The axe cuts the sandalwood, and the sandalwood still leaves its fragrance on the axe.
rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.misuse: Staying kind is not the same as staying within reach of the axe.
rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.claim: The good do good even to those who harm them, as sandalwood leaves its fragrance on the axe that cuts it.
rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.needs: that the reader is out of the axe's reach and is asking who they want to be

rcm.7.4.chaupai.6.speaker: Bharat
rcm.7.4.chaupai.6.line: Nothing in the world equals this news. I can never repay you.
rcm.7.4.chaupai.6.claim: Bharat counts the news of Ram's return beyond any gift and himself forever in the messenger's debt.

rcm.7.40.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.40.chaupai.1.line: A good person is saddened by others' sorrow and gladdened by others' joy.
rcm.7.40.chaupai.1.claim: The good are not greedy for pleasure, grieve at others' sorrow, rejoice at others' joy, and hold no one an enemy.

rcm.7.40.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.40.chaupai.4.line: Never speak a harsh word. Let praise and blame land on you the same way.
rcm.7.40.chaupai.4.claim: The good never waver from self-control or speak harshly, hold praise and blame alike, and give their love to Ram's feet.

rcm.7.43.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
