rcm.7.43.chaupai.1.line: No duty equals doing good to others, and nothing is lower than causing others pain.
rcm.7.43.chaupai.1.claim: No duty equals doing good to others, and no baseness equals causing others pain.

rcm.7.45.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.45.chaupai.3.line: If I say anything wrong, stop me. Don't be afraid.
rcm.7.45.chaupai.3.claim: Ram asks his people to stop him without fear if he says anything unjust.

rcm.7.48.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.48.chaupai.3.line: No grudges, no quarrels, no craving, no fear: for such a person every direction is joy.
rcm.7.48.chaupai.3.claim: One with no enmity, quarrel, craving or fear finds every direction full of joy.

rcm.7.6.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.6.chaupai.2.line: Heaven may be praised by all. It isn't as dear to me as the town where I was born.
rcm.7.6.chaupai.2.claim: Ram says even Vaikuntha is not as dear to him as Ayodhya, the city of his birth.

rcm.7.61.chaupai.2.speaker: Shiva
rcm.7.61.chaupai.2.line: Doubts don't end in a passing conversation. They clear with long time in good company.
rcm.7.61.chaupai.2.claim: Doubt is not cleared in a passing talk; it ends only through long time in good company.

rcm.7.68.chaupai.6.speaker: Garuda
rcm.7.68.chaupai.6.line: Only the one scorched by the sun knows the shade. Without my doubt, I'd never have found you.
rcm.7.68.chaupai.6.claim: Only one scorched by the sun knows the worth of shade; his confusion is what led him to his teacher.

rcm.7.69.chaupai.4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.69.chaupai.4.line: Who hasn't been blinded, made to dance by desire, maddened by craving, burned by anger?
rcm.7.69.chaupai.4.claim: Delusion, desire, craving and anger have overcome everyone; no one in the world is exempt.

rcm.7.70.chaupai.2.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.70.chaupai.2.line: Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? You are not the only one.
rcm.7.70.chaupai.2.claim: Envy, grief, worry and illusion have touched everyone; no one in the world is exempt.

rcm.7.72.chaupai.2.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.72.chaupai.2.line: Diseased eyes see a yellow moon. From a moving boat, the shore seems to move.
rcm.7.72.chaupai.2.claim: A person's own defect or motion makes him misjudge what he sees, as one on a moving boat thinks the shore moves.

rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.line: A mother has the boil lanced though the child cries. Some humbling is like that.
rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.misuse: Not every pain is for your good; don't use this to excuse harm done to anyone.
rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.claim: The Lord removes his servant's pride as a mother has her child's boil lanced, ignoring the cries for the sake of the cure.
rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.needs: belief in a loving Lord, and a pain that was a humbling of pride and not harm done by another person

rcm.7.83.chaupai.3.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.83.chaupai.3.line: Every comfort without devotion is like a feast without salt.
rcm.7.83.chaupai.3.claim: Without devotion every virtue and pleasure is tasteless, like many dishes without salt.
rcm.7.83.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader is open to devotion as the answer

rcm.7.87.chaupai.8.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.87.chaupai.8.line: Without knowing, there is no trust. Without trust, there is no love.
rcm.7.87.chaupai.8.claim: Without knowing there is no trust, without trust no love, and without love devotion does not hold.

rcm.7.87.sortha.5.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.87.sortha.5.line: No one finds rest without contentment, any more than a boat moves without water.
rcm.7.87.sortha.5.claim: No one finds rest without natural contentment, however he strains, as a boat cannot move without water.

rcm.1.135.sortha.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.135.sortha.1.line: Old age arrived at home, the cravings stayed, and he grieved for the years spent elsewhere.
rcm.1.135.sortha.1.claim: Manu grieves in old age that his life has passed at home without detachment or devotion to Hari.

rcm.1.141.chaupai.3.speaker: Manu
rcm.1.141.chaupai.3.line: Like a poor man before the wishing tree, we hesitate to ask for what we really want.
rcm.1.141.chaupai.3.claim: One who does not know the giver's greatness hesitates to ask for much, like a poor man before the wishing tree.

rcm.1.153.sortha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.153.sortha.1.line: Even the clever are fooled by a fine look. The peacock sings like nectar and eats snakes.
rcm.1.153.sortha.1.claim: A fine appearance deceives even the clever; the peacock is beautiful and sweet-voiced, and it eats snakes.

rcm.1.180.chhand.4.speaker: Kausalya
rcm.1.180.chhand.4.line: Put away the grand form, child. Just be little with me; there is no joy like it.
rcm.1.180.chhand.4.claim: Kausalya asks the Lord to put away his cosmic form and be simply her child, the joy she counts highest.

rcm.1.196.chaupai.3.speaker: Dasharath
rcm.1.196.chaupai.3.line: Every child is dear as life, and some partings a parent can hardly bear to make.
rcm.1.196.chaupai.3.misuse: Love that never lets go can hold a child back; in the story he does let Ram go.
rcm.1.196.chaupai.3.claim: A father cannot bring himself to send his young son into danger.

rcm.1.258.doha.1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm.1.258.doha.1.line: The capable let their work speak. It is the insecure who keep announcing what they can do.
rcm.1.258.doha.1.claim: The brave show their valour in deeds and do not announce it; cowards facing an enemy talk of their own prowess.

rcm.1.3.chaupai.5.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.3.chaupai.5.line: Good company can change the worst of us; the good keep their light even in bad company.
rcm.1.3.chaupai.5.claim: Good company reforms even the wicked, and the good keep their own nature even in bad company.

rcm.1.54.chaupai.2.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.54.chaupai.2.line: When you know the fault is yours, words fail, and the heart burns quietly like a kiln.
rcm.1.54.chaupai.2.misuse: Guilt is a signal to make amends, not a sentence to burn forever.
rcm.1.54.chaupai.2.claim: Knowing the fault is her own, Sati cannot speak, and her heart burns within like a potter's kiln.

rcm.1.76.doha.1.speaker: Parvati
rcm.1.76.doha.1.line: Others may list the faults. The heart wants the one it has chosen.
rcm.1.76.doha.1.misuse: Choosing for yourself still means listening honestly to those who care.
rcm.1.76.doha.1.claim: Whatever faults others list, the heart wants only the one it has settled on.

rcm.1.8.chaupai.6.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.8.chaupai.6.line: Everyone loves their own work. Rare is the person who is truly glad about someone else's.
rcm.1.8.chaupai.6.claim: Everyone likes their own work; rare is the person who delights in another's.

rcm.2.212.chaupai.1.speaker: Brihaspati
rcm.2.212.chaupai.1.line: You're anxious because of your own interests. The fault isn't theirs; it's your confusion.
rcm.2.212.chaupai.1.claim: Envy's distress comes from one's own self-interest and delusion, not from any fault in the one envied.

rcm.2.253.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.253.chaupai.1.line: Stop torturing yourself with doubts. Love and hostility cannot be hidden; people know which you carry.
rcm.2.253.chaupai.1.claim: Do not torment yourself with baseless reasoning; love and enmity cannot be hidden, and your love is plain.

rcm.2.280.chaupai.4.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.280.chaupai.4.line: Duty and self-interest pull against each other. Hatred is blind, and love can't reason.
rcm.2.280.chaupai.4.claim: Service is the hardest duty because it conflicts with self-interest, and neither hatred nor love can judge clearly.

rcm.2.281.chaupai.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.281.chaupai.1.line: Easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few words, boundless meaning.
rcm.2.281.chaupai.1.claim: Bharat's speech was simple yet deep, gentle yet firm, few in words and vast in meaning.

rcm.2.310.chaupai.4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.2.310.chaupai.4.line: He lived amid the riches like a bee in a champak garden, untouched by them.
rcm.2.310.chaupai.4.claim: Bharat lives amid royal wealth untouched by it, as lovers of Ram give up luxury like something vomited.

rcm.2.54.chaupai.2.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.54.chaupai.2.line: Caught between duty and love, like a snake that can neither swallow nor let go.
rcm.2.54.chaupai.2.claim: Hemmed in by duty on one side and love on the other, a mother can neither keep her son nor let him go.

rcm.2.74.chaupai.3.speaker: Sumitra
rcm.2.74.chaupai.3.line: A mother's send-off: never let attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion rule you, even in dreams.
rcm.2.74.chaupai.3.claim: Never come under attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion; put them aside and serve with mind, deed and word.

rcm.2.93.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.93.chaupai.3.line: There is no duty higher than truth. Abandoning it costs more than anything it saves.
rcm.2.93.chaupai.3.claim: There is no duty equal to truth, and to abandon it brings disgrace in all three worlds.

rcm.3.27.chaupai.5.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.27.chaupai.5.line: For someone whose heart is set on the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach.
rcm.3.27.chaupai.5.claim: For one whose heart is given to others' good, nothing in the world is out of reach.

rcm.3.32.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.32.chaupai.3.line: Be simple and without guile with everyone, neither carried away by joy nor crushed by setbacks.
rcm.3.32.chaupai.3.claim: The ninth devotion is being guileless with all and trusting Ram at heart, without elation or dejection; it is open to anyone.

rcm.3.34.doha.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.34.doha.1.line: Desire, anger and greed can unsettle even the wisest mind in a moment.
rcm.3.34.doha.1.claim: Desire, anger and greed are so strong that they unsettle even sages' minds in an instant.

rcm.4.17.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.17.chaupai.2.line: Contentment dries up greed the way the autumn sun dries the puddles.
rcm.4.17.chaupai.2.claim: Contentment dries up greed, and a heart freed of pride and delusion is clear like autumn water.

rcm.4.17.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.17.chaupai.4.line: Fish panic as the pond shrinks, like a careless household when the money runs out.
rcm.4.17.chaupai.4.misuse: Not a judgement on anyone struggling with money; a nudge to plan for dry seasons.
rcm.4.17.chaupai.4.claim: As ponds shrink the fish grow distressed, like an imprudent householder when the money runs out.

rcm.4.29.chaupai.2.speaker: Sampati
rcm.4.29.chaupai.2.line: My brother turned back from the sun. I, in my pride, flew closer, and my wings burned.
rcm.4.29.chaupai.2.claim: Sampati, in his pride, flew on toward the sun when his brother turned back, and fell with burned wings.

rcm.4.8.chaupai.10.speaker: Sugriva
rcm.4.8.chaupai.10.line: If I fought my brother even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.10.claim: Sugriva, in a moment of dispassion, calls his enemy brother his benefactor, since through him he met Ram.

rcm.4.8.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.8.chaupai.2.line: A friend steers you off the wrong path, speaks of your strengths, and keeps your faults private.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.2.misuse: Keeping faults private means discretion, not covering up harm.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.2.claim: A friend turns you from the wrong path to the right, makes your virtues known and covers your faults.

rcm.4.8.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.8.chaupai.3.line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.3.claim: A true friend gives and takes without suspicion, helps as far as he can, and loves a hundredfold more in hard times.

rcm.4.8.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.8.chaupai.4.line: Sweet to your face, harmful behind your back: it is best to walk away from such a friend.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.4.claim: One who speaks sweetly to your face and works harm behind your back is a false friend best given up.

rcm.5.21.chaupai.3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.21.chaupai.3.line: Wealth with no deep source is a rain-fed river: gone as soon as the rains stop.
rcm.5.21.chaupai.3.claim: Wealth and power of one turned away from Ram are as good as lost, like rivers with no spring that dry after rain.

rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.line: The good still wish you well when you strike them.
rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.misuse: Wishing someone well does not mean staying to be hurt; Vibhishan leaves.
rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.claim: The good do good even to those who harm them; struck by his brother, Vibhishan still tells him where his good lies.
rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.needs: the next doha, where he leaves; goodwill here does not mean staying

rcm.5.4.chaupai.1.speaker: Lankini
rcm.5.4.chaupai.1.line: Walk into the hard task carrying what you love in your heart, and even poison turns to nectar.
rcm.5.4.chaupai.1.claim: Whoever enters hard work holding Ram in the heart finds poison turn to nectar and enemies to friends.

rcm.5.42.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.42.chaupai.3.line: Deceit and tricks win nothing lasting. People with a clean mind are the ones who are trusted.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.3.claim: A person of clean mind reaches Ram, who dislikes deceit, and Ram fears no loss in sheltering even a suspect.

rcm.5.44.chaupai.4.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.44.chaupai.4.line: Better to live in hell than to be stuck in the company of the cruel.
rcm.5.44.chaupai.4.claim: Living in hell is better than being forced into the company of the wicked.

rcm.6.12.chaupai.3.speaker: Prahasta
rcm.6.12.chaupai.3.line: Good advice won't take on someone set on ruin, like medicine on the dying.
rcm.6.12.chaupai.3.claim: Sound advice does not take on one bent on ruin, as medicine fails a person in death's grip.

rcm.6.62.chaupai.4.speaker: Kumbhakarna
rcm.6.62.chaupai.4.line: Blessed, blessed are you, brother. You have become the pride of our family.
rcm.6.62.chaupai.4.claim: Kumbhakarna, though fighting for Ravana, praises Vibhishan for leaving him and calls him the ornament of their clan.

rcm.6.8.chaupai.3.speaker: Mandodari
rcm.6.8.chaupai.3.line: Pick your fights only where your wits and strength can actually win.
rcm.6.8.chaupai.3.claim: Take up enmity only with one you can overcome by wit and strength; Ravana beside Ram is a firefly beside the sun.

rcm.7.108.doha.2.speaker: Shiva
rcm.7.108.doha.2.line: When you see the divine in everyone, who is left to quarrel with?
rcm.7.108.doha.2.claim: Those devoted to Ram's feet, free of desire, pride and anger, see the world as filled with their Lord and oppose no one.

rcm.7.117.chaupai.17.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.117.chaupai.17.line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.17.claim: Possessiveness, envy, the swings of elation and dejection, and burning at another's happiness are diseases of the mind.

rcm.7.117.chaupai.6.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.117.chaupai.6.line: We throw away the philosopher's stone and take shards of glass in exchange.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.6.claim: To have a human body and not worship Hari is to throw away the philosopher's stone and take glass shards.

rcm.7.117.chaupai.7.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.117.chaupai.7.line: No sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.7.claim: There is no sorrow like poverty and no joy like meeting the good, whose nature is to help others.

rcm.7.20.chaupai.2.speaker: Angad
rcm.7.20.chaupai.2.line: You are my teacher, my father and mother now. Where would I go?
rcm.7.20.chaupai.2.claim: Angad, fatherless, begs Ram not to send him away: you are my lord, teacher, father and mother.

rcm.7.22.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.22.chaupai.2.line: You are my friend, a brother to me. Keep visiting, always.
rcm.7.22.chaupai.2.claim: Ram calls the boatman chief his friend and a brother equal to Bharat, and asks him to keep visiting.

rcm.7.41.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.41.chaupai.2.line: Envy burns at another's success and feasts on gossip as if it found treasure.
rcm.7.41.chaupai.2.claim: The wicked burn at the sight of another's prosperity and rejoice on hearing others slandered.

rcm.7.48.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.48.chaupai.1.line: No grand effort needed: a simple nature, an honest mind, and contentment with what comes.
rcm.7.48.chaupai.1.claim: The path of devotion needs no yoga, sacrifice or fasting, only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness and contentment.

rcm.7.73.chaupai.3.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.73.chaupai.3.line: Pride is the root of countless pains and every sorrow.
rcm.7.73.chaupai.3.claim: Ram never lets pride stay in his devotee, because pride is the root of rebirth and the giver of every sorrow.

rcm.7.86.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.86.chaupai.1.line: One parent, many children, each different in gifts and nature, and the love for all is the same.
rcm.7.86.chaupai.1.claim: A father loves all his differently gifted sons alike, yet the one devoted to him in thought, word and deed is dearest.

rcm.7.95.chaupai.4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.95.chaupai.4.line: Parents call their children and teach them only what fills the stomach.
rcm.7.95.chaupai.4.claim: In a degraded age teachers take money without removing sorrow, and parents teach children only what fills the belly.

rcm.2.211.chaupai.2.speaker: Brihaspati
rcm.2.211.chaupai.2.line: The world runs on action: as you do, so you reap.
rcm.2.211.chaupai.2.misuse: Read as encouragement to act well, not as judgement on anyone's misfortune.
rcm.2.211.chaupai.2.claim: Though Ram is impartial, he has made action the law of the world: as one acts, so one tastes the fruit.

rcm.4.15.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.15.chaupai.3.line: Little streams overflow after one rain, the way small minds swagger after a little money.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.3.claim: A petty person swaggers on a little wealth as small streams burst their banks after rain.

rcm.2.165.doha.1.speaker: Vasishtha
rcm.2.165.doha.1.line: Loss and gain, life and death, praise and blame: much of it was never in your hands.
rcm.2.165.doha.1.misuse: Said to lift a grieving son's guilt, not to excuse inaction. Your effort is still one of the five causes of any outcome (Gita 18.14).
rcm.2.165.doha.1.claim: What is destined is powerful: loss and gain, life and death, honour and dishonour lie in the Creator's hands.
rcm.2.165.doha.1.needs: said to lift guilt after a loss, never to explain away a wrong done by someone

bg.18.16.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.16.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
bg.18.16.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.
bg.18.16.claim: Since action has five causes, one who through untrained understanding sees the self alone as doer does not see.

vr.6.21.6.speaker: Ram
vr.6.21.6.line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.
vr.6.21.6.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.
vr.6.21.6.claim: Calm, forbearance, straightforwardness and gentle speech are taken for weakness by those without virtue.

vr.6.21.11.speaker: Ram
vr.6.21.11.line: My patience was taken for weakness. Gentle asking didn't work. Lakshman, bring my bow.
vr.6.21.11.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.
vr.6.21.11.claim: Because I am forbearing the ocean thinks me incapable; gentle means have failed, so bring my bow.

rcm.5.55.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating Ram)
rcm.5.55.doha.1.line: Three days of humble asking, ignored. Some people only listen once they see you'll act.
rcm.5.55.doha.1.misuse: About a stubborn party who ignores repeated humble requests, not a rule for love or for people close to you. Patience comes first; Ram waited three days and forgave the ocean the moment it came.
rcm.5.55.doha.1.claim: When three days of humble request are ignored, Ram speaks in anger: without fear there is no regard.
rcm.5.55.doha.1.needs: the three days of asking before and the forgiveness after; never about love between people close to each other

bh.niti.3.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.3.line: The ignorant can be taught and the expert persuaded. The half-knower not even God can convince.
bh.niti.3.misuse: Not a licence to dismiss everyone who disagrees with you as a half-knower; check yourself first.
bh.niti.3.claim: The ignorant and the expert are easily satisfied, but one puffed up with a scrap of knowledge cannot be satisfied by anyone.

bh.niti.4.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.4.line: You can pull a gem from a crocodile's jaws, but you cannot change a mind that has dug in.
bh.niti.4.misuse: Use it to stop exhausting yourself in arguments, not to write people off.
bh.niti.4.claim: Impossible feats may be done, but the mind of an obstinate fool cannot be won over.

bh.niti.8.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.8.line: When I knew a little, I thought I knew everything. Learning from the wise, my fever of pride broke.
bh.niti.8.claim: Knowing little I was blind with pride; learning from the wise I saw my ignorance and pride left like a fever.

bh.niti.14.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.14.line: Better to roam wild hills with animals than to live in a palace among fools.
bh.niti.14.misuse: About the company you choose to keep, not contempt for people.
bh.niti.14.claim: Wandering wild mountains with forest creatures is better than the company of fools even in Indra's palace.

bh.niti.16.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.16.line: Learning is wealth no thief can see. It grows when you give it away and never perishes.
bh.niti.16.claim: Learning is an inner wealth that no thief sees, that grows when given and never perishes.

bh.niti.18.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.18.line: Fate can take away the swan's lake. It cannot take its gift of telling milk from water.
bh.niti.18.claim: An angry fate may take the swan's lotus lake but cannot take its skill of separating milk from water.

bh.niti.19.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.19.line: Jewellery wears out. Well-chosen speech is the one ornament that lasts.
bh.niti.19.claim: Ornaments wear away; refined speech is the one adornment that truly adorns a person.

bh.niti.20.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.20.line: In a foreign land, what you have learned is your family: a treasure no one can see.
bh.niti.20.misuse: The last phrase is a poet's jab, not a judgement on people without schooling.
bh.niti.20.claim: Learning is a person's hidden treasure, teacher, kin in foreign lands and highest deity, honoured above wealth.

bh.niti.21.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.21.line: With patience, who needs armour? With anger, who needs enemies? With a true friend, who needs medicine?
bh.niti.21.misuse: Forbearance protects you; it is not permission for others to keep hurting you.
bh.niti.21.claim: With forbearance no armour is needed, with anger no enemy, with a friend no medicine, with learning no wealth.

bh.niti.23.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.23.line: Good company clears the mind, puts truth in your speech and lifts your spirit. What does it not do?
bh.niti.23.claim: Good company removes dullness, brings truth to speech, raises dignity, clears the mind and spreads good name.

bh.niti.25.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.25.line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
bh.niti.25.claim: A good child, loving spouse, gracious employer, true friend and untroubled mind come to one with whom Hari is pleased.

bh.niti.26.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.26.line: Harm no one, take nothing that isn't yours, speak truly, give in time, cut craving, be kind to all.
bh.niti.26.claim: Non-killing, not taking others' wealth, truth, timely giving, checking craving, humility and compassion are the path common to all scriptures.

bh.niti.27.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.27.line: Some never start for fear of obstacles; some quit when obstacles hit. The best keep going.
bh.niti.27.misuse: Perseverance is not refusing ever to change course; weigh honestly whether the goal still deserves you.
bh.niti.27.claim: The low never begin for fear of obstacles, the middling stop when hindered, and the best never abandon what they began.

bh.niti.28.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.28.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
bh.niti.28.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.
bh.niti.28.claim: The good do not beg from the wicked or from a poor friend, earn justly, and stand tall in adversity.

bh.niti.31.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.31.line: The dog grovels before whoever feeds it. The elephant waits with quiet dignity.
bh.niti.31.misuse: Dignity, not arrogance: it does not mean making others beg you.
bh.niti.31.claim: A dog grovels before whoever feeds it, while the elephant looks on steadily and eats only when coaxed.

bh.niti.40.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.40.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
bh.niti.40.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.
bh.niti.40.claim: The same person with the same senses, mind and speech becomes someone else the moment wealth's warmth is gone.

bh.niti.41.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.41.line: Have money and suddenly you are wise, well-born and charming. All virtues seem to lodge in gold.
bh.niti.41.misuse: Satire on the world's flattery, not advice to chase money.
bh.niti.41.claim: Whoever has wealth is called well-born, learned and handsome; all virtues take shelter in gold.

bh.niti.42.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.42.line: Affection fades with distance, friendship without warmth, wealth with carelessness, a child with spoiling.
bh.niti.42.misuse: Distance strains affection; it does not doom it. The verse is a call to tend what you love.
bh.niti.42.claim: Each good thing is ruined by its own neglect: affection by absence, friendship by coldness, wealth by carelessness.

bh.niti.43.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.43.line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.
bh.niti.43.claim: Wealth has three ends, giving, enjoying and loss; what is neither given nor enjoyed is lost.

bh.niti.45.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.45.line: Starving, a handful of grain is everything. Full, the whole earth looks like straw.
bh.niti.45.claim: A person's own condition makes the same things seem great or small.

bh.niti.46.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.46.line: Want results from your people? Nourish them first, as you feed the calf before milking.
bh.niti.46.claim: A ruler who wants the earth's yield must first nourish the people, as a calf is fed before milking.

bh.niti.49.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.49.line: A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
bh.niti.49.misuse: Not a reason to stop working or asking for fair pay; a reason not to grovel.
bh.niti.49.claim: One receives the wealth fate has written whether in a desert or on Meru, so be steady and do not grovel.

bh.niti.51.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.51.line: Some clouds bring rain, some only thunder. Don't plead with everyone you meet.
bh.niti.51.claim: Not all clouds give rain, so do not speak pleading words before everyone you see.

bh.niti.53.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.53.line: Avoid a cruel person even if brilliant. A snake wearing a jewel still bites.
bh.niti.53.misuse: It means keeping distance from people who harm you, not labelling everyone who annoys you.
bh.niti.53.claim: A wicked person should be avoided even if learned, as a snake is dangerous even with a jewel.

bh.niti.54.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.54.line: To a spiteful critic, modesty is dullness and courage is cruelty. No virtue escapes them.
bh.niti.54.misuse: Not every criticism is spite; use it to stop taking malice personally, not to ignore fair feedback.
bh.niti.54.claim: The wicked brand every virtue as a fault, so no quality of the good escapes their smear.

bh.niti.55.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.55.line: If your mind is pure, what need of pilgrimage? If you speak truth, what need of penance?
bh.niti.55.misuse: 'Disgrace is worse than death' is old rhetoric about honour, never a reason to harm yourself.
bh.niti.55.claim: A pure mind needs no pilgrimage and truth no austerity; greed is fault enough and disgrace worse than death.

bh.niti.57.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.57.line: Fire burns even the hand that feeds it. A raging temper keeps no one close.
bh.niti.57.claim: Fierce-tempered rulers have no one who is truly their own, as fire burns even the priest who feeds it.

bh.niti.58.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.58.line: Quiet, you're dull; talkative, a show-off; patient, weak. Serving a boss is harder than yoga.
bh.niti.58.claim: Whatever a servant does is faulted, silent or speaking, near or far, patient or not; service is harder than yoga.

bh.niti.60.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.60.line: Bad friendships start big and shrink. Good ones start small and keep growing, like afternoon shade.
bh.niti.60.claim: The friendship of the wicked starts large and shrinks; that of the good starts small and grows, like shade.

bh.niti.62.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.62.line: Seek good company, delight in others' gifts, love learning, master yourself: bow to such people.
bh.niti.62.claim: Those who love good company, others' merits, learning and self-mastery, and shun the wicked, are worthy of reverence.

bh.niti.63.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.63.line: Steady in bad times, forbearing in good ones, eloquent among people, eager to learn: that is greatness.
bh.niti.63.claim: Steadiness in adversity, forbearance in success, eloquence, courage and love of learning are natural to the great.

bh.niti.64.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.64.line: Give in secret, stay quiet about your favours, praise others' help aloud, stay humble in wealth.
bh.niti.64.claim: The good give in secret, welcome guests, stay silent about their favours, proclaim others' help and stay humble in wealth.

bh.niti.66.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.66.line: In good times be soft as a lotus. In hard times be firm as mountain rock.
bh.niti.66.claim: The heart of the great is soft as a lotus in prosperity and hard as rock in adversity.

bh.niti.67.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.67.line: One drop vanishes on hot iron, shines on a lotus leaf, becomes a pearl in a shell. Company shapes us.
bh.niti.67.claim: The same drop vanishes on hot iron, shines on a lotus leaf, becomes a pearl in an oyster; qualities follow company.

bh.niti.68.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.68.line: A true friend is the same in your troubles as in your good times.
bh.niti.68.misuse: The verse's picture of a wife is one-sided; the card uses only the line on friendship.
bh.niti.68.claim: A true son pleases his father, a true wife seeks her husband's good, a true friend is constant in trouble and joy.

bh.niti.70.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.70.line: They rise by bowing, show their worth by praising others, and silence slanderers with patience.
bh.niti.70.misuse: Patience with slander is strength; it does not mean staying silent about abuse.
bh.niti.70.claim: The good rise by bowing, show their worth by praising others, and shame slanderers by forbearance alone.

bh.niti.71.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.71.line: Fruit-laden trees bow low. The truly successful are not puffed up.
bh.niti.71.claim: Trees bend with fruit and clouds hang low with rain; likewise the good are not made haughty by prosperity.

bh.niti.72.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.72.line: Ears shine by listening, hands by giving, the body by helping others, not by ornaments.
bh.niti.72.claim: Learning, giving and helping others adorn the ear, hand and body, not earrings, bracelets or sandal paste.

bh.niti.73.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.73.line: A true friend stops you doing wrong, keeps your secrets, praises you, and stays when trouble comes.
bh.niti.73.claim: A true friend restrains you from wrong, guards your secrets, makes your merits known, and does not leave in trouble.

bh.niti.75.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.75.line: Some help at their own cost, some when convenient, some harm for gain. Some harm for nothing at all.
bh.niti.75.claim: Some serve others at their own cost, some when convenient, some harm for gain, and some harm for no reason.

bh.niti.76.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.76.line: Milk boils over to follow water into the fire, and settles when water returns. That is friendship.
bh.niti.76.claim: Milk and water each give themselves for the other in the fire; such is the friendship of the good.

bh.niti.78.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.78.line: Cut craving, forgive, drop arrogance, speak truth, win over even enemies, be kind to those suffering.
bh.niti.78.misuse: Winning over an enemy is not the same as tolerating harm.
bh.niti.78.claim: Cut craving, practise forbearance, drop arrogance, speak truth, honour the worthy, conciliate enemies and pity the suffering.

bh.niti.79.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.79.line: How rare are those who make a mountain out of the smallest good in others.
bh.niti.79.claim: Rare are the good who magnify the smallest merit in others and rejoice in it.

bh.niti.81.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.81.line: The gods churned past jewels and past poison until they reached nectar. The steady don't stop halfway.
bh.niti.81.misuse: Steadiness is not refusing to reassess a goal.
bh.niti.81.claim: The steadfast do not stop short of their settled aim, as the gods churned past jewels and poison to nectar.

bh.niti.82.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.82.line: Floor or bed, greens or fine rice, rags or silk: someone set on a goal counts neither.
bh.niti.82.claim: A person of spirit set on a purpose counts neither hardship nor comfort.

bh.niti.83.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.83.line: Courtesy adorns power, humility adorns learning, calm adorns knowledge. Character adorns everything.
bh.niti.83.claim: Each strength has its ornament, as forbearance adorns the powerful and humility the learned, and character adorns all.

bh.niti.84.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.84.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
bh.niti.84.claim: Whether praised or blamed, rich or poor, dying today or ages hence, the steadfast do not leave the just path.

bh.niti.85.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.85.line: A ball knocked down bounces back up. For good people, setbacks rarely last.
bh.niti.85.misuse: Not a promise that suffering is always short, or that people who suffer long did something wrong.
bh.niti.85.claim: A ball struck down rises again; the misfortunes of those of good conduct do not last.

bh.niti.86.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.86.line: Laziness is the enemy living in your own body. There is no friend like effort.
bh.niti.86.misuse: Rest is not laziness; burnout needs rest, not more effort.
bh.niti.86.claim: Laziness is the great enemy within the body and effort the best friend; one who works does not sink.

bh.niti.87.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.87.line: A cut tree grows back; the waning moon fills again. Remembering this, the wise do not despair.
bh.niti.87.claim: A cut tree grows again and the waned moon waxes; reflecting on this the good are not tormented.

bh.niti.90.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.90.line: Much is shaped by past actions. Still, think carefully before you act.
bh.niti.90.misuse: Karma is not a reason to stop choosing well; the verse's own point is the second line.
bh.niti.90.claim: Though results depend on past action and even the mind follows it, the wise must still act after careful thought.

bh.niti.93.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.93.line: Fate shapes a person full of every goodness, then takes them in a moment. Alas, what folly.
bh.niti.93.claim: Fate creates a jewel of a person and then breaks him in a moment; what folly in the Creator.

bh.niti.95.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.95.line: Even fate only delivers the fruit of actions. Bow to what you do.
bh.niti.95.claim: Gods and fate only deliver the fruit of action, so salutations to action, over which fate has no power.

bh.niti.100.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.100.line: Weigh the outcome before you act. Rash deeds leave a thorn that burns for years.
bh.niti.100.claim: The wise weigh the outcome before acting, for a deed done in haste burns the heart like a thorn until death.

bh.niti.102.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.102.line: Dive deep, climb high, master every skill: what is not meant to be still will not happen.
bh.niti.102.misuse: Show with the verse on effort (Niti 86). This is for letting go after trying, not for not trying.
bh.niti.102.claim: However great the effort, what is not to be does not happen and what is to be cannot fail.
bh.niti.102.needs: That the reader has already tried fully

bh.niti.104.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.104.line: What is real loss? Missing your moment. Who is a hero? One who has mastered himself.
bh.niti.104.misuse: 'Happiness is not living abroad' voices homesickness; it is not a verdict on emigrants.
bh.niti.104.claim: Real gain is good company, real loss a missed moment, the real hero one who has mastered his senses.

bh.niti.105.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.105.line: The world is lit, here and there, by people poor in harsh words and rich in kind ones.
bh.niti.105.claim: Rare are those poor in harsh words, rich in kind ones, content with their own spouse and free of slander.

bh.niti.106.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.106.line: Turn a torch upside down and its flame still rises. Steadiness survives humiliation.
bh.niti.106.claim: The steadiness of the steadfast cannot be wiped out by mistreatment, as an inverted torch still burns upward.

bh.niti.107.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.niti.107.line: Whoever isn't burned by anger or dragged by greed has conquered the whole world.
bh.niti.107.claim: One whose mind is not pierced by desire, burned by anger or dragged by greed conquers the three worlds.

bh.vairagya.3.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.3.line: I dug, sailed, flattered kings, chased every scheme, and gained not a broken coin. Enough, craving.
bh.vairagya.3.claim: I tried every scheme for wealth and gained not even a broken cowrie; craving, be satisfied now.

bh.vairagya.4.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.4.line: I swallowed insults and forced laughter with an empty heart. Hope, how much longer will you make me dance?
bh.vairagya.4.claim: I bore insults, hid tears and laughed with an empty mind to please the rich; hope, how long must I dance?

bh.vairagya.6.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.6.line: We forgave, but not out of forgiveness; gave up comforts, but not out of contentment, and missed the fruit.
bh.vairagya.6.claim: We did everything the sages do, forbearing, renouncing, enduring, but for the wrong reasons, and so missed its fruit.

bh.vairagya.7.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.7.line: We didn't enjoy pleasures; they consumed us. Time didn't pass; we did. Craving never aged; we did.
bh.vairagya.7.claim: Pleasures were not enjoyed, we were consumed; time did not pass, we passed; craving did not age, we aged.

bh.vairagya.8.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.8.line: Wrinkles on the face, grey in the hair, slack limbs. Only craving stays young.
bh.vairagya.8.claim: The face wrinkles, the hair greys and the limbs slacken, but craving alone grows young.

bh.vairagya.9.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.9.line: Friends gone, eyes dim, rising with a stick, and still the body flinches at the thought of death.
bh.vairagya.9.claim: Desire gone, respect gone, friends dead, eyes dim, rising on a stick, the body still starts at death.

bh.vairagya.10.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.10.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
bh.vairagya.10.claim: Hope is a river of wishes with waves of craving and high banks of worry, crossed only by the pure in mind.

bh.vairagya.12.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.12.line: Every pleasure leaves someday. Released freely, it brings peace; torn away, it brings torment.
bh.vairagya.12.misuse: About things and pleasures; not advice to leave people before they leave you.
bh.vairagya.12.claim: Pleasures leave in any case; when they leave by themselves they torment, and when given up willingly they bring peace.

bh.vairagya.18.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.18.line: The moth doesn't know the flame burns. We know, and still we don't let go.
bh.vairagya.18.claim: The moth and the fish perish unknowing, but we know the danger and still do not let go of desires.

bh.vairagya.19.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.19.line: Drinking when thirsty is relief, not joy. We mistake easing a craving for happiness.
bh.vairagya.19.claim: People mistake the relief of a craving, like drinking when thirsty, for happiness.

bh.vairagya.21.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.21.line: A proud man would never beg for himself. For his hungry family, he swallows his pride.
bh.vairagya.21.claim: A self-respecting man would never beg for his own belly; he does it only on seeing his hungry family.

bh.vairagya.29.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.29.line: The contented already have their joy; the greedy never quench their thirst. Who is wealth really for?
bh.vairagya.29.claim: The contented already have unbroken joy and the greedy never end their craving, so wealth serves neither.

bh.vairagya.31.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.31.line: Wealth fears loss, fame fears disgrace, beauty fears age. Only letting go is free of fear.
bh.vairagya.31.misuse: Dispassion is not giving up on life; it is holding things without clutching.
bh.vairagya.31.claim: Every worldly good carries its own fear; dispassion alone is free of fear.

bh.vairagya.33.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.33.line: Illness, setbacks, loss: what has fate ever made that lasts?
bh.vairagya.33.claim: Illness uproots health, disaster follows fortune and death takes all that is born; fate has made nothing stable.

bh.vairagya.35.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.35.line: Pleasures flash like lightning; life trembles like water on a lotus leaf. Turn inward soon.
bh.vairagya.35.claim: Pleasures flicker like lightning and life is fragile as water on a lotus leaf, so set the mind on yoga soon.

bh.vairagya.36.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.36.line: Life is a wave, youth a few days, money a passing thought. Even embraces end.
bh.vairagya.36.claim: Life, youth, wealth, pleasure and even a loved one's embrace are brief, so fix the mind on Brahman.

bh.vairagya.38.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.38.line: Life leaks away like water from a cracked pot, and still we spend it hurting each other.
bh.vairagya.38.claim: Old age threatens, disease strikes and life leaks like water from a cracked pot, yet people still do what harms them.

bh.vairagya.41.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.41.line: That city, that king, that court, those stories: all of it now only memory. Bow to Time.
bh.vairagya.41.claim: That city, king, court and its stories have all passed into memory by Time's power; salutations to Time.

bh.vairagya.42.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.42.line: A full house, then one person, then many, then no one. Time plays dice with our lives.
bh.vairagya.42.claim: Time plays dice with living beings, filling and emptying houses as night and day roll.

bh.vairagya.43.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.43.line: Each sunrise takes a day from us, and, busy with work, we never notice time slipping by.
bh.vairagya.43.claim: Life shrinks each day unnoticed under the weight of tasks; the world is drunk on the wine of heedlessness.

bh.vairagya.44.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.44.line: Same night, same day, the same tasks on repeat. We run in circles and call it living.
bh.vairagya.44.claim: Night and day repeat with the same tasks, and worn by this round we still feel no shame at it.

bh.vairagya.47.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.47.line: I neither learned, nor earned, nor truly cared for my parents. Time slipped away chasing scraps.
bh.vairagya.47.claim: I gained no learning, earned no wealth, did not serve my parents with care; my time went chasing scraps.

bh.vairagya.48.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.48.line: Our parents are memories, our childhood friends too. Now we stand like trees on a crumbling riverbank.
bh.vairagya.48.claim: Our parents and childhood companions are now memories, and we stand like trees on a crumbling riverbank.

bh.vairagya.49.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.49.line: Half of life goes in sleep, much in childhood and age, the rest in illness and serving others.
bh.vairagya.49.claim: Half of life passes in sleep, more in childhood and age, the rest in illness and service; where is happiness?

bh.vairagya.50.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.50.line: A child, a lover, broke, then rich, then old: like an actor, we exit behind the curtain.
bh.vairagya.50.claim: A person plays child, lover, pauper and rich man in turn, then like an actor exits behind death's curtain.

bh.vairagya.51.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.51.line: You have wealth, I have learning. If you turn away from me, I need nothing from you.
bh.vairagya.51.claim: You have wealth and I have wisdom and fame; if you turn from me, I want nothing from you.

bh.vairagya.53.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.53.line: When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor? The poor one has the biggest craving.
bh.vairagya.53.claim: When the mind is content there is no rich or poor; the poor one is he whose craving is vast.

bh.vairagya.57.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.57.line: Others ruled whole worlds and gave them away like straw. Why this fever of pride over a few towns?
bh.vairagya.57.claim: Others created, ruled and gave away whole worlds, so pride over lordship of a few towns is a fever.

bh.vairagya.61.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.61.line: Why exhaust yourself daily winning others' approval? Settle inside, and your own clarity grants every wish.
bh.vairagya.61.claim: The heart wears itself out pleasing others, when its own inner clarity would fulfil every wish.

bh.vairagya.62.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.62.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
bh.vairagya.62.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.
bh.vairagya.62.claim: The mind should rest, since what will be will be; not recalling the past or planning the future, one takes what comes.
bh.vairagya.62.needs: That one's part has already been done

bh.vairagya.67.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.67.line: Got every comfort: so what? Beat your rivals: so what? Lived for ages: so what?
bh.vairagya.67.claim: Wealth gained, enemies beaten, friends won, even bodies lasting an age: what of it?

bh.vairagya.70.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.70.line: Mind, you roam the underworld, the sky and every direction. Why never turn to the stillness within?
bh.vairagya.70.claim: The restless mind roams everywhere yet never remembers the pure Brahman, its own self, where it would find peace.

bh.vairagya.71.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.71.line: Scripture and ritual without inner peace is just trading. Seek the joy within.
bh.vairagya.71.misuse: Not a dismissal of scripture; a warning against religion as a transaction.
bh.vairagya.71.claim: Scriptures and rites that aim only at heaven are mere trade beside entry into the bliss of one's own self.

bh.vairagya.73.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.73.line: In old age, family stops listening and even a son turns cold. Alas for the aged.
bh.vairagya.73.misuse: A lament, not a prediction; read it as a call to keep listening to the old.
bh.vairagya.73.claim: In old age the body fails, relatives ignore one's words, and even one's son turns hostile.

bh.vairagya.75.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.75.line: While you are healthy, do what matters most. No one digs a well once the house is burning.
bh.vairagya.75.claim: While the body is healthy, age far off, senses sound and life not run down, the wise should strive hard for their highest good; no one digs a well once the house burns.
bh.vairagya.75.needs: atma-shreyas is the self's highest good, not any worthwhile goal

bh.vairagya.76.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.76.line: Retreat, family, study or art? We cannot choose, and a life lasts only a few blinks.
bh.vairagya.76.claim: We do not know whether to choose austerity, family life, study or poetry, in a life that lasts a few blinks.

bh.vairagya.82.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.82.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
bh.vairagya.82.claim: Freedom to move, food without humiliation, noble company, calming learning and a quiet mind are the fruit of some great austerity.

bh.vairagya.84.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.84.line: I see no real difference between Shiva and Vishnu; still, my heart goes to Shiva.
bh.vairagya.84.claim: There is no difference in essence between Shiva and Vishnu, yet my devotion rests in Shiva.

bh.vairagya.92.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.92.line: The ocean is not stirred by a small fish's flick. Petty things needn't shake you.
bh.vairagya.92.claim: To the high-minded the universe is a small ring with nothing to covet, as a fish's flick does not disturb the ocean.

bh.vairagya.94.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.94.line: Earth for a bed, an arm for a pillow, the moon for a lamp: the content sleep like kings.
bh.vairagya.94.claim: With earth as bed, arm as pillow and moon as lamp, the sage wedded to renunciation sleeps happy as a king.

bh.vairagya.96.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.96.line: Let people argue about who you are. Walk on, neither angry nor flattered.
bh.vairagya.96.misuse: The verse sets caste labels aside as other people's chatter; it does not endorse them.
bh.vairagya.96.claim: Yogis go their way neither angry nor pleased while people argue aloud about who and what they are.

bh.vairagya.100.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh.vairagya.100.line: Mother Earth, Father Wind, Friend Fire, Kin Water, Brother Sky: my last bow, with thanks.
bh.vairagya.100.claim: With a last bow of thanks to earth, wind, fire, water and sky, I merge into the supreme Brahman.

yv.1.1.7.speaker: Agastya
yv.1.1.7.line: A bird flies on two wings. You need both understanding and action to get anywhere that matters.
yv.1.1.7.claim: As a bird flies on two wings, the highest state is reached through knowledge and action together.

yv.1.10.9.speaker: Rama's attendant
yv.1.10.9.line: Ever since he came back from the trip, he hasn't been himself.
yv.1.10.9.claim: Ever since Rama returned from his pilgrimage he has been low in spirit.

yv.1.10.19.speaker: Rama's attendant
yv.1.10.19.line: He no longer laughs at jokes, enjoys pleasures, or stays with his work. He just goes quiet.
yv.1.10.19.misuse: If this describes you for weeks, talk to someone you trust or a doctor. Rama too was helped by others.
yv.1.10.19.claim: He does not brighten at jokes, sink into pleasures or stay with his duties; he only keeps silent.

yv.1.12.15.speaker: Rama
yv.1.12.15.line: What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?
yv.1.12.15.misuse: Rama's question opens the teaching; it isn't the answer. Follow it with 6a.115.43 or 1.30.17.
yv.1.12.15.claim: What is kingship or pleasure to me? Who am I, and what is this that has come about?

yv.1.12.22.speaker: Rama
yv.1.12.22.line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
yv.1.12.22.misuse: Holding tears in is not strength. Rama's healing began when he finally said it aloud.
yv.1.12.22.claim: My heart is packed with the stones of sorrow, yet I do not weep, out of fear of my own people.

yv.1.13.8.speaker: Rama
yv.1.13.8.line: People stay gentle with friends and strangers alike, until money hardens them.
yv.1.13.8.claim: People stay gentle with their own and with strangers only until wealth hardens them.

yv.1.13.11.speaker: Rama
yv.1.13.11.line: Rich and still respected, brave and not boastful, powerful and fair: these three are rare.
yv.1.13.11.claim: A wealthy person beyond reproach, a brave one who does not boast, and a ruler who sees all alike are rare.

yv.1.14.10.speaker: Rama
yv.1.14.10.line: A life is truly lived when it reaches what is worth reaching, and leaves no grief behind.
yv.1.14.10.claim: That alone is called living by which what is worth attaining is attained and one grieves no more.

yv.1.16.3.speaker: Rama
yv.1.16.3.line: The mind is a wicker basket in water: pour in riches, and it still never fills.
yv.1.16.3.claim: The mind is never filled within, even by great riches, like a wicker basket dipped in water.

yv.1.16.22.speaker: Rama
yv.1.16.22.line: The mind pounces on a task like a bird on food, then drops it like a bored child's toy.
yv.1.16.22.claim: The mind swoops on tasks like a bird on meat and a moment later drops them like a child's toy.

yv.1.16.25.speaker: Rama
yv.1.16.25.line: Your world rises and falls with your mind. Tend to it with care.
yv.1.16.25.claim: The mind is the cause of things; the world exists and fades with it, so it must be treated with effort.

yv.1.17.14.speaker: Rama
yv.1.17.14.line: Craving leads us around like a bullock on a rope, knotted inside and hard to cut.
yv.1.17.14.claim: Craving, knotted within and hard to cut, drags a person along as a rope drags a bullock.

yv.1.17.43.speaker: Rama
yv.1.17.43.line: Let go of worry and most sorrow goes with it. That is the cure for craving.
yv.1.17.43.claim: People shed all sorrow by giving up brooding; giving up brooding is the remedy for the sickness of craving.

yv.1.17.50.speaker: Rama
yv.1.17.50.line: Craving can shrink even the wisest, bravest, steadiest person to a blade of grass in a moment.
yv.1.17.50.claim: Craving alone reduces even the wise, brave and steady to a blade of grass in an instant.

yv.1.26.11.speaker: Rama
yv.1.26.11.line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
yv.1.26.11.misuse: Not a reason to blame yourself. Vasishtha's answer is that the same mind can lift itself.
yv.1.26.11.claim: The senses are the enemies; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.

yv.1.26.21.speaker: Rama
yv.1.26.21.line: Bad company comes easily; good company is rare and hard to find.
yv.1.26.21.claim: Steadiness gives way, people keep rising and falling; bad company is easy to find and good company rare.

yv.1.26.39.speaker: Rama
yv.1.26.39.line: The happy ones stay cool inside, help others, and feel others' pain as their own.
yv.1.26.39.claim: Only the awakened are happy: cool within, working for others' good and moved by others' pain.

yv.1.27.9.speaker: Rama
yv.1.27.9.line: Winning battles isn't real bravery. The brave are those who ride out the waves of their own mind.
yv.1.27.9.claim: True heroes cross the ocean of body and senses with its waves of mind, more than the ocean of battle.

yv.1.27.19.speaker: Rama
yv.1.27.19.line: After a day of running around, who sleeps well if nothing good was done in it?
yv.1.27.19.claim: Who can sleep at night after a day of wandering that held none of the good work the wise rely on?

yv.1.28.17.speaker: Rama
yv.1.28.17.line: Those days, those people, that wealth, those deeds are memories now. We too will pass soon.
yv.1.28.17.misuse: Not a call to despair; it wakes Rama up to what matters now.
yv.1.28.17.claim: Those days, those great ones, that wealth and those deeds have all become memory; we too go in a moment.

yv.1.29.22.speaker: Rama
yv.1.29.22.line: There is no trouble that good people's company can't ease, as moonlight eases the night.
yv.1.29.22.claim: No trouble of the mind fails to fade in the company of the noble-minded, as night's darkness fades before the moon.

yv.1.30.17.speaker: Rama
yv.1.30.17.line: How do you live and work fully in the world and stay untouched, like water on a lotus leaf?
yv.1.30.17.claim: How can a person live and act in the world and not be bound, like water on a lotus leaf?

yv.1.31.7.speaker: Rama
yv.1.31.7.line: Nothing is so small or dull that a wise mind can't make it beautiful.
yv.1.31.7.claim: Nothing on earth or in heaven is so trivial that the wise cannot make it delightful.

yv.1.31.17.speaker: Rama
yv.1.31.17.line: Teach me how to keep working in the world without the work filling me with sorrow.
yv.1.31.17.claim: Tell me the method by which sorrow does not come to me while I carry on with life's work.

yv.2.4.12.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.4.12.line: Want it, work for it step by step, and you will get there, unless you quit halfway.
yv.2.4.12.misuse: Effort shapes results, but not every outcome is yours to control; see 2.6.21.
yv.2.4.12.claim: Whoever wants a thing and works for it step by step surely attains it, unless he turns back halfway.

yv.2.4.17.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.4.17.line: Your past effort shaped today; your effort today can quickly change what the past set in motion.
yv.2.4.17.misuse: You are not stuck with your past. It does not mean every hardship is your own doing.
yv.2.4.17.claim: Effort is of two kinds, past and present, and past effort is quickly overcome by present effort.

yv.2.5.5.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.5.5.line: Your past and present efforts butt heads like two rams. Make today's the stronger one.
yv.2.5.5.claim: Past and present effort fight like two rams and the weaker yields, so strive so that today's effort wins.

yv.2.5.12.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.5.12.line: Yesterday's mistake can be undone by what you do well today.
yv.2.5.12.claim: Past faults are certainly stilled by present virtues, as yesterday's fault is undone by today's good.

yv.2.5.20.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.5.20.line: 'Fate made me do it' is what a tired mind says. Good fortune turns away from that excuse.
yv.2.5.20.misuse: Aimed at using fate as an excuse to stop trying, not at anyone grieving a loss they couldn't prevent (see 2.6.21).
yv.2.5.20.claim: 'Fate drives me' is the talk of ruined minds; fortune turns away from those who look only to the unseen.

yv.2.5.30.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.5.30.line: If not for laziness, who wouldn't be learned and well off?
yv.2.5.30.misuse: About your own sloth, not a judgment on people who are poor; poverty has many causes.
yv.2.5.30.claim: But for laziness, who would not be wealthy or learned? Through laziness the earth is full of the poor and dull.

yv.2.6.1.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.6.1.line: Fate is only your past effort. Put it aside and lift yourself with good people and good books.
yv.2.6.1.misuse: Fate here means your own past choices, not a curse, and it can be changed. Not 'you caused your suffering'.
yv.2.6.1.claim: Fate is nothing but past effort; set it aside and lift yourself firmly through good company and good teachings.

yv.2.6.2.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.6.2.line: Results follow effort. Call it fate if you like, but it is the same effort.
yv.2.6.2.claim: As the effort, so the fruit; there is only effort, and what is called fate is that same effort.

yv.2.6.3.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.6.3.line: When we say 'it was fate', often we are just saying 'this hurts'.
yv.2.6.3.misuse: The pain is real. The verse only says the word 'fate' names the pain; it doesn't explain it.
yv.2.6.3.claim: As people cry 'how painful' in pain, 'alas, fate' is only another word for the same cry.

yv.2.6.18.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.6.18.line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
yv.2.6.18.claim: Present and past effort overpower each other by strength; it is always human striving, and the unagitated one wins.

yv.2.6.21.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.6.21.line: Don't torment yourself over what was never in your power. Otherwise you'd weep daily that you can't stop death.
yv.2.6.21.misuse: Not 'don't feel loss'. It means don't add self-torment for what you couldn't control.
yv.2.6.21.claim: Do not grieve over wealth lost despite effort; where my strength has no power, lamenting is useless.

yv.2.7.12.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.7.12.line: When your mind drifts to harmful things, steer it back to good ones. That's the whole teaching.
yv.2.7.12.claim: When the mind is sunk in the harmful, bring it by effort to the good; this is the gist of all teaching.

yv.2.7.17.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.7.17.line: The eater gets full, the walker arrives, the speaker is heard. Effort is what bears fruit.
yv.2.7.17.claim: The eater is satisfied, the walker arrives, the speaker speaks; human effort bears fruit.

yv.2.7.21.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.7.21.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
yv.2.7.21.claim: Effort brings its fruit sooner or later according to place and time, and that arrival is what people call fate.

yv.2.9.30.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.9.30.line: Your habits flow like a river with two channels. With effort, you choose which one it runs in.
yv.2.9.30.claim: The river of tendencies flows by good and bad channels; by one's own effort it must be turned to the good.

yv.2.9.33.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.9.33.line: Raise your mind like a child: gently, patiently, little by little, never by force.
yv.2.9.33.claim: Tend the child that is your mind with evenness and coaxing, little by little, never abruptly.

yv.2.9.39.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.9.39.claim: Whatever one practises, one becomes of that nature.

yv.2.11.58.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.11.58.line: Stay close to good people and good judgment grows. From it come both a good life and inner freedom.
yv.2.11.58.claim: Discernment is born from constant contact with good people, and its fruits are both enjoyment and freedom.

yv.2.13.53.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.13.53.line: Be calm and clear inside, and even an enemy starts to become a friend.
yv.2.13.53.misuse: Calm is not putting up with abuse; it gives you the clarity to set boundaries.
yv.2.13.53.claim: For one content in calm and cool within, even an enemy turns to friendship.

yv.2.13.64.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.13.64.line: Whatever you do or eat with a calm mind tastes sweeter.
yv.2.13.64.claim: Whatever you do or eat with a mind cooled by calm tastes sweet as nothing else does.

yv.2.13.67.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.13.67.line: Calm is armour. Sorrows strike it like arrows on diamond rock and fall away.
yv.2.13.67.claim: Sorrows do not pierce one armoured in the nectar of calm, as arrows do not pierce diamond rock.

yv.2.13.72.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.13.72.line: Calm is meeting the pleasant and the unpleasant without being thrown up or knocked down.
yv.2.13.72.claim: One who meets pleasant and unpleasant through every sense without elation or dejection is called calm.

yv.2.13.78.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.13.78.line: Calm is being cool inside, not drowning in things, busy with life yet clear-headed.
yv.2.13.78.claim: One who is cool within, does not sink into things, and acts in the world undeluded is called calm.

yv.2.14.2.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.14.2.line: Honest inquiry sharpens the mind. It is the great medicine for life's long ache.
yv.2.14.2.claim: Sharpened by inquiry, the intellect sees the highest; inquiry is the great medicine for the long illness of worldly life.

yv.2.14.11.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.14.11.line: A mind opened by clear thinking doesn't sink in hard times. It floats, like a gourd on water.
yv.2.14.11.claim: Minds opened by discernment do not sink in misfortune, as gourds do not sink in water.

yv.2.14.50.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.14.50.line: Ask honestly: Who am I? How did I get caught in this? That questioning is inquiry.
yv.2.14.50.claim: Reflecting rightly on 'Who am I? How did this trouble called worldly life come to me?' is called inquiry.

yv.2.14.53.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.14.53.line: Inquiry leads to truth, truth to inner rest, rest to a calm mind, and a calm mind ends sorrow.
yv.2.14.53.claim: From inquiry comes truth, from truth rest in the self, from that a calm mind and the end of all sorrow.

yv.2.15.1.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.15.1.line: Contentment is the highest good. The contented rest deeply.
yv.2.15.1.claim: Contentment is the highest good and is itself happiness; the contented reach the deepest rest.

yv.2.15.11.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.15.11.line: With a content, untroubled mind, a person with nothing lives like an emperor.
yv.2.15.11.misuse: Not a reason to dismiss real financial hardship; it is about the mind's endless hunger.
yv.2.15.11.claim: One whose mind is content and untroubled enjoys an emperor's happiness even while owning nothing.

yv.2.15.19.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.15.19.line: A calm, contented face gives people more joy than a pile of money.
yv.2.15.19.claim: People take more joy in a face made beautiful by evenness than in heaps of wealth.

yv.2.16.3.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.16.3.line: In good company, emptiness fills, misfortune feels like fortune, and even death loses its terror.
yv.2.16.3.claim: In the company of the wise, emptiness becomes fullness, misfortune looks like fortune, and even death becomes a festival.

yv.2.16.8.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.16.8.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
yv.2.16.8.claim: Even in the hardest straits and helplessness, one should not let go of good company in the least.

yv.2.16.19.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.16.19.line: Contentment is the greatest gain, good company the best path, clear thinking the best knowledge, calm the greatest joy.
yv.2.16.19.claim: Contentment is the highest gain, good company the highest refuge, inquiry the highest knowledge and calm the highest happiness.

yv.2.16.32.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.2.16.32.line: One good habit feeds the others. One bad habit feeds the rest of them too.
yv.2.16.32.claim: When one virtue grows, other virtues grow and conquer faults; when one fault grows, faults grow and destroy virtues.

yv.3.16.24.speaker: The brahmins
yv.3.16.24.line: Discipline and prayer can achieve almost anything, but no one can win freedom from death.
yv.3.16.24.misuse: Not fatalism about care: look after the sick fully. This is about the fear itself.
yv.3.16.24.claim: Austerity, prayer and discipline win every attainment, yet immortality is never gained.
yv.3.16.24.needs: The reader is not in the middle of a loved one's medical crisis.

yv.5.9.46.speaker: Janaka
yv.5.9.46.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
yv.5.9.46.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
yv.5.9.46.claim: Fortunes the mind clings to are calamities, and misfortunes the mind accepts are fortunes.

yv.5.9.59.speaker: Janaka
yv.5.9.59.line: I've cried 'I'm ruined' again and again. What's gone is gone. I won't keep weeping now.
yv.5.9.59.misuse: Grief needs its time. This is the moment you choose to stop replaying it, not a rule to skip it.
yv.5.9.59.claim: I have lamented 'I am ruined' again and again; what is gone is gone, and I will weep no more.

yv.5.10.9.speaker: Janaka's doorkeeper
yv.5.10.9.line: Get up and do today's work. Great people don't let the hour slip by.
yv.5.10.9.claim: Rise quickly and do your appointed work; the great do not let the time for their duties pass.

yv.5.11.6.speaker: Janaka
yv.5.11.6.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
yv.5.11.6.claim: The more you idly imagine streams of possibilities, the more your world of trouble swells by your own thinking.

yv.5.12.14.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.12.14.line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
yv.5.12.14.claim: He does not pursue the future or brood on the past; he goes along with the present moment, smiling.

yv.5.12.23.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.12.23.line: Good judgment finishes a job even without help; poor judgment ruins even a great opportunity.
yv.5.12.23.claim: The wise finish a task even without help; the unwise ruin even a great undertaking.

yv.5.12.26.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.12.26.line: Put the effort you spend earning money into growing wiser first.
yv.5.12.26.claim: The effort people give to gaining outer things should first be given to growing wisdom.

yv.5.21.6.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.21.6.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
yv.5.21.6.claim: Worry grows by being thought, as fire by fuel, and dies when not thought, as fire without fuel.

yv.5.21.9.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.21.9.line: Make good judgment your friend and wisdom your companion, and crises won't bewilder you.
yv.5.21.9.claim: With discernment as friend and mature understanding as companion, one moves through crises without being bewildered.

yv.5.21.10.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.21.10.line: When every door shuts and even family lets go, your own courage is what lifts you out.
yv.5.21.10.misuse: Not 'go it alone'. It means don't wait to be rescued; accepting help is fine.
yv.5.21.10.claim: When every means is blocked and kin have let go, nothing but one's own fortitude lifts one out of crisis.

yv.5.21.14.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.21.14.line: For someone wearing shoes, the whole earth is paved in leather. A full mind finds the world full.
yv.5.21.14.claim: To a full mind the whole world is full of nectar, as the whole earth is leather-covered for one wearing shoes.

yv.5.22.34.speaker: Bali
yv.5.22.34.line: Day again, night again, the same tasks again, over and over. A thinking person feels mocked by it.
yv.5.22.34.misuse: Bali's question starts his awakening. The answer he finds is not quitting but mastering the mind; pair with 6a.115.43.
yv.5.22.34.claim: Again day, again night, again the same chain of tasks; to a thinking person this is a mockery.

yv.5.24.19.speaker: Virochana
yv.5.24.19.line: Unpractised, it feels impossible. Well practised, it comes easily.
yv.5.24.19.claim: It is very hard to attain when unpractised and easily attained when well practised.

yv.5.43.9.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.43.9.line: Sometimes you wake up by your own effort; sometimes grace wakes you, through devotion. Both are real paths.
yv.5.43.9.claim: Sometimes the self awakens by its own power, and sometimes it is awakened through Vishnu, who is reached by devotion.

yv.5.43.25.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.43.25.line: We pray to the gods with love. Why not speak to our own mind with the same love?
yv.5.43.25.misuse: Not a dismissal of prayer; it asks for the same care toward your inner life.
yv.5.43.25.claim: As people lovingly petition Vishnu and other gods, why not make the same loving appeal to one's own mind?

yv.5.43.32.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.43.32.line: Daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens.
yv.5.43.32.claim: Through constant practice and discernment the mind soon grows clear, as a mango ripens slowly.

yv.5.66.34.speaker: Bhasa
yv.5.66.34.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
yv.5.66.34.claim: Borne on endless waves of tasks the mind gets no moment's rest; tangled in 'done, doing, to do', it faints.

yv.6a.26.8.speaker: Bhushunda
yv.6a.26.8.line: I don't brood over the past or the future. I keep my attention on now.
yv.6a.26.8.claim: I never brood on past or future; I stay with my attention on the present.

yv.6a.26.12.speaker: Bhushunda
yv.6a.26.12.line: I don't fret 'I got this today; next I'll get that.' That's why I live long and well.
yv.6a.26.12.claim: I do not worry 'I got this today, I will get that next', so I live long and well.

yv.6a.26.18.speaker: Bhushunda
yv.6a.26.18.line: 'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
yv.6a.26.18.claim: I have no fever of 'what happened today, what will come tomorrow', and so I live free of illness.

yv.6a.26.28.speaker: Bhushunda
yv.6a.26.28.line: Whenever I learn something new, I don't let it make me arrogant.
yv.6a.26.28.claim: Whenever I come to know something my mind does not turn arrogant, and so I live free of illness.

yv.6a.26.34.speaker: Bhushunda
yv.6a.26.34.line: I'm glad when others are glad and sad when they're sad. Being everyone's friend keeps me well.
yv.6a.26.34.claim: Glad with the glad and pained with the pained, I am a friend to all, and so I live well.

yv.6a.93.29.speaker: Kumbha (Queen Chudala in disguise)
yv.6a.93.29.line: Giving up your kingdom, your body, or living in a hut won't free you. Real letting go is inside.
yv.6a.93.29.misuse: Not 'never change your life'. It says outer escape without inner change doesn't work.
yv.6a.93.29.claim: Complete renunciation does not come from giving up the body, the kingdom, or comfort in a hut.

yv.6a.93.43.speaker: Kumbha (Queen Chudala in disguise)
yv.6a.93.43.line: Letting go of the clinging mind is letting go of everything. The rest follows.
yv.6a.93.43.claim: Giving up the mind is known as complete renunciation; when that is achieved, the truth is experienced.
yv.6a.93.43.needs: Some acquaintance with the idea that the mind, not circumstances, binds.

yv.6a.115.1.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.6a.115.1.line: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, a great letter-go. Drop your doubts and hold steady.
yv.6a.115.1.claim: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer and a great renouncer, casting off all doubt and holding to lasting steadiness.

yv.6a.115.17.speaker: Shiva
yv.6a.115.17.line: Act at the right time, do what the task needs, and don't cling. That is a great doer.
yv.6a.115.17.claim: One who acts at the right time, unattached in mind, as the task requires, is called a great doer.

yv.6a.115.26.speaker: Shiva
yv.6a.115.26.line: Take in big joys and big sorrows the way the ocean takes in rivers: evenly.
yv.6a.115.26.claim: One who receives great joys and sorrows evenly, as the ocean receives rivers, is called a great enjoyer.

yv.6a.115.43.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.6a.115.43.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
yv.6a.115.43.claim: Turned inward while doing all outer work, you never grow weary and become free of the sense of doership.

viv.1.judge_character.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.judge_character.line: Watch a man do his most common actions; those are indeed the things which will tell you the real character of a great man.
viv.1.judge_character.claim: Real character shows in a person's most common actions, not in great performances.

viv.1.blows_inner_fire.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.blows_inner_fire.line: it was blows that brought out their inner fire more than praise.
viv.1.blows_inner_fire.misuse: Not a reason to seek out hardship or to tell someone in pain that it is good for them.
viv.1.blows_inner_fire.claim: Misery, poverty and blows have taught great characters more than happiness, wealth and praise.
viv.1.blows_inner_fire.needs: Never to someone wronged or bereaved, to whom it says the hurt was good for them.

viv.1.make_ourselves.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.make_ourselves.line: We are responsible for what we are; and whatever we wish ourselves to be, we have the power to make ourselves.
viv.1.make_ourselves.misuse: Not a claim that every circumstance or injustice is your own fault.
viv.1.make_ourselves.claim: We are responsible for what we are and have the power to make ourselves whatever we wish to be.
viv.1.make_ourselves.needs: 'Responsible for what we are' wounds someone who was harmed by others or by illness.

viv.1.dont_think_result.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.dont_think_result.line: If you want to do a great or a good work, do not trouble to think what the result will be.
viv.1.dont_think_result.misuse: Not 'never plan'; it is about not letting expected returns drive or poison the work.
viv.1.dont_think_result.claim: To help someone or do good work, do not think about their attitude to you or what the result will be.

viv.1.silence_in_activity.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.silence_in_activity.line: in the midst of the intensest activity finds the silence and solitude of the desert.
viv.1.silence_in_activity.claim: The ideal person finds intense activity in silence and the silence of the desert in intense activity.

viv.1.not_hate_ourselves.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.not_hate_ourselves.line: Our first duty is not to hate ourselves, because to advance we must have faith in ourselves first and then in God.
viv.1.not_hate_ourselves.claim: Our first duty is not to hate ourselves; faith in oneself comes first and then faith in God.

viv.1.apple_standard.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.apple_standard.line: To judge the apple tree you must take the apple standard, and for the oak, its own standard.
viv.1.apple_standard.claim: Each person should be judged by the standard of their own ideal, as an apple tree by the apple standard.

viv.1.without_approbation.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.without_approbation.line: for a man to constantly do good without caring for the approbation of his fellow men is indeed the highest sacrifice man can perform.
viv.1.without_approbation.claim: To keep doing good without caring for anyone's approval is the hardest thing and the highest sacrifice.
viv.1.without_approbation.needs: Not to someone whose credit was taken; it tells them to stop minding.

viv.1.sneers_ridicule.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.sneers_ridicule.line: A man must go about his duties without taking notice of the sneers and the ridicule of the world.
viv.1.sneers_ridicule.claim: Fear is weakness; one must do one's duty without noticing the world's sneers and ridicule.
viv.1.sneers_ridicule.needs: The line alone is safe. The passage's 'fear is a sign of weakness' shames an anxious reader.

viv.1.good_impressions.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.good_impressions.line: if a man thinks good thoughts and does good works, the sum total of these impressions will be good;
viv.1.good_impressions.claim: Good thoughts and good works leave impressions whose sum forces a person toward good even in spite of himself.

viv.1.master_not_slave.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.master_not_slave.line: you should work like a master and not as a slave;
viv.1.master_not_slave.claim: One should work incessantly, as a master and not as a slave.
viv.1.master_not_slave.needs: About inner attachment, not about one's employer.

viv.1.love_no_pain.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.love_no_pain.line: love only brings a reaction of bliss; if it does not, it is not love;
viv.1.love_no_pain.misuse: Pain in a relationship does not prove you failed to love; it can be a signal to set boundaries.
viv.1.love_no_pain.claim: Love brings only bliss; what brings a painful reaction is something else mistaken for love.
viv.1.love_no_pain.needs: To a grieving or heartbroken person it says their love was not love.

viv.1.position_of_giver.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.position_of_giver.line: Attachment comes only where we expect a return.
viv.1.position_of_giver.misuse: Giving freely is not the same as letting yourself be used.
viv.1.position_of_giver.claim: Attachment comes only where a return is expected; give as a free offering and work will not bind.

viv.1.through_their_eyes.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.through_their_eyes.line: see the duty of others through their own eyes, and never judge the customs of other peoples by our own standard.
viv.1.through_their_eyes.claim: One should see others' duty through their own eyes and not judge their customs by one's own standard.

viv.1.forbear.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.forbear.line: In all these little roughnesses that we meet with in life, the highest expression of freedom is to forbear.
viv.1.forbear.misuse: Forbearing small daily irritations; not tolerating mistreatment or abuse.
viv.1.forbear.claim: In life's small daily roughnesses, the highest expression of freedom is to forbear.

viv.1.duty_sweet_love.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.duty_sweet_love.line: Duty is sweet only through love, and love shines in freedom alone.
viv.1.duty_sweet_love.claim: Duty runs smoothly only when love greases its wheels; duty is sweet only through love.
