viv.1.duty_next_to_us.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.duty_next_to_us.line: The only way to rise is by doing the duty next to us,
viv.1.duty_next_to_us.claim: The only way to rise is by doing the duty next to us and gathering strength from it.

viv.1.no_duty_ugly.speaker: The Vyadha (in Vivekananda's retelling)
viv.1.no_duty_ugly.line: no duty is ugly, no duty is impure.
viv.1.no_duty_ugly.claim: No duty is ugly and no duty is impure.

viv.1.end_and_means.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.end_and_means.line: "Let the end and the means be joined into one."
viv.1.end_and_means.claim: The secret of work is to join end and means into one and think of nothing beyond the work in hand.

viv.1.state_of_mind.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.state_of_mind.line: Life is good or evil according to the state of mind in which we look at it, it is neither by itself.
viv.1.state_of_mind.misuse: Not a denial of real hardship; it is about the lens we add to it.
viv.1.state_of_mind.claim: Life is good or evil according to the state of mind in which we look at it; it is neither in itself.
viv.1.state_of_mind.needs: Dismissive to someone in real loss or mistreatment.

viv.1.grateful_to_helped.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.grateful_to_helped.line: Be grateful to the man you help, think of him as God.
viv.1.grateful_to_helped.claim: Be grateful to the one you help and think of him as God.

viv.1.moral_gymnasium.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.moral_gymnasium.line: The world is a grand moral gymnasium wherein we have all to take exercise so as to become stronger and stronger spiritually.
viv.1.moral_gymnasium.claim: We are debtors to the world, which owes us nothing; it is a moral gymnasium for growing spiritually stronger.
viv.1.moral_gymnasium.needs: Tells a mistreated person the mistreatment is training. Not for them.

viv.1.dependent_on_me.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.dependent_on_me.line: It is a weakness to think that any one is dependent on me,
viv.1.dependent_on_me.misuse: Not a reason to neglect people who really do rely on you; it frees care from control.
viv.1.dependent_on_me.claim: To think anyone depends on me, or that I can do good to another, is weakness and the root of attachment.
viv.1.dependent_on_me.needs: False and hurtful to a parent of a young child or anyone caring for a sick relative.

viv.1.witness.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.witness.line: do not mix in the fray, hold yourself as a witness and go on working.
viv.1.witness.claim: To work properly, give up attachment, stay out of the fray as a witness and go on working.

viv.1.misery_attachment.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.misery_attachment.line: "Misery comes through attachment, not through work."
viv.1.misery_attachment.claim: Misery comes through attachment, not through work; it is identifying with the work that hurts.

viv.1.duty_disease.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.duty_disease.line: Be at rest, be free, and work.
viv.1.duty_disease.misuse: Not permission to drop real responsibilities; it is about working without compulsion.
viv.1.duty_disease.claim: Duty can become a disease that drags a person on; one should be at rest, be free, and work.

viv.1.unknown_heroes.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.unknown_heroes.line: Seek no praise, no reward, for anything you do.
viv.1.unknown_heroes.misuse: Not a reason to let others take credit unchallenged; it is about where your worth comes from.
viv.1.unknown_heroes.claim: Seek no praise or reward; the desire for credit brings misery, and the greatest have lived and worked unknown.
viv.1.unknown_heroes.needs: Not to someone whose work was taken by another.

viv.1.five_minutes.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.five_minutes.line: we all die, and in five minutes the world forgets us.
viv.1.five_minutes.claim: We think ourselves great, but we all die and in five minutes the world forgets us.

viv.1.inside_the_machine.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.inside_the_machine.line: Do not fly away from the wheels of the world-machine, but stand inside it and learn the secret of work.
viv.1.inside_the_machine.misuse: Not 'never leave a job'; it says escape is not the only path to peace.
viv.1.inside_the_machine.claim: Do not flee the world-machine; stand inside it and learn the secret of work.
viv.1.inside_the_machine.needs: Not an instruction to stay in a harmful job or home.

viv.1.monkey_mind.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.monkey_mind.line: The human mind is like that monkey, incessantly active by its own nature;
viv.1.monkey_mind.claim: The mind is like a maddened monkey, restless by nature and made wilder by desire, jealousy and pride.

viv.1.wait_and_watch.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.wait_and_watch.line: Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
viv.1.wait_and_watch.claim: Sit and let the mind run while you wait and watch; each day it grows calmer.

viv.1.take_up_one_idea.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.take_up_one_idea.line: Take up one idea. Make that one idea your life — think of it, dream of it, live on that idea.
viv.1.take_up_one_idea.claim: Take up one idea, make it your life and leave every other idea alone; that is the way to success.

viv.1.suppress_anger.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.suppress_anger.line: Each time we suppress hatred, or a feeling of anger, it is so much good energy stored up in our favour;
viv.1.suppress_anger.misuse: Restraining a reaction, not bottling up feelings; anger about real harm still needs to be addressed.
viv.1.suppress_anger.claim: Each time hatred or anger is held back, good energy is stored and converted into higher powers.
viv.1.suppress_anger.needs: 'Suppress' in the yogic sense of not acting it out. Not for someone told to stay quiet about a wrong.

viv.1.potentially_divine.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.potentially_divine.line: Doctrines, or dogmas, or rituals, or books, or temples, or forms, are but secondary details.
viv.1.potentially_divine.claim: Each soul is potentially divine, and the goal is to manifest that divinity; doctrines, rituals and temples are secondary.

viv.1.true_to_nature.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.true_to_nature.line: The greatest religion is to be true to your own nature. Have faith in yourselves!
viv.1.true_to_nature.claim: The greatest religion is to be true to one's own nature, with faith in oneself.

viv.1.tolerance_acceptance.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.tolerance_acceptance.line: We believe not only in universal toleration, but we accept all religions as true.
viv.1.tolerance_acceptance.claim: Hinduism has taught both tolerance and universal acceptance, holding all religions to be true.

viv.1.streams_to_sea.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.streams_to_sea.line: the different paths which men take through different tendencies, various though they appear, crooked or straight, all lead to Thee.
viv.1.streams_to_sea.claim: As streams from different sources all reach the sea, the different paths people take all lead to the Lord.

viv.1.frog_in_well.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.frog_in_well.line: I am sitting in my own little well and thinking that the whole world is my little well.
viv.1.frog_in_well.claim: Each of us sits in his own little well and takes it for the whole world.

viv.1.assimilate_grow.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.assimilate_grow.line: each must assimilate the spirit of the others and yet preserve his individuality
viv.1.assimilate_grow.claim: No one need convert; each should absorb the spirit of the others, keep his individuality and grow by his own law.

viv.1.help_not_fight.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.help_not_fight.line: "Help and not Fight," "Assimilation and not Destruction," "Harmony and Peace and not Dissension."
viv.1.help_not_fight.claim: Holiness belongs to no single church; every religion's banner will read help, assimilation and harmony, not fight.

viv.1.come_up_lions.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.come_up_lions.line: Come up, O lions, and shake off the delusion that you are sheep;
viv.1.come_up_lions.claim: People are children of God and sharers of immortal bliss; to call them sinners is a libel on human nature.

viv.1.truth_to_truth.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.truth_to_truth.line: man is not travelling from error to truth, but from truth to truth,
viv.1.truth_to_truth.claim: A person travels not from error to truth but from lower truth to higher truth.

viv.2.means_and_end.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.means_and_end.line: pay as much attention to the means of work as to its end.
viv.2.means_and_end.claim: Pay as much attention to the means of work as to its end; with the means right, the end must come.

viv.2.cannot_give_up.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.cannot_give_up.line: perhaps it is a failure and yet we cannot give it up.
viv.2.cannot_give_up.claim: Our greatest sorrow is that we pour ourselves into something, it fails, and yet we cannot give it up.

viv.2.strength_is_life.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.strength_is_life.line: This is the great fact: strength is life, weakness is death.
viv.2.strength_is_life.misuse: Not a judgment on illness, depression or anyone who is struggling; inner strength can be built and helped.
viv.2.strength_is_life.claim: Miseries cannot take hold until the mind is weakened; strength is life and weakness is death.
viv.2.strength_is_life.needs: Tells an anxious or ill person their suffering is their weakness.

viv.2.stony_heart.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.stony_heart.line: the man who never loves, who is hard and stony, escaping most of the miseries of life, escapes also its joys.
viv.2.stony_heart.claim: One who never loves escapes most of life's miseries and also escapes its joys.

viv.2.love_in_return.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.love_in_return.line: not from the fact that we love, but from the fact that we want love in return.
viv.2.love_in_return.misuse: Wanting care from a partner or parent is human; this is about love that turns into bookkeeping.
viv.2.love_in_return.claim: The misery in love comes not from loving but from wanting love in return.
viv.2.love_in_return.needs: Not for someone neglected or mistreated in a relationship.

viv.2.calm_mind_works.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.calm_mind_works.line: It is the calm, forgiving, equable, well-balanced mind that does the greatest amount of work.
viv.2.calm_mind_works.claim: The calm, forgiving, balanced mind does the most work; anger breaks a person and accomplishes nothing.

viv.2.hands_before_eyes.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.hands_before_eyes.line: It is we who have put our hands before our eyes and cry that it is dark.
viv.2.hands_before_eyes.claim: All power is already ours; we cover our own eyes and cry that it is dark.
viv.2.hands_before_eyes.needs: The chosen line says the darkness is one's own doing, which hurts a depressed reader.

viv.2.condemn_none.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.condemn_none.line: Condemn none; if you can stretch out a helping hand, do so.
viv.2.condemn_none.misuse: Not condemning is not the same as approving harm or staying where you are mistreated.
viv.2.condemn_none.claim: Condemn no one; help if you can, and if you cannot, bless them and let them go their own way.

viv.2.remedy_weakness.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.remedy_weakness.line: The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.
viv.2.remedy_weakness.claim: The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness but thinking of strength.

viv.2.atheist_himself.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.atheist_himself.line: The new religion says that he is the atheist who does not believe in himself.
viv.2.atheist_himself.claim: The real atheist is the one who does not believe in himself.
viv.2.atheist_himself.needs: Calls the self-doubting an atheist; a sting for someone already low.

viv.2.help_from_within.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.help_from_within.line: All the help that has come was from within yourselves.
viv.2.help_from_within.misuse: Not a reason to refuse help or therapy; it says your own effort is never wasted.
viv.2.help_from_within.claim: All the help that ever came to you came from within yourself.
viv.2.help_from_within.needs: The passage calls help from others vain. Never for someone who needs to reach out, or who is in despair.

viv.2.temple_of_man.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.temple_of_man.line: the moment I stand in reverence before every human being and see God in him
viv.2.temple_of_man.claim: The moment one sees God seated in every human body and stands in reverence before each person, one is free.

viv.2.eyes_of_love.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.eyes_of_love.line: we should see others with eyes of love, with sympathy, knowing that they are going along the same path that we have trodden.
viv.2.eyes_of_love.claim: We should look on others with love and sympathy, knowing they walk the path we have walked.

viv.2.reason_not_authority.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.reason_not_authority.line: it is better that mankind should become atheist by following reason
viv.2.reason_not_authority.claim: It is better to become an atheist by following reason than to believe blindly on anyone's authority.
viv.2.reason_not_authority.needs: The full sentence dismisses 'two hundred millions of gods'; abrasive for a devotional reader.

viv.2.mistakes_made_me.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.mistakes_made_me.line: without every one of those mistakes I should not be what I am today,
viv.2.mistakes_made_me.misuse: Not 'mistakes don't matter'; he says in the same breath not to commit them wilfully.
viv.2.mistakes_made_me.claim: Without each of my mistakes I would not be what I am; do not mope, for all comes out straight.

viv.2.strike_a_match.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.strike_a_match.line: Strike a match and light comes in a moment.
viv.2.strike_a_match.claim: Lamenting old darkness does not remove it; strike a match, bring in light and build character.
viv.2.strike_a_match.needs: 'Weep and wail' in the passage is brisk; use the line.

viv.2.angels_unawares.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.angels_unawares.listener: Class at the Home of Truth, Los Angeles
viv.2.angels_unawares.line: We shall make mistakes, but they may be angels unawares.
viv.2.angels_unawares.claim: Growth comes through struggle for an ideal, and the mistakes made on the way may be angels unawares.

viv.2.little_mental_universe.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.little_mental_universe.listener: Class at the Home of Truth, Los Angeles
viv.2.little_mental_universe.line: we are always inclined to think that our little mental universe is all that is;
viv.2.little_mental_universe.claim: We wrongly judge others by assuming our own little mental universe is all there is.

viv.2.hundred_thousand_ways.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.hundred_thousand_ways.line: truth may be expressed in a hundred thousand ways, and that each of these ways is true as far as it goes.
viv.2.hundred_thousand_ways.claim: Truth can be expressed in a hundred thousand ways, each true as far as it goes.

viv.2.child_teaches_himself.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.child_teaches_himself.line: Your duty is to afford opportunities and to remove obstacles.
viv.2.child_teaches_himself.misuse: Not 'leave children to it'; protecting and providing is the hedge he describes.
viv.2.child_teaches_himself.claim: No one can teach a child; the child teaches himself, and one's duty is to give opportunity and remove obstacles.

viv.2.do_not_destroy.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.do_not_destroy.line: Say not a word against any man's convictions so far as they are sincere.
viv.2.do_not_destroy.claim: Help if you can; if not, stand by without injuring, and say nothing against anyone's sincere convictions.

viv.2.grow_from_inside.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.grow_from_inside.line: You have to teach yourself; your growth must come from inside.
viv.2.grow_from_inside.claim: No one else can make you spiritual; you must teach yourself and grow from inside.

viv.2.difference_sign_of_thought.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.difference_sign_of_thought.line: Thinking beings must differ; difference is the first sign of thought.
viv.2.difference_sign_of_thought.claim: Thinking beings must differ; difference is the first sign of thought.

viv.2.language_of_soul.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.language_of_soul.line: They must speak your own language, the language of your soul,
viv.2.language_of_soul.claim: Spiritual ideas satisfy only when they come in one's own way and speak the language of one's own soul.

viv.2.never_mind_failures.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.never_mind_failures.line: hold the ideal a thousand times, and if you fail a thousand times, make the attempt once more.
viv.2.never_mind_failures.claim: Failures are natural and are the beauty of life; hold the ideal and after a thousand failures attempt once more.

viv.2.razor_edge.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.razor_edge.line: the way is long and perilous, but struggle on, do not despair.
viv.2.razor_edge.claim: The way is long and hard as a razor's edge; struggle on, and stop not till the goal is reached.

viv.2.creator_of_destiny.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.creator_of_destiny.line: know that you are the creator of your own destiny.
viv.2.creator_of_destiny.misuse: Not 'everything that happens to you is your doing'; it is about what you build from here.
viv.2.creator_of_destiny.claim: Take the whole responsibility on yourself; you are the creator of your own destiny and all strength is within you.
viv.2.creator_of_destiny.needs: 'Whole responsibility' is cruel to someone harmed by others, by illness or by loss.

viv.3.be_not_afraid.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.be_not_afraid.line: it is fearlessness that brings heaven even in a moment.
viv.3.be_not_afraid.claim: Fear is the great cause of misery and the greatest superstition; fearlessness brings heaven in a moment.
viv.3.be_not_afraid.needs: 'The moment you fear, you are nobody' in the passage shames an anxious person; fear for a sick relative is not superstition.

viv.3.arise_awake.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.arise_awake.line: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
viv.3.arise_awake.claim: Rise out of the belief that you are weak and keep going until the goal is reached; the soul is infinite.
viv.3.arise_awake.needs: That weakness is a mistaken view of oneself, not a fact about one's worth.

viv.3.real_worship.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.real_worship.line: This is the gist of all worship — to be pure and to do good to others.
viv.3.real_worship.claim: The heart of all worship is to be pure and do good to others; one who sees Shiva in the poor and sick truly worships.

viv.3.do_not_become_others.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.do_not_become_others.line: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
viv.3.do_not_become_others.claim: Learn everything good from others, but absorb it in your own way; do not become a copy of them.

viv.3.seed_becomes_tree.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.seed_becomes_tree.line: It becomes the mighty plant, the mighty tree, after its own nature, having absorbed everything that was given to it.
viv.3.seed_becomes_tree.claim: A seed takes in earth, air and water yet grows into its own tree; take from all and grow after your own nature.

viv.3.refuses_to_learn.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.refuses_to_learn.line: that man who refuses to learn is already dead.
viv.3.refuses_to_learn.claim: We have much to learn from others; the man who refuses to learn is already dead.

viv.3.realised_not_heard.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.realised_not_heard.line: Religion is to be realised, not only heard; it is not in learning some doctrine like a parrot.
viv.3.realised_not_heard.claim: Religion is to be realised in one's own experience, not only heard or recited like a parrot.

viv.3.where_we_agree.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.where_we_agree.line: Let us preach where we all agree and leave the differences to remedy themselves.
viv.3.where_we_agree.claim: Speak from what everyone agrees on and leave the differences to settle by themselves.
viv.3.where_we_agree.needs: Fits disagreements of view, not real harm; a wronged person is not asked to drop it.

viv.3.reject_as_poison.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.reject_as_poison.line: anything that makes you weak physically, intellectually, and spiritually, reject as poison;
viv.3.reject_as_poison.claim: Whatever makes you weak in body, mind or spirit, reject as poison; truth is strengthening.

viv.3.dares_to_differ.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.dares_to_differ.line: as soon as he dares to differ, that sympathy is gone, that love vanishes.
viv.3.dares_to_differ.claim: People speak of tolerance, but their sympathy often lasts only while you agree; dare to differ and their love vanishes.

viv.3.whatever_you_think.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.whatever_you_think.line: If you think yourselves weak, weak you will be; if you think yourselves strong, strong you will be;
viv.3.whatever_you_think.claim: You become what you think yourself to be: think yourself weak and you will be weak, strong and you will be strong.
viv.3.whatever_you_think.needs: Can read as blame to someone whose weakness is illness or grief.

viv.3.make_children_strong.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.make_children_strong.line: Make your children strong from their very childhood;
viv.3.make_children_strong.misuse: Strong does not mean hard; elsewhere he says love is the only law of life.
viv.3.make_children_strong.claim: Make children strong from childhood: teach them not weakness or empty forms but the glory of the soul.
viv.3.make_children_strong.needs: Strong means rooted in the soul's worth, not hard; see the library misuse note.

viv.3.servant_first.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.servant_first.line: Always first learn to be a servant, and then you will be fit to be a master.
viv.3.servant_first.claim: First learn to be a servant; then you will be fit to be a master.

viv.3.hospitality_west.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.hospitality_west.line: how wonderfully and how hospitably I was received in every country in the West.
viv.3.hospitality_west.claim: Vivekananda says he would be ungrateful not to tell how hospitably he was received in every Western country.

viv.3.dare_to_be_free.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.3.dare_to_be_free.line: dare to be free, dare to go as far as your thought leads, and dare to carry that out in your life.
viv.3.dare_to_be_free.claim: Dare to be free: go as far as your thought leads and carry it out in your life.
viv.3.dare_to_be_free.needs: In the lecture freedom is the soul's freedom; the line is not a licence for any impulse.

viv.4.education_religion.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.education_religion.line: Education is the manifestation of the perfection already in man.
viv.4.education_religion.claim: Education draws out the perfection already in a person; religion draws out the divinity already there.

viv.4.live_for_others.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.live_for_others.line: they alone live who live for others, the rest are more dead than alive.
viv.4.live_for_others.misuse: Living for others includes caring for yourself; it is not a call to burn out.
viv.4.live_for_others.claim: Life is short and the world's vanities pass; only those who live for others truly live.
viv.4.live_for_others.needs: Living for others includes caring for yourself; not a call to burn out.

viv.4.servant_while_leading.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.servant_while_leading.listener: Alasinga Perumal and the Madras group
viv.4.servant_while_leading.line: Be the servant while leading. Be unselfish, and never listen to one friend in private accusing another. Have infinite patience, and success is yours.
viv.4.servant_while_leading.claim: Lead as a servant, stay unselfish, never listen to one friend accusing another in private, and have infinite patience.

viv.4.love_pays.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.love_pays.listener: Alasinga Perumal and the Madras group
viv.4.love_pays.line: It is love that pays; it is character that cleaves its way
viv.4.love_pays.claim: Money, name, fame and learning do not pay; love does, and character cuts through walls of difficulty.

viv.4.struggle_motto.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.struggle_motto.listener: Alasinga Perumal and the Madras group
viv.4.struggle_motto.line: When it was all dark, I used to say, struggle; when light is breaking in, I still say, struggle.
viv.4.struggle_motto.claim: Struggle when all is dark and keep struggling when light breaks; that was his motto for ten years.

viv.4.hearts_purified.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.hearts_purified.line: The more we come out and do good to others, the more our hearts will be purified, and God will be in them.
viv.4.hearts_purified.claim: The more we go out and do good to others, the purer our hearts become, and God comes to dwell in them.

viv.4.hold_on_brave_heart.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.hold_on_brave_heart.line: Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come.
viv.4.hold_on_brave_heart.claim: Even when the sun is hidden and hopes are blighted, hold on a while; no work is lost and no good is undone.

viv.4.no_winter.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.no_winter.line: No winter was but summer came behind,
viv.4.no_winter.claim: No winter ever passed without summer after it; light and shade push each other, so be steady and brave.

viv.4.calm_of_heart.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.calm_of_heart.line: The silence between speaking; Between two fits of passion — It is the calm of heart.
viv.4.calm_of_heart.claim: Peace is the calm of heart, like the silence between words and the pause between two fits of passion.

viv.4.praise_blame_one.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.praise_blame_one.line: No praise or blame can be Where praiser praised, and blamer blamed are one.
viv.4.praise_blame_one.claim: Where the one praised and the one who blames are one Self, there is no praise or blame; so stay calm and say nothing.
viv.4.praise_blame_one.needs: Spoken to a sannyasin; 'say naught' when kicked is a renunciant's vow, not advice to accept mistreatment.

viv.4.requiescat.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.requiescat.line: Remembrance sweet, that kills all space and time, Like altar roses fill thy place behind!
viv.4.requiescat.claim: A farewell to a friend who has died: may his soul go on to eternal peace, and sweet remembrance fill the place he left.

viv.4.deep_down_calm.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.deep_down_calm.listener: D. R. Balaji Rao, after a severe bereavement
viv.4.deep_down_calm.line: deep down there is the stratum of infinite calmness, infinite peace, and infinite bliss.
viv.4.deep_down_calm.claim: Waves may roll and storms rage on the surface, but deep down there is a layer of infinite calm, peace and bliss.

viv.8.early_violet.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.early_violet.line: Change not thy nature, gentle bloom, Thou violet, sweet and pure, But ever pour thy sweet perfume Unasked, unstinted, sure!
viv.8.early_violet.misuse: Staying kind is not staying put; you can keep your nature and still leave.
viv.8.early_violet.claim: Even if love fails and bad prevails over good, do not change your gentle nature; keep giving your fragrance unasked.
viv.8.early_violet.needs: Keep your nature, not your place. Never serve as 'keep giving to the one who hurt you'.

viv.6.the_cup.speaker: Swami Vivekananda (the poem speaks in the Divine's voice)
viv.6.the_cup.line: it is not meant for any other hand,
viv.6.the_cup.misuse: Accepting your path is not accepting abuse or injustice; act where you can.
viv.6.the_cup.claim: Your task, joyless as it may seem, is meant for no other hand and has its place; take it without needing to understand.
viv.6.the_cup.needs: Accepting your path is not accepting abuse or injustice.

viv.5.great_convictions.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.great_convictions.line: Have faith in yourselves, great convictions are the mothers of great deeds.
viv.5.great_convictions.claim: Have faith in yourselves; great convictions are the mothers of great deeds.

viv.5.hero_in_silence.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.hero_in_silence.line: cowards assume the attitude of the brave when everything is sure to turn out well, but the true hero works in silence.
viv.5.hero_in_silence.claim: Anyone can stand up to be praised or look brave when success is certain; the true hero works in silence.
viv.5.hero_in_silence.needs: Not advice to stay quiet when your credit is taken.

viv.5.ridicule_opposition.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.ridicule_opposition.line: Each work has to pass through these stages — ridicule, opposition, and then acceptance.
viv.5.ridicule_opposition.claim: Every work passes through ridicule, then opposition, then acceptance; whoever thinks ahead of his time will be misunderstood.

viv.5.not_in_a_day.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.not_in_a_day.listener: Dr. Nanjunda Rao, starting a magazine in Madras
viv.5.not_in_a_day.line: Do not expect success in a day or a year.
viv.5.not_in_a_day.claim: Go on bravely; do not expect success in a day or a year; hold to the highest, be steady, avoid jealousy and selfishness.

viv.6.three_essentials.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.three_essentials.line: Purity, patience, and perseverance are the three essentials to success and, above all, love.
viv.6.three_essentials.claim: Do nothing in haste; purity, patience and perseverance, and above all love, are the essentials of success.

viv.6.nothing_lasts.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.nothing_lasts.line: Never mind, nothing is to last for ever.
viv.6.nothing_lasts.claim: There seems to be a gloom over your mind; never mind, nothing lasts for ever.
viv.6.nothing_lasts.needs: 'Never mind' can sound dismissive without the first sentence.

viv.6.fearful_to_hurt.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.fearful_to_hurt.line: by being so fearful to hurt we hurt more.
viv.6.fearful_to_hurt.claim: Being nervous and fearful, we injure others; trying so hard not to hurt, we hurt more.

viv.6.glad_blunders.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.glad_blunders.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
viv.6.glad_blunders.claim: Looking back, he is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad of his big blunders, and glad to enter peace.

viv.6.behind_my_work.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.behind_my_work.line: Behind my work was ambition, behind my love was personality,
viv.6.behind_my_work.claim: Looking honestly, he finds ambition behind his work, personality behind his love, fear behind his purity, power behind his guidance.

viv.6.strive_to_be_great.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.strive_to_be_great.line: Even if he fails in life, still I will have the satisfaction that he strove to become great
viv.6.strive_to_be_great.claim: Even if he fails in life, it is enough that he strove to become great and useful; let him be bold and cut a new path.

viv.8.come_good_come_evil.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.come_good_come_evil.line: Be brave and face everything — come good, come evil, both welcome,
viv.8.come_good_come_evil.claim: Be brave and face everything; come good, come evil, both are welcome, both are my play.

viv.6.essence_of_education.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.essence_of_education.line: To me the very essence of education is concentration of mind, not the collecting of facts.
viv.6.essence_of_education.claim: The essence of education is the power of concentration and detachment, not collecting facts.

viv.6.power_of_detachment.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.power_of_detachment.line: Almost all our suffering is caused by our not having the power of detachment.
viv.6.power_of_detachment.claim: Almost all our suffering is caused by our not having the power of detachment.
viv.6.power_of_detachment.needs: Detachment here is the trained power to withdraw the mind, not coldness.

viv.6.one_thing_at_a_time.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.one_thing_at_a_time.line: Do one thing at a time and while doing it put your whole soul into it to the exclusion of all else.
viv.6.one_thing_at_a_time.claim: Do one thing at a time, and while doing it put your whole soul into it to the exclusion of all else.

viv.7.thoughts_live.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.7.thoughts_live.line: We are what our thoughts have made us; so take care of what you think.
viv.7.thoughts_live.claim: We are what our thoughts have made us, so take care of what you think; thoughts live and travel far.

viv.7.neither_seek_nor_avoid.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.7.neither_seek_nor_avoid.line: Neither seek nor avoid, take what comes.
viv.7.neither_seek_nor_avoid.misuse: Not passivity about problems you can fix; it is about not clutching or fleeing.
viv.7.neither_seek_nor_avoid.claim: Neither seek nor avoid; take what comes, and be unattached rather than merely enduring.
viv.7.neither_seek_nor_avoid.needs: Not passivity about what you can fix.

viv.8.comfort_no_test.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.comfort_no_test.line: "Comfort" is no test of truth; on the contrary, truth is often far from being "comfortable"
viv.8.comfort_no_test.claim: Comfort is no test of truth; truth is often far from comfortable.

viv.8.lotus_bees.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.lotus_bees.line: Bring your own lotus to blossom: the bees will come of themselves.
viv.8.lotus_bees.claim: Deepen your own thought and love; bring your own lotus to blossom and the bees will come of themselves.

viv.5.same_unity.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.same_unity.line: We may call it God, Allah, Jehovah, the Spirit, Love;
viv.5.same_unity.claim: Whether called God, Allah, Jehovah, Spirit or Love, it is the same unity that animates all life.

viv.1.weakness_as_forgiveness.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.1.weakness_as_forgiveness.listener: Class on the Gita, San Francisco
viv.1.weakness_as_forgiveness.line: Many a time comes when we want to interpret our weakness and cowardice as forgiveness
viv.1.weakness_as_forgiveness.misuse: Not a push to retaliate; forgiveness chosen from strength is the real thing.
viv.1.weakness_as_forgiveness.claim: We often dress up our weakness and cowardice as forgiveness and renunciation; a beggar's renunciation has no merit.
viv.1.weakness_as_forgiveness.needs: Not a push to retaliate; forgiveness chosen from strength is the real thing.

viv.2.fear_of_death.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.fear_of_death.line: Those moments alone we live when our lives are in the universe, in others;
viv.2.fear_of_death.claim: We truly live only when our lives are in others; fear of death is conquered when one knows one lives as long as any life lives.

vr.2.44.9.speaker: Sumitra
vr.2.44.9.line: Where you can't reach him tonight, the cool moonlight will hold him the way a father would.
vr.2.44.9.claim: The cool moon will embrace your blameless son like a father as he sleeps, and gladden him.

vr.3.66.9.speaker: Lakshman
vr.3.66.9.line: Even the sun and the moon, which light the whole world, go through eclipses.
vr.3.66.9.claim: Even the mighty sun and moon, the eyes of the world, undergo eclipse.

vr.3.66.17.speaker: Lakshman
vr.3.66.17.line: Your wisdom isn't gone. Grief has only put it to sleep for a while.
vr.3.66.17.claim: Your understanding is beyond even the gods; grief has only put your knowledge to sleep, and I am waking it.

vr.5.36.44.speaker: Narrator
vr.5.36.44.line: Relief at the news and grief at his pain, both at once: like a moon rising through rain clouds.
vr.5.36.44.claim: Relieved by hearing of Rama and grieved equally by his grief, Sita was like an autumn night with a half-clouded moon.

vr.5.38.32.speaker: Sita (message to Ram)
vr.5.38.32.line: I have someone who is mine, and still I feel like a person with no one at all.
vr.5.38.32.claim: Show me your compassion; though I have you as my protector, I appear like one who has no one.

vr.5.39.20.speaker: Sita
vr.5.39.20.line: Stay a little longer. Just having you near lifts this heavy sorrow, even if only for a moment.
vr.5.39.20.claim: For one as unlucky as I am, your nearness would free me from this great sorrow, if only for a moment.

vr.5.39.40.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.39.40.line: Take heart. Hold on and wait for the time to turn. It won't be long now.
vr.5.39.40.misuse: Holding on while help is on its way, not passive waiting; Hanuman leaves to bring help.
vr.5.39.40.claim: Take heart and await the time; before long you will see Rama, blazing like fire.

vr.2.21.46.speaker: Ram
vr.2.21.46.line: Hold your sorrow gently, mother. I will keep my word, and I will come home to you.
vr.2.21.46.claim: Contain your grief in your heart, mother, and do not sorrow; I will return once I have kept my father's word.

vr.7.72.10.speaker: Shatrughna
vr.7.72.10.line: I can't go on living so far from you, like a calf that has lost its mother.
vr.7.72.10.claim: Be gracious to me; I cannot go on living far away, like a calf without its mother.

vr.7.72.14.speaker: Ram
vr.7.72.14.line: You are dearer to me than my own life. Stay with me a while before you go back.
vr.7.72.14.claim: You are dearer to me than life, yet the kingdom must be cared for; stay seven nights with me, then return.

vr.2.25.2.speaker: Kausalya
vr.2.25.2.line: May the good you have lived by, gladly and faithfully, now protect you.
vr.2.25.2.misuse: A mother's blessing, not a promise that good people never suffer.
vr.2.25.2.claim: May the dharma you guard with love and discipline guard you in turn.

rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.line: I never turn away anyone who comes to me. The moment you turn toward me, your past is washed away.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.misuse: Not a licence to keep doing harm; the turning has to be real.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.claim: Ram never turns away one who comes for refuge, whatever his sins; the moment a soul faces him, its past wrongs are destroyed.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.5.42.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.42.chaupai.4.line: If someone comes to me afraid, looking for shelter, I will keep them as dear as my own life.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.4.claim: Ram will keep as dear as his own life anyone who comes to him afraid and seeking refuge.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.4.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.5.45.chaupai.4.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.45.chaupai.4.line: I had never done anything good, and still he was glad to hold me to his heart.
rcm.5.45.chaupai.4.misuse: Vibhishan's self-judgement is harsh; the point is the welcome, not the self-contempt.
rcm.5.45.chaupai.4.claim: Vibhishan, who counts himself low and without one good deed, is gladly held to the Lord's heart.

rcm.5.12.chaupai.5.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.12.chaupai.5.line: Don't think you've been forgotten. He hurts because you hurt, and his love for you is twice yours.
rcm.5.12.chaupai.5.claim: Ram grieves in Sita's grief, and his love for her is twice her own, so she need not feel diminished.

rcm.7.7.chhand.2.speaker: Bharat
rcm.7.7.chhand.2.line: I was drowning in missing you, and you took me by the hand.
rcm.7.7.chhand.2.claim: Bharat, speechless at the reunion, says he was drowning in separation and Ram took him by the hand.

rcm.7.8.chhand.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.7.8.chhand.1.line: Like cows running home at dusk to their calves, the mothers ran to hold their sons again.
rcm.7.8.chhand.1.claim: The mothers run to Ram like cows running home at dusk to the calves they had to leave, and their pain of separation ends.

rcm.2.290.doha.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.2.290.doha.1.line: In what you do, say and think, you are clean. There is no one like you.
rcm.2.290.doha.1.claim: Ram tells Bharat he is spotless in deed, word and mind, and that none is his equal.
rcm.2.290.doha.1.needs: that the reader's guilt is larger than anything they actually did

rcm.2.165.chaupai.4.speaker: Narrator
rcm.2.165.chaupai.4.line: Even the wise old teacher's eyes filled with tears as he spoke of the ones he loved.
rcm.2.165.chaupai.4.claim: Even the wise sage Vasishtha is overcome by sorrow and affection as he speaks of Ram, Lakshman and Sita.

rcm.2.56.chaupai.1.speaker: Kausalya
rcm.2.56.chaupai.1.line: May you be guarded the way eyelids guard the eyes.
rcm.2.56.chaupai.1.claim: A mother asks the gods and ancestors to guard her departing son as eyelids guard the eyes.

rcm.4.4.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.4.4.chaupai.4.line: Don't feel small. You are twice as dear to me as my own brother.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.4.claim: Ram tells Hanuman not to feel small: the servant with no other refuge is twice as dear to him as his own brother.

rcm.4.6.chaupai.4.speaker: Sugriva
rcm.4.6.chaupai.4.line: Put down your worry and steady your heart. I'll help you in every way I can.
rcm.4.6.chaupai.4.claim: A friend tells the grieving Ram to steady his heart and promises to serve in every way until Sita is found.

rcm.2.286.chaupai.2.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.286.chaupai.2.line: Come once, bow once, and you are taken in. Your faults are seen, but never held against you.
rcm.2.286.chaupai.2.claim: Ram takes in whoever comes before him for refuge after a single bow, and never keeps their faults in his heart.
rcm.2.286.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

mbh.3.262.51.speaker: Vyasa
mbh.3.262.51.line: After sorrow, happiness comes round again, the way each spoke of a wheel comes back to the top.
mbh.3.262.51.claim: Sorrow follows happiness and happiness follows sorrow, turning to a person like spokes of a wheel.

bg.12.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.7.line: Whoever rests their heart in me, I lift out of the drowning sea, and soon.
bg.12.7.claim: For those whose minds are set on Krishna, he soon becomes the deliverer from the ocean of death-bound samsara.
bg.12.7.needs: a devotional reader; the sea is death and rebirth, so not for someone with an ill relative

yv.1.11.37.speaker: Vishvamitra
yv.1.11.37.line: Say freely what is on your heart, blameless one. These sorrows need not keep wounding you.
yv.1.11.37.claim: Say at once whatever you wish and you shall have it, so that these anguishes no longer pierce you.

yv.3.16.50.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.3.16.50.line: Seeing her undone by grief, the goddess was moved, like first rain reaching a fish in a drying pond.
yv.3.16.50.claim: Sarasvati took pity on the shattered queen, as the first rain pities a fish gasping in a drying pond.

yv.5.41.3.speaker: Prahlada
yv.5.41.3.line: So many decisions, so many duties, I was utterly worn out. For a moment now, I've found rest.
yv.5.41.3.claim: Worn out by weighing right and wrong and by a hundred royal duties, I have found a moment's rest.

yv.5.61.2.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.61.2.line: Seeing this way, the mind stops burning, like a child lost in the dark who is handed a lamp.
yv.5.61.2.claim: Holding to this vision the mind no longer burns, like a child in deep darkness who has been given a lamp.
yv.5.61.2.needs: The 'vision' is the non-dual understanding taught just before; it needs that context.

yv.5.64.33.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.5.64.33.line: A kind person is a shady tree: cool words for leaves, smiles for flowers. Rest there a while.
yv.5.64.33.claim: Under the tree of a good person, with cool words for leaves and smiles for flowers, one rests deeply at once.

yv.6b.44.32.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.6b.44.32.line: In its shade the tired deer of the mind rests, like a traveller worn out by a long, noisy road.
yv.6b.44.32.claim: In its shade the weary deer of the mind rests, a traveller worn out since birth on a noisy road.

viv.8.not_good_enough.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 492
viv.8.not_good_enough.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.not_good_enough.listener: Mary Hale, whose father had just died
viv.8.not_good_enough.line: the most curious cause of suffering when somebody goes off is the feeling that I was not good enough to that person.
viv.8.not_good_enough.claim: When someone dies, a strange cause of suffering is the feeling that I was not good enough to them; it is only a form of sorrow.

viv.8.heart_lives_on.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 492
viv.8.heart_lives_on.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.heart_lives_on.listener: Mary Hale, whose father had just died
viv.8.heart_lives_on.line: I am sorry, because in spite of monastic training, the heart lives on;
viv.8.heart_lives_on.claim: Even after monastic training the heart lives on; he is sorry at the death of one of the best souls he knew.

viv.8.smiles_and_tears.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 493
viv.8.smiles_and_tears.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.smiles_and_tears.listener: Mary Hale, in her first great grief
viv.8.smiles_and_tears.line: We learn, through smiles and tears we learn. We don't know why, but we see it is so; and that is enough.
viv.8.smiles_and_tears.claim: Experience is the one teacher; through smiles and tears we learn, without knowing why, and that is enough.
viv.8.smiles_and_tears.needs: Fits weeks after a loss, not the first days; can sound like 'grief is a lesson'.

viv.8.exchange_grief.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 493
viv.8.exchange_grief.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.exchange_grief.listener: Mary Hale, whose father had just died
viv.8.exchange_grief.line: if it were possible to exchange grief, and had I a cheerful mind, I would exchange mine for your grief ever and always.
viv.8.exchange_grief.claim: If grief could be exchanged and he had a cheerful mind, he would take his friend's grief for his own, always.

viv.5.soul_is_a_star.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 5, Epistles – First Series, XXXI, p. 70
viv.5.soul_is_a_star.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.soul_is_a_star.listener: Sara Ole Bull ('Dhira Mata'), on the death of her father
viv.5.soul_is_a_star.line: Each soul is a star, and all stars are set in that infinite azure, that eternal sky, the Lord.
viv.5.soul_is_a_star.claim: Each soul is a star set in the eternal sky of the Lord; the departed has put off an old garment and stands where he always was.
viv.5.soul_is_a_star.needs: The soul beyond the body and the frame of rebirth.

viv.7.round_us_this_minute.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 7, Epistles – Third Series, XXXV, p. 500
viv.7.round_us_this_minute.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.7.round_us_this_minute.listener: Prof. John Henry Wright, whose 16-year-old daughter had died
viv.7.round_us_this_minute.line: All that we ever had are round us this minute, for the spirit can neither come nor go, it only changes its plane of manifestation.
viv.7.round_us_this_minute.claim: The spirit neither comes nor goes; all we ever had are round us this minute, only changed in how they appear.
viv.7.round_us_this_minute.needs: The passage frames the world as Maya with the Lord alone true; that framing can feel like denial to a fresh griever.

viv.4.agony_at_the_heart.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 4, Writings: Prose: A Message Of Sympathy To A Friend, p. 355
viv.4.agony_at_the_heart.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.agony_at_the_heart.listener: D. R. Balaji Rao, who had lost his son
viv.4.agony_at_the_heart.line: There is, Father of Love, an agony at the heart which is fighting against that calm resignation which Thou teachest
viv.4.agony_at_the_heart.claim: Even knowing we are to submit, there is an agony at the heart that fights against the calm acceptance God teaches.

viv.8.soul_of_light.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Writings: Poems: Light, p. 168
viv.8.soul_of_light.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.soul_of_light.line: I look behind and after And find that all is right, In my deepest sorrows There is a soul of light.
viv.8.soul_of_light.claim: Looking back and ahead he finds all is right; in his deepest sorrows there is a soul of light.

viv.8.never_never_never.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, XXIII, p. 316
viv.8.never_never_never.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.never_never_never.line: Sister, there is a God — a Father — a Mother who never leaves His Children, never, never, never.
viv.8.never_never_never.claim: There is a God, a Father and a Mother, who never leaves His children, never, never, never.

viv.8.faith_totters.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, XXIII, p. 316
viv.8.faith_totters.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.faith_totters.line: What a rogue am I that in the face of such mercies sometimes the faith totters — seeing every moment that I am in His hands.
viv.8.faith_totters.claim: Even surrounded by mercies and knowing he is in God's hands, his faith sometimes totters and his mind grows despondent.

viv.6.tropics_or_poles.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 6, Epistles – Second Series, LXII, p. 304
viv.6.tropics_or_poles.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.tropics_or_poles.listener: Sara Bull (letter), addressed as a prayer to God
viv.6.tropics_or_poles.line: Thou wilt be with me in the tropics or at the poles, on the tops of mountains or in the depth of oceans.
viv.6.tropics_or_poles.claim: Wherever he goes, tropics or poles, mountain tops or ocean depths, the Lord will be with him and never leave him.

viv.7.i_am_near.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 7, Epistles – Third Series, IX, p. 452
viv.7.i_am_near.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.7.i_am_near.listener: Prof. John Henry Wright (poem sent in a letter)
viv.7.i_am_near.line: Meseems I hear Thee whispering sweet My love, "I am near", "I am near". My heart gets strong.
viv.7.i_am_near.claim: He hears the Beloved whisper 'I am near', and his heart grows strong.

viv.6.weary_take_my_hand.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 6, Notes of Class Talks and Lectures: On Bhakti-Yoga, p. 91
viv.6.weary_take_my_hand.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.6.weary_take_my_hand.line: Lord! I have become weary. Oh, take me by the hand, Lord, I take shelter with Thee
viv.6.weary_take_my_hand.claim: A prayer: I have become weary; take me by the hand, Lord, I take shelter with You.

viv.8.take_things_easy.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CXXIV, p. 448
viv.8.take_things_easy.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.take_things_easy.line: The Lord is watching over us; there is no fear; do not lose your nerves, keep your health and take things easy.
viv.8.take_things_easy.claim: Do not lose your nerve, keep your health and take things easy; the best work is done by alternating work and rest.

viv.7.want_a_bit_of_peace.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 7, Epistles – Third Series, LII, p. 525
viv.7.want_a_bit_of_peace.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.7.want_a_bit_of_peace.listener: Mrs. Blodgett ('Aunt Roxy'), his hostess in Los Angeles
viv.7.want_a_bit_of_peace.line: I just want a bit of peace badly — pray for me.
viv.7.want_a_bit_of_peace.claim: In failing health, he writes that he wants a bit of peace badly and asks to be prayed for.

viv.5.bob_up_soon.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 5, Epistles – First Series, CIII, p. 160
viv.5.bob_up_soon.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.5.bob_up_soon.line: Yet I am sure to bob up soon and am waiting for the next turn.
viv.5.bob_up_soon.claim: Things are gloomy, a friend has died and his health is wretched, yet he is sure to bob up soon and waits for the next turn.

viv.8.mental_hell_lifted.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVII, p. 494
viv.8.mental_hell_lifted.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.mental_hell_lifted.line: I have been living in mental hell. It is partially lifted now, and I hope for better days, better states.
viv.8.mental_hell_lifted.claim: The last two years were a mental hell; it is partly lifted now, and he hopes for better days.

viv.2.nothing_is_lost.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 2, Hints On Practical Spirituality, p. 36
viv.2.nothing_is_lost.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.nothing_is_lost.line: But though it is so hard to reach the goal, yet even our smallest attempts are not in vain. We know that nothing is lost.
viv.2.nothing_is_lost.claim: Though the goal is hard to reach, even our smallest attempts are not in vain; nothing is lost.

viv.2.still_small_voice.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 2, Jnana-Yoga: Maya And Freedom, p. 123
viv.2.still_small_voice.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.2.still_small_voice.line: in the midst of sorrow and suffering, even in this world where life and death are synonymous, even here, there is a still small voice
viv.2.still_small_voice.claim: Even in a world of sorrow where life and death are one, a still small voice in every heart says there is a way out.
viv.2.still_small_voice.needs: The lecture's frame is Maya as a prison; the line rests on it.

viv.4.circle_of_light.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 4, Lectures and Discourses: Christ, The Messenger, p. 153
viv.4.circle_of_light.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.4.circle_of_light.line: there is always somewhere in our heart of hearts, however low and degraded we may be, a little circle of light
viv.4.circle_of_light.claim: However low we may be, there is always in our heart of hearts a little circle of light in touch with the divine.

viv.8.all_right_long_run.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Lectures and Discourses: Is Vedanta The Future Religion?, p. 127
viv.8.all_right_long_run.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
viv.8.all_right_long_run.line: There are mistakes but no sin; and in the long run everything is going to be all right.
viv.8.all_right_long_run.claim: There are mistakes but no sin; in the long run everything is going to be all right.
viv.8.all_right_long_run.needs: 'No sin' is about the self's nature; it does not excuse harm done to others.

tulsi_vp.72.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.72.line: Water does not drown the grass it once watered. The one who raised you will not let you sink.
tulsi_vp.72.claim: Ram did the poet good out of his own goodness, as water does not drown the grass it has itself nourished.
tulsi_vp.72.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.160.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.160.line: I have fallen, and you lift the fallen. We are a perfect match.
tulsi_vp.160.claim: The poet is fallen and Hari is the purifier of the fallen, so the two are well matched.
tulsi_vp.160.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.179.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.179.line: Where do I go, whom do I tell? You are the support of those who have none.
tulsi_vp.179.claim: With nowhere to go and no one who will listen, the poet finds in Ram the only support of the supportless.

tulsi_vp.184.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.184.line: Say his name, and slowly the burning in the heart eases.
tulsi_vp.184.claim: Repeating Ram's name removes the burning of the heart.
tulsi_vp.184.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

tulsi_vp.232.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.232.line: Who else feels another's pain as their own? To whom else would I tell mine?
tulsi_vp.232.claim: There is no other friend of the lowly who feels another's pain, so there is no one else to tell.

tulsi_vp.250.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.250.line: "You are mine. Do not lose heart, do not tremble."
tulsi_vp.250.claim: Afraid of the cruelty of the age, the poet asks Ram to say: Tulsi, you are mine, do not lose heart.

tulsi_vp.261.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.261.line: What I could not fix in ages, grace can mend in a moment.
tulsi_vp.261.misuse: Not a reason to stop trying; a release from the belief that everything rests on you.
tulsi_vp.261.claim: What the poet could not set right in countless ages, Ram sets right in a quarter of a moment.
tulsi_vp.261.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.270.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.270.line: Good or bad, I am still your own. Look my way, and let my faults go.
tulsi_vp.270.claim: The poet asks Ram to look his way and pass over his countless faults, since good or bad he is Ram's own.

tulsi_vp.274.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.274.line: When every limb has lost its strength, there is still a place where you are kept.
tulsi_vp.274.claim: There is no place for the suffering and destitute except the master who shelters even one with no strength left.

tulsi_dv.96.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.96.line: Tell the kind one everything, good and bad. The heaviness thins; peace grows.
tulsi_dv.96.claim: Telling the gracious Ram all one's merits and faults makes misery lean and contentment full.
tulsi_dv.96.needs: that the reader is willing to pray

tulsi_dv.100.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.100.line: When no one around you helps, good can still come from somewhere kinder.
tulsi_dv.100.claim: When everyone hinders and no one helps, whatever good comes will come from the gracious Ram.

tulsi_dv.143.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.143.line: Let the worry go. The trouble will pass; the heart's hope can still be met.
tulsi_dv.143.claim: Remembering the feet that freed Ahalya from her curse, give up worry: trouble will end and the heart's hope be met.
tulsi_dv.143.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.57.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.57.line: Abandoned as a child, he poured out his hunger just once, and was held.
tulsi_kv.7.57.claim: Abandoned by his parents and scorned, Tulsidas once told Ram his hunger and found a master who held nothing against him.

tulsi_kv.7.53.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.53.line: Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there I am still kept.
tulsi_kv.7.53.claim: Where no friend, spouse, child or parent can go with one, Ram alone forgives every fault and keeps one through the worst.
tulsi_kv.7.53.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_hb.34.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.34.line: You are the water and I the fish; you the mother, I the child. Stroke the place that hurts.
tulsi_hb.34.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
tulsi_hb.34.claim: In pain, the poet calls Hanuman water to his fish and mother to his infant, his only support, and asks to be soothed.

tulsi_hb.33.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.33.line: Put your hand on my head. Let me not be left alone in this pain.
tulsi_hb.33.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
tulsi_hb.33.claim: The suffering poet asks Hanuman to lay a hand on his head: the servant of such a protector should not suffer.

tulsi_hb.17.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.17.line: Troubles and worries tear like cobwebs when you call on the one you trust.
tulsi_hb.17.claim: All troubles and worries tear like spider webs when Hanuman's name is taken.

tulsi_gv.2.52.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating)
tulsi_gv.2.52.line: She held his little shoes to her heart, and some mornings still went to wake him.
tulsi_gv.2.52.claim: After Ram leaves, Kausalya holds his childhood bow and little shoes to her heart and sometimes goes to wake him as before.

sur.vp.1.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.1.line: By grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see.
sur.vp.1.misuse: Not a medical promise; a hope that limits are not the last word.
sur.vp.1.claim: By Hari's grace the lame cross mountains, the blind see, and the pauper walks under a royal canopy.

sur.vp.2.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.2.line: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one.
sur.vp.2.claim: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one.

sur.vp.107.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.107.line: In the hardest days he walked beside me and kept me as the eyelid keeps the eye.
sur.vp.107.claim: In my troubles you met me whenever I remembered you and guarded me as the eyelid guards the eye.

sur.vp.167.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.167.line: Lord, do not weigh my good points against my faults. Just keep me.
sur.vp.167.claim: Lord, do not weigh my virtues and faults.

sur.vp.236.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.236.line: Good or bad, we are still yours.
sur.vp.236.claim: Good or bad, we are yours, and our shame and honour are yours to carry.

sur.vp.271.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.271.line: The touchstone turns any iron to gold, the shrine's or the butcher's.
sur.vp.271.claim: Lord, do not hold my faults in mind; like the touchstone that turns any iron to gold, carry me across.

sur.bgs.316.speaker: the gopis
sur.bgs.316.line: "Since he left, it has been monsoon in our eyes."
sur.bgs.316.claim: Since Shyam went away our eyes rain night and day; it is always monsoon for us.

kabir.kk.66.speaker: Kabir
kabir.kk.66.line: The lily lives in water, the moon in the sky. Those we love are never far.
kabir.kk.66.claim: The lily lives in water and the moon in the sky, yet whoever is dear to one is near.

kabir.kk.71.speaker: Kabir
kabir.kk.71.line: Even if I am a wayward child, I am still my father's child.
kabir.kk.71.claim: Father, forgive my faults; even if I am a bad son, my honour is still my father's care.

kabir.sdg.samrathai.1.speaker: Kabir
kabir.sdg.samrathai.1.line: Whoever has no one has you. At your door, no one is turned away.
kabir.sdg.samrathai.1.claim: Whoever has no one has you, and at your court no one is left deprived.

rahim.193.speaker: Rahim
rahim.193.line: Remembering is a kind of nearness. People who were parted do meet again.
rahim.193.claim: Remembrance that returns again and again is best; those who were parted meet again.

rahim.91.speaker: Rahim
rahim.91.line: People may laugh at your sorrow. There is one who listens, and having listened, helps.
rahim.91.claim: People laugh on hearing one's sorrow and give no steadiness; Raghuvir listens and then acts.

rahim.89.speaker: Rahim
rahim.89.line: Being brought low has one gift: the Friend of the lowly comes close.
rahim.89.misuse: Not a call to accept humiliation; about the closeness found in low times.
rahim.89.claim: The blind world does not know the sweetness of lowliness, which wins the Friend of the lowly as friend.

rahim.61.speaker: Rahim
rahim.61.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
rahim.61.claim: To the one given body and mind and housed in the heart, what joy or sorrow remains to be told?

meera.kk.3.ref: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
meera.kk.3.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.3.line: "No one knows my pain. Only the wounded know the wounded."
meera.kk.3.claim: No one knows my pain; only the wounded know the state of the wounded.

rcm.1.19.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.19.doha.1.line: Want light inside and out? Keep Ram's name like a lamp on the doorstep of your tongue.
rcm.1.19.doha.1.claim: Keeping Ram's name on the tongue lights both the inner and the outer life.
rcm.1.19.doha.1.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

rcm.1.19.chaupai.3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.19.chaupai.3.line: Remember the name even when you cannot see the form, and love wells up in the heart.
rcm.1.19.chaupai.3.claim: Remembering the name even without seeing the form brings a special love into the heart.
rcm.1.19.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

rcm.1.25.chaupai.4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.25.chaupai.4.line: When no practice, devotion or wisdom seems within reach, the name of Ram is still a support.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.4.claim: In this age neither ritual, devotion nor discernment is within reach; the name of Ram is the one support.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.4.needs: that the reader wants a devotional support

rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.line: The name of Ram is a father and a mother, a well-wisher in this world and the next.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.claim: In a terrible age the name of Ram is a wish-giving tree, and a father and mother in this world and the next.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader wants a devotional support

rcm.1.26.chaupai.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.26.chaupai.1.line: With love or without, even irritated or lazy: say the name, and good comes from every side.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.1.claim: Repeated with love or without, even in irritation or laziness, the name brings good from every direction.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.1.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.line: I am a poor servant; he is a good master who looks from his side and still cares for me.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.claim: Ram is a good master who looks from his own side and cares for even a poor servant.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.1.27.chaupai.3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.27.chaupai.3.line: He does not keep your mistake in mind. He remembers your heart a hundred times.
rcm.1.27.chaupai.3.claim: The Lord does not keep a devotee's lapse in mind and remembers the devotee's heart a hundred times.
rcm.1.27.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader relates to Ram as Lord

rcm.1.27.chaupai.2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.27.chaupai.2.line: Even when it comes out badly, he hears what you meant.
rcm.1.27.chaupai.2.claim: Ram is pleased by what his servant means in the heart, even when it is badly said.
rcm.1.27.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader relates to Ram as Lord

rcm.1.26.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.26.doha.1.line: He made stones float and monkeys wise. He will honour even a clumsy servant's love.
rcm.1.26.doha.1.claim: Ram, who made stones float and monkeys into wise ministers, will honour even a foolish servant's love.
rcm.1.26.doha.1.needs: that the reader relates to Ram as Lord

rcm.1.186.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.186.doha.1.line: The infinite one lies in a mother's lap, won over by love.
rcm.1.186.doha.1.claim: The formless, unborn Absolute lies in Kausalya's lap, brought there by love and devotion.

rcm.1.8.chaupai.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.8.chaupai.1.line: Seeing the whole world as full of Sita and Ram, I bow to every being with folded hands.
rcm.1.8.chaupai.1.claim: Knowing the whole world of beings to be filled with Sita and Ram, Tulsidas bows to all with folded hands.

rcm.2.127.doha.1.speaker: Valmiki
rcm.2.127.doha.1.line: The one who wants nothing from you and simply loves you: that heart is your own home.
rcm.2.127.doha.1.claim: Ram lives always in the heart of one who wants nothing from him and simply loves him.

rcm.2.196.doha.1.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.196.doha.1.line: Not wealth, not pleasure, not even liberation: only love for Ram, life after life.
rcm.2.196.doha.1.claim: Bharat asks for neither wealth, duty, pleasure nor liberation, only love for Ram's feet in every birth.

rcm.2.197.chaupai.4.speaker: Triveni (a voice from the rivers)
rcm.2.197.chaupai.4.line: You torment yourself with guilt for nothing. No one is dearer to Ram than you.
rcm.2.197.chaupai.4.claim: Bharat is good in every way and dearest of all to Ram, so his guilt is baseless.
rcm.2.197.chaupai.4.needs: that the reader's guilt is larger than anything they actually did

rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.line: Whether he turns me away or takes me in, my refuge is still at his feet.
rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.claim: Whether Ram rejects him or honours him, Bharat's only refuge is Ram's feet; the fault is the servant's.
rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.needs: knowing Bharat is blameless; and that the refuge is in God, not in a person who mistreats you

rcm.2.225.chaupai.3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.2.225.chaupai.3.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
rcm.2.225.chaupai.3.claim: Shame over his mother's deed holds Bharat back, and remembering Ram's nature quickens his steps.

rcm.2.235.chaupai.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.2.235.chaupai.1.line: He understood each hurting person, and met each one in the way they longed for.
rcm.2.235.chaupai.1.claim: Ram understood every distressed person and met each in the way that person longed for.

rcm.2.285.chaupai.1.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.285.chaupai.1.line: You are father, mother, friend, teacher, master: the one who values what is good in us and lifts our faults.
rcm.2.285.chaupai.1.claim: Ram is father, mother, friend, teacher and master, who values merits, removes faults and protects those who seek refuge.
rcm.2.285.chaupai.1.needs: that the reader relates to Ram as Lord

rcm.2.287.chaupai.1.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.287.chaupai.1.line: I came out of grief and love, even against your wish, and you took it all kindly.
rcm.2.287.chaupai.1.claim: Though Bharat came against his father's order out of grief and love, Ram looked from his own side and took it all as good.

rcm.3.2.sortha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.3.2.sortha.1.line: He had done wrong, and still, when he came for shelter, the Lord let him go out of tenderness.
rcm.3.2.sortha.1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm.3.2.sortha.1.claim: Though Jayant's offence deserved death, Ram, out of tenderness, let him go when he came for refuge.
rcm.3.2.sortha.1.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram and owns the harm done

rcm.3.7.chaupai.3.speaker: Sutikshna
rcm.3.7.chaupai.3.line: I have no devotion, no wisdom, no steady love. But he loves the one who has nowhere else to go.
rcm.3.7.chaupai.3.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm.3.7.chaupai.3.claim: Sutikshna finds in himself no devotion, wisdom or practice, and relies on this: the Lord loves one who has no other refuge.

rcm.3.7.chaupai.7.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.3.7.chaupai.7.line: The Lord hid behind a tree to watch his devotee's joy.
rcm.3.7.chaupai.7.claim: Seeing his devotee's overflowing love, Ram watches from hiding and then appears in his heart.

rcm.3.13.chaupai.6.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.13.chaupai.6.line: The one whose voice catches and eyes fill at my name, without pride or pretence: I am theirs.
rcm.3.13.chaupai.6.claim: Ram lives always in the power of one who sings his praise with tears and has no lust, pride or pretence.

rcm.3.13.doha.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.13.doha.1.line: In the heart of the one who loves without wanting anything back, I rest always.
rcm.3.13.doha.1.claim: Ram rests always in the heart of those who make him their goal in word, deed and mind and worship without desire.

rcm.3.26.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.3.26.doha.1.line: He touched the dying bird's head, and looking at that face, all his pain was gone.
rcm.3.26.doha.1.claim: Ram touches the dying Jatayu's head, and gazing at Ram's face all Jatayu's pain leaves him.

rcm.3.32.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.32.chaupai.4.line: You are most dear to me. What even yogis struggle to reach has become easy for you today.
rcm.3.32.chaupai.4.claim: Ram tells Shabari she is most dear to him and that the state hard for yogis is easy for her today.

rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.speaker: Shiva
rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.line: I tell you from my own experience: love for God is real; the rest passes like a dream.
rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.misuse: Not 'nothing in your life matters'; Shiva is naming what lasts.
rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.claim: Shiva says from his own experience that worship of Hari is real and the whole world is a dream.
rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.needs: a reader asking what lasts; not someone in fresh loss

rcm.3.38.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.38.chaupai.2.line: Do I ever hide anything from my own? Never let go of this trust.
rcm.3.38.chaupai.2.claim: Ram withholds nothing from his own, and asks that this trust never be given up.
rcm.3.38.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.line: Those who rely on me, I guard always, as a mother pulls her child back from the fire.
rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.misuse: A mother's protection includes saying no; this is not a promise that nothing painful will happen. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.claim: Ram guards those who worship him with no other reliance as a mother pulls her child back from fire or a snake.
rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram; the refusal in question was of his own desire

rcm.3.39.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram
rcm.3.39.chaupai.4.line: The humble devotee is like my little child, and has my strength to lean on.
rcm.3.39.chaupai.4.claim: The humble devotee is like the Lord's small child and relies on his strength, while the wise rely on their own.
rcm.3.39.chaupai.4.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.4.4.chaupai.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.4.4.chaupai.1.line: I have many faults, Lord. Don't let your servant slip from your mind.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.1.claim: Hanuman owns many faults and asks only that the master not forget his servant; the soul is freed by the Lord's tenderness.

rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.line: A child relies on its mother and stops worrying; she has to look after it.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.claim: One who knows no method of worship can rely on the Lord as a child relies on its mother, and live without worry.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.4.4.chaupai.3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.4.4.chaupai.3.line: Ram lifted him up, held him close, and cooled him with his own tears.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.3.claim: Ram lifts the distressed Hanuman, holds him to his heart and cools him with his own tears.

rcm.4.30.chaupai.2.speaker: Sampati
rcm.4.30.chaupai.2.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
rcm.4.30.chaupai.2.claim: Even sinners cross the world's ocean by Ram's name; as his messengers, give up timidity, hold Ram in the heart and act.

rcm.5.1.shloka.2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.5.1.shloka.2.line: There is no other longing in my heart. Give me full devotion, and a mind free of craving.
rcm.5.1.shloka.2.claim: The devotee has no other longing and asks Ram for full devotion and a mind free of desire and its kin.
rcm.5.1.shloka.2.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

rcm.5.1.doha.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.1.doha.1.line: He thanked the mountain and said: how can I rest before Ram's work is done?
rcm.5.1.doha.1.misuse: About commitment to a task that matters; rest is allowed, and Hanuman thanks the one who offers it.
rcm.5.1.doha.1.claim: Hanuman honours the offered rest and declines it: there is no rest for him until Ram's work is done.

rcm.5.6.chaupai.2.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.6.chaupai.2.line: I have no practice and no love to speak of. But meeting you tells me grace has found me.
rcm.5.6.chaupai.2.claim: Vibhishan, with no practice and no love to show, takes hope: one meets a saint only by Hari's grace.

rcm.5.6.doha.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.6.doha.1.line: Even on someone as ordinary as me, he showed kindness. Remembering it, Hanuman wept.
rcm.5.6.doha.1.claim: Hanuman says that even on one as lowly as himself Ram showed kindness, and weeps remembering it.

rcm.5.13.chaupai.5.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.13.chaupai.5.line: Hold steady, mother. Remember Ram, and let my words take away your fear.
rcm.5.13.chaupai.5.claim: Hanuman asks Sita to hold courage, remember Ram who gives his servants joy, call his power to mind and put away fear.

rcm.5.14.doha.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.14.doha.1.line: We have no great strength of our own. By the Lord's power, the small can do the impossible.
rcm.5.14.doha.1.claim: Monkeys have no great strength or wit of their own, but by the Lord's power a tiny snake can swallow Garuda.

rcm.5.20.doha.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.20.doha.1.line: Even now, go to him for refuge and he will protect you and forget your offence.
rcm.5.20.doha.1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm.5.20.doha.1.claim: Ram protects those who bow to him; if even Ravana goes to him for refuge, he will forget the offence.
rcm.5.20.doha.1.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram and owns the wrong

rcm.5.28.doha.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.28.doha.1.line: Your name guards her day and night; thinking of you is the door. How could life slip away?
rcm.5.28.doha.1.misuse: Speaks of how remembrance kept Sita going through captivity; if you are in danger or despair, reach out for help too.
rcm.5.28.doha.1.claim: Sita's life cannot leave her because Ram's name guards her, meditation on him is the door, and her eyes are fixed on her feet.

rcm.5.30.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.30.chaupai.1.line: Hearing of her pain, his eyes filled: can one who takes refuge in me ever truly be lost?
rcm.5.30.chaupai.1.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
rcm.5.30.chaupai.1.claim: Ram weeps on hearing of Sita's suffering and asks whether calamity can touch one whose only refuge is him.

rcm.5.30.chaupai.2.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.30.chaupai.2.line: Real calamity is only this: the moment we stop remembering you.
rcm.5.30.chaupai.2.claim: The only real calamity is when remembrance and worship of the Lord stop.
rcm.5.30.chaupai.2.needs: a devotee's frame; said about Sita, whose remembrance never broke

rcm.5.32.chaupai.1.speaker: Hanuman
rcm.5.32.chaupai.1.line: Offered anything, he asked only for a love that never leaves.
rcm.5.32.chaupai.1.claim: Offered any reward, Hanuman asks only for unfailing devotion.

rcm.5.41.chaupai.4.speaker: Sugriva / Ram
rcm.5.41.chaupai.4.line: You have reasoned well, friend. But my vow is to take away the fear of whoever comes for refuge.
rcm.5.41.chaupai.4.claim: Ram grants that suspicion is sound policy, yet holds to his vow to remove the fear of whoever comes for refuge.

rcm.5.42.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.42.chaupai.2.line: If they were truly wicked, would they have turned toward me at all?
rcm.5.42.chaupai.2.claim: One truly wicked at heart never takes to worship, so whoever comes before Ram is not wicked at heart.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.5.43.doha.1.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.43.doha.1.line: I heard of you and came. Save me, you who take away distress.
rcm.5.43.doha.1.claim: Vibhishan, having heard of Ram's fame, comes crying to be saved by the one whose refuge brings joy.

rcm.5.44.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.44.chaupai.3.line: You lived among the cruel day and night. I know how you kept your goodness.
rcm.5.44.chaupai.3.claim: Ram acknowledges that Vibhishan lived day and night among the wicked and still kept his dharma.

rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.line: Even one who has harmed everyone, if they come afraid and drop their pride, I make good at once.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.claim: Ram at once makes saintly even an enemy of all beings who comes to him in fear, giving up pride, delusion and deceit.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram and gives up deceit

rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.line: Gather every thread of love into one cord, and tie your heart to me.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.misuse: Not 'give up your family': it is gathering one's loves into a single devotion. Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.claim: One who gathers every attachment into one cord tied to Ram's feet, even-minded and wanting nothing, lives in Ram's heart.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

rcm.5.47.chaupai.3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm.5.47.chaupai.3.line: I came with my own wants. They were carried away in the river of love.
rcm.5.47.chaupai.3.claim: Vibhishan admits he came with a desire in his heart, and that love for Ram's feet has carried it away.

rcm.6.19.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.6.19.doha.1.line: He walked into the hostile room remembering Ram, steady as a lion.
rcm.6.19.doha.1.claim: Angad enters the enemy's court remembering Ram's feet, with a lion's bearing, steady and fearless.

rcm.6.19.sortha.3.speaker: Angad (thinking)
