rcm.6.19.sortha.3.line: The work is already done; I've only been given the honour of carrying it.
rcm.6.19.sortha.3.claim: Angad sees that the Lord's work accomplishes itself and that being sent is only an honour given to him.

rcm.6.111.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.6.111.doha.1.line: The one sages cannot reach in meditation is laughing and joking with the monkeys.
rcm.6.111.doha.1.claim: The one whom sages cannot reach in meditation and the Vedas call 'not this' plays and jokes with monkeys.

rcm.6.111.doha.2.speaker: Shiva
rcm.6.111.doha.2.line: No practice wins his kindness the way plain love does.
rcm.6.111.doha.2.claim: Yoga, chanting, charity, austerity, sacrifice and vows do not win Ram's grace as pure love does.

rcm.7.4.chaupai.8.speaker: Bharat
rcm.7.4.chaupai.8.line: Tell me: does he ever think of me?
rcm.7.4.chaupai.8.claim: After fourteen years Bharat asks only whether Ram ever remembers him, as one remembers a servant.

rcm.7.46.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.46.chaupai.3.line: This life is the boat, my grace the wind behind it, a good teacher at the helm.
rcm.7.46.chaupai.3.claim: The human body is a boat across the sea of becoming, with Ram's grace as the wind and a true teacher at the helm.

rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.line: If you call yourself mine and still hang every hope on others, what kind of trust is that?
rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.misuse: Not 'never accept help from people'; it is about where the heart's final reliance rests. Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.claim: One who is called Ram's servant and still rests his hopes on men does not really trust.
rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.needs: a committed devotee; this is a challenge, not a comfort

rcm.7.85.chaupai.5.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.85.chaupai.5.line: Without love, even the creator is just another being. With love, the lowliest is dear as life.
rcm.7.85.chaupai.5.claim: Without devotion even Brahma is dear to Ram only as any creature; with devotion the lowliest being is dear as life.

rcm.7.86.chaupai.2.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.86.chaupai.2.line: The child who simply loves the father is dear to him as life, though skilled at nothing.
rcm.7.86.chaupai.2.claim: A father loves all his sons alike, yet the one wholly devoted to him is dear as life though unskilled in everything.

rcm.7.86.doha.1.speaker: Ram
rcm.7.86.doha.1.line: Man, woman, any gender, any being: whoever loves me without deceit is supremely dear to me.
rcm.7.86.doha.1.claim: Man, woman, neither, or any being at all: whoever worships Ram wholeheartedly without deceit is supremely dear to him.

rcm.7.87.chaupai.4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.87.chaupai.4.line: The Lord of all cried for his mother, and she ran and held him close.
rcm.7.87.chaupai.4.claim: The child Ram cries, and his mother runs to him, holds him to her heart and feeds him.

rcm.7.116.chaupai.1.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.116.chaupai.1.line: Devotion is a jewel that shines day and night; it needs no lamp, no oil, no wick.
rcm.7.116.chaupai.1.claim: Devotion to Ram is a wish-granting jewel that lights the heart day and night without lamp, ghee or wick.

rcm.7.116.chaupai.9.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm.7.116.chaupai.9.line: The ocean gives rain only through clouds; grace reaches us through good people.
rcm.7.116.chaupai.9.claim: Devotion to Hari, the fruit of all practice, is found by no one without the saints, as rain reaches us through clouds.

rcm.7.121.doha.2.speaker: Shiva
rcm.7.121.doha.2.line: No gain is like good company, and good company itself is a grace.
rcm.7.121.doha.2.claim: There is no gain like the company of saints, and it does not come without Hari's grace.

rcm.7.126.chaupai.3.speaker: Shiva / Tulsidas
rcm.7.126.chaupai.3.line: Remember Ram, sing Ram, keep listening to what is good in him.
rcm.7.126.chaupai.3.claim: In this age there is no other means: remember Ram, sing of Ram, and always hear his virtues.
rcm.7.126.chaupai.3.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

rcm.7.126.doha.1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.7.126.doha.1.line: No one is as poor as me, and no one befriends the poor like you. Take this fear away.
rcm.7.126.doha.1.claim: None is as destitute as I and none befriends the destitute like Ram; so, Ram, remove my dread of worldly existence.

rcm.7.126.doha.2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.7.126.doha.2.line: As money is dear to the greedy, may you be that dear to me, always.
rcm.7.126.doha.2.claim: The poet asks that Ram be as constantly dear to him as a woman is to the lustful and money to the greedy.
rcm.7.126.doha.2.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

vr.6.18.26.speaker: Ram (quoting the sage Kandu)
vr.6.18.26.line: Whoever comes to you for shelter, frightened or proud, even a former enemy: protect them.
vr.6.18.26.claim: An enemy who seeks refuge, whether distressed or proud, must be protected by the self-possessed even at the cost of life.

vr.6.18.23.speaker: Ram
vr.6.18.23.line: A dove sheltered even the one who took its mate. How much more should I?
vr.6.18.23.claim: A dove received even the one who took its mate when he came for shelter; how much more should one like me.

vr.6.19.4.speaker: Narrator
vr.6.19.4.line: He comforted him with words and looked at him as if drinking him in with his eyes.
vr.6.19.4.claim: Rama comforted him with words and seemed to drink him in with his eyes.

vr.7.40.6.speaker: Ram
vr.7.40.6.line: My only request: remember me with love. Now go, free of worry.
vr.7.40.6.claim: Remember me always with great affection, and go free of distress.

vr.7.40.10.speaker: Hanuman
vr.7.40.10.line: Hearing your story will clear my longing for you, as wind clears the clouds.
vr.7.40.10.claim: Hearing the nectar of your deeds, I will dispel my longing for you as wind scatters a bank of cloud.

vr.7.40.12.speaker: Ram
vr.7.40.12.line: For each kindness you did me I'd give my life. May you never be in trouble needing it repaid.
vr.7.40.12.claim: For each service I would give my life; may I never have to repay you, since repayment needs your trouble.

ram_gita.5.speaker: Lakshman
ram_gita.5.line: I take refuge at your feet. Teach me how to cross over, simply.
ram_gita.5.claim: I take refuge at your feet, Lord, which free from the world; teach me so I may cross the endless ocean of ignorance easily.

ram_gita.61.speaker: Ram
ram_gita.61.line: Whoever turns to me in the heart, even now and then, becomes a light like the sun.
ram_gita.61.claim: Whoever serves me in the heart, now and then, as beyond or with qualities, becomes me and purifies the three worlds like the sun.

tulsi_vp.30.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.30.line: Remember him and worry loosens. His kind glance is a mine of blessings.
tulsi_vp.30.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_vp.30.claim: Remembering Hanuman frees one from trouble and worry, and his kind glance is a mine of every blessing.

tulsi_vp.34.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.34.line: Don't hold it against the hurting; they speak without thinking. Forgive me, looking from your side.
tulsi_vp.34.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_vp.34.claim: Those in great distress speak without thinking and should not be held to it; the poet asks pardon for what he said in pain.

tulsi_vp.35.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.35.line: In hard times we say bitter things. A good master understands and does good anyway.
tulsi_vp.35.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_vp.35.claim: In dire straits one speaks bitterly, and a good master understands and still does good to the one who wronged him.
tulsi_vp.35.needs: that the one addressed is God or a truly good elder

tulsi_vp.69.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.69.line: Friend of the helpless, luck of the unlucky, mother and father to the hungry: remember that name.
tulsi_vp.69.claim: Ram's name is provision for the destitute, friend of the helpless, family of the familyless and parents to the hungry.
tulsi_vp.69.needs: that the reader wants a devotional support

tulsi_vp.76.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.76.line: I said: I have no one anywhere. He patted my back, took my arm, and made me his own.
tulsi_vp.76.claim: When the poet said he had no one and clasped Ram's feet, Ram patted his back and made him his own.

tulsi_vp.102.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.102.line: The one who tied this knot is the one who can untie it.
tulsi_vp.102.claim: Hari gave the rare human body out of grace, and only he who tied the soul with delusion's rope can untie it.
tulsi_vp.102.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.103.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.103.line: Wherever my mistakes drag me, don't stop watching over me, as the tortoise watches her eggs.
tulsi_vp.103.claim: The poet prays that Ram remove every other reliance and never withdraw his care wherever karma drags him.

tulsi_vp.125.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.125.line: My heart is your house, and thieves have moved in. Come and see to your own home.
tulsi_vp.125.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_vp.125.claim: The poet's heart is Ram's house and many thieves have settled in it; his worry is that Ram's name will suffer.

tulsi_vp.128.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.128.line: Will you ever rest that hand on my head? Day and night I long for its shade.
tulsi_vp.128.claim: The poet longs day and night for Ram's hand on his head, the hand that makes the distressed fearless.

tulsi_vp.150.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.150.line: I worry about myself, and I don't. You have many like me; I have only you.
tulsi_vp.150.claim: The poet both worries for himself and does not: Ram has many like him, and he has only Ram.

tulsi_vp.165.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.165.line: In his court the rich are passed over and the poor are honoured. It has always been so.
tulsi_vp.165.claim: Ram's greatness is that in his court the wealthy are passed over and the poor are honoured.

tulsi_vp.167.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.167.line: Devotion is easy to talk about and hard to live. Only those who live it know.
tulsi_vp.167.claim: Devotion to Ram is easy to speak of and hard to practise; only one in whom it has taken hold knows it.

tulsi_vp.172.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.172.line: Will I ever live like this: content, kind, cool when insulted, speaking of others' good, not their faults?
tulsi_vp.172.claim: The poet longs to live as a saint: content, wanting nothing, devoted to others' good, unburned by harsh words, even in joy and sorrow.

tulsi_vp.177.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.177.line: Even if you leave me, Ram, I won't leave you. You are my father and mother.
tulsi_vp.177.claim: Even if Ram abandons him, the poet will not abandon Ram, who is father and mother to a bad son.
tulsi_vp.177.needs: that this is said to God; never a model for holding on to a person who has left or harmed you

tulsi_vp.181.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.181.line: Like Sugriva hiding from Bali, I'm afraid. Somehow, look my way; let me live under your arm.
tulsi_vp.181.claim: Terrified of his own karma as Sugriva was of Bali, the poet asks to live in the shelter of Ram's arm.

tulsi_vp.182.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.182.line: By your glance a losing throw turns into a winning one.
tulsi_vp.182.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_vp.182.claim: The poet hands the finding of a way to Ram, by whose glance a losing throw wins and the unseen is seen.
tulsi_vp.182.needs: surrender after effort, not in place of it

tulsi_vp.189.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.189.line: The road is hard and I've lost my way. Walk on, saying Ram.
tulsi_vp.189.claim: On a hard road with no provisions and the way forgotten, keep walking saying Ram's name.
tulsi_vp.189.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

tulsi_vp.191#2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.191#2.line: Once you take his shelter, he ties you in his cloth like a coin and never tests you again.
tulsi_vp.191#2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_vp.191#2.claim: However sinful, one who takes shelter of the name is kept by Ram like a coin tied in his cloth, never tested again.
tulsi_vp.191#2.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.201.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.201.line: What is a human life for, if we never help with someone else's load?
tulsi_vp.201.claim: A human body is gained to no purpose if one never, in body, word or mind, helps another's work.

tulsi_vp.217.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.217.line: If there were anyone else, why would I keep coming to you in tears?
tulsi_vp.217.claim: If there were anyone else to turn to, the poet would not keep coming to Ram in tears.

tulsi_vp.226.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.226.line: Where your love and trust are, your work gets done. For me those two syllables are mother and father.
tulsi_vp.226.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_vp.226.claim: Let others trust what they will; for the poet Ram's name is the wishing tree and his mother and father.

tulsi_vp.227.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.227.line: I wandered hungry; even sorrow pitied me. By the grace of the name, I now bear sweet fruit.
tulsi_vp.227.claim: The poet once wandered hungry, pitied even by sorrow, and by the grace of the name the thorn tree now bears mangoes.

tulsi_vp.229.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.229.line: I am always at peace on this strength: I belong somewhere great.
tulsi_vp.229.claim: The poet belongs to Ram alone, has lived on Ram's bread birth after birth, and is at peace on that strength.
tulsi_vp.229.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.240.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.240.line: Ram is won by plain, natural love. Everything else just floats on top.
tulsi_vp.240.claim: He alone is virtuous with whom Ram is pleased, and Ram is won by natural love; all else is oil on water.

tulsi_vp.257.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.257.line: Everyone is good to their own. Your feet, Ram, are good to everyone.
tulsi_vp.257.claim: Everyone is good to their own people, but Ram's feet are good to all, and the poor have no other refuge.

tulsi_vp.266.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.266.line: The more I try to come close, the further I fall. Still, I am yours.
tulsi_vp.266.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_vp.266.claim: The more the poet tries to come near, the farther he falls, yet he is Ram's though full of faults.

tulsi_vp.267.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.267.line: I've lain down at your door. I won't get up until you say: you are mine.
tulsi_vp.267.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_vp.267.claim: The poet vows to lie at Ram's door and not rise all his life until Ram says: you are mine.
tulsi_vp.267.needs: that the door is God's; never a model for waiting on a person who withholds acceptance

tulsi_vp.268.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.268.line: I'll know you've accepted me when my heart turns toward you as easily as it once turned away.
tulsi_vp.268.claim: The poet will know Ram has accepted him when his mind loves the Lord as naturally as it once clung to pleasures.

tulsi_vp.275.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.275.line: Door to door, no one spoke to me. Then good people said: don't worry; he turns no one away.
tulsi_vp.275.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_vp.275.claim: Ignored at every door where he begged, the poet was told by saints that Ram casts off no one who takes refuge.

tulsi_dv.85.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.85.line: People call me a heap of faults. I have one virtue: I trust you.
tulsi_dv.85.claim: People call the poet a store of faults, but he has one virtue: a sound trust in Ram.

tulsi_dv.152.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.152.line: A straight heart, straight words, straight deeds: that is what love for God gives birth to.
tulsi_dv.152.claim: Straightness of mind, speech and every deed is born of love for Ram.

tulsi_dv.256.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.256.line: Clinging to home loses it, fleeing home loses it too. Live in between, in the city of love.
tulsi_dv.256.claim: Both clinging to home and abandoning home lose it; one should dwell between house and forest in the city of Ram's love.

tulsi_dv.282.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.282.line: One trust, one strength, one hope: like the rain-bird waiting for its one cloud.
tulsi_dv.282.claim: The poet, like the rain-bird, has one trust, one strength and one hope: Ram, the dark cloud.

tulsi_dv.278.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.278.line: Whether you answer on time or stay silent my whole life, my heart still hopes in you.
tulsi_dv.278.misuse: About trust in God through unanswered seasons; not a reason to stay where a person ignores your needs.
tulsi_dv.278.claim: Whether the cloud rains in season or stays indifferent all his life, the rain-bird heart still hopes in Ram.
tulsi_dv.278.needs: that the one waited on is God; never a model for staying with a person who ignores you

tulsi_dv.405.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.405.line: When the person you trusted most turns on you, the Lord of the world still guards you.
tulsi_dv.405.misuse: Comfort after betrayal; it does not replace getting real-world help or protection.
tulsi_dv.405.claim: Against the treachery of one you trusted enough to sleep with your head in their lap, only the Lord of the world is guardian.

tulsi_dv.528.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.528.line: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the sea. Hanuman, out of love, simply leapt.
tulsi_dv.528.claim: A servant who knows his duty is greater than his master: Ram bridged the sea, and Hanuman leapt it.

tulsi_kv.7.7.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.7.line: Even when we fail beyond measure, he does not hold it in his heart.
tulsi_kv.7.7.claim: Ram does not take to heart even the unfathomable offences of his own people.
tulsi_kv.7.7.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.11.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.11.line: For the hurting and the alone, he makes shade with his own hand.
tulsi_kv.7.11.claim: Ram himself shades with his own hand the distressed, the poor and those with no protector.
tulsi_kv.7.11.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.36.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.36.line: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, friend, child and beloved. My trust is in him.
tulsi_kv.7.36.claim: Ram is the poet's mother, father, teacher, brother, companion, friend, son, master and beloved, and his only trust.
tulsi_kv.7.36.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.37.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.37.line: I don't speak for everyone. For me, this is the fruit of a life: my heart with Ram.
tulsi_kv.7.37.claim: For the poet, speaking only for himself, the fruit of living is to have mind, goal, love and strength in Ram.

tulsi_kv.7.48.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.48.line: If Ram is protecting, whom should I fear?
tulsi_kv.7.48.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_kv.7.48.claim: Prahlad felt no despair because of Narasimha's strength; if Ram protects, no one can kill, so there is no one to fear.
tulsi_kv.7.48.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.50.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.50.line: Where a million dangers surround you and no family is near, he is still there, with Hanuman.
tulsi_kv.7.50.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_kv.7.50.claim: Where countless dangers surround one and no kin is near, Ram, whose servant is Hanuman, protects and is the one helper.
tulsi_kv.7.50.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.67.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.67.line: High hopes, low luck, no job, no trade, no skill. The name of Ram saved my game.
tulsi_kv.7.67.claim: With high tastes, low fortune and no job, land, trade or skill, the poet's game was saved by Ram's name alone.

tulsi_kv.7.129.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.129.line: Wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.
tulsi_kv.7.129.claim: Ram, protector of the distressed, stands present wherever anyone remembers him.
tulsi_kv.7.129.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.182.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.182.line: Call his name and he comes running, like a cow who hears her calf cry.
tulsi_kv.7.182.claim: Ram comes running when his name is called, as a cow runs with flowing milk at her calf's cry.
tulsi_kv.7.182.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_kv.7.128.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.128.claim: Prahlad does not flee his father's drawn sword and answers that Ram is everywhere, even in the pillar.
tulsi_kv.7.128.needs: a story of faith under persecution; not advice to stay near someone violent

tulsi_gv.5.42.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_gv.5.42.line: Rich or poor, wise or foolish, weak or strong: whoever goes to him for refuge is held.
tulsi_gv.5.42.claim: Whoever goes to Ram for refuge fares well: rich or poor, great or small, wise or foolish, weak or strong, lame or blind.

tulsi_gv.5.44.speaker: Vibhishan
tulsi_gv.5.44.line: You know my sorrows, so I won't list them. Just look at me kindly, and I'll know I'm yours.
tulsi_gv.5.44.claim: The Lord already knows his servants' joys and sorrows; a kind look from him is how one knows one is accepted.

tulsi_gv.5.45.speaker: Ram
tulsi_gv.5.45.line: Whoever comes with nothing and nowhere to go, I take in and never abandon. I say it, arm raised.
tulsi_gv.5.45.claim: Ram never abandons one who comes for refuge lacking everything and with no place anywhere; none is dearer to him than his servant.
tulsi_gv.5.45.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_gv.6.7.speaker: Ram
tulsi_gv.6.7.line: All my strength is spent. And still my chest is full of worry for the one who came to me.
tulsi_gv.6.7.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a specific outcome, and it doesn't replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_gv.6.7.claim: Ram, his strength spent beside his fallen brother, still carries one worry: what will become of the one who took refuge with him.

tulsi_hb.10.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.10.line: A body like iron, a heart full of compassion. Remembering him eases my pain.
tulsi_hb.10.claim: Hanuman is hard as a thunderbolt in body and compassionate in mind, and remembering him takes away the poet's pain.

tulsi_hb.22.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.22.line: For someone as weak as me, you are the pillow I lean on.
tulsi_hb.22.claim: For one as poor and weak as the poet, Hanuman is the support he leans on.

tulsi_hb.29.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.29.line: I went door to door for scraps. You called me and raised me like your own child.
tulsi_hb.29.claim: The poet, once a destitute child begging scraps house to house, was called and raised like a son, and asks not to be forgotten.

tulsi_hb.30.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.30.line: I've tried every medicine; it keeps getting worse. Your delay hurts more than the pain.
tulsi_hb.30.misuse: An honest prayer in illness, not advice to stop treatment. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_hb.30.claim: After every medicine and charm has failed and the pain has grown, the poet tells Hanuman that his delay hurts more than the pain.

tulsi_hb.40.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.40.line: Even while I was doing wrong, you took me as your own and made me fit for Ram.
tulsi_hb.40.claim: Even while the poet practised bad conduct, Hanuman took him as his own and made him fit for Ram's hand.

bg.6.39.speaker: Arjuna
bg.6.39.line: Only you can clear this doubt completely. There is no one else I can ask.
bg.6.39.claim: Arjuna asks Krishna to cut this doubt completely, for no one but Krishna can remove it.

bg.7.1.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.1.line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
bg.7.1.claim: With mind attached to Krishna, practising yoga under his refuge, one will know him fully and without doubt.

bg.7.7.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.7.line: Everything is strung on me like pearls on a single thread.
bg.7.7.claim: Nothing is higher than Krishna; all this is strung on him like gems on a thread.

bg.7.18.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.18.line: Everyone who turns to me, even in need, is noble. The one who loves me is my very self.
bg.7.18.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
bg.7.18.claim: All four kinds of devotee are noble, but the wise one, steadfast and resorting to Krishna alone, is his very self.

bg.9.6.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.6.line: As the wind, wherever it blows, always rests in the sky, all beings rest in me.
bg.9.6.claim: As the mighty wind moving everywhere always rests in space, so all beings rest in Krishna.

bg.10.1.speaker: Krishna
bg.10.1.line: Listen again. I am telling you this for your good, because you are dear to me.
bg.10.1.claim: Krishna will speak his supreme word again for Arjuna's good, because Arjuna delights in it and is dear.

bg.11.42.speaker: Arjuna
bg.11.42.line: For every careless joke, every time I took you for granted, alone or in company, forgive me.
bg.11.42.claim: Arjuna asks the immeasurable Lord's forgiveness for disrespect shown in jest at play, rest, seat or meals, alone or in company.
bg.11.42.needs: the feeling of having taken someone for granted; the scene is the cosmic form

bg.11.54.speaker: Krishna
bg.11.54.line: By a love that looks nowhere else, I can truly be known, seen, and entered.
bg.11.54.claim: By undivided devotion alone Krishna can be known in this form, seen in truth and entered into.

bg.12.2.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.2.line: Those who rest their mind in me, always, with deep trust, I count as closest to me.
bg.12.2.claim: Those who fix their minds on Krishna and worship him ever united, with supreme faith, he deems the best yogis.

bg.12.6.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.6.line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
bg.12.6.claim: Those who resign all actions to Krishna, hold him supreme and worship him in single-minded meditation, he soon delivers from samsara.
bg.12.6.needs: a devotional reader; the record joins 12.6 and 12.7, so it overlaps bg.12.7

mbh.3.264.8.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.264.8.line: Krishna, Krishna... you who take away the pain of everyone who bows to you.
mbh.3.264.8.misuse: Calling on God in a crisis is prayer, not a promise that help will come in a particular form or time.
mbh.3.264.8.claim: Krishna, mighty-armed, imperishable lord of the world, destroyer of the pain of those who bow to you.

mbh.3.264.10.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.264.10.line: You give a way to those who have no way.
mbh.3.264.10.misuse: A way, not necessarily the one we wanted; keep taking practical steps too.
mbh.3.264.10.claim: You give a way to those who have no way, ancient one beyond breath, mind and thought.

mbh.3.264.11.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.3.264.11.line: I have come to you for shelter. Look after me with kindness; you love those who come to you.
mbh.3.264.11.claim: I have come to you for refuge; protect me in your compassion, you who love those who take refuge.

mbh.3.264.40.speaker: Krishna
mbh.3.264.40.line: I knew you were in trouble. Draupadi thought of me, so I came quickly.
mbh.3.264.40.misuse: Not a promise that every prayer is answered the same day; it shows that being thought of moves him.
mbh.3.264.40.claim: Knowing your danger, and because Draupadi thought of me, I came at once.

mbh.3.264.44.speaker: the Pandavas and Draupadi
mbh.3.264.44.line: With you beside us we got through it, like drowning people who reach a boat.
mbh.3.264.44.claim: With you as protector we crossed an impassable danger, like the drowning reaching a boat.

mbh.3.12.46.speaker: Krishna
mbh.3.12.46.line: You are mine and I am yours. Whoever is mine is yours.
mbh.3.12.46.claim: You are mine and I am yours; whoever hates you hates me and whoever follows you follows me.

mbh.5.81.26.speaker: Draupadi
mbh.5.81.26.line: When those who should have protected me only watched, I called to you in my heart: protect me.
mbh.5.81.26.misuse: Draupadi's inner prayer did not replace speaking up: she also challenged the whole court. Prayer is not a reason to stay silent about abuse.
mbh.5.81.26.claim: While the Pandavas sat unmoved and only watched, I called on you in my mind: Govinda, protect me.

mbh.12.46.14.speaker: Vaishampayana
mbh.12.46.14.line: Lying on a bed of arrows, Bhishma folded his hands and turned his whole mind to Krishna.
mbh.12.46.14.claim: Bhishma on the bed of arrows, pure and with folded hands, fixed his thought on Krishna in deed, mind and word.

mbh.12.46.122.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.46.122.line: Those who bow to Govinda, dark as a flax flower and dressed in yellow, have nothing to fear.
mbh.12.46.122.misuse: Fear may still come; devotion is a refuge within it, not a guarantee against bad events.
mbh.12.46.122.claim: Those who bow to Govinda, dark as the flax flower and clad in yellow, have no fear.

mbh.12.46.125.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.46.125.line: He is the piece of wood to hold on to in the whirlpools of life.
mbh.12.46.125.claim: Vishnu is the protecting circle against terror and the log to hold in the whirlpools of the river of samsara.

mbh.12.46.127.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.46.127.line: Food for the long road, medicine, rescue from grief: just two syllables, Ha-ri.
mbh.12.46.127.misuse: The name as a place to rest, not a cure that replaces medical, legal or emotional help.
mbh.12.46.127.claim: The two syllables 'Hari' are provision for life's wilderness, medicine for samsara and rescue from sorrow and grief.

mbh.12.46.131.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.46.131.line: I've come to you. Whatever is truly best for me, you think of it.
mbh.12.46.131.misuse: This surrender comes at the end of Bhishma's long life of effort and duty; it is not a reason to stop making choices.
mbh.12.46.131.claim: For your devotee who has taken refuge and seeks his goal, think of whatever is truly best.
mbh.12.46.131.needs: This comes at the end of a life of effort and duty

mbh.12.51.11.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.51.11.line: I can't tell up from down anymore. I'm standing only on your strength.
mbh.12.51.11.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
mbh.12.51.11.claim: I can no longer make out directions, sky or earth, and I stand only by your strength.

mbh.12.53.17.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.53.17.line: The burning, the fog, the exhaustion, the pain: by your grace they lifted at once.
mbh.12.53.17.misuse: This is Bhishma's experience of grace, not a promise of healing. Keep up medical care.
mbh.12.53.17.claim: Burning, confusion, exhaustion, weariness, faintness and pain all left me at once by your grace.

mbh.12.53.23.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.12.53.23.line: Thinking of you has made me feel young again. By your grace I can speak.
mbh.12.53.23.claim: Strengthened by meditating on you I feel young again and am able to speak what is good.

mbh.13.273.39.speaker: Bhishma
mbh.13.273.39.line: I am yours and you are my goal. Look after me always. Now let me go, Krishna.
mbh.13.273.39.claim: Protect always your calm, unpossessing devotee whose goal you are, and give me leave to go.

mbh.13.254.145.speaker: Arjuna
mbh.13.254.145.line: Lotus-eyed one, be the protector of those who love you.
mbh.13.254.145.claim: Lotus-eyed Janardana, be the protector of the devotees who love you.

mbh.13.43.45.speaker: Vishnu
mbh.13.43.45.line: For those stuck deep in the mud of confusion and chasing, Hari is the way out.
mbh.13.43.45.claim: For those sunk in the mire of delusion and wealth Hari is the way; the single-minded reach him through renunciation.

mbh.12.210.16.speaker: Narada
mbh.12.210.16.line: I have taken refuge in the one who holds the past, the present and the future.
mbh.12.210.16.claim: I have taken refuge in the Lord, protector of the world and master of past, future and present.

mbh.3.192.43.speaker: Narayana
mbh.3.192.43.line: When everything was flooded and you were frightened, I knew. So I showed you the world inside me.
mbh.3.192.43.claim: Seeing everything lost in one ocean you were distressed; I knew it, and so I showed you the world.

mbh.3.192.56.speaker: Markandeya
mbh.3.192.56.line: He is father and mother to every being. Go to him for shelter.
mbh.3.192.56.claim: Madhava is father and mother of all beings; go to him for refuge.

mbh.14.52.7.speaker: Arjuna
mbh.14.52.7.line: With you as our protector, we crossed an ocean, using you as our raft.
mbh.14.52.7.claim: With you as protector the Pandavas crossed the Kuru ocean, using you as a raft.

mbh.14.66.15.speaker: Kunti
mbh.14.66.15.line: You are our way and the ground we stand on. This family rests on you.
mbh.14.66.15.misuse: In the story the child is revived; prayer is not a promise of that outcome. Keep this card away from pregnancy-loss and child-loss contexts.
mbh.14.66.15.claim: You are our way and our foundation, and this family depends on you.

vishnu_gita.1.58.speaker: the devas
vishnu_gita.1.58.line: We exist only because of you, and we lean on you. Still we forget you.
vishnu_gita.1.58.claim: By your being alone we exist and are yours, Lord; though we depend on you, we fools forget you through maya.

sur.vp.11.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.11.line: I've never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in trouble, and he comes and stands beside you.
sur.vp.11.misuse: A friend who stands with you, not a guarantee that the trouble disappears.
sur.vp.11.claim: There is no friend like Hari; remembered in trouble, he comes at that moment and stands in between.

sur.vp.14.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.14.line: Govind accepts everyone's love, in whatever way they serve. He knows what is really in the heart.
sur.vp.14.claim: Govind accepts everyone's love in whatever spirit they serve, knowing the movement of the heart.

sur.vp.16.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.16.line: The Lord whose feet the whole world honours washed others' feet with his own hands.
sur.vp.16.claim: The Lord whose foot-water Shiva bears washed others' feet with his own hands for the Pandavas' sake.

sur.vp.32.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.32.line: Lord, your word is worth trusting. The one who holds up the whole world holds you too.
sur.vp.32.misuse: Trust is not a reason to stop earning or planning; Surdas's next words scold fretting, which the card leaves out.
sur.vp.32.claim: Trust in your word is true, Lord; the sustainer of the universe feeds and bears us.

sur.vp.37.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.37.line: When Krishna holds you close, not a hair on your head is harmed, even if the world turns against you.
sur.vp.37.misuse: Poetic assurance of inner safety, not a guarantee against harm; seek real protection from real threats.
sur.vp.37.claim: One whom Manmohan takes as his own loses not a hair, even if the whole world turns hostile.

sur.vp.71.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.71.line: Mind, stay Govind's. Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune: take whatever comes your way.
sur.vp.71.misuse: Accepting what comes is not accepting mistreatment; it is not chasing or dreading outcomes.
sur.vp.71.claim: O mind, remain Govind's, and accept whatever sorrow, joy, fame or fortune falls to you.

sur.vp.76.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.76.line: Make Krishna the master of your house, and live there as his helper.
sur.vp.76.claim: Make Nandanandan the master of the house and live in it as his servant.

sur.vp.125.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.125.line: The chatak bears every hardship waiting for the rain cloud, and asks no other water.
sur.vp.125.claim: The chatak bears every hardship in hope of the rain cloud and asks for no other water.

sur.vp.141.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.141.line: The name is a great shelter. Whoever comes to him is never turned away; he builds walls of kindness.
sur.vp.141.claim: Great is the shelter of the name; the Lord never turns out one who comes for refuge.

sur.vp.144.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.144.line: The joy of singing to Gopal doesn't come from rituals or a million pilgrimages.
sur.vp.144.claim: The joy of singing of Gopal does not come from japa, austerity or bathing at countless holy places.

sur.vp.153.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.153.line: Ram is the wealth of those with nothing: no thief takes it, it never runs out.
sur.vp.153.misuse: Inner wealth, not a financial plan: keep paying the bills and asking for help.
sur.vp.153.claim: Rama is the wealth of the poor: no thief takes it, it never lessens, and it serves in hard times.

sur.vp.170.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.170.line: You did so much for me. Even in the dark of the womb, you did not forget me.
sur.vp.170.claim: Lord, you did so much for me and never forgot me, even in the womb, though I achieved nothing.

sur.vp.173.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.173.line: Anyone would love a perfect servant. The Lord's greatness is that the lowly find shelter with him.
sur.vp.173.claim: Anyone would love a virtuous servant; the Lord's greatness is that the lowly find shelter with him.

sur.vp.176.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.176.line: Do whatever it takes so that I never let go of your feet, not even for a moment.
sur.vp.176.claim: Kind Lord, do whatever will keep your servant from leaving your feet even for a moment.

sur.vp.211.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.211.line: Who doesn't honour their own? A child may do a million wrongs; a mother doesn't keep count.
sur.vp.211.misuse: About God's forgiveness, not a reason to excuse harm done to real people.
sur.vp.211.claim: Who does not honour their own? A child may do countless wrongs and the mother does not count them.

sur.vp.215.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.215.line: Apart from your name, Lord, tell me: what other strength do I have?
sur.vp.215.claim: Apart from your name, Lord of the world, what other strength do I have?

sur.vp.219.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.219.line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.
sur.vp.219.claim: Keep me in your shelter, Lord; by your grace elders were sent who caught my hand as I was being swept away.

sur.vp.229.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.229.line: Who will listen? I see no one else who can help. Who do I tell my pain to, Krishna?
sur.vp.229.misuse: Telling God is good; telling a person too is also good.
sur.vp.229.claim: Who will hear my story? I see no one able but you; to whom shall I tell my pain?

sur.vp.235.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.235.line: You are my way and my keeper. I'm known as yours; whose else could I be?
sur.vp.235.claim: You are my refuge and keeper; elsewhere I find sorrow, and being called yours I can be no one else's.

sur.vp.245.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.245.line: He is the protector of those who have no one: kind, full of love, knowing every heart.
sur.vp.245.claim: The Lord is master of those who have no one, kind to the lowly, full of love, knower of every heart.

sur.vp.250.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.250.line: You never once delayed. You are easy to reach, and remembering you is enough to win you.
sur.vp.250.claim: You have never delayed; easy to reach by nature and won by remembrance, you give your devotees the undying.

sur.vp.258.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.258.line: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
sur.vp.258.misuse: About the worth of small sincere offerings, not a transaction for material gain.
sur.vp.258.claim: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives his all.

sur.vp.270.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.270.line: Remember me, Lord of Braj. There's no one else to set my life right.
sur.vp.270.misuse: A prayer from a lonely place, not advice to cut off from people.
sur.vp.270.claim: Remember me, Lord of Braj; I have no one else in the world to set me right.

sur.vp.279.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.279.line: Good times turn hard and hard times turn good. Trees flower, fruit and shed, each in its season.
sur.vp.279.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
sur.vp.279.claim: Fortune turns to trouble and trouble to fortune by nature, as trees flower, fruit and shed in season.

sur.vp.281.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.281.line: Not every day will be like this one. Remember Hari while you're well.
sur.vp.281.claim: Not all days pass alike, so remember and sing of Hari while the body is well.

sur.vp.295.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.295.line: Speak gently, be humble with everyone, and stay joyful.
sur.vp.295.claim: Speak gently, be humble with everyone, and remain always joyful.

sur.vp.297.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.297.line: How could he forget someone who comes to him? He fed you in the womb, then turned blood into milk.
sur.vp.297.misuse: Trust alongside work and planning; the pada's earlier lines about not caring for food or family are left out.
sur.vp.297.claim: How could the Lord forget one who takes refuge? He fed the child in the womb and turned blood into milk.

sur.vp.300.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.300.line: Where else will my heart find rest? Like a bird on a ship at sea, it flies off and returns.
sur.vp.300.claim: Where else can my mind find happiness? Like a ship's bird at sea, it flies off and returns to the ship.

sur.vp.301.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.301.line: Loving you is my breath. Without it I'd wither, like a leaf with no water.
sur.vp.301.claim: Devotion to you is my life-breath; without it your servant would be like a leaf without water.

sur.vp.423.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.423.line: Like a river that has reached the sea and never flows back, my heart doesn't wander from him.
sur.vp.423.claim: As a river that meets the sea never flows back, Sur's mind does not stray from the lotus-eyed one.

sur.bgs.34.speaker: a gopi (Bhramargeet)
sur.bgs.34.line: I can't forget his face for a moment, asleep or awake.
sur.bgs.34.claim: I cannot forget Mohan's face for a moment, asleep or awake.

sur.bgs.315.speaker: Radha (Bhramargeet)
sur.bgs.315.line: Come and see me once, Madhav. Who knows how long there is. Don't leave the wish unfulfilled.
sur.bgs.315.claim: Come and meet me once, Madhav; who knows when breath will leave and the heart's wish stay unmet.

meera.kk.2.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.2.line: My pain will ease only when Krishna himself is the healer.
meera.kk.2.misuse: A love-song image, not medical advice: keep seeing real doctors and counsellors.
meera.kk.2.claim: Meera's pain will end only when the dark Lord himself becomes the physician.

meera.kk.4.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.4.line: I'm in your shelter now. Keep me, you who are all kindness.
meera.kk.4.claim: Now I am in your shelter; keep me, treasure of grace.

meera.kk.5.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.5.line: I watch the road and sweep the path, standing there, looking for you.
meera.kk.5.claim: I watch the road and sweep the path, standing and gazing down the way.

meera.kk.6.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.6.line: You are all goodness; I am full of faults. I have no merit, but you are the one who forgives.
meera.kk.6.claim: You are the gracious master full of virtue and I am full of faults, without merit; you are the forgiver.

meera.kk.12.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.12.line: Mind, rest at Hari's feet: cool, soft as a lotus, taking away every burning.
meera.kk.12.claim: O mind, touch Hari's feet, lovely, cool and lotus-soft, which take away the threefold fire.

meera.kk.13.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.13.line: I found the treasure of the name. Spending never empties it, no thief can steal it, it grows every day.
meera.kk.13.misuse: Inner wealth, not a money promise.
meera.kk.13.claim: I have found the jewel of Rama's name, a wealth that spending cannot exhaust, thieves cannot take, and that grows daily.

up_shwetashwetar.6.18.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.6.18.line: Longing to be free, I take refuge in the God who lights up my understanding.
up_shwetashwetar.6.18.misuse: Refuge here comes at the end of a whole Upanishad of inquiry and meditation; it is not a substitute for effort.
up_shwetashwetar.6.18.claim: Seeking freedom, I take refuge in the God who gave Brahma the Vedas and lights up the understanding of the self.

up_shwetashwetar.3.17.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.3.17.line: The Lord of everything is also everyone's refuge and everyone's friend.
up_shwetashwetar.3.17.claim: The Lord who shines through all the senses and rules all is the refuge and friend of all.

up_shwetashwetar.3.20.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.3.20.line: The Lord is hidden in your own heart. By his grace one sees him, and sorrow lifts.
up_shwetashwetar.3.20.misuse: Grace here is not a reward for being good enough; the verse pairs it with letting go of grasping.
up_shwetashwetar.3.20.claim: The self is hidden in every creature's heart; one free of desire sees it by grace and is freed from sorrow.

up_shwetashwetar.4.21.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.4.21.line: Afraid, I come to you, Rudra. With your kind face, protect me always.
up_shwetashwetar.4.21.misuse: A prayer for protection, not a promise that nothing bad will happen; it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
up_shwetashwetar.4.21.claim: A frightened person takes refuge in Rudra as the Unborn and asks to be protected always by his kind face.
up_shwetashwetar.4.21.needs: A prayer, not a promise about outcomes.

up_shwetashwetar.3.5.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.3.5.line: Rudra, turn your gentle, peaceful form toward us, and look upon us.
up_shwetashwetar.3.5.claim: A prayer that Rudra look upon us with his auspicious, unfrightening, most peaceful form.

up_shwetashwetar.4.11.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.4.11.line: Knowing the kind Lord in whom everything rests, one comes to a peace that does not end.
up_shwetashwetar.4.11.claim: Knowing the one Lord in whom all this gathers and dissolves, the giver of blessings, one reaches lasting peace.

up_shwetashwetar.4.14.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.4.14.line: In the middle of chaos is the kind One who holds the world. Knowing him brings lasting peace.
up_shwetashwetar.4.14.misuse: Peace here is inner steadiness, not a promise that the chaos outside will stop.
up_shwetashwetar.4.14.claim: Knowing the auspicious One, subtle, in the midst of confusion, creator and sole encompasser of all, one reaches lasting peace.

up_shwetashwetar.4.15.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.4.15.line: He guards the world through time, hidden in every being. Knowing him loosens death's hold.
up_shwetashwetar.4.15.claim: Knowing the guardian of the world hidden in all beings, one cuts the nooses of death.
up_shwetashwetar.4.15.needs: 'Loosens death's hold' means freedom through knowledge, not recovery from illness.

up_shwetashwetar.6.11.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.6.11.line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.
up_shwetashwetar.6.11.claim: One God, hidden in all beings, is their inner self, the overseer of action, the witness, pure awareness, beyond qualities.

up_shwetashwetar.4.22.speaker: Seer
up_shwetashwetar.4.22.line: Rudra, spare our little ones, our children, our lives. We call on you always.
up_shwetashwetar.4.22.misuse: A parent's prayer of fear, not a promise of a particular outcome; it does not replace medical help.
up_shwetashwetar.4.22.claim: A prayer that Rudra not harm our children, our lives or our people in his anger.
up_shwetashwetar.4.22.needs: A prayer of fear, no promise of an outcome; never in place of medical help.

up_devi.9.speaker: The gods
up_devi.9.line: I take refuge in Durga, the blazing Goddess. She clears away the darkness.
up_devi.9.misuse: Refuge in the Goddess is strength to face hardship, not a guarantee it will vanish.
up_devi.9.claim: I take refuge in the goddess Durga, fire-coloured and blazing with tapas, who destroys darkness.

up_devi.16.speaker: The gods
up_devi.16.line: Goddess, I bow to you. Mother, protect us on every side.
up_devi.16.misuse: A child's prayer for protection, not a promise that nothing will go wrong.
up_devi.16.claim: Salutations to the Goddess; may the Mother protect us on every side.

up_devi.19.speaker: The gods
up_devi.19.line: I bow to her always: she takes away pain, she is pure, she is a refuge, she is kind.
up_devi.19.misuse: 'Takes away pain' is a devotee's praise, not a promise of a particular outcome; it does not replace care.
up_devi.19.claim: I bow always to the Goddess who removes affliction, grants enjoyment and liberation, and is the kind refuge.

up_devi.25.speaker: The gods
up_devi.25.line: I bow to you, Goddess: you end great fear, you ease great hardship, you are compassion itself.
up_devi.25.misuse: Praise of the Goddess's compassion, not a promise that hardship will disappear; seek practical help too.
up_devi.25.claim: I bow to the Goddess who destroys great fear, calms great hardship and is compassion in form.

up_devi.29.speaker: Seer
up_devi.29.line: She is called Durga because she carries us safely through hard places.
up_devi.29.claim: The Goddess is called Durga because nothing is higher than her and because she rescues from hardship.
up_devi.29.needs: Strength to face hardship, not a guarantee it disappears.

up_devi.30.speaker: Seer
up_devi.30.line: Frightened by life, I bow to Durga, who carries us across the ocean of the world.
up_devi.30.claim: Afraid of worldly existence, I bow to Durga, destroyer of wrongdoing, who carries us across its ocean.

up_devi.15.speaker: Seer
up_devi.15.line: She is the power within the self and the great wisdom. Whoever knows her crosses beyond grief.
up_devi.15.misuse: Crossing grief is not being told to stop grieving; it is a direction, not a deadline.
up_devi.15.claim: The Goddess is the power of the self and the great knowledge; whoever knows her so crosses beyond grief.
up_devi.15.needs: A direction, not a deadline for grieving.

up_skand.1.speaker: Seer
up_skand.1.line: Mahadeva, by just a trace of your compassion I stand unshaken. What more could I want?
up_skand.1.claim: By a trace of Mahadeva's compassion I am unshaken; I am pure consciousness, I am Shiva.

up_dakhsinamurti.26.speaker: Markandeya
up_dakhsinamurti.26.line: Fill the lamp with letting go, make devotion its wick, and light rises by itself in the dark.
up_dakhsinamurti.26.claim: With dispassion as oil and devotion as wick, the lamp of knowledge rises by itself in the darkness of delusion.

up_narayana.16.speaker: Devotee
up_narayana.16.line: I bow to Vishnu, peaceful in form, who takes away the fear of life and holds the universe.
up_narayana.16.claim: I bow to Vishnu, peaceful in form, support of the universe, who removes the fear of worldly existence.

up_shiv_sankalp.1.speaker: Seer
up_shiv_sankalp.1.line: My mind wanders far, awake or asleep. May that mind of mine hold only good intentions.
up_shiv_sankalp.1.claim: May my mind, the far-travelling light of lights in waking and in sleep, be of auspicious resolve.

up_shiv_sankalp.6.speaker: Seer
up_shiv_sankalp.6.line: The mind steers us like a charioteer steers horses. May my mind hold only good intentions.
up_shiv_sankalp.6.claim: May my mind, which leads people as a good charioteer leads horses, be of auspicious resolve.

shambhu_gita.6.91.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita.6.91.line: When the hurting and the seeking take refuge in me, my nature turns toward them like a mother.
shambhu_gita.6.91.misuse: Being met with a mother's care is not a promise of getting every wish; it does not replace practical help.
shambhu_gita.6.91.claim: When the distressed, the seeking and the wanting take refuge in me, my nature becomes a mother, fulfils them, and draws them forward.

shambhu_gita.7.53.speaker: The ancestors (pitris)
shambhu_gita.7.53.line: You who live in devotees' hearts: we come to you alone. Do whatever is truly good for us.
shambhu_gita.7.53.misuse: Handing over the outcome comes after the effort; it is not a reason to stop acting.
shambhu_gita.7.53.claim: Dweller in devotees' hearts, all-pervading one, we come to you alone for refuge; Shambhu, do now whatever will quickly bring us good.

shambhu_gita.7.65.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita.7.65.line: Here is an easy way: even in the hardest work, you need not drift from devotion.
shambhu_gita.7.65.claim: Shiva offers an easy, excellent means by which, even in the hardest work, one never turns away from devotion to him.
shambhu_gita.7.65.needs: the means itself is given in the verses that follow

shambhu_gita.7.80.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita.7.80.line: Among all reverent touches, I am the embrace, full of love, warmth, devotion and trust.
shambhu_gita.7.80.claim: Among touches worthy of reverence, Shiva says, I am the embrace filled with love, affection, devotion and faith.

shambhu_gita.6.75.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita.6.75.line: Devotees who know the Self cross the ocean of sorrow. One God is hidden in every being.
shambhu_gita.6.75.misuse: Crossing sorrow takes time; this is not an instruction to stop grieving.
shambhu_gita.6.75.claim: Self-knowing devotees surely cross the ocean of sorrow; the one God is hidden in all beings, beyond doubt.

shambhu_gita.2.43.speaker: Shiva
shambhu_gita.2.43.line: A gentle power, made of goodness, protects the world and always works for its good.
shambhu_gita.2.43.claim: Shiva's gentle power, whose form is dharma, protects the world; she is eternal and always works for the world's good.

shakti_gita.1.39.speaker: The gods
shakti_gita.1.39.line: Forgive our clumsy words, Mother. Even your forgiving us comes from your boundless grace.
shakti_gita.1.39.claim: We tried in a rush of feeling to speak of what is beyond words; forgive us, Mother, though even this forgiving is your boundless grace.
shakti_gita.1.39.needs: the fault is inadequate praise, not a real wrong done to someone

shakti_gita.1.47.speaker: The gods
shakti_gita.1.47.line: Your grace has no limit, Mother. Even those who can't understand you, you look on with kindness.
shakti_gita.1.47.claim: The Mother's grace has no limit; to devotees who cannot grasp her, she shows herself and gives both freedom and well-being.

shakti_gita.1.51.speaker: The gods
shakti_gita.1.51.line: Those who stay near your feet like bees near a lotus, Mother, you never let slip away.
shakti_gita.1.51.claim: Those who with undivided devotion hover like bees at the Mother's lotus feet she never lets slip from her sight.

shakti_gita.6.27.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita.6.27.line: When anyone comes to me for refuge, I draw them toward me in many ways.
shakti_gita.6.27.claim: When beings come to her for refuge, the Mother draws them toward herself in many different ways.

shakti_gita.6.149.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita.6.149.line: Like a mother, she lifts the devotee into her lap and carries him, for his good, to me.
shakti_gita.6.149.claim: For her wise devotees, Nature as knowledge frees them from all actions, holds them in her lap and, for their good, merges into the Mother.

shakti_gita.7.118.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita.7.118.line: I am your goal, your support, your mother, your home, your refuge, your friend.
shakti_gita.7.118.claim: I am the goal, sustainer, lord, mother, dwelling, refuge and friend; origin, dissolution, ground, treasure-house and imperishable seed.

shakti_gita.5.133.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita.5.133.line: Take shelter in me, and do your work with your mind joined to me.
shakti_gita.5.133.misuse: Shelter does not mean stepping back from the work; the instruction is to keep working.
shakti_gita.5.133.claim: Take up pure dependence on me and my shelter, and as my devotees always do your work joined to me.

shakti_gita.5.137.speaker: Devi
shakti_gita.5.137.line: Sheltered in her, devotees rise above ups and downs, let go of envy, and do good work.
shakti_gita.5.137.claim: Sheltered so, her devotees rise above the pairs, free of envy, engaged in fitting work, free of wrong and devoted to her.

dheesh_gita.1.4.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita.1.4.line: Father and friend of the world, he loves those who come to him and sets them free.
dheesh_gita.1.4.claim: The Lord, father and friend of the world, beyond the intellect yet presiding over it, loves those who seek refuge and frees them; so he is called Dheesh.

dheesh_gita.1.42.speaker: The seers
dheesh_gita.1.42.line: Lord, no peace came to our minds. So we have come to you for refuge.
dheesh_gita.1.42.claim: So no peace came into our minds, Lord; we have come to your world and taken refuge in you.

dheesh_gita.1.46.speaker: Dheesh (Ganesha)
dheesh_gita.1.46.line: I have no form, yet loving devotees see me in the form they long for, and are fulfilled.
dheesh_gita.1.46.claim: Though formless and all-pervading, the Lord is seen by loving devotees in many forms, as body or as light, and they are fulfilled.

dheesh_gita.4.19.speaker: Dheesh (Ganesha)
dheesh_gita.4.19.line: All beings are fed and protected, constantly, by a motherly care at the heart of things.
dheesh_gita.4.19.claim: By the dharma-filled motherly nature of his Prakriti, beings are protected and nourished without end.

dheesh_gita.7.27.speaker: The seers
dheesh_gita.7.27.line: Ganapati, guard my mind from wrong action, day and night, and turn it toward the good.
dheesh_gita.7.27.claim: Ganapati, ocean of compassion, may your radiance guard our minds day and night from wrong action and urge them to good.

surya_gita.6.60.speaker: The sages
surya_gita.6.60.line: My mind is restless as the wind. Teach me to steady it, to remember you and be at peace.
surya_gita.6.60.claim: Lord, teach us how to restrain this mind, restless as wind, so that we may remember you for lasting peace.

surya_gita.6.64.speaker: Surya
surya_gita.6.64.line: The love you feel for friends, the trust you feel for parents: turned toward God, that is devotion.
surya_gita.6.64.claim: The love one has for spouse and friends and the trust one has for parents, turned to God, is called devotion.

rcm.1.1.sortha.4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.1.sortha.4.line: Shiva, home of compassion, loves the lowly. May he be kind to me.
rcm.1.1.sortha.4.claim: Shiva, the home of compassion who loves the lowly, is asked to show grace.

rcm.1.15.chaupai.2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm.1.15.chaupai.2.line: Shiva and Parvati are my teacher, father and mother: friends of the lowly, giving every day.
rcm.1.15.chaupai.2.claim: Shiva and Parvati are teacher, father and mother to the poet, friends of the lowly and his well-wishers without motive.

rcm.1.54.chaupai.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.54.chaupai.1.line: Shiva, an ocean of compassion, never named her mistake aloud.
rcm.1.54.chaupai.1.misuse: Not naming a fault is mercy, not a model for never talking about problems in a relationship.
rcm.1.54.chaupai.1.claim: Sati, recalling her own deed, is filled with untold worry, and sees that Shiva in his compassion did not speak her fault aloud.

rcm.1.66.chaupai.2.speaker: Narada
rcm.1.66.chaupai.2.line: Shiva may seem hard to reach, but sincere effort pleases him quickly.
rcm.1.66.chaupai.2.claim: Shiva is the all-capable Lord, hard to worship yet quickly pleased by one who undertakes hardship for him.

rcm.1.67.doha.1.speaker: Himavan
rcm.1.67.doha.1.line: Let go of this worry and remember God. The one who made our daughter will look after her.
rcm.1.67.doha.1.misuse: Himavan then advises a concrete step (Parvati's tapas, 1.68); trust sits beside action, not instead of it.
rcm.1.67.doha.1.claim: A worried parent is told to put away worry and remember God: he who made the child will bring about her good.
rcm.1.67.doha.1.needs: trust in God; and the action that follows in the story, sending Parvati to do tapas

rcm.1.70.doha.1.speaker: Voice from the sky (Brahma)
rcm.1.70.doha.1.line: Your longing has borne fruit. Put down these hard struggles now; he will be yours.
rcm.1.70.doha.1.claim: Parvati is told her longing has borne fruit and she may now give up her unbearable austerities.

rcm.1.72.chaupai.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.1.72.chaupai.1.line: Though beyond all desire, the Lord still grieved at being parted from his devotee.
rcm.1.72.chaupai.1.claim: Shiva, though free of desire, is pained by separation from his devotee.

rcm.1.74.chaupai.3.speaker: Parvati
rcm.1.74.chaupai.3.line: Call it foolish if you like: my heart wants only Shiva, always.
rcm.1.74.chaupai.3.claim: Parvati owns that her mind is set past all advice, trusting Narada's word, and wants Shiva alone.

rcm.1.102.chaupai.2.speaker: Parvati
rcm.1.102.chaupai.2.line: One who lives under the wishing tree need not suffer want. You are my shelter: clear my confusion.
rcm.1.102.chaupai.2.claim: One who lives beneath the wishing tree should not suffer want; so Parvati asks Shiva to remove her confusion.

rcm.1.109.chaupai.5.speaker: Shiva
rcm.1.109.chaupai.5.line: The formless, unseen, unborn One takes on a form out of love for his devotees.
rcm.1.109.chaupai.5.claim: The formless and the personal God are not different; the unborn, unseen One takes form out of love for devotees.

rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.speaker: Shiva
rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.line: Those who remember him with love cross life's ocean as easily as a puddle in a hoofprint.
rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.misuse: Praise of remembrance, not a promise that life's problems will vanish; practical help still matters.
rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.claim: Even an involuntary utterance of his name burns the sins of many births, and reverent remembrance makes the world's ocean a hoofprint.
rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.needs: that the reader wants a devotional practice

rcm.1.113.chaupai.1.speaker: Parvati
rcm.1.113.chaupai.1.line: Your words fell like cool moonlight. The heat of my confusion is gone; you took away every doubt.
rcm.1.113.chaupai.1.claim: A teacher's words, cool as moonlight, removed the heat of delusion and every doubt.

yv.5.31.35.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
yv.5.31.35.line: With all my being, all my mind, all my strength: he alone is my refuge.
yv.5.31.35.claim: With my whole being, mind and striving, that God alone is my refuge; there is no other way.

yv.5.31.37.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
yv.5.31.37.line: From this moment on, I take refuge in Narayana. Wherever I am, I am full of him.
yv.5.31.37.claim: From this moment I take refuge always in the unborn Narayana; everywhere I am filled with him.

yv.5.31.38.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
yv.5.31.38.line: 'Namo Narayanaya' never leaves my heart, just as the wind never leaves the sky.
yv.5.31.38.misuse: 'Every aim' is a devotee's praise of the name, not a promise of particular results.
yv.5.31.38.claim: The mantra 'Namo Narayanaya' never leaves the chamber of my heart, as wind never leaves the sky.

yv.5.33.19.speaker: Prahlada
yv.5.33.19.line: Refuge of those who have no refuge: Hari, the unfailing one, I take refuge in you.
yv.5.33.19.claim: I take refuge in Hari, the unborn and unfailing Lord, refuge of those who have no refuge.

yv.5.36.1.speaker: Prahlada
yv.5.36.1.line: After so long, I remember you. By good fortune, Lord, you are found.
yv.5.36.1.claim: The self beyond all words has returned to memory after long; by good fortune you are found, Lord.

yv.5.41.4.speaker: Prahlada
yv.5.41.4.line: By your grace, Lord, I have found steadiness. In meditation or out of it, I am the same.
yv.5.41.4.claim: By your grace I have reached a rightly settled state; in absorption or out of it I am always the same.

yv.6a.29.108.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.6a.29.108.line: For those whose minds are full of the joy of remembering you, nothing is out of reach, nothing feared.
yv.6a.29.108.misuse: Remembrance eases fear; it is not a promise that hardship will not come.
yv.6a.29.108.claim: For those whose minds reel with the joy of remembering you, nothing is hard to reach and there are no fears.

yv.6a.29.111.speaker: Vasishtha
yv.6a.29.111.line: Remembering you, Lord, is a jar of wisdom's nectar, a moon of steadiness, a door to freedom.
yv.6a.29.111.claim: Remembering you, Lord, is the jar of wisdom's nectar, the moon of steadiness and the door to freedom.

yv.6a.39.2.speaker: Shiva
yv.6a.39.2.line: Walking or standing, awake or asleep, worship can run through everything you do.
yv.6a.39.2.claim: Walking or standing, awake or asleep, this worship made of meditation runs through every activity.

rcm.5.13.chaupai.4.speaker: Ram (message)
rcm.5.13.chaupai.4.line: My heart is always with you. That is all you need to know about my love.
rcm.5.13.chaupai.4.claim: Ram's heart stays always with Sita, and in that she is to know the whole of his love.

rcm.5.25.chaupai.2.speaker: Sita
rcm.5.25.chaupai.2.line: You are kind to those in trouble. Remember that now, and lift this heavy weight from me.
rcm.5.25.chaupai.2.misuse: A prayer in crisis, not a replacement for practical help.
rcm.5.25.chaupai.2.claim: Sita asks Ram, who lacks nothing, to remember his vow of kindness to the helpless and remove her heavy trouble.

rcm.7.7.chaupai.4.speaker: Narrator
rcm.7.7.chaupai.4.line: He lay on the ground and would not rise. So Ram lifted him up and held him to his heart.
rcm.7.7.chaupai.4.claim: Bharat lies on the ground and will not rise, and Ram lifts him by force and holds him to his heart, weeping.

rcm.3.31.chaupai.2.speaker: Shabari and Ram
rcm.3.31.chaupai.2.line: I don't measure people the way the world does. The only kinship I recognise is love.
rcm.3.31.chaupai.2.misuse: The first half is Shabari's harsh self-description, which Ram's reply overturns; never show it on its own.
rcm.3.31.chaupai.2.claim: Ram answers Shabari's self-abasement by saying he recognises only one kinship, that of devotion.

rcm.3.29.chaupai.1.speaker: Narrator
rcm.3.29.chaupai.1.line: His heart is tender, and his kindness doesn't need a reason.
rcm.3.29.chaupai.1.claim: Ram is tender-hearted and gracious without cause: to a flesh-eating vulture he gave the end yogis beg for.

rcm.6.112.chaupai.3.speaker: Ram
rcm.6.112.chaupai.3.line: Go home now. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone.
rcm.6.112.chaupai.3.claim: Ram sends his companions home, telling them to remember him and fear no one.

rcm.2.285.doha.1.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.285.doha.1.line: Through your kindness, even my faults were turned into something good.
rcm.2.285.doha.1.claim: By Ram's own goodness Bharat's faults became like ornaments and his good name spread everywhere.

rcm.2.204.chaupai.4.speaker: Bharadwaj
rcm.2.204.chaupai.4.line: Don't worry so much. Your sorrow will lift the moment you see him again.
rcm.2.204.chaupai.4.claim: The sage tells the grieving Bharat not to worry so, for all sorrow will end on seeing Ram's feet.

rcm.2.293.chaupai.4.speaker: Bharat
rcm.2.293.chaupai.4.line: Give me something to hold on to, so I can get through these years.
rcm.2.293.chaupai.4.claim: Accepting Ram's command to return, Bharat asks for some support he can serve to get through the years of separation.

vr.3.74.22.speaker: Shabari
vr.3.74.22.line: My teachers are gone, but the flowers they offered here still haven't withered.
vr.3.74.22.claim: The flowers they offered in worship here have still not withered.

tulsi_vp.79.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.79.line: Father, mother, teacher, friend: you are mine in every way. Choose any bond, only keep me close.
tulsi_vp.79.claim: Every bond joins the poet to Ram: beggar and giver, servant and master, child and parent; he asks only for shelter.

tulsi_vp.78.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.78.line: You lift up the poor, and I am yours. Just say it once: "You are mine."
tulsi_vp.78.claim: Ram cherishes the poor and the poet is his poor one, who asks him to say just once: Tulsidas is mine.

tulsi_vp.101.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.101.line: Where would I go but to you? Who else holds the fallen so dear?
tulsi_vp.101.claim: There is nowhere to go on leaving Ram's feet; no one else purifies the fallen or holds the lowliest so dear.

tulsi_vp.105.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.105.line: What is lost is lost, but the night is over. Awake now, I begin again.
tulsi_vp.105.claim: What was wasted until now will be wasted no more; by Ram's grace the night is over, and he will not sleep again.

tulsi_vp.137.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.137.line: When grace is with you, others' ill will cannot even bend a hair.
tulsi_vp.137.misuse: Not a promise that harm never happens; a reassurance to steady fear.
tulsi_vp.137.claim: If Ram's grace is with the devotee, no one's enmity can bend a hair of him, whatever schemes are tried.
tulsi_vp.137.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.144.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.144.line: The compassionate one needs no reason to take your fears away.
tulsi_vp.144.claim: There is no one Ram failed to protect for the honour of his name; without any cause he removes the whole burden of fear.
tulsi_vp.144.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.162.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.162.line: Who else melts for the hurting without asking anything first?
tulsi_vp.162.claim: No one in the world is as generous as Ram, who melts for the wretched without any service rendered.
tulsi_vp.162.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.166.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.166.line: Utterly tender, full of compassion, doing good without needing a reason.
tulsi_vp.166.claim: Ram is the well-wisher of the lowly: most tender, a store of compassion, doing good to others without cause.
tulsi_vp.166.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.183.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.183.line: Love takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
tulsi_vp.183.claim: Ram knows the way of love, which removes the greatness of the great and the smallness of the small.

tulsi_vp.221.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.221.line: Day and night I watch the road for your kindness. I do not know when, but I wait.
tulsi_vp.221.claim: Day and night the poor poet watches the road for Ram's grace, not knowing when it will come.

tulsi_vp.253.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.253.line: Keep me now, as you have kept me every day until now.
tulsi_vp.253.claim: The poet asks Ram to keep him in refuge as he has kept him every day until now.

tulsi_vp.254.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.254.line: Your name is my mother and father, my teacher, my friend, my family.
tulsi_vp.254.claim: Ram's name is the poet's mother and father, kin, teacher, master and friend, and love for it is his lasting wealth.
tulsi_vp.254.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_vp.271.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.271.line: A broken arm is still held close in a sling.
tulsi_vp.271.claim: Whatever he is, the poet is Ram's own and asks not to be cast off: a broken arm is still slung from one's neck.

tulsi_vp.273.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_vp.273.line: Who else has such natural tenderness for the hurting and the alone?
tulsi_vp.273.claim: Apart from Ram the poet has no one to tell and no well-wisher with natural tenderness for the suffering and unprotected.

tulsi_dv.84.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.84.line: Whatever I am, I am yours. So I am well, now and always.
tulsi_dv.84.claim: Such as he is, the poet belongs to Ram alone, and therefore it is well with him in every world and time.
tulsi_dv.84.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_dv.95.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.95.line: When you belong without conditions, even losing is a kind of winning.
tulsi_dv.95.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_dv.95.claim: Hold Ram in awe and give him your attachment, love and trust; one who is wholly Ram's wins even in losing.
tulsi_dv.95.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram; surrender after doing one's part

tulsi_dv.101.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.101.line: As parents pull a child back from the fire, you are kept safe more often than you know.
tulsi_dv.101.misuse: Not a promise that nothing bad happens; a reminder of care.
tulsi_dv.101.claim: Sita and Ram guard their own as parents guard a child who plays with a snake or reaches into fire.
tulsi_dv.101.needs: that the reader wants refuge in Ram

tulsi_dv.424.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.424.line: Over every head, including yours, there is a guardian.
tulsi_dv.424.claim: It is good to step away and good to shield oneself, and not good to strike a wound; Ram stands guard over every head.

tulsi_dv.109.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_dv.109.line: He once begged for scraps door to door. Where you are now is not where you end.
tulsi_dv.109.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_dv.109.claim: The poet who begged scraps from house to house without Ram later had kings honour his feet, with Ram as his helper.

tulsi_kv.7.73.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_kv.7.73.line: He once thought four chickpeas were everything. Grace made someone lighter than straw weigh more than a mountain.
tulsi_kv.7.73.claim: Born to beggars and raised wailing from door to door, the poet became a mighty master's servant by the power of Ram's name.

tulsi_hb.13.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_hb.13.line: Whoever keeps that brave call in their heart will be cared for like a child.
tulsi_hb.13.claim: One in whose heart Hanuman's roar rings gladly will be cared for like a child by gracious sages and siddhas.

bg.9.18.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.18.line: I am your goal, your support, your witness, your home, your shelter and your friend.
bg.9.18.claim: Krishna is the goal, sustainer, lord, witness, abode, refuge and friend, the origin, dissolution, ground, treasury and imperishable seed.

bg.9.17.speaker: Krishna
bg.9.17.line: I am the father of this world, and its mother, and the one who holds it all up.
bg.9.17.misuse: Not a replacement for a parent who is gone; a reassurance that care runs through everything.
bg.9.17.claim: Krishna is the father, mother, sustainer and grandfather of this world, the knowable, the purifier, Om and the three Vedas.

bg.8.14.speaker: Krishna
bg.8.14.line: For the one who keeps remembering me, I am easy to reach.
bg.8.14.claim: For the ever-united yogi who remembers Krishna constantly with undivided mind, Krishna is easy to reach.

bg.11.50.speaker: Sanjaya
bg.11.50.line: Seeing Arjuna frightened, Krishna took his gentle, familiar form again and comforted him.
bg.11.50.claim: Having spoken, Krishna showed his own form again and, becoming gentle, comforted the frightened Arjuna.
bg.11.50.needs: the scene of the cosmic form

bg.11.51.speaker: Arjuna
bg.11.51.line: Seeing your gentle human face again, I am calm. I feel like myself again.
bg.11.51.claim: Seeing Krishna's gentle human form, Arjuna is composed again and restored to his own nature.
bg.11.51.needs: the scene of the cosmic form

bg.18.56.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.56.line: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.
bg.18.56.claim: Even while always doing all actions, one who takes refuge in Krishna attains by his grace the eternal, imperishable abode.

bg.18.61.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.61.line: The divine lives in the heart of every being, yours included.
bg.18.61.misuse: The second half is about nature moving us, not fatalism or excusing harm; use the first half as the card.
bg.18.61.claim: The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, making them revolve by his maya as if mounted on a machine.
bg.18.61.needs: a reader open to God; the second half can read as 'you are a puppet' without 18.62

bg.18.64.speaker: Krishna
bg.18.64.line: Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.
bg.18.64.claim: Krishna will again speak his supreme and most secret word for Arjuna's good, because Arjuna is firmly beloved to him.

bg.7.14.speaker: Krishna
bg.7.14.line: This tangle is hard to get through. Those who take shelter in me get through it.
bg.7.14.claim: Krishna's divine maya of the three gunas is hard to cross; those who take refuge in him alone cross it.

bg.12.8.speaker: Krishna
bg.12.8.line: Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.
bg.12.8.claim: Fixing the mind and settling the intellect in Krishna alone, one will dwell in him thereafter, without doubt.
bg.12.8.needs: a devotional reader; 12.9-11 give easier steps for one who cannot

vishnu_gita.1.60.speaker: The gods
vishnu_gita.1.60.line: We have come to you for shelter. Please make this fear, born of confusion, go away.
vishnu_gita.1.60.claim: We have come to you for refuge, lover of those who seek shelter; do what will destroy our fear born of confusion.

mbh.3.12.134.speaker: Krishna
mbh.3.12.134.line: The sky could fall and the oceans dry up, but my word to you will not fail.
mbh.3.12.134.misuse: In context the vow is that her wrongs will be answered; use it as 'someone stands with you', never as a call to revenge.
mbh.3.12.134.claim: The sky may fall and the ocean dry up, but my word to you will not prove false.

sur.vp.18.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.18.line: Every time someone was hurting, kindness came. No one else feels your pain like that.
sur.vp.18.claim: No one else feels the pain of his people; whenever the lowly suffered, Balbir showed mercy.

sur.vp.220.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.220.line: Some days a feast, some days hunger; some days riding high, some days carrying loads. You already know.
sur.vp.220.misuse: Acceptance is not resignation to mistreatment.
sur.vp.220.claim: As you keep me so I will live; sometimes fed, sometimes hungry, sometimes riding high, sometimes bearing loads.

sur.vp.256.speaker: Surdas
sur.vp.256.line: When you are cornered, you are not alone. He is the companion of tight places.
sur.vp.256.claim: Hari, you are the companion of those in a tight place.

sur.bgs.9.speaker: Krishna (message to Yashoda)
sur.bgs.9.line: "The city has every splendour, but nothing pleases me without you." Even Krishna was homesick.
sur.bgs.9.claim: Mathura has great splendour, yet nothing pleases me without you.

sur.bgs.10.speaker: Krishna (message to Yashoda)
sur.bgs.10.line: "Since I left you, no one has called me by my pet name."
sur.bgs.10.claim: Since I was parted from you, mother, no one has called me Kanhaiya.

meera.kk.8.ref: Meera pada "Tum suno ji mharo arji"
meera.kk.8.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.8.line: "Hear me. I am being swept away. Pull me out."
meera.kk.8.claim: Hear my plea: I am being swept away in the ocean of the world; pull me out, if it is your will.

meera.kk.10.ref: Meera pada "Tanak Hari chitvau ji mori or"
meera.kk.10.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.10.line: "Look my way, just a little. All my hope is here." Waiting without an answer is allowed to hurt.
meera.kk.10.claim: Hari, look my way a little; I keep looking and you do not, and I have no other place of hope.

meera.kk.11.ref: Meera pada "Hari mere jivan pran adhar"
meera.kk.11.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.11.line: When nothing else holds you up, there is still a support for your life and breath.
meera.kk.11.claim: Hari, you are the support of my life and breath; in the three worlds I have no shelter but you.

meera.kk.14.ref: Meera pada "Koi kahiyau re prabhu aavan ki"
meera.kk.14.speaker: Meera
meera.kk.14.line: "My eyes will not listen; they flow like monsoon rivers."
meera.kk.14.claim: These two eyes will not obey me; they flow like rivers in the monsoon.

vr.5.11.26.speaker: Valmiki (narrator)
vr.5.11.26.line: As he looked at those women, a great dread of breaking dharma came over him.
vr.5.11.26.claim: Seeing what he should not, a good person is seized by the fear of having broken dharma.

vr.5.11.27.speaker: Hanuman
vr.5.11.27.line: Looking at another man's sleeping wives is a serious violation of my duty.
vr.5.11.27.claim: Looking at another person's spouse while she sleeps unguarded is a breach of dharma.

vr.5.11.29.speaker: Valmiki (narrator)
vr.5.11.29.line: The wise one's mind, fixed on the task, brought forth a new thought that showed him the way forward.
vr.5.11.29.claim: When the mind stays fixed on its purpose, a clearer thought arrives that shows the way forward.

vr.5.11.30.speaker: Hanuman
