st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.title: Ordered by his father to kill his mother, the slow son thinks it over
st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.source_ref: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva, Mokshadharma Parva, Chirakari Upakhyana, adhyaya 272 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.teaching: When an order comes in anger, slowness is wisdom; think it through and you will not live with regret.
st.mbh.chirakari_takes_his_time.whole_arc_note: The mother was innocent; the father admits his own jealousy. Keep that, and never let the story read as if the mother's punishment were in question. The point is the son's refusal to act on an angry order, and the father's repentance.

st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.title: Asked how to live, the swan says: when they insult you, do not answer back
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.source_ref: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva, Mokshadharma Parva, Hamsa Gita, adhyaya 305 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.teaching: Do not return harsh words; the restraint of the one who bears them protects him and turns the harm back.
st.mbh.hamsa_on_being_insulted.whole_arc_note: The swan speaks of restraint in speech, not of accepting abuse or staying in danger. For someone being harmed, pair with stories that defend dignity; never use this to tell a wronged person to keep quiet about real wrong.

st.mbh.the_python_sage.title: A king finds a sage lying content in the dust and asks how
st.mbh.the_python_sage.source_ref: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva, Mokshadharma Parva, Ajagara vow, adhyaya 177 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.the_python_sage.teaching: Accept what rightly comes, do not chase what is hard to get, and watch rise and fall without being thrown.
st.mbh.the_python_sage.whole_arc_note: This is a portrait of contentment, not a command to stop working; Bhishma tells Yudhishthira many tales urging effort too. Use for people who are fine and want to stay fine, and for the restless, not for someone struggling to meet basic needs.

st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.title: A woman ascetic tests the king who says he is free
st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.source_ref: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva, Mokshadharma Parva, Sulabha-Janaka Samvada, adhyaya 325 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.teaching: Freedom is tested by how one reacts, not by what one says about oneself.
st.mbh.sulabha_tests_janaka.whole_arc_note: Sulabha is the teacher and the text gives her the last word. Keep her central. Janaka is not mocked; he is shown as someone whose words outran his practice.

st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.title: 'You were born after him. How could you have taught him?'
st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.source_ref: Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva, Bhagavadgita Parva; Bhagavad Gita 4.1-8
st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.teaching: An honest doubt, spoken to the teacher, opens the teaching instead of closing it.
st.bg.arjuna_how_could_you_have_taught_t.whole_arc_note: Keep Krishna's answer with the question; the scene affirms asking, and the answer is a claim of divinity that the tradition (Shankara, Ramanuja) reads literally. Do not reduce it to 'question everything'.

st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.title: An old mother, her son dead of snakebite, and the hunter who wants to kill the snake
st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, opening adhyaya 1 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ); Bhishma tells it to a guilt-stricken Yudhishthira
st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.teaching: A loss has many hands in it and none of them is the whole cause; seeing this frees both the griever and the one who blames himself.
st.mbh.gautami_and_the_serpent.whole_arc_note: The story's two uses must stay apart. For the guilt-ridden survivor, its message is 'you were not the sole cause'. Its explanation for the child's death is the child's own past karma, which must never be told to a bereaved parent as consolation; do not serve this to a parent who has lost a child. Gautami's refusal of revenge is hers to make; do not use it to tell the wronged to let go.

st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.title: The parrot who would not leave the dead tree
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, adhyaya 11 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.teaching: Stay by the one who sheltered you when they flourished, now that they are failing.
st.mbh.parrot_and_the_withered_tree.whole_arc_note: Bhishma tells this to praise compassion and loyalty to a dependant, not to say one must stay in any situation forever. The tree did no wrong to the parrot; do not use it for staying with someone who harms you.

st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.title: A poor mother mixes flour in water and tells her boy it is milk
st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, Danadharma Parva, Upamanyu's account to Krishna, adhyaya 45, verses 96 onward (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.teaching: When you cannot give your child what they want, give them the truth and something greater to lean on.
st.mbh.upamanyu_and_the_flour_milk.whole_arc_note: The mother's grief and honesty are the scene; the devotional ending is the text's own and should not be dropped. Do not use to suggest poverty is solved by prayer alone; the text tells a lifetime of discipline after.

st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.title: A king and queen serve a guest who seems determined to break them
st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, Danadharma Parva, Chyavana and Kushika, adhyayas 87 to 91 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.teaching: Service without resentment, under provocation, is the strongest proof of a good heart.
st.mbh.kushika_serves_chyavana.whole_arc_note: This is a test by a sage, announced at the end, with a reward. Real caregiving and real difficult elders give no such guarantee, and the text does not ask anyone to accept harm. Use for the inner work of serving a demanding person without bitterness, not to tell anyone to accept abuse.

st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.title: A worm runs from a cart, and Vyasa asks why it bothers to live
st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, adhyayas 179 to 181 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.teaching: Every creature clings to life; what we will regret at the end is how we treated others.
st.mbh.the_worm_on_the_road.whole_arc_note: Two truths sit together: every creature loves its life, and a selfish life is regretted. Do not use as 'you should be grateful you are not a worm'. The worm's past-birth caste and later rise through castes are in the text; tell it without endorsing hierarchy.

st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.title: A parent whose two families destroyed each other is offered one of them back
st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, adhyaya 34 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.teaching: A parent's love may favour one set of children, but humble truthfulness won back all of them.
st.mbh.bhangashvana_and_the_two_sets_of_.whole_arc_note: Do not hide the frame: Bhishma tells this to answer a question about sexual pleasure, and the ending is about that. The usable core is the grief of a parent whose two families turned on each other, and the humility that won all of them back. Mark gender_sensitive. Do not use to make claims about women's nature.

st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.title: After fifty-eight nights on the arrows, Bhishma asks leave to go
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, Bhishma-svargarohana section, adhyaya 273 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.teaching: At the end, finish your duties to the living, speak plainly, and let go into what you trust.
st.mbh.bhishma_fifty_eight_nights.whole_arc_note: Bhishma's frankness to Dhritarashtra about his sons is part of it; do not soften it into general comfort. His long endurance was by choice and vow. Use for elders facing the end and for those sitting by them; not as a model of enduring pain without relief.

st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.title: A mother outlives her very old son and asks why her heart does not break
st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.source_ref: Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva, Bhishma-svargarohana section, adhyaya 274 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.teaching: Even a goddess grieves her child, however old; grief does not measure love, and comfort can come from those who stand with us.
st.mbh.ganga_weeps_for_bhishma.whole_arc_note: Her guilt at not breaking is honest and common; keep it. The consolation is specific to Bhishma's divine origin; when used for a human parent, lean on her grief and the presence of those who sat with her, not on the promise.

st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.title: 'How does a steady person talk, sit and walk?'
st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.source_ref: Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva, Bhagavadgita Parva; Bhagavad Gita 2.54-72
st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.teaching: To grow steady, first see clearly what steadiness looks like in a person.
st.bg.arjuna_what_does_a_steady_person_l.whole_arc_note: Read as Arjuna's honest request, not a test answer; the tradition (Shankara) reads the marks both as the description of the realised and as the discipline of the seeker.

st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.title: Arjuna, after the war, admits he has forgotten what Krishna taught him
st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, Anugita Parva, adhyaya 17 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI 14.16)
st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.teaching: Even what changed your life can slip away in ordinary days; go back and ask again.
st.mbh.arjuna_forgot_the_gita.whole_arc_note: Keep Krishna's rebuke; it is part of the scene and the tradition reads it as a warning against careless listening. Keep also his second teaching; the door is not closed.

st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.title: The king collapses on the riverbank, and Krishna tells him his real war has started
st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, Ashvamedhika Parva, adhyayas 1 and 12 to 13 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.teaching: After the outer battle is won, the war with one's own mind remains, and it is fought alone.
st.mbh.the_war_inside_after_victory.whole_arc_note: Krishna does not deny the grief; he names its new field. Keep the context: it is after victory that the inner war begins. Do not read 'not mine' as coldness; the tradition reads it as freedom from possessiveness. Bhima said the same words to him months earlier (12.16.21-22, see st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words); Krishna repeats them after the grief has run its course, and only now do they land.

st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.title: A sage, furious that God did not stop the war, threatens to curse him
st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, Anugita Parva, the Uttanka (Udanka) episode, adhyayas 53 to 56 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.teaching: Anger at God may be heard and answered; but grace can come in a form our prejudice refuses.
st.mbh.uttanka_confronts_krishna.whole_arc_note: Keep both halves: the honest rage at God for allowing suffering, which Krishna hears and answers; and the test Uttanka fails through prejudice. Do not drop the second half, it is the teaching. Do not use the episode to endorse caste revulsion; it rebukes it.

st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.title: A mongoose with half a golden body says the emperor's great sacrifice is worth less than a handful of flour
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, adhyayas 91 to 95, the mongoose's account at 92 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.teaching: A small gift, honestly earned and given out of one's own need, outweighs a lavish one.
st.mbh.the_half_golden_mongoose.whole_arc_note: Do not use this to shame people who give a lot, or to tell a poor family they must give what they cannot afford. The point is measure: what you give against what you have, given sincerely. The family's choice was free.

st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.title: The heir is born still, and the grandmother tells Krishna to keep his promise
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, adhyayas 66 to 69 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.teaching: Truth kept without exception carries power; the women's grief and Krishna's vow meet in one child.
st.mbh.parikshit_born_still.whole_arc_note: This is a miracle tied to Krishna's specific vow; it must never be served to a family who has lost a baby as consolation or hope. Its use is the women's grief and the power of truthfulness, and as a devotional story for those who are not newly bereaved.

st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.title: A son comes out humbly to greet his father, and is told to fight him
st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, adhyayas 79 to 82 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.teaching: A child may have to stand up to a parent in the way the parent demands; the cost can be heavy and still lead to a truer bond.
st.mbh.babhruvahana_fights_his_father.whole_arc_note: Do not cut at the son's victory or at the father's insult. The text shows a father whose pride cost him; the son's courage is real and so is his anguish. Arjuna's taunt compares softness to a woman; leave that phrase out in retelling.

st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.title: After fifteen years as a guest in his nephew's palace, the old king asks to go
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashramavasika Parva, Ashramavasa Parva, opening adhyayas (Gita Press and BORI 15.1 to about 15.15; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.teaching: When the time comes, an elder may choose to lay down his place with dignity and ask forgiveness for what he could not set right.
st.mbh.dhritarashtra_asks_to_leave.whole_arc_note: Keep both sides: Yudhishthira's sincere care and Bhima's quiet cruelty. The old man's leaving is his own choice, guided by Vyasa, not an exile. Do not read it as 'elders should get out of the way'.

st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.title: Her sons beg her to stay in the palace she fought for, and Kunti walks to the forest
st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashramavasika Parva, Ashramavasa Parva (Gita Press about adhyayas 16 to 17; BORI about 15.22 to 15.23; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.teaching: One who fought for others' dignity does not need to collect a reward; she can walk away when the work is done.
st.mbh.kunti_will_not_stay.whole_arc_note: Do not read this as a mother abandoning her children; she has finished her work and chooses her own path. Keep her stated reason.

st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.title: Yudhishthira finds Vidura in the forest, and Vidura gives himself to him
st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashramavasika Parva, Ashramavasa Parva (Gita Press about adhyaya 26; BORI about 15.33; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.teaching: The one who taught us can pass into us; what he was continues in the one he chose.
st.mbh.vidura_enters_yudhishthira.whole_arc_note: This is a death, told as a giving. Keep the strangeness; do not convert it to metaphor only. For the bereaved it says the one who taught you lives on in you, which the text states literally.

st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.title: For one night, the dead rise out of the Ganga to meet the living
st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashramavasika Parva, Putradarshana Parva (BORI about 15.36 to 15.44; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.teaching: Those we lost, and those we fought, are at peace beyond anger; seeing that can loosen what we carry.
st.mbh.night_of_the_dead.whole_arc_note: The scene's ending includes widows choosing to follow their husbands into the river; this must not be presented as a model, and the episode should be told with that part named, not hidden. Do not offer the night as something the bereaved can expect; offer the image of the dead at peace and without anger.

st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.title: News comes that his mother died in a forest fire, far from him
st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.source_ref: Mahabharata, Ashramavasika Parva, Naradagamana Parva (BORI about 15.45 to 15.47; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.teaching: A parent who chose their own path and end was not abandoned; the child's guilt can rest on that truth.
st.mbh.the_elders_in_the_forest_fire.whole_arc_note: The elders' choice to stay in the fire is presented by the text as a yogic end, not as despair; do not model it. The usable part is the son's guilt at a parent dying far away, and the reframe that the parent chose their way.

st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.title: Bored young men play a joke on visiting sages, and a whole clan begins to end
st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.source_ref: Mahabharata, Mausala Parva, adhyayas 1 to 2 (Gita Press and BORI; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.teaching: Prosperity that makes us careless and contemptuous plants the seed of its own end.
st.mbh.the_prank_and_the_iron_pestle.whole_arc_note: Read with the next episode; this is the cause, not the whole story. The pregnancy joke is the text's detail; tell it without making a woman the butt of the joke.

st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.title: On a drunken holiday, an old wound is reopened and a clan kills itself
st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.source_ref: Mahabharata, Mausala Parva, adhyaya 3 (Gita Press and BORI; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.teaching: Grudges never laid to rest, stirred by drink and pride, can destroy a family no enemy could touch.
st.mbh.yadavas_destroy_each_other.whole_arc_note: This is the darkest episode in the epic's ending; keep it whole and do not make it entertainment. Its lesson is about unhealed grudges, alcohol and contempt, not about violence as spectacle.

st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.title: A hunter shoots at a deer, and finds he has hit Krishna
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.source_ref: Mahabharata, Mausala Parva, adhyaya 4 (Gita Press; BORI about 16.5; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.teaching: Even at his death Krishna comforts the one who wounded him by mistake.
st.mbh.krishna_and_the_hunter_jara.whole_arc_note: The death of Krishna is told quietly in the text; keep it quiet. The hunter's guilt and Krishna's comfort are the human centre. Do not turn it into a message that accidental harm does not matter; the hunter's horror is right, and the comfort is grace.

st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.title: The greatest archer cannot string his bow, and Vyasa tells him why
st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.source_ref: Mahabharata, Mausala Parva, adhyayas 7 to 8 (Gita Press; BORI about 16.8 to 16.9; numbers from memory)
st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.teaching: Strength and skill are given for a season; when the season ends, know it, and let go.
st.mbh.arjunas_bow_fails.whole_arc_note: Do not soften the failure; the text lets Arjuna be powerless. Vyasa's answer is not 'you did your best' but 'your season is over', which is both hard and freeing. The abduction of women is a fact in the story; tell it as Arjuna's failure to protect, not as a spectacle.

st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.title: On the last walk, one by one they fall, and Bhima asks why
st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.source_ref: Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva, adhyayas 1 to 2 (Gita Press and BORI; from memory)
st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.teaching: Each person carries some small pride to the very end; the last journey reveals it.
st.mbh.the_final_walk_who_fell.whole_arc_note: Do not read Yudhishthira as cold; he has made his grief already and the walk is a renunciation. Draupadi's 'fault' is the text's reading; present it as Yudhishthira's verdict, not as a statement about women. This is a story about the small vanities that stay with us to the end.

st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.title: Offered heaven if he leaves the dog behind, Yudhishthira refuses
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.source_ref: Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva, adhyaya 3 (Gita Press and BORI 17.3; from memory)
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.teaching: Do not abandon one who is devoted to you, not even for heaven.
st.mbh.yudhishthira_and_the_dog.whole_arc_note: The text gives the reason in Yudhishthira's own words: loyalty to one who depends on you. Keep that reason. Do not end at 'he got into heaven'; the next episode tests him again.

st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.title: Yudhishthira reaches heaven and finds Duryodhana seated there in glory
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.source_ref: Mahabharata, Svargarohana Parva, adhyaya 1 (Gita Press and BORI; from memory)
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.teaching: Even the righteous must put down the grudge before they can rest; enmity has no place in heaven.
st.mbh.duryodhana_in_heaven.whole_arc_note: Do not resolve this by saying Duryodhana was good. The text keeps his wrongs and still says the grudge must end. Yudhishthira's anger is real and named. Pair with the next episode.

st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.title: In the darkness, voices beg him to stay, and Yudhishthira chooses hell
st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.source_ref: Mahabharata, Svargarohana Parva, adhyayas 2 to 3 (Gita Press and BORI; from memory)
st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.teaching: To stay with those you love in their pain, choosing it freely, is the last and highest test of dharma.
st.mbh.stay_a_moment_in_hell.whole_arc_note: Keep the anger at the gods; the text allows it. Keep the reason: the half-truth to Drona. And keep the choice: he chose to stay in pain to comfort others before he knew it was a test.

st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.title: Draupadi tells her husband: you promised us, and now you are breaking our hearts
st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.source_ref: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana Parva, adhyaya 14 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ); one of the family speeches, see also st.mbh.family_argues_yudhishthira_back
st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.teaching: You do not get to walk away from the people who endured everything on the strength of your promise.
st.mbh.draupadi_reminds_him_of_his_word.whole_arc_note: Draupadi speaks as a bereaved mother who still chooses to call him back to duty; keep her grief in view. One line in her speech uses an insult about manhood; leave it out in retelling. Her argument is about keeping one's word to those who suffered with you.

st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.title: Bhima tells his brother: you know the books and miss their meaning
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.source_ref: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana Parva, adhyaya 10 and adhyaya 16 (Kumbakonam-edition numbering as in the local corpus; BORI and Gita Press numbers differ)
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.teaching: Words of scripture repeated without their meaning can become a hiding place from duty.
st.mbh.bhima_you_only_repeat_the_words.whole_arc_note: Bhima is harsh, and the text lets him be. Do not present his words as cruelty; they come from love and pain, and he says so. Use for people whose spirituality has become a way out of responsibility, and for the frank sibling who has to say so.

st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.title: Tulsidas begins a work he feels too small for
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 8 to 13 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.teaching: A small capacity joined to a great purpose is reason enough to begin.
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.whole_arc_note: His humility is not a refusal to act. Do not clip it to self-deprecation; the passage ends in a decision to write.

st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.title: Tulsidas salutes his critics before they have spoken
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 4 to 9 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.teaching: Expect the fault-finder, greet him, and do not let him set your course.
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.whole_arc_note: The salutation is ironic and sincere at once. It does not say critics are right, and it does not say they should be fought. He sees them clearly and keeps walking.

st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.title: Sati doubts, tests in secret, and hides it from Shiva
st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 44 to 52 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.teaching: A doubt brought into the open can be answered; a doubt acted on in secret and then denied breaks trust.
st.rcm.sati_doubt_test_lie.whole_arc_note: The text does not punish questioning: Parvati later asks the same question openly and receives the whole Manas as the answer. What costs Sati is testing in disguise and then lying about it. Keep both halves.

st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.title: Sati lives beside a husband who has silently withdrawn
st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 53 to 56 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.teaching: Guilt that cannot be spoken to the person hardens into distance; the text turns it toward prayer.
st.rcm.sati_years_of_silence.whole_arc_note: Her wish to leave the body belongs to her story and its rebirth; it is not counsel. The usable part is the cost of an unspoken breach and the turn toward the one wronged. Shiva's restraint in not shaming her is also part of the picture.

st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.title: Sati goes to her father's house where her husband is not welcome
st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 56 to 61 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.teaching: Where a grudge is held against the one you love, your own welcome is also withdrawn, whatever the blood tie.
st.rcm.sati_goes_uninvited.whole_arc_note: This is not a lesson in obeying a husband; Shiva lets her go with attendants. The point is his reading of the situation: a home that insults your partner has not invited you either. Her death must never be offered as an example.

st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.title: Shiva, bereaved, wanders and finds rest in hearing the story
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 71 to 73 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher); with Shiva's own account at Uttar Kand doha 56
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.teaching: Grief is not reasoned away; it is carried into remembrance and good company until it loosens.
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.whole_arc_note: Even Shiva grieves, and the text lets him wander first. Do not shorten it to chant and move on. Listening comes after a long season of roaming.

st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.title: Parvati is told by seven sages that she has chosen badly
st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 74 to 78 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.teaching: One who has no trust in the teacher's word finds neither ease nor success, even in dreams.
st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.whole_arc_note: The sages are testing, not sincere; her firmness is honoured, not corrected. This is steadiness in a considered vow made on a teacher's word, and the text does not present it as a licence for every stubbornness.

st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.title: Kamadeva accepts a task he knows will destroy him
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 79 to 83 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.teaching: Helping others is the highest dharma, and the text takes care to honour who pays for it.
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.whole_arc_note: Include Rati. The text does not leave the cost of his sacrifice unacknowledged, and the god who burned him is the one who consoles her.

st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.title: Maina sees the man her daughter has chosen and breaks down
st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 86 to 97 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.teaching: Appearance frightens love; knowledge of who the person is settles it.
st.rcm.maina_sees_the_groom.whole_arc_note: Maina's fear is love and is not mocked. Her line about women's dependence is a mother's cry at parting. It is her lament, and the scripture does not offer it as a rule. The turn comes from knowing more about the groom; she is not simply told to be quiet.

st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.title: Parvati asks the question that once cost her everything
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 100 to 113 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.teaching: Ask plainly and at the right time; an honest question is a gift to everyone who hears the answer.
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.whole_arc_note: Read with Sati's story. Same person, same question, opposite method. The text praises the asking.

st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.title: Narad conquers desire, grows proud of it, and is undone by desire
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 121 to 134 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.teaching: The Lord's vow is the good of his servant, and that sometimes means refusing what the servant begs for.
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.whole_arc_note: Do not stop at the monkey face as a joke. The whole arc: a real victory, pride in it, the warning ignored, the fall into the very thing he had conquered, rage at God, and a denial that was the kindness. Later Ram tells Narad he guards his devotees as a mother keeps a child from fire and snake.

st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.title: Manu and Shatarupa realise late that a full life has left something out
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 134 to 144 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.teaching: It is not too late to turn; and before God one may ask for exactly what one wants.
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.whole_arc_note: A devotional story of a couple acting together in the fourth stage of life. It does not tell a person with dependents to walk out; Manu settles the succession first. And the boon is asked honestly, with the heart's real wish.

st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.title: Pratapbhanu trusts a flatterer who promises he can have it all
st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 144 to 165 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.teaching: Ambition without a limit makes a man easy for the flatterer who tells him there is a shortcut.
st.rcm.pratapbhanu_false_counsellor.whole_arc_note: He was a good king, which is the warning. The curse falls on a deception he did not intend; the text locates the fault earlier, in the boon he asked for and the secrecy he agreed to. Do not flatten it to a tale about bad luck.

st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.title: The gods argue about where to go to find God
st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 173 to 174 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.teaching: God is everywhere equally and shows himself where there is love.
st.rcm.where_is_hari_to_be_found.whole_arc_note: A devotional claim, not a dismissal of temples or pilgrimage. Its point is that love is the means by which the present becomes evident.

st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.title: Kaushalya is overwhelmed by the child she is raising
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 189 to 190 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.teaching: Awe passes; what the mother asks to keep is the simple relationship.
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.whole_arc_note: A devotional vignette. Its human note is small and true: a parent glimpses that the child is far more than hers, and chooses the daily love over the vision.

st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.title: Dasharath is asked to send his young sons into danger
st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 193 to 197 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.teaching: Holding a child back out of love can keep him from the very road that makes him.
st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.whole_arc_note: His refusal is not shamed; the sage is pleased by the love in it. He lets go on the strength of counsel he trusts, without pretending he is unafraid.

st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.title: Ahalya, after a long frozen wait, speaks without bitterness
st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 198 to 199 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.teaching: Seen from the far side of grace, even the long hard stretch can be owned as the road that led here.
st.rcm.ahalya_counts_it_grace.whole_arc_note: This is her own first-person reading after release, as a devotee. It must never be turned outward as advice that a wronged or shamed person should be grateful for what was done to them. Tulsi keeps the cause in the background and gives her the dignity of the last word.

st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.title: Janak, the detached king, finds his heart pulled
st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 203 to 204 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.teaching: Detachment is not the last word; love can still surprise the one who thought he was done.
st.rcm.janak_dispassion_moved.whole_arc_note: The text treats this as the completion of his knowledge. Love for the Lord is shown as more compelling than impersonal peace.

st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.title: Ram notices his heart is stirred and says so to his brother
st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 214 to 222 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.teaching: A mind that has kept itself clean can trust its own stirring, and the right way to carry a new feeling is in the open.
st.rcm.ram_tells_lakshman_his_heart.whole_arc_note: Tulsi's scene is love inside maryada. Clip it to love at first sight and the self-examination is lost; clip it to restraint and the frank admission is lost.

st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.title: Sita wants something she is not free to ask for
st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 222 to 224 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.teaching: What cannot be said to anyone can be laid before the one who already knows the heart.
st.rcm.sita_prays_to_gauri.whole_arc_note: A prayer scene. The blessing comes before the outcome, and she still has to sit through the contest. Do not present it as wish fulfilment on demand.

st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.title: Sita watches the contest that will decide her life
st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 243 to 246 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.teaching: Whoever holds a true love for another is certain to be joined to them.
st.rcm.sita_at_the_bow.whole_arc_note: Her frustration with her father is in the text and is not rebuked. The steadiness comes from her own truthfulness of love. She has no assurance of the result when she finds it.

st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.title: Janak speaks in despair and Lakshman takes it as an insult
st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 235 to 240 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.teaching: Words said in despair wound bystanders who were never the target; the reply that settles it is quiet action at the right moment.
st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.whole_arc_note: Three things together: a father's words spoken from pain and not meant as an attack, a young man's rightful sting at being written off, and an elder brother who neither shames the anger nor lets it run.

st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.title: Sunayana fears the boy is too slight for the task
st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 241 to 243 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.teaching: Do not judge the brilliant by their size.
st.rcm.sunayana_too_young.whole_arc_note: Light and brief; it is consolation offered to a frightened mother by a friend, with reasons.

st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.title: Parashuram storms in; Lakshman needles him and Ram disarms him
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 247 to 271 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.teaching: A hot answer feeds anger; a calm one that gives no ground on the facts lets it burn out.
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.whole_arc_note: Both brothers are needed. Lakshman's wit says what everyone is thinking and nearly gets them killed; Ram's courtesy carries the same truth to a place the angry man can hear it. Ram also says, mildly, that even the crooked moon is spared by Rahu: straightforwardness can be a fault with some people.

st.rcm.janak_vidai.title: Janak, the knower of the Self, cannot let his daughter go
st.rcm.janak_vidai.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 313 to 322 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.janak_vidai.teaching: Wisdom does not cancel a father's love, and love does not excuse him from letting go.
st.rcm.janak_vidai.whole_arc_note: The poem does not correct his tears with philosophy. A wise man weeps, and then does what the hour requires. Both stand.

st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.title: Dasharath sees a white hair and decides to hand over
st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 2 to 5 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.teaching: The body tells you when it is time to pass the work on; the wise act on the first sign.
st.rcm.dasharath_grey_hair.whole_arc_note: The handover is wise and still goes wrong for reasons outside it. Do not make the story promise that letting go on time guarantees a smooth result.

st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.title: Ram hears he is to be crowned and is troubled for his brothers
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 8 to 12 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.teaching: To feel the unfairness of your own advantage is a mark of love.
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.whole_arc_note: It is the root of the later scene. A man who was uneasy at being preferred is not broken when he is passed over.

st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.title: Kaikeyi, who loved Ram, is talked into fearing him
st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 13 to 26 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.teaching: A settled, loving mind can be turned by one insinuating voice if it keeps listening.
st.rcm.kaikeyi_mind_turned.whole_arc_note: Tulsi adds that the gods moved Sarasvati to twist Manthara's mind, and never makes Kaikeyi a simple villain. Her remorse at Chitrakoot and Ram greeting her first belong to the same story. The lesson concerns a voice one keeps listening to and does not concern women or stepmothers.

st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.title: Dasharath is held to a promise that will destroy what he loves
st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 26 to 40 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.teaching: Life may go, but the given word may not; so be careful what you give it to.
st.rcm.dasharath_bound_by_his_word.whole_arc_note: The text honours his truthfulness and shows its price. It does not say he should have broken his word, and it does not hide that the promise was made carelessly. Both are true.

st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.title: Ram is told he has lost the throne and must leave by morning
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 40 to 50 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.teaching: To one not bound to the prize, losing it can feel like release.
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.whole_arc_note: This is Ram's own nature and choice. It is not a rule that someone cheated out of what is theirs must smile. The text shows the city furious at the injustice, and does not blame them.

st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.title: Kaushalya can neither keep her son nor tell him to go
st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 50 to 59 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.teaching: Love that sees dharma clearly can bless the very thing that breaks its heart.
st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.whole_arc_note: She does not simply submit. She first asserts a mother's standing above the father's command, and then counts Kaikeyi as his mother too. Her grief is not removed; she acts through it.

st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.title: Sita refuses to be left behind in comfort
st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 60 to 67 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.teaching: To one who loves, hardship shared is lighter than comfort apart; and that is for her to say.
st.rcm.sita_insists_on_going.whole_arc_note: Her speech uses the idiom of a wife's devotion, and it is also an argument she wins against her husband and the elders. The scene shows a woman's own decision prevailing and should not be used to tell anyone to follow a spouse.

st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.title: Sumitra tells her son to go, and means it
st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 69 to 75 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.teaching: Home is where the one you serve is; a mother's love can be the thing that frees a son to go.
st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.whole_arc_note: She has no share in the quarrel and gains nothing. Her firmness is spoken through grief, in an ill hour she recognises as such. Devotional in its reasoning; the human core is a mother who removes herself as her son's excuse.

st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.title: Ram slips away at night from people who will not let him go
st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 77 to 85 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.teaching: Sometimes those who love you cannot release you, and you must go without the goodbye they want.
st.rcm.ram_leaves_the_sleeping_city.whole_arc_note: It is the only quiet deception Ram practises on those who love him, and the text presents it as the kindest option available. It does not license disappearing on people in general.

st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.title: Guha rages at Kaikeyi; Lakshman tells him no one gives another joy or sorrow
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 86 to 94 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.teaching: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow.
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.whole_arc_note: This is said by the injured party, about his own family's misfortune, to a friend whose anger is on their behalf. It is not said to a victim about their abuser. Lakshman himself explodes later when he thinks Bharat is coming to attack; the text keeps both.

st.rcm.kevat_bargains.title: Kevat the boatman refuses to ferry Ram until he has his way
st.rcm.kevat_bargains.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 98 to 102 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kevat_bargains.teaching: Love may bargain, tease and insist; what it will not do is take payment.
st.rcm.kevat_bargains.whole_arc_note: Three movements: playful boldness of a poor man who knows his own worth before God, service insisted upon as a right, and then refusal of wages. Clip any one and it becomes either a joke or servility.

st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.title: Sumantra must drive the empty chariot home and face the king
st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 94 to 98 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher); and dohas 139 to 150
st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.teaching: Some duties are only heavy; the faithful do them anyway and tell it straight.
st.rcm.sumantra_returns_alone.whole_arc_note: Do not add a silver lining. The story honours the bearer of bad news: his shame is undeserved and the text knows it, and he delivers the truth without softening.

st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.title: Ram, homeless, asks Valmiki where he should live
st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 121 to 128 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.teaching: The Lord's dwelling is the heart of one who listens, serves and holds no deceit.
st.rcm.valmiki_where_to_live.whole_arc_note: Devotional teaching wrapped around a real need for shelter. Valmiki still answers the practical question; he does not leave the travellers with a metaphor.

st.rcm.forest_people_hosts.title: The Kols and Kirats have nothing fit to offer and offer it
st.rcm.forest_people_hosts.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 128 to 133 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.forest_people_hosts.whole_arc_note: Their self-description is their own humility and is not the text's verdict on them. The scene exists to say that birth and polish count for nothing with Ram.

st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.title: Dasharath dies remembering a wrong he did long ago
st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 144 to 150 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.teaching: A life can end unresolved and still end in love.
st.rcm.dasharath_last_night.whole_arc_note: The memory of the old wrong is confessed, not explained away, and it does not cancel his goodness. Do not turn this into a karma lecture for someone grieving a parent.

st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.title: Bharat returns to find a crime has been done in his name
st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 153 to 158 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.teaching: To be the innocent cause of another's loss is its own grief, and the answer is to refuse the gain.
st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.whole_arc_note: His fury at Kaikeyi is harsh and the text records it without making it a model; later he will not let anyone else abuse her. The lasting point is his refusal to profit from a wrong done on his behalf.

st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.title: Kaushalya takes in her arms the son of the woman who ruined her
st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 157 to 163 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.teaching: Grief need not make one unjust; the innocent can be seen as innocent even from inside great loss.
st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.whole_arc_note: No one asks her to forgive and she is not told to. It comes from her own straightforward nature, and from knowing Bharat. It must not be used to press a wronged person toward forgiveness; it shows what the freedom to see the innocent clearly looks like.

st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.title: Bharat is advised by everyone he respects to accept, and says no
st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 163 to 178 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.teaching: When lawful advice and a clear conscience part ways, one may decline with folded hands.
st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.whole_arc_note: He does not call his teacher wrong. He grants the advice its merit and still declines it. The text presents this as higher obedience and gives no general permission to ignore elders.

st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.title: Guha sees an army coming and decides Bharat means harm
st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 182 to 196 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.teaching: The fool acts at once and regrets it; find out a person's nature before you fight him.
st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.whole_arc_note: Guha's loyalty is admirable and his inference reasonable. The story does not mock suspicion; it adds one step before acting on it.

st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.title: Bharat, sure he is despised, is told who he really is
st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 195 to 205 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.teaching: A person may be the opposite of what his circumstances make him appear, and it helps to hear a truthful elder say so.
st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.whole_arc_note: The reassurance is not flattery; the sage is the one person with no reason to console him. And Bharat's prayer is devotional in the strict sense: he asks for love, not relief.

st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.title: Bharat spends a night in conjured luxury and does not touch it
st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 205 to 208 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.teaching: A heart given wholly to one thing can sit beside every comfort untouched.
st.rcm.bharat_unmoved_by_the_feast.whole_arc_note: He is not contemptuous of comfort, and the sage is not wrong to offer it. His mind is simply elsewhere. A light story about what a clear purpose does to temptation.

st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.title: Indra, afraid of losing out, wants to sabotage a good man
st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 209 to 212 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.teaching: Scheming against a good person out of fear for your own interest harms only you.
st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.whole_arc_note: Indra relapses later in the kand, and the text is frank about it: self-interest does not learn in one lesson. Keep that if the story is told at length.

st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.title: Lakshman sees dust on the horizon and is ready to kill his brother
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 218 to 224 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.teaching: Judge a person by his known character, not by how the situation looks from where your hurt is standing.
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.whole_arc_note: Ram praises Lakshman's political sense before correcting his reading of this particular man. The anger had a real cause; only its target was wrong.

st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.title: Bharat walks toward Ram not knowing if he will be received
st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 224 to 232 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.teaching: Go to the one you fear has cause to reject you, relying on their nature and not on your case.
st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.whole_arc_note: Bharat did nothing wrong, and still walks as the guilty one. The embrace does not come because he argued his innocence. Keep the oscillation on the road; it is the truest part.

st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.title: Kaikeyi burns with remorse; Ram goes to her before anyone else
st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 235 to 243 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher); and doha 262
st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.teaching: The one who was wronged can choose to lift the wrongdoer's shame, and when he does, he does it first and without ceremony.
st.rcm.ram_meets_kaikeyi_first.whole_arc_note: Ram's act is his own and freely given; no one demanded it of him, and the citizens' anger at her is not condemned. Her wish for death is remorse and should be flagged, not quoted to the vulnerable.

st.rcm.chitrakoot_sabha.title: At Chitrakoot two brothers each try to give the decision to the other
st.rcm.chitrakoot_sabha.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 243 to 263 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.chitrakoot_sabha.teaching: When each side offers the other the right to decide, the knot loosens without a loser.
st.rcm.chitrakoot_sabha.whole_arc_note: It is slow in the text, across days, with Janak's arrival in between, and that slowness is the healing. Nobody wins the argument. Do not compress it into Bharat asked and Ram refused.

st.rcm.kaushalya_and_sunayana.title: Two mothers sit together at night and decline to blame anyone
st.rcm.kaushalya_and_sunayana.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 268 to 273 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kaushalya_and_sunayana.teaching: Loss and gain move by causes too deep to pin on one person.
st.rcm.kaushalya_and_sunayana.whole_arc_note: Kaushalya has the most cause to blame and she is the one who declines to. It is her own stance about her own loss. And even here she is thinking practically about Bharat's safety; her acceptance has not made her passive.

st.rcm.sita_with_her_parents.title: Sita meets her parents in her ascetic's dress
st.rcm.sita_with_her_parents.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 273 to 275 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sita_with_her_parents.teaching: A parent's respect for a child's chosen hardship is a greater gift than rescue.
st.rcm.sita_with_her_parents.whole_arc_note: A small scene of a grown daughter between two homes, handled without anyone being asked to choose loudly. The parents take pride in her hard choice instead of grieving over it.

st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.title: Bharat asks for something to lean on and rules for fourteen years as a trustee
st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 283 to 312 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.teaching: One can carry a great responsibility as a trust, doing all the work and claiming none of the seat.
st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.whole_arc_note: It is not gloom. The text says he was as glad of the sandals as if Sita and Ram had stayed. And it is not abdication: he does the full work while refusing the ownership.

st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.title: Jayant wrongs Ram and finds no one will take him in
st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand, dohas 1 to 2 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.teaching: When you have wronged someone, every other refuge fails; the way out is to return to them and own the deed.
st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.whole_arc_note: Do not clip either end. The deed is named plainly as malice and foolishness, and there is a consequence (one eye). The mercy comes only after he stops running and owns what he did. It is not a story of wrongdoing without cost.

st.rcm.sutikshna_too_unworthy_to_hope.title: Sutikshna is sure he has nothing to offer, and runs anyway
st.rcm.sutikshna_too_unworthy_to_hope.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand, dohas 7 to 8 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sutikshna_too_unworthy_to_hope.teaching: A person need not be worthy before turning toward grace; having no other refuge is itself enough.
st.rcm.sutikshna_too_unworthy_to_hope.whole_arc_note: His list of what he lacks is true and stays true; the text does not say he was secretly accomplished. What carries him is the trust that Ram's way is to love the one with no other support. Do not turn it into 'you are better than you think'.

st.rcm.maricha_two_deaths.title: Maricha is ordered by a powerful master to do what will kill him
st.rcm.maricha_two_deaths.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand, dohas 21 to 23 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.maricha_two_deaths.teaching: When both roads end badly, choose the one on which your heart faces what is good.
st.rcm.maricha_two_deaths.whole_arc_note: Maricha first speaks the truth to Ravana's face; the turn to refuge comes after his honest counsel is refused, not instead of it. The text still calls the deed a deception. It does not make obedience to a wrong order a virtue; it shows what a cornered person can still choose: where his heart faces.

st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.title: Ram comes home to an empty hut and asks the birds where she has gone
st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand, doha 26 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.teaching: Even the highest grieve openly for the one they love; grief that keeps walking finds its way.
st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.whole_arc_note: Do not tidy Ram's grief into composure. The Manas lets the Lord of the worlds ask the trees. Manas Piyush reads it as lila that sanctifies the grief of separation. Keep the next step too: he keeps walking and searching.

st.rcm.jatayu_old_and_outmatched.title: An old vulture fights a king he cannot beat, and dies content
st.rcm.jatayu_old_and_outmatched.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand, dohas 25 to 28 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.jatayu_old_and_outmatched.teaching: Acting for another's good is complete in itself, even when it fails; such a person lacks nothing.
st.rcm.jatayu_old_and_outmatched.whole_arc_note: He did not save Sita, and the text does not pretend he did. What he did was act, at his age, for someone else, and the text counts that as complete. Ram's own grief and shame (do not tell my father) belong in the telling.

st.rcm.shabari_waited_and_was_taught.title: Shabari waits years for Ram and is told the nine ways to love him
st.rcm.shabari_waited_and_was_taught.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand, dohas 30 to 32 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.shabari_waited_and_was_taught.teaching: Devotion is the only kinship the Lord counts; any one of the nine ways, held firmly, is enough.
st.rcm.shabari_waited_and_was_taught.whole_arc_note: Her self-description uses the low estimate society gave her; the point of the scene is that Ram overturns it, and Tulsi closes by saying even such a person was freed. Keep Ram's answer; do not quote her line alone. Also keep the waiting: years, on a teacher's word.

st.rcm.hanuman_forgot_his_master.title: Hanuman realises he did not recognise the one he was waiting for
st.rcm.hanuman_forgot_his_master.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 2 to 4 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.hanuman_forgot_his_master.teaching: Not recognising grace at first is human; the answer is not shame but service.
st.rcm.hanuman_forgot_his_master.whole_arc_note: His confession is not dramatised humility: he really did not recognise Ram at first. The reply does not deny the confusion; it refuses to let him shrink because of it.

st.rcm.sugriva_what_a_friend_is.title: A frightened exile is told what a real friend does
st.rcm.sugriva_what_a_friend_is.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 6 to 8 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sugriva_what_a_friend_is.teaching: A friend counts your small grief as a mountain and his own large grief as dust.
st.rcm.sugriva_what_a_friend_is.whole_arc_note: The rift began as a misunderstanding (a waiting brother, blood, a sealed cave) that hardened into injury. Sugriva's fear is real and so is his wrong. Ram's later killing of Bali raises its own questions; this story is about the pact and the definition of friendship, not a verdict on Bali.

st.rcm.ram_waits_out_the_rains.title: Ram can do nothing for four months and reads the season while he waits
st.rcm.ram_waits_out_the_rains.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 13 to 18 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_waits_out_the_rains.teaching: When nothing can be done, the mind can still be turned to see; fear admitted is fear that does not rule.
st.rcm.ram_waits_out_the_rains.whole_arc_note: The lessons do not replace the longing; the next season opens with 'no news of Sita'. This is waiting, honestly done, not a cure for grief.

st.rcm.sugriva_forgets_his_friend.title: Sugriva gets everything he wanted and forgets the friend who gave it
st.rcm.sugriva_forgets_his_friend.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 19 to 22 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sugriva_forgets_his_friend.teaching: Comfort intoxicates; the cure is to own it quickly and go back to work.
st.rcm.sugriva_forgets_his_friend.whole_arc_note: The earlier renunciation was sincere, and the forgetting is real; the text keeps both (and Ram smiled at the first because he knew). Ram is hurt and angry enough to speak of the arrow that killed Bali, and still sends fear rather than harm. The forgiveness follows an honest confession.

st.rcm.search_party_past_deadline.title: The search party misses its deadline and sits down by the sea to die
st.rcm.search_party_past_deadline.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 27 to 28 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.search_party_past_deadline.teaching: When the deadline has passed and both roads look like death, keep speaking of what is good; help can come from where you least expect.
st.rcm.search_party_past_deadline.whole_arc_note: Do not drop the low point: they really did resolve to die, and Angad's fear of Sugriva is spelled out. The way forward came from the most unlikely quarter, a grounded old bird who had overheard them talking about duty and devotion. This story carries self_harm_theme and must be filtered accordingly.

st.rcm.sampati_wings_regrow.title: Sampati, grounded by an old act of pride, gets his wings back by helping
st.rcm.sampati_wings_regrow.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 28 to 30 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sampati_wings_regrow.teaching: Pride grounds us; service is what gives back the wings.
st.rcm.sampati_wings_regrow.whole_arc_note: The fall was his own doing and the text says so. The restoration is promised, but it waits for one specific act of service. Grief for his brother comes first: he asks to be carried to the sea to offer water to Jatayu before he helps.

st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.title: Jambavan asks Hanuman why he is sitting silent
st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, dohas 30 to 31 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.teaching: Sometimes strength waits for someone to name it; then it needs a clear, limited task.
st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.whole_arc_note: Keep both halves: the reminder that releases his strength, and Jambavan's limit on it. The first without the second would be hype; the text has an elder who first admits his own age, then calls out the younger one, then keeps him to the job.

st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.title: Hanuman will not rest until the work is done, and passes a test by shrinking
st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 1 to 2 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.teaching: On a mission, rest comes after the work; and a test of strength can sometimes be passed only by becoming small.
st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.whole_arc_note: Both halves matter. Refusing rest is not refusing courtesy: he touches the mountain and bows. And the test is passed by humility and cleverness after the contest of size has gone as far as it can.

st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.title: The guard of Lanka is knocked down and remembers what she was told
st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 3 to 4 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.teaching: A shock can be the sign we were told to wait for; one moment with the good outweighs heaven.
st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.whole_arc_note: The text gives her a long-remembered warning, so the turn is not random grace. It is a person who has stood guard over something wrong for a long time and recognises, when struck, that the end she was told to watch for has come.

st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.title: Vibhishan lives inside Lanka like a tongue among teeth
st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 5 to 7 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.teaching: A good person in a hostile place survives by one true friendship; meeting a saint is itself a sign of grace.
st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.whole_arc_note: He has not yet left Lanka, and the text does not judge him for staying; the courage comes later. What this scene gives is the loneliness of living among people you cannot be honest with, and how much one meeting with a like-minded person does.

st.rcm.sita_asks_for_a_pyre.title: Sita asks for a pyre, and a ring falls in front of her
st.rcm.sita_asks_for_a_pyre.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 9 to 12 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.sita_asks_for_a_pyre.teaching: In the darkest hour a sign can come; it is right to test it, and then to let trust in.
st.rcm.sita_asks_for_a_pyre.whole_arc_note: This story has a self_harm_theme: Sita asks for her own death in so many words. Keep the order exactly: despair, the sign, her own doubt, her questions, then trust. Do not jump from the pyre to the ring as if trust were instant; the text gives her the right to check.

st.rcm.trijata_the_one_kind_guard.title: Trijata, one of the guards, uses a dream to protect the prisoner
st.rcm.trijata_the_one_kind_guard.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 10 to 11 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.trijata_the_one_kind_guard.teaching: Even inside a cruel system, one person can use whatever standing she has to protect someone.
st.rcm.trijata_the_one_kind_guard.whole_arc_note: She is not a rescuer and the text does not make her one. Her goodness is the kind available to someone with no power: words, presence, a reframe that changes how others behave.

st.rcm.ram_message_no_one_to_tell.title: Ram sends word: telling the pain eases it, but whom could I tell?
st.rcm.ram_message_no_one_to_tell.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 12 to 13 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_message_no_one_to_tell.teaching: Speaking pain eases it; where there is no one to tell, love itself carries the message.
st.rcm.ram_message_no_one_to_tell.whole_arc_note: The message is an admission of loneliness by Ram himself, not a performance of strength. Do not turn it into 'share your feelings' advice; it says speaking helps and that there was no one he could speak to, and that love lives in the mind that stays with the beloved.

st.rcm.hanuman_bound_before_ravana.title: Hanuman stands bound before the most powerful man alive and pleads with him
st.rcm.hanuman_bound_before_ravana.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 18 to 23 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.hanuman_bound_before_ravana.teaching: Dignity does not depend on not being bound; speak truth to power humbly, and let the work stay the point.
st.rcm.hanuman_bound_before_ravana.whole_arc_note: Keep the order: he pleads first, with joined palms, for Ravana's own good, and only after Ravana sets him on fire does the city burn. The text does not make the burning the point; it is the consequence of a refused plea.

st.rcm.hanuman_gives_the_credit_away.title: Ram says he can never repay Hanuman, and Hanuman says it was all Ram
st.rcm.hanuman_gives_the_credit_away.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 28 to 31 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.hanuman_gives_the_credit_away.teaching: When praised most, give the credit to its source; praise is where pride enters.
st.rcm.hanuman_gives_the_credit_away.whole_arc_note: Do not flatten this into false modesty. Hanuman did the work and the text says so; he declines ownership of the power, which is a devotee's view, not self-erasure. For a secular reader, it is about praise as a danger.

st.rcm.mandodari_warning_dismissed.title: Mandodari begs her husband to step back, and he laughs at her fear
st.rcm.mandodari_warning_dismissed.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 34 to 35 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.mandodari_warning_dismissed.teaching: A clear warning dismissed as fear is still the truth; the one who dismisses it pays.
st.rcm.mandodari_warning_dismissed.whole_arc_note: The dismissive line about women is Ravana's, and the Manas presents it as delusion (at 6.18 Tulsi has Ravana laugh and say the same, and frames it 'aho moha mahima balavana'). Keep that framing; do not quote his line as a teaching. Mandodari is right every time.

st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.title: Vibhishan advises his brother honestly and is kicked in open court
st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 36 to 40 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.teaching: Speak the truth to family with love; if you are struck for it, wish them well and walk away openly.
st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.whole_arc_note: He does not leave after the first refusal; he leaves after being publicly struck, and says clearly why. He does not curse Ravana; he holds his good to the end. This is honest counsel to family, not instant defection. Keep that he was wronged; the text does not ask him to stay and endure.

st.rcm.vibhishan_refuge_debate.title: Ram's camp argues over whether to trust a defector
st.rcm.vibhishan_refuge_debate.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 40 to 43 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.vibhishan_refuge_debate.teaching: Never turn away one who comes for refuge; caution is right, but strength can afford to keep its word.
st.rcm.vibhishan_refuge_debate.whole_arc_note: Do not drop Sugriva's caution or Ram's praise of it: the text treats suspicion as legitimate policy. Ram's decision rests on two grounds: his vow, and the plain judgement that even a spy cannot hurt them. Refuge here is not naivety; it is strength choosing to keep its word.

st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.title: Ram asks the ocean humbly for three days, then takes up the bow
st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand, dohas 48 to 58 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.teaching: Be humble first, but do not let humility be taken for granted; and forgive the moment the other side yields.
st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.whole_arc_note: The whole arc is the teaching: three days of humility, then firmness, then immediate forgiveness when the other side yields. Clip any part and it becomes either 'be meek' or 'use force'. Note: within the ocean's apology (5.57.chaupai.3) is the line 'dhol ganvar shudra pashu nari'. It is the ocean's speech, it demeans women and shudras, and it is excluded from every use of this story. The library prasang rcm.p.ocean spans it; anchor verses must skip it.

st.rcm.angad_the_envoy.title: Angad, sent to negotiate, is taunted with his father's death
st.rcm.angad_the_envoy.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand, dohas 19 to 35 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.angad_the_envoy.teaching: In a hostile negotiation, stay on the brief; let insults fall and do not let them move your foot.
st.rcm.angad_the_envoy.whole_arc_note: Ram's brief is the frame: the aim is the work done and the other side's good, not humiliation. Angad's wit is sharp but in service of the message. His grief about his father is not resolved here; it surfaces at the farewell (st.rcm.angad_asks_to_stay).

st.rcm.ram_lament_for_lakshman.title: Lakshman lies struck down, and Ram, waiting for dawn, breaks
st.rcm.ram_lament_for_lakshman.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand, dohas 48 to 60 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_lament_for_lakshman.teaching: Fear for a loved one's life can undo the steadiest person; help can arrive in the middle of the worst hour.
st.rcm.ram_lament_for_lakshman.whole_arc_note: The lament is extreme and that is the point: Ram, who held steady through exile and abduction, collapses at the thought of losing his brother. Note that one line (6.60.chaupai.6) ranks the loss of a wife below that of a brother; it is part of the lament's hyperbole of grief, but it is kept out of key_verses and should not be quoted. Do not end the story before Hanuman returns.

st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.title: Kumbhakarna tells Ravana he is wrong, and still goes out to fight for him
st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand, dohas 60 to 63 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.teaching: Tell family the truth to their face; honour the one who chose rightly even when you cannot.
st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.whole_arc_note: This is not a model of 'stand by family whatever they do'. The text praises Vibhishan for leaving and has Kumbhakarna say so; Kumbhakarna's own staying is framed as the pull of fate. What is admirable is his honesty to Ravana's face and his blessing of the brother who chose differently.

st.rcm.dharma_rath.title: Vibhishan panics to see Ram on foot against a chariot, and Ram describes the chariot that wins
st.rcm.dharma_rath.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand, dohas 78 to 79 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.dharma_rath.teaching: Victory rides on character: courage and steadiness as wheels, truth as flag, self-control as horses, devotion as charioteer.
st.rcm.dharma_rath.whole_arc_note: The question is a reasonable fear, not weak faith, and Ram answers it with patience. The external equipment is not dismissed (Ram fights with weapons); the point is what actually wins.

st.rcm.ram_hurries_home.title: Ram wins everything and will not stay a day, because his brother is waiting
st.rcm.ram_hurries_home.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand, dohas 110 to 111 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.ram_hurries_home.teaching: Success means little if it keeps you from the person who has been waiting for you.
st.rcm.ram_hurries_home.whole_arc_note: He does not refuse Vibhishan's love coldly; he says it is all his. He simply names whose need is more urgent. The pairing with st.rcm.bharat_last_day shows that the urgency was real.

st.rcm.bharat_last_day.title: One day is left and there is no news, and Bharat's mind swings
st.rcm.bharat_last_day.source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Uttar Kand, dohas 2 to 4 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts can run a few dohas higher)
st.rcm.bharat_last_day.teaching: When waiting turns into self-blame, lean on what you know of the other's nature, not on your own record.
st.rcm.bharat_last_day.whole_arc_note: Bharat is blameless and has done everything right; his self-reproach is not the text's verdict on him. It is the shape love takes when it is waiting and hears nothing. This story touches self_harm_theme (he will not live past the deadline); filter accordingly.

st.rcm.angad_asks_to_stay.title: Angad, whose father Ram killed, begs not to be sent away
