st.vr.ram_remembers_one_kindness.whole_arc_note: This describes a strong man's own choice about his own memory. Never turn it on a hurt person as 'you should forget what they did'.

st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.title: An ageing king rushes to hand over
st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 1 to 4
st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.teaching: A right decision carried out in fear and haste can undo itself.
st.vr.dasharatha_hurries_the_coronation.whole_arc_note: The decision itself was right and the whole city wanted it. What the text lets us see is the fear in the timing. Do not make Dasharatha a fool or a schemer.

st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.title: One voice in her ear: how Kaikeyi's mind was turned
st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 7 to 9
st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.teaching: A mind at peace can be turned in an hour by one adviser who speaks to its fear.
st.vr.manthara_turns_kaikeyi.whole_arc_note: Show that she began in goodwill; that is the warning. This is about a trusted adviser who feeds fear, and a mind that stops checking. Never frame it as the nature of women or of stepmothers. Kaikeyi was the queen who once saved the king's life in battle.

st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.title: Dasharatha swears first and hears the request after
st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 10 to 14
st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.teaching: Give your word only after you have heard what is being asked.
st.vr.dasharatha_trapped_by_his_promise.whole_arc_note: The text treats truthfulness as binding and does not offer him an escape, and it also shows plainly what the careless oath cost. Both stand. Do not teach 'break promises when they hurt', and do not praise the oath as noble.

st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.title: Ram hears he is exiled, on the morning he was to be crowned
st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 18 and 19
st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.teaching: A person whose worth does not rest on the prize can lose the prize without losing himself.
st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.whole_arc_note: The calm is not numbness. A few nights later, across the river, he speaks his hurt to Lakshman (sarga 53). Use the two together. Also: this is Ram's own choice about his own loss; do not hand it to a wronged person as an instruction to accept.

st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.title: Kausalya: I waited seventeen years for this day
st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 20 and 24
st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.teaching: A long hurt has to be spoken and heard before a person can let go.
st.vr.kausalya_hoped_her_sons_time_would.whole_arc_note: Her pain about the marriage is legitimate in the text and Ram does not correct it. The request that she stay with Dasharatha is Ram's to his mother in that hour; do not make it a rule that a neglected wife must stay and serve.

st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.title: Kausalya blesses the journey she begged him not to take
st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.teaching: When you cannot stop someone you love from going, you can still send your love with them.
st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.whole_arc_note: The blessing comes after the protest, and the fear is still in it. Do not present her as serene from the start.

st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.title: Lakshman is angrier about Ram's exile than Ram is
st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 21 to 23
st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.teaching: Anger on behalf of someone you love is best spent standing beside them in what they have chosen.
st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.whole_arc_note: The text gives Lakshman's case for effort real weight and never calls his anger wrong in itself. Ram does not win by argument; he asks as a brother. Do not clip to 'accept your fate', and note his words about his father are spoken in heat.

st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.title: Sita refuses to be left behind
st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 26 to 30
st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.teaching: Sharing a hard road by your own choice is a different thing from being protected from it.
st.vr.sita_chooses_the_forest.whole_arc_note: Some of her arguments use the idiom of a wife's duty; the thread to carry is that she insists on being a partner in the decision and wins. Do not use this to tell anyone they must follow a spouse into hardship. It is her will, stated against his wish.

st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.title: Lakshman picks up a spade and a basket
st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sarga 31, with sarga 40
st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.teaching: Service chosen freely, and described in concrete tasks, is a form of love.
st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.whole_arc_note: This is chosen service by a strong man who has other options, blessed by a mother who lets him go. Valmiki says nothing here of Urmila; do not invent her scene. Do not use it to tell someone in a one-sided relationship to keep giving.

st.vr.ram_gives_everything_away_trijata.title: Ram empties his house, and laughs with a poor brahmin
st.vr.ram_gives_everything_away_trijata.teaching: You can meet a great loss with open hands and even with humour.
st.vr.ram_gives_everything_away_trijata.whole_arc_note: A small scene; keep it small. It shows the temper of the man on the day he lost a kingdom. It is not advice to give away one's savings.

st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.title: Stay one more night: a father's last request
st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.teaching: Some goodbyes cannot be made easier, and love is shown in how they are said.
st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.whole_arc_note: No comfort is added. The text lets a father's plea go unanswered and does not call either of them wrong. Use it for the grief of partings that cannot be softened, not as a rule that duty outranks a parent's need.

st.vr.ram_first_night_bitterness.title: The calm one breaks, in private, on the first night across the river
st.vr.ram_first_night_bitterness.teaching: Composure in public and grief in private can belong to the same strong person.
st.vr.ram_first_night_bitterness.whole_arc_note: This sarga is the other half of the famous calm in sarga 19. Showing only the calm makes Ram unreal; showing only this makes him bitter. His words about Kaikeyi here are a night's fear, and later he forbids anyone to blame her.

st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.title: Ram slips away while the people who love him sleep
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 45 to 47
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.teaching: Sometimes love means not letting others carry what is yours to carry.
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.whole_arc_note: They are hurt by it, and the text shows that. The act is care, and it has a cost. Do not use it to excuse disappearing on people; he had already said his farewells in the city.

st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.title: Sumantra drives an empty chariot home
st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 52, 57 and 58
st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.teaching: Carrying hard news home, whole and unsoftened, is a service too.
st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.whole_arc_note: He reports faithfully, including Lakshman's harsh words, and then he consoles. Both are part of the job of bringing bad news. Do not make him a mere messenger; the text gives him his own grief.

st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.title: Sumitra consoles Kausalya, though her own son has gone too
st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.teaching: Comfort a frightened person with what is true and specific about the one they fear for.
st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.whole_arc_note: Sumitra's own loss is never mentioned by her, and a writer may note that quietly. Her words work because they are specific and because she shares the loss. Not a model for telling the bereaved to stop crying; Ram is alive.

st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.title: Kausalya says the cruel thing, and takes it back
st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 61 and 62
st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.teaching: Grief can speak in a voice that is not yours, and the repair can begin the moment you hear it.
st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.whole_arc_note: Her anger was fair; he had wronged her and their son. The text does not say she was wrong to feel it. It shows grief speaking through a person, and repair being made in the same hour. Do not use this to tell a wronged spouse to apologise.

st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.title: An old mistake comes due: Dasharatha remembers the boy at the river
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 63 and 64
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.teaching: An act done without thought does not vanish; it waits, and it is best met with open confession.
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.whole_arc_note: He was careless, not malicious, and he owned it at once to the parents. The text links act and consequence without calling Ram's exile a punishment of Ram. Do not turn it into 'your suffering is your karma' for a grieving reader.

st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.title: Bharata comes home to a silent city
st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 69 to 72
st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.teaching: Bad news that reaches you late and all at once has to be taken in before anything can be decided.
st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.whole_arc_note: The shock is the story. He was away, he was not consulted, and he arrives when nothing can be undone. Keep his innocence clear and do not hurry him to the noble response.

st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.title: Bharata's anger at the mother who did wrong for his sake
st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 73 and 74
st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.teaching: You can refuse a benefit that was won by wrongdoing, even when the wrongdoer is your own parent.
st.vr.bharata_rage_at_his_mother.whole_arc_note: His fury is given full voice and the text does not scold him for it; the wrong was real. What he does with the anger is the point: he acts to repair. Read with Ram's later request to him to protect Kaikeyi (sarga 112).

st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.title: Bharata is suspected by everyone he meets
st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 75, 85 and 90
st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.teaching: When you are blamed for what your family did, your own plain word and steady conduct are your answer.
st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.whole_arc_note: The suspicion is unjust and also understandable, and Bharata treats it as both. He is not told to be patient; he answers and acts. Do not suggest that the wrongly accused should stay silent.

st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.title: After the rites are done, the grief arrives
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 76 and 77
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.teaching: Grief often waits until the duties end; when it comes, what helps is knowing this is every creature's lot.
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.whole_arc_note: Vasishtha speaks after the collapse, once the tears have come, and what he offers is that this is the common lot. It is a hand up. Do not use his line to stop someone crying.

st.vr.bharata_stops_shatrughna.title: Bharata stops his brother's hand
st.vr.bharata_stops_shatrughna.teaching: When anger is justified, ask whether the act would let you face the one you most respect.
st.vr.bharata_stops_shatrughna.whole_arc_note: He admits the wish to strike; the restraint is honest. His stated reasons include the rule against harming women, in the idiom of the time; the usable core is asking 'what would the person I respect most think of this act'.

st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.title: Bharata refuses a throne everyone says is his
st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 79 and 82
st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.teaching: What came to you through a wrong does not become yours because everyone tells you to keep it.
st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.whole_arc_note: He is under no legal fault and still refuses, and he pairs the refusal with a plan. Do not reduce it to modesty; it is a judgement about how the thing was got.

st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.title: Bharata sees where his brother slept
st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 87 and 88
st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.teaching: Seeing closely what another has borne for you changes what you can accept for yourself.
st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.whole_arc_note: He was not at fault, and the text knows it; the vow is solidarity, not self-punishment for a crime. A writer should not recommend self-denial to someone drowning in guilt. The point is the question he asked and what the sight did to him.

st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.title: Lakshman sees an army and assumes the worst of his brother
st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 96 and 97
st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.teaching: Judge a person's intent by all you know of them, not by the most frightening reading of one sight.
st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.whole_arc_note: Lakshman's fear was reasonable on the evidence, and Ram corrects him without contempt; the joke about the kingdom stings a little and should stay. Do not use it to tell someone that a person with a real record of harm deserves trust.

st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.title: Ram on a hillside: I do not miss the kingdom
st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 94 and 95
st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.teaching: Joy does not wait for circumstances to be restored; it can be found in what is here and who is beside you.
st.vr.ram_content_at_chitrakoot.whole_arc_note: This is contentment spoken by a man at peace with his choice, months in. It comes after the grief of sarga 53, not in place of it. Never use it to tell someone who has lost a home that they should feel fine.

st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.title: Ram learns, in the forest, that his father has died
st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 102 and 103
st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.teaching: Mourning done from where you are, with what you have, is whole.
st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.whole_arc_note: The collapse is complete and is not shortened. The rite is done with what he has, and the text counts it a full rite. Good for anyone who could not be present or could not do things 'properly'.

st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.title: Ram, grieving himself, steadies his grieving brother
st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.teaching: Everything gathered is scattered and every meeting ends in parting; knowing it, use the days you have.
st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.whole_arc_note: This comes the day after Ram fell senseless with the same grief; the teaching is spoken by a mourner to a mourner. It belongs on a steady day, never as the first word to someone newly bereaved.

st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.title: A well-meaning elder tells Ram to drop his promise
st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 108 and 109
st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.teaching: A reasonable argument for dropping your word still has to answer who you become if you do.
st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.whole_arc_note: Jabali is not a villain; the tradition reads him as arguing a position to win Ram back, and he says so. Ram's reply is sharp. Use the scene for holding one's word under reasonable pressure, not for mocking doubt or doubters.

st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.title: The sandals: two brothers who both refuse to win
st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 111 and 112
st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.teaching: When two right duties collide, look for the arrangement in which both can be kept.
st.vr.bharata_and_the_sandals.whole_arc_note: The compromise costs Bharata fourteen years and he does not get what he came for. His vow to enter the fire is in the text and is a measure of his love, spoken in the heroic idiom; do not present it as a model. Mark and handle with care.

st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.title: Fourteen years of running what is not yours
st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.teaching: You can give your whole effort to work you hold in trust for another, and take none of it as yours.
st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.whole_arc_note: Trusteeship here is active, skilled rule, with full effort and no claim. The text notes he did it 'burning with grief'; it was not easy. Do not use it to tell an exploited worker to give without credit.

st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.title: Ram will not let anyone speak ill of Kaikeyi
st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sarga 112; Aranya Kanda, sarga 16
st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.teaching: The one who was wronged may choose not to keep the wrong alive in his own house.
st.vr.ram_will_not_hear_kaikeyi_blamed.whole_arc_note: This is the wronged person's own free choice, made from strength, and he never says the act was right. A plan must never hand it to a wronged user as a duty. It suits someone who already wants to stop feeding a family grudge.

st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.title: Before anything else, Ram asks his brother how he is running things
st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.teaching: Leadership is examined in small daily things: when you rise, whom you consult, whether people are paid on time.
st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.whole_arc_note: The chapter is a checklist in question form and is best excerpted honestly as such. Some questions are about spies, forts and armies; choose the ones that travel and do not pretend the list is complete.

st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.title: Sita tells Ram she is worried about what he is becoming
st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 9 and 10
st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.teaching: You can question someone you love by reminding, with affection and respect, and still be heard.
st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.whole_arc_note: She does not win the argument and the text still honours the speech; Ram calls it worthy of her. Keep both: her freedom to question, and his reasoned answer. Do not tell it as a wife being corrected.

st.vr.ram_thanks_lakshman_for_the_hut.title: Ram stops to thank the brother who built the hut
st.vr.ram_thanks_lakshman_for_the_hut.teaching: Say the thanks while the day is ordinary, and say exactly what the person is to you.
st.vr.ram_thanks_lakshman_for_the_hut.whole_arc_note: A small scene. Its weight is that the thanks is specific and unprompted. It should not be stretched into a sermon.

st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.title: Maricha tells his king the truth and is told: obey or die
st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 31 and 35 to 41
st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.teaching: Pleasant advisers are common; the one who tells you the unwelcome truth is rare, and so is the one willing to hear it.
st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.whole_arc_note: This is a warning, with no rescue in it. Honest counsel was given, once even heeded, and then crushed by a threat; compliance under threat still ended in ruin for both. Do not present Maricha's choice as wise. It names the bind of anyone ordered to do wrong by someone with power over them.

st.vr.the_golden_deer.title: The golden deer: wanting the thing that is too good to be true
st.vr.the_golden_deer.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 42 and 43
st.vr.the_golden_deer.teaching: When something dazzles you and a clear voice says it is false, notice how quickly you find reasons.
st.vr.the_golden_deer.whole_arc_note: The text gives the wanting to both of them: Sita asks, and Ram is himself captivated and decides. Lakshman's warning was correct and clear. Never tell this as a woman's greed bringing ruin. It is about how a bright object and a ready argument silence good advice.

st.vr.lakshman_between_an_order_and_an_a.title: Lakshman is accused by the person he is guarding
st.vr.lakshman_between_an_order_and_an_a.teaching: Fear for one we love can make us wound the very person who is protecting us.
st.vr.lakshman_between_an_order_and_an_a.whole_arc_note: Sita's words are panic, and the text shows her striking herself in fear; they are not her view of him. Lakshman's reply in the Sanskrit includes a bitter generalisation about women, spoken in hurt, which must not be quoted or endorsed. Blame neither. The thread is what fear makes us say and what accusation makes us do.

st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.title: Jatayu, old and outmatched, fights anyway
st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 50 and 51
st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.teaching: Some things are worth standing up for even when you are sure to lose.
st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.whole_arc_note: He does not win and the text does not pretend he does. His worth is in the stand and in the information he lived to give. He tried words first. Do not turn it into 'courage always succeeds'.

st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.title: Sita, carried off, does the one thing she can
st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sarga 54; Kishkindha Kanda, sarga 6
st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.teaching: When almost nothing is in your hands, the small thing that is can still be done.
st.vr.sita_drops_her_ornaments.whole_arc_note: The act is tiny and she cannot know it will matter. The payoff comes much later and through others. Keep that gap; it is the point.

st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.title: Ram, in panic, blames the brother who came to find him
st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 57 to 59
st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.teaching: In the first minutes of fear we look for someone to blame, and it is usually whoever is nearest.
st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.whole_arc_note: Ram is unfair here and the poet lets him be. Lakshman answers once and then carries it. Do not tidy it into Ram being right. It is useful to both sides: the one who blamed in panic, and the one who was blamed.

st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.title: Ram's grief turns to rage at the whole world
st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 60 to 65
st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.teaching: Grief with no one to blame can turn on everything; what calls a person back is being reminded of his own nature.
st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.whole_arc_note: Nothing here is softened: he raves, he wants to die, he threatens everything. He is brought back by being reminded who he is, not by being told to calm down. Do not skip the madness to get to the lesson, and do not present the rage as righteous.

st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.title: The younger brother has to hold up the elder
st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.teaching: To steady someone greater than you, remind them that the greatest have been struck too, and then turn to what can be done.
st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.whole_arc_note: Lakshman speaks from below, with deference ('who am I to teach you'). The counsel names fate and then at once turns to effort. Do not clip it to 'everyone suffers, get over it'.

st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.title: Ram gives a bird the rites of a father
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 67 and 68
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.teaching: Honour the one who stood up for you, whether or not they succeeded.
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.whole_arc_note: Jatayu did not save Sita. Ram honours the attempt in full and never mentions the failure. He also nearly shot him; grief had made him ready to see an enemy.

st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.title: Kabandha's advice: find someone who has lost what you have lost
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 69 to 73
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.teaching: When you are down, seek the friend who has suffered the same loss; you will understand and serve each other.
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.whole_arc_note: Help comes from an unlikely mouth and points to an unlikely ally: an exiled monkey, not a king. Ram takes both seriously. Do not gloss the oddness.

st.vr.shabari_waits.title: Shabari's long wait
st.vr.shabari_waits.teaching: Faithful practice kept up through years without result is itself the preparation for the day it is answered.
st.vr.shabari_waits.whole_arc_note: Stay with Valmiki: there are no tasted berries here, and nothing is made of her birth. She is a great ascetic honoured by other ascetics. Her entering the fire is the yogic leaving of the body at the end of a fulfilled life; tell it as completion and do not dwell on the manner.

st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.title: Spring at Pampa: beauty hurts when she is not there to see it
st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.teaching: Longing is sharpest in beautiful places, and it is answered by energy turned toward getting the person back.
st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.whole_arc_note: The lament runs for about a hundred verses before Lakshman speaks, and the poet does not hurry it. The line on utsaha is a brother's push after long listening. Do not serve it as a cure for missing someone.

st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.title: After his brother's betrayal, Sugriva sees an assassin in every stranger
st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.teaching: After a betrayal the mind sees the betrayer everywhere; send judgement ahead of fear and find out.
st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.whole_arc_note: His fear has a real cause; his brother did try to kill him. Hanuman does not deny the danger, he asks for evidence. Do not mock the fear.

st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.title: Hanuman's first words, and what Ram noticed about them
st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.teaching: How you speak in the first meeting, clear, unhurried, truthful and warm, opens what force cannot.
st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.whole_arc_note: The praise is of manner in the service of truth. Hanuman's content was straight. Do not sell it as a persuasion trick.

st.vr.ram_asks_a_monkey_for_help.title: The one everyone leaned on has to ask for help
st.vr.ram_asks_a_monkey_for_help.teaching: Even the one who has sheltered everyone may need shelter, and asking for it plainly is no fall.
st.vr.ram_asks_a_monkey_for_help.whole_arc_note: The text says this is Lakshman speaking with tears. The reversal is painful and is not disguised. Help follows because the need was stated honestly.

st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.title: A friend with the same wound tells Ram to stop crying
st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 5 to 7
st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.teaching: A friend who carries the same loss can say 'enough now', because he says it from inside.
st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.whole_arc_note: Sugriva is blunt and it works because he shares the loss and has just promised to act. From a stranger with no stake the same words would be cruel. Keep the promise and the shared wound in the telling.

st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.title: The cave: how two brothers who loved each other became enemies
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 9 and 10
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.teaching: A rift between brothers can begin with each one reading the evidence honestly and one refusing to listen.
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.whole_arc_note: This is Sugriva's account, given to Ram. Even on his telling, both acted from what they saw: one from apparent evidence, one from apparent betrayal. Vali's later taking of Ruma goes beyond misunderstanding and is what the text condemns.

st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.title: Sugriva asks for proof, and Ram is not offended
st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 11 and 12
st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.teaching: Someone who has been burned may ask for proof, and a true friend gives it without taking offence.
st.vr.sugriva_needs_proof_before_he_trus.whole_arc_note: The doubter is treated with respect and so is the doubt. Sugriva even asks for a second proof. The text presents confidence as something a friend may fairly ask to be shown.

st.vr.sugriva_let_down_in_the_first_duel.title: Sugriva is beaten while his ally stands watching
st.vr.sugriva_let_down_in_the_first_duel.teaching: When a friend's failure hurts you, say so to him; a true friend answers with the reason and a remedy.
st.vr.sugriva_let_down_in_the_first_duel.whole_arc_note: The complaint is fair and is spoken to the friend's face; the answer is an explanation and a practical change, with no wounded pride on either side. That exchange is the whole value of the scene.

st.vr.tara_warns_vali.title: Tara tells Vali what he does not want to hear
st.vr.tara_warns_vali.teaching: The person who loves you may be seeing the danger your pride cannot see.
st.vr.tara_warns_vali.whole_arc_note: Tara was right in every detail and the text has Vali admit it too late. She speaks from intelligence and care. Do not make her a nagging wife or Vali a brute; he is tender with her and proud.

st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.title: Vali, dying, asks Ram: what did I do to you?
st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 17 and 18
st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.teaching: A person certain he was wronged may, on hearing the whole account, see his own act within it.
st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.whole_arc_note: This is a contested episode and must be told whole. Vali's charge is serious and the text gives it full force; it is not to be brushed aside. Ram's reply rests on a king's duty to punish a grave wrong (the taking of Ruma), and commentators such as Govindaraja stress that Vali himself accepts it. A writer must not present ambush as generally acceptable, nor decide the matter beyond what the text does. Serve only where a reader wants the full argument.

st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.title: Vali's last words to the brother he wronged and the son he leaves
st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.teaching: Even at the very end a quarrel can be closed and a child's future secured by saying the plain words.
st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.whole_arc_note: Reconciliation comes at the last hour and only from the one who had the power. Sugriva was the wronged one; nothing here says he owed forgiveness earlier. Vali's advice to Angada about fitting in at court is a father's realism, not a general rule to submit.

st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.title: Tara, suddenly widowed, is told to think of her son
st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 19 to 21 and 24
st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.teaching: In fresh grief a person needs to be held, and the duties come back in their own time.
st.vr.tara_widowed_asks_to_follow.whole_arc_note: Keep both halves: her refusal to be hurried, and her later strength. Do not use Hanuman's 'think of your son' as a rebuke to a fresh griever; in the text it does not work at first. Her wish to die is real and must be flagged.

st.vr.sugriva_won_and_cannot_bear_it.title: Sugriva gets everything he fought for and is sick with guilt
st.vr.sugriva_won_and_cannot_bear_it.teaching: Getting what you fought for does not end the grief of having fought your own.
st.vr.sugriva_won_and_cannot_bear_it.whole_arc_note: Sugriva was genuinely wronged by Vali; his remorse does not cancel that. The story is about how winning a fight against family can still leave grief and guilt, and about saying it honestly. His wish to die is stated; flag it.

st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.title: Ram has to wait four months and cannot bear the waiting
st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 27 and 28
st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.teaching: Brooding wears down every purpose; a wait can be used to keep resolve alive.
st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.whole_arc_note: The waiting is imposed by the world, not chosen. Ram does not stop missing Sita; he stops letting the missing decide what he does.

st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.title: Hanuman reminds a comfortable king of a promise
st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.teaching: A friend's work done late is a promise broken, however grand the effort later.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.whole_arc_note: Hanuman's counsel is respectful and timed; it begins the correction but does not finish it. Keep that it took Lakshman's anger too.

st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.title: Once he is safe, Sugriva forgets the man who saved him
st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 28 to 31
st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.teaching: Ease makes people forget their debts; a promise kept is what makes a person great.
st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.whole_arc_note: Sugriva is not wicked; he is a rescued man who relaxed. Keep Ram's hurt and his warning both; Ram is not being petty, and Sugriva does recover.

st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.title: Tara walks out to meet an angry man and lowers the temperature
st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 33 to 35
st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.teaching: Admit the fault, point to the shared aim, show the first step taken; anger has nothing left to push against.
st.vr.tara_calms_lakshman.whole_arc_note: Tara does not excuse Sugriva's drift; she names it. She calms Lakshman by agreeing on the facts and showing the work has begun. Lakshman's anger was justified; Tara does not tell him he was wrong to feel it.

st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.title: Sugriva apologises without grovelling or excuses
st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.teaching: A good apology names the debt, admits the lapse, and moves straight to the work.
st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.whole_arc_note: The apology comes after real fault and with real action. Keep that it includes gratitude, admission and a next step together.

st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.title: The search party misses its deadline and wants to give up and die
st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 53 to 55
st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.teaching: Fear of how others will react can talk a whole group into despair; the way forward can appear at the lowest point.
st.vr.angada_deadline_missed.whole_arc_note: Must not end at the fast. The despair is shown as a spiral fed by fear and old resentment, and it is broken by information, not by willpower. Self-harm theme is explicit.

st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.title: An old bird who lost everything is told to wait, because he will be needed
st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 56 to 63
st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.teaching: A life that feels useless may be holding exactly what someone else will need.
st.vr.sampati_lived_on_for_a_reason.whole_arc_note: Both despairs meet: the old bird who wanted to die and the young team who were fasting to die. Each is saved by the other. Keep the long wait; it is the point. Self-harm theme is explicit. Do not quote 4.61.11, which names the method he considered.

st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.title: Everyone states what they can do, and the old bear admits he is past it
st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.teaching: An honest account of your limits frees you to give what you can give.
st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.whole_arc_note: Do not read his age as defeat; it is the moment he becomes most useful. Keep the honest listing of limits by every leader; no one inflates themselves.

st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.title: Hanuman sits apart, silent, until someone tells him who he is
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda, sargas 66 and 67
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.teaching: Sometimes the strength is already there and someone who knows your story has to name it.
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.whole_arc_note: In Kishkindha Kanda itself Valmiki shows only the silence and the reminder; the curse explanation comes later in Uttara Kanda. Do not overstate either. The story works because someone else sees him clearly.

st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.title: Hanuman is offered rest halfway and says no, kindly
st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.teaching: A pledged task can decline even good comforts, so long as the giver is honoured.
st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.whole_arc_note: He does not reject the giver; he touches the mountain and accepts the goodwill while declining the stop. Not a lesson against rest in general; it is about a pledged task with a deadline.

st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.title: Hanuman meets a test he cannot win by growing bigger
st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.teaching: When matching force only escalates, a humbler move can fulfil the condition and open the way.
st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.whole_arc_note: He respects her boon and wins by humility and wit, not force. The test was sent by the gods to measure his strength; his intelligence is what passes it.

st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.title: Hanuman has looked at sleeping women and his conscience stops him
st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sarga 11 (library vr.5.11.26 to 34; Gita Press 5.11.37 to 45)
st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.teaching: Judge an act by the mind behind it and by its necessity; examine yourself honestly, then go on.
st.vr.hanuman_uneasy_in_ravanas_chambers.whole_arc_note: He does not dismiss the worry, and he does not wallow in it. He tests his intention, the necessity of the act, and his inner state, then proceeds. This is not a licence to excuse anything by 'my intention was pure'; it is inquiry made under a real duty.

st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.title: Hanuman cannot find Sita, thinks of ending it, and talks himself back
st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 12 and 13 (library vr.5.12.10, vr.5.13.3 to 54)
st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.teaching: Despondency is the enemy of every aim; while one lives, good can still be seen.
st.vr.hanuman_despair_and_self_talk_in_l.whole_arc_note: Keep both the depth of the despair and the reasoning back. Do not clip at the thought of dying, and do not jump to the finding as if the despair did not matter. Self-harm theme is explicit: serve only when risk is none, and never quote the verses that list ways of dying (13.33, 13.37 to 39). The catastrophising chain he builds is shown as part of the despair, not as fact.

st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.title: Hanuman finally finds Sita and cannot stop weeping at her state
st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 15 and 16
st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.teaching: Even the best protected can be overtaken by hard times; seeing someone's suffering clearly is the start of real help.
st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.whole_arc_note: Finding is not fixing. The joy of success is immediately overtaken by grief for the person found; keep both.

st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.title: Sita, alone and threatened, puts a blade of grass between herself and Ravana
st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 20 to 22
st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.teaching: Dignity can hold a line that power cannot cross, even when one is helpless and afraid.
st.vr.sita_blade_of_grass.whole_arc_note: Her courage does not mean she is unafraid; she trembles and weeps throughout. The firmness is in what she says, not in feeling calm. She is wronged; nothing here asks her to adjust or forgive.

st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.title: Sita, threatened every day, reaches the end of what she can bear
st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 25 to 29
st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.teaching: At the very edge, hold on for the next sign; help may already be closer than it looks.
st.vr.sita_at_the_end_of_her_strength.whole_arc_note: This is self-harm theme in its plainest form; serve only when risk is none. Keep the arc whole: the despair is answered by signs of hope and then by an actual messenger. Do not make her strength sound easy. Do not quote the verse in which she takes hold of her braid (5.28.17 in this numbering); it names a method.

st.vr.trijata_dream.title: One of the guards takes the prisoner's side
st.vr.trijata_dream.teaching: A single voice for the vulnerable, from within, can change the room.
st.vr.trijata_dream.whole_arc_note: Trijata is one of the guards. Her goodness comes from inside the wrong side, not from outside it.

st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.title: Hanuman thinks through how to speak to a frightened woman without scaring her
st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.teaching: Before you speak to someone in fear, think of how your words will land in their state.
st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.whole_arc_note: Keep how long he deliberates; the story is the thinking. It is care for her state, not tactics alone.

st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.title: Sita has been deceived once and fears the kind stranger is another trick
st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 32 to 35
st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.teaching: After betrayal, trust is rebuilt by patient, concrete proof, not by asking someone to trust.
st.vr.sita_fears_it_is_another_trick.whole_arc_note: Her suspicion is reasonable after what was done to her. Hanuman earns trust patiently and does not blame her for doubting.

st.vr.sita_refuses_the_easy_rescue.title: Offered a quick escape, Sita says she wants it done properly
st.vr.sita_refuses_the_easy_rescue.teaching: Sometimes the quick way out costs what matters most; a resolution has to be the right one.
st.vr.sita_refuses_the_easy_rescue.whole_arc_note: Several reasons together, practical and personal: safety, Hanuman's risk, Ram's honour, her own vow. Do not reduce it to one. It is her choice, made from strength, not passivity.

st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.title: Hanuman lets himself be bound, because it gets him to the king
st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.teaching: Pride can be set aside for a purpose; being underestimated can be the way in.
st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.whole_arc_note: Accepting humiliation here is a choice made from strength, for a purpose; it is not a counsel to bear mistreatment in general.

st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.title: Bound in the enemy's court, Hanuman tells the king what no one else dares
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 50 and 51
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.teaching: Truth to the powerful is best spoken respectfully and plainly, whatever they do with it.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.whole_arc_note: Speaking truth to power does not guarantee it will be heard. Keep that Ravana refuses; the worth of the act is in its rightness, not its result.

st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.title: Vibhishana stands up in court to stop his brother killing a messenger
st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.teaching: Anger in someone powerful can sometimes be turned by appealing to what they know is right.
st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.whole_arc_note: This is the first of Vibhishana's stands; it partly succeeds. Keep it linked to his later counsel and exile.

st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.title: Hanuman burns the city in anger and then fears he has destroyed what he came to save
st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 54 and 55
st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.teaching: Anger acts first and thinks later; when fear of the damage comes, check the facts before condemning yourself.
st.vr.hanuman_burns_lanka_then_panics.whole_arc_note: Keep both the honest admission that anger led him and the stop before despair. He does not excuse the anger; he also does not drown in guilt before checking. Self-harm theme is present.

st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.title: The team comes home with good news and celebrates a little too hard
st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda, sargas 61 to 63
st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.teaching: A wise leader reads what a team's behaviour says before reacting to it.
st.vr.monkeys_raid_the_honey_garden.whole_arc_note: A light episode. Do not make it moralising about drinking; the point is a leader who reads a team's mood rightly and lets a success be celebrated.

st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.title: Ram has nothing worthy to give Hanuman, so he gives himself
st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.teaching: When you cannot repay a great kindness, give yourself fully in thanks.
st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.whole_arc_note: Gratitude here is not payment. Ram names his inability to repay, then gives the one thing he can, wholly.

st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.title: At the ocean shore Ram loses heart again, and a friend will not let him
st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 1 and 2
st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.teaching: Despondency sinks every aim; a friend's honest push can restore the will to act.
st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.whole_arc_note: Despair returns even after good news; it is not a single battle. The friend who was once comforted by Ram now comforts him.

st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.title: Vibhishana tells his brother the truth and is called a traitor for it
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 9 to 16
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.teaching: Rare is the one who says the unwelcome truth, and rarer the one who listens to it.
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.whole_arc_note: He leaves only after repeated, respectful counsel and a public insult; he does not abandon lightly. He still wishes his brother well as he goes. Keep the cost.

st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.title: Vibhishana leaves the wrong side and the right side does not trust him
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 17 and 18
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.teaching: One who comes in good faith is not turned away; honesty about where you come from earns shelter.
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.whole_arc_note: Keep both the suspicion and the trust. The suspicion is reasonable; Ram does not dismiss his advisers, he hears them and decides. Vibhishana's honesty is what gets him in.

st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.title: Ram asks the ocean politely for three days, then picks up his bow
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 21 and 22
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.teaching: Be humble and patient first; when that is taken for weakness, be firm, and stop as soon as you are heard.
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.whole_arc_note: This is the defining whole-arc story: humble first, for a real length of time, then firm. Do not clip either half. The firmness ends the moment the other side responds.

st.vr.ram_lets_the_spies_go.title: Enemy spies are caught in his camp and Ram lets them walk around
st.vr.ram_lets_the_spies_go.teaching: One who is prepared and in the right need not fear being seen.
st.vr.ram_lets_the_spies_go.whole_arc_note: Confidence here is real, built on preparation. It is not naivety; Vibhishana caught them first.

st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.title: Sita is shown her husband's head, and a friend in the enemy house tells her it is a lie
st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 31 to 34
st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.teaching: At the worst news, a steady friend who checks the truth can bring one back.
st.vr.sita_shown_a_false_head.whole_arc_note: Her grief is fully real even though the cause was false. Do not mock it. The help comes from someone inside the enemy's house.

st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.title: Ravana is told by the elders to make peace and says he will break before he bows
st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 35 and 36
st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.teaching: Pride that knows itself and still will not bend brings down everything around it.
st.vr.ravana_would_rather_break_than_ben.whole_arc_note: A cautionary story. The striking thing is that Ravana knows it is a fault and keeps it anyway. Use as a mirror, never as a label for a user.

st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.title: Ram has his enemy beaten and tells him to go home and come back rested
st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.teaching: Even against one who has wronged you, keep your own code; do not strike the defenceless.
st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.whole_arc_note: Ram's restraint does not mean he gives up the fight or forgives Ravana's wrong; he defeats him later. It is about how he fights.

st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.title: Kumbhakarna tells his brother he is wrong, then goes out to fight for him anyway
st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.teaching: Say the truth to family plainly; loyalty to a wrong cause still shares its fate.
st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.whole_arc_note: The text shows both his honesty and the cost of his loyalty. The tradition does not hold up fighting for adharma as right; it shows why it ends in ruin. Use for the bind of family loyalty, never as advice to support wrongdoing.

st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.title: Lakshman falls in battle and Ram no longer wants to win
st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 101 and 102
st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.teaching: Grief for someone we cannot live without can empty victory of meaning; help and their own voice bring us back.
st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.whole_arc_note: The line about wives and kin is grief speaking in the extremity, not a valuation of Sita below Lakshman; keep it in its scene. Ram's collapse is real and is honoured, not corrected.

st.vr.ram_exhausted_before_the_last_figh.title: Ram stands exhausted and anxious before the final battle
st.vr.ram_exhausted_before_the_last_figh.teaching: Before the hardest moment, draw strength from what is greater than you, then act.
st.vr.ram_exhausted_before_the_last_figh.whole_arc_note: Even Ram is shown exhausted and anxious before the hardest moment; the remedy is spiritual and immediate. Do not present it as a substitute for effort; he still fights.

st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.title: Vibhishana left his brother for the right side, and still grieves when he dies
st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 108 and 109
st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.teaching: Enmity ends at death; one can grieve the person while having rejected the wrong.
st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.whole_arc_note: Leaving someone who did wrong and mourning them when they die are not contradictions. The text allows both. Keep that Ram, the injured party, is the one who says so.

st.vr.mandodari_grieves_a_husband_who_di.title: Mandodari mourns a husband she loved and could not save from himself
st.vr.mandodari_grieves_a_husband_who_di.teaching: One can mourn someone and still see plainly how they brought their fall upon themselves.
st.vr.mandodari_grieves_a_husband_who_di.whole_arc_note: Her grief is real and her judgement is clear; keep both. It is not a story about blaming the other woman; Mandodari places the fault in Ravana's own unchecked desire.

st.vr.sita_will_not_punish_her_guards.title: Sita is offered revenge on the women who tormented her, and refuses
st.vr.sita_will_not_punish_her_guards.teaching: The noble keep their own standard of conduct; compassion is shown even to those who erred, for no one never errs.
st.vr.sita_will_not_punish_her_guards.whole_arc_note: She is the wronged person and the choice is entirely hers; nothing here says a wronged person must forgive. She chooses compassion from strength, after the danger has ended, and distinguishes the order-giver from those who obeyed.

st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.title: Sita is doubted in public by the person who knows her best, and answers
st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 115 to 118
st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.teaching: Character is in what was in one's own power; a false charge can be answered with dignity and plain truth.
st.vr.sita_answers_public_suspicion.whole_arc_note: Contested episode; include only for Sita's answer. Her words are the centre: she names the injustice to his face. Ram's stated reason (public proof, sarga 118) must be given in full, without endorsing the harshness. Never use to suggest a wronged person should prove themselves. Her walking into the fire is a refusal to live under a false charge; flag self_harm honestly.

st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.title: Coming home after fourteen years, Ram is ready to let his brother keep the throne
st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.teaching: One who holds possessions lightly can let go even of what is rightfully theirs, to keep a brother.
st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.whole_arc_note: Ram is not testing Bharata to catch him out; he is preparing himself to let go. Keep that he would truly have stepped aside.

st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.title: Bharata gives back the kingdom he held for fourteen years, grown tenfold
st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 126 and 127
st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.teaching: What is held in trust is to be grown and returned without claim; that completes a life's purpose.
st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.whole_arc_note: Trusteeship is the whole story: he grew what he held and claimed nothing. Keep his long years of austerity, not only the happy handover.

st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.title: Ram tells Hanuman he hopes he never gets the chance to repay him
st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.teaching: Some debts are best carried with love rather than repaid, since repayment would need the friend's misfortune.
st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.whole_arc_note: Gratitude here is a lifelong debt held gladly, not a burden to discharge. Keep both Hanuman's request and Ram's reply.

st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.title: After a private grief, a king realises his people have waited four days
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda, sargas 53 to 55
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.teaching: Those who depend on us keep waiting while we grieve; returning to them is part of carrying the grief.
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.whole_arc_note: This comes right after his own great grief; it does not deny the grief. It shows a leader returning to duty because others are waiting on him, without self-pity.

st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.title: Lakshman has to take Sita to the forest and tell her she is not coming back
st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda, sargas 45 to 47
st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.teaching: When made the instrument of a hard order, at least carry it with truth and compassion.
st.vr.lakshman_carries_out_the_order_he_.whole_arc_note: Contested episode. The story is Lakshman's anguish as the one made to carry it out; the text does not present the exile as just, and Lakshman's own grief says so. Never use to suggest a wronged person should accept such treatment.

st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.title: Sita, abandoned and pregnant, chooses what she will say and how she will live
st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda, sargas 48 and 49
st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.teaching: Even when wronged without cause, one can keep one's own truth and dignity and go on living for what one carries.
st.vr.sita_abandoned_and_still_herself.whole_arc_note: Contested episode. The story must not be read as endorsing her abandonment. Her innocence is stated by her and by the text. Her restraint is hers to choose; a wronged reader must never be told to endure similar treatment. Self-harm thought is present.

st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.title: Ram wants the greatest sacrifice of all, and his younger brother talks him out of it
st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.teaching: A wise leader drops a grand plan that would harm others when a junior speaks the truth.
st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.whole_arc_note: The leader asks for honest counsel and actually changes his mind. Keep that he is pleased, not wounded.

st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.title: Asked to prove her purity a second time, Sita leaves instead
st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda, sargas 96 and 97
st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.teaching: There is a point at which a person of integrity will not keep proving themselves.
st.vr.sita_will_not_prove_herself_again.whole_arc_note: Contested and painful. It is the dignity of refusing a second test. Do not frame it as a happy ending or as a model of disappearing. Strongly gender sensitive; it is about the limits of what anyone owes to public suspicion.

st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.title: Lakshman chooses to break a rule and pay for it alone, to save everyone else
st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda, sargas 105 and 106
st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.teaching: One who takes the cost on himself so that others are spared acts from a love larger than fear.
st.vr.lakshman_takes_the_curse_on_himsel.whole_arc_note: A story about a promise's cost and a brother's self-giving. Lakshman's departure is a yogic leaving of the body, not despair; still, flag it truthfully and do not serve when risk is present. Do not present it as a model of self-sacrifice to vulnerable readers.

st.vr.guha_offers_everything_to_a_fallen.title: A friend offers his whole kingdom to Ram on the first night of exile
st.vr.guha_offers_everything_to_a_fallen.teaching: A true friend comes on foot at the low point and offers all; a true friend can accept love while declining gifts.
st.vr.guha_offers_everything_to_a_fallen.whole_arc_note: Friendship that does not depend on status. Ram's refusal honours both his vow and Guha; nothing is lost between them.

st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.title: Lakshman will not sleep on the first night of exile
st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda, sargas 50 and 51
st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.teaching: When someone we love is brought low, keeping watch beside them is itself a form of love.
st.vr.lakshman_cannot_sleep_while_ram_sl.whole_arc_note: This is grief and loyalty together; it is not a prescription to deny oneself rest. Keep Guha as the listener; Lakshman shares the burden with someone.

st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.title: Sita realises the holy man at her door is Ravana and does not shrink
st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.source_ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda, sargas 47 and 48
st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.teaching: Dignity speaks the truth to a predator even when it cannot stop him.
st.vr.sita_faces_ravana_at_the_hut.whole_arc_note: Her courage does not prevent the abduction; the text does not pretend that words are protection. Keep that the wrong is entirely his.

prasang:bg.p01.2.title: The conches sound on both sides
prasang:bg.p01.2.teaching: Before any hard moment there is noise and bravado; the real test comes after.

prasang:bg.p01.3.title: Arjuna surveys the armies
prasang:bg.p01.3.teaching: Sometimes the hardest moment is simply seeing clearly who is on the other side.

prasang:bg.p11.1.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
prasang:bg.p11.1.teaching: Ask humbly for what you long to see.

prasang:bg.p11.2.title: Krishna describes his cosmic form
prasang:bg.p11.2.teaching: Some truths need new eyes, not more effort.

prasang:bg.p11.3.title: Sanjaya describes the cosmic form to Dhritarashtra

prasang:bg.p11.4.title: Arjuna sees the cosmic form and praises it
prasang:bg.p11.4.teaching: Facing something vast can shake you to the core, and that's human.

prasang:bg.p11.7.title: Krishna returns to his gentle form
prasang:bg.p11.7.teaching: After the storm, kindness and a familiar face restore us.

prasang:hans_gita.p.swan_and_sadhyas.title: The golden swan and the Sadhyas
prasang:hans_gita.p.swan_and_sadhyas.teaching: Self-control, calm under insult and truth are the best way to live.

prasang:vr.p.bridge.title: Building the bridge
prasang:vr.p.bridge.teaching: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

prasang:rcm.p.ram_bharat_resolution.title: Ram and Bharat settle it
prasang:rcm.p.ram_bharat_resolution.teaching: A good resolution gives each person a role and something to hold on to.

prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_bali.title: Sugriva and Bali: brothers split by a misunderstanding
prasang:rcm.p.sugriva_bali.teaching: Brothers can become enemies over one misread moment; ask before you assume betrayal.

prasang:rcm.p.prahasta_mandodari.title: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
prasang:rcm.p.prahasta_mandodari.teaching: Some people cannot hear good advice; give it, then stop beating yourself up.

prasang:rcm.p.bharat_milap.title: Ram comes home
prasang:rcm.p.bharat_milap.teaching: Homecoming means gratitude to those who carried you and kindness to those ashamed to face you.

prasang:viv.p.chicago.paper_on_hinduism.title: 'Children of immortal bliss': the Paper on Hinduism (Chicago, 19 September 1893)
prasang:viv.p.chicago.paper_on_hinduism.teaching: You are not a sinner to be fixed; you are a soul to be uncovered.

prasang:viv.p.chicago.final_session.title: 'Help and not fight': the closing address (Chicago, 27 September 1893)
prasang:viv.p.chicago.final_session.teaching: Take in what is good from others, and keep growing as yourself.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.title: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.vibhishan_refuge.teaching: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

prasang:vr.p.bhakti.refuge.title: Valmiki: Ram's vow of refuge and the dove
prasang:vr.p.bhakti.refuge.teaching: Refuge is a vow, not a reward for the deserving: once someone says 'I'm yours', they are safe.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kevat.title: Kevat washes Ram's feet
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.kevat.teaching: Love can be playful and stubborn; God enjoys being loved that way.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shabari.title: Shabari's wait and the nine forms of devotion
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.shabari.teaching: Your simple offering is enough; love, not status, is the only kinship that counts.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sugriva.title: Sugriva: frightened, lifted, forgetful, forgiven
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.sugriva.teaching: Fear is heard, failure is forgiven, and then you get back to the work.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.bharat.title: Bharat's love: the boon, the meeting, the sandals
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.bharat.teaching: Love can be lived as responsibility: do the work in the name of the one you love.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_vibhishan.title: Hanuman finds a devotee in Lanka
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.hanuman_vibhishan.teaching: In a hostile place, one friend who shares your faith can be enough.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.spear.title: Ram takes the spear meant for Vibhishan
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.spear.teaching: A promise of shelter is kept with one's own body.

prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.farewell.title: The friends who couldn't leave
prasang:rcm.p.bhakti.farewell.teaching: Pure love moves God more than any practice; it can even change his plans.

prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.petition.title: Tulsidas's petition is signed
prasang:tulsi.p.bhakti.petition.teaching: After all the pleading, the book ends held: you were already noticed.

prasang:mbh.p.k.vidura_hospitality.title: Krishna refuses the king's feast and eats at Vidura's house
prasang:mbh.p.k.vidura_hospitality.teaching: God accepts love, not lavishness; a simple meal given with devotion is the real feast.

prasang:sur.p.k.sudama.title: Sudama at Krishna's door (as Surdas sings it)
prasang:sur.p.k.sudama.teaching: Old friendship and love do not check your bank balance at the door.

prasang:up.p.devi_who_are_you.title: The gods ask the Goddess: who are you?
prasang:up.p.devi_who_are_you.teaching: The Mother who is everything is also near enough to be called on in fear.
